title: Building Enterprise AI-Powered Software Engineering Tools with Multi-Modal Agent Architecture
short_summary: Windsurf developed an enterprise-focused AI-powered software development platform that extends beyond traditional code generation to encompass the full software engineering workflow. The company built a comprehensive system including a VS Code fork (Windsurf IDE), custom models, advanced retrieval systems, and integrations across multiple developer touchpoints like browsers and PR reviews. Their approach focuses on human-AI collaboration through "flows" while systematically expanding from code-only context to multi-modal data sources, achieving significant improvements in code acceptance rates and demonstrating frontier performance compared to leading models like Claude Sonnet.

title: Refining Input Guardrails for Safer LLM Applications Through Chain-of-Thought Fine-Tuning
short_summary: Capital One developed enhanced input guardrails to protect LLM-powered conversational assistants from adversarial attacks and malicious inputs. The company used chain-of-thought prompting combined with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and alignment techniques like Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) to improve the accuracy of LLM-as-a-Judge moderation systems. Testing on four open-source models (Mistral 7B, Mixtral 8x7B, Llama2 13B, and Llama3 8B) showed significant improvements in F1 scores and attack detection rates of over 50%, while maintaining low false positive rates, demonstrating that effective guardrails can be achieved with small training datasets and minimal computational resources.

title: Structured AI Workflow Orchestration for Developer Productivity at Scale
short_summary: Shopify's Augmented Engineering team developed Roast, an open-source workflow orchestration framework that structures AI agents to solve developer productivity challenges like flaky tests and low test coverage. The team discovered that breaking complex AI tasks into discrete, structured steps was essential for reliable performance at scale, leading them to create a convention-over-configuration tool that combines deterministic code execution with AI-powered analysis, enabling reproducible and testable AI workflows that can be version-controlled and integrated into development processes.

title: Implementing MCP Gateway for Large-Scale LLM Integration Infrastructure
short_summary: Anthropic faced the challenge of managing an explosion of LLM-powered services and integrations across their organization, leading to duplicated functionality and integration chaos. They solved this by implementing a standardized MCP (Model Context Protocol) gateway that provides a single point of entry for all LLM integrations, handling authentication, credential management, and routing to both internal and external services. This approach reduced engineering overhead, improved security by centralizing credential management, and created a "pit of success" where doing the right thing became the easiest thing to do for their engineering teams.

title: Enterprise Unstructured Data Quality Management for Production AI Systems
short_summary: Anomalo addresses the critical challenge of unstructured data quality in enterprise AI deployments by building an automated platform on AWS that processes, validates, and cleanses unstructured documents at scale. The solution automates OCR and text parsing, implements continuous data observability to detect anomalies, enforces governance and compliance policies including PII detection, and leverages Amazon Bedrock for scalable LLM-based document quality analysis. This approach enables enterprises to transform their vast collections of unstructured text data into trusted assets for production AI applications while reducing operational burden, optimizing costs, and maintaining regulatory compliance.

title: Building Secure Generative AI Applications at Scale: Amazon's Journey from Experimental to Production
short_summary: Amazon faced the challenge of securing generative AI applications as they transitioned from experimental proof-of-concepts to production systems like Rufus (shopping assistant) and internal employee chatbots. The company developed a comprehensive security framework that includes enhanced threat modeling, automated testing through their FAST (Framework for AI Security Testing) system, layered guardrails, and "golden path" templates for secure-by-default deployments. This approach enabled Amazon to deploy customer-facing and internal AI applications while maintaining security, compliance, and reliability standards through continuous monitoring, evaluation, and iterative refinement processes.

title: Generating 3D Shoppable Product Visualizations with Veo Video Generation Model
short_summary: Google developed a three-generation evolution of AI-powered systems to transform 2D product images into interactive 3D visualizations for online shopping, culminating in a solution based on their Veo video generation model. The challenge was to replicate the tactile, hands-on experience of in-store shopping in digital environments while making the technology scalable and cost-effective for retailers. The latest approach uses Veo's diffusion-based architecture, fine-tuned on millions of synthetic 3D assets, to generate realistic 360-degree product spins from as few as one to three product images. This system now powers interactive 3D visualizations across multiple product categories on Google Shopping, significantly improving the online shopping experience by enabling customers to virtually inspect products from multiple angles.

title: Hybrid LLM-Optimization System for Trip Planning with Real-World Constraints
short_summary: Google Research developed a hybrid system for trip planning that combines LLMs with optimization algorithms to address the challenge of generating practical travel itineraries. The system uses Gemini models to generate initial trip plans based on user preferences and qualitative goals, then applies a two-stage optimization algorithm that incorporates real-world constraints like opening hours, travel times, and budget considerations to produce feasible itineraries. This approach was implemented in Google's "AI trip ideas in Search" feature, demonstrating how LLMs can be effectively deployed in production while maintaining reliability through algorithmic correction of potential feasibility issues.

title: Implementing Evaluation Framework for MCP Server Tool Selection
short_summary: Neon developed a comprehensive evaluation framework to test their Model Context Protocol (MCP) server's ability to correctly use database migration tools. The company faced challenges with LLMs selecting appropriate tools from a large set of 20+ tools, particularly for complex stateful workflows involving database migrations. Their solution involved creating automated evals using Braintrust, implementing "LLM-as-a-judge" scoring techniques, and establishing integrity checks to ensure proper tool usage. Through iterative prompt engineering guided by these evaluations, they improved their tool selection success rate from 60% to 100% without requiring code changes.

title: Scaling AI Applications with LLMs: Dynamic Context Injection and Few-Shot Learning for Order Processing
short_summary: Choco built a comprehensive AI system to automate food supply chain order processing, addressing challenges with diverse order formats across text messages, PDFs, and voicemails. The company developed a production LLM system using few-shot learning with dynamically retrieved examples, semantic embedding-based retrieval, and context injection techniques to improve information extraction accuracy. Their approach prioritized prompt-based improvements over fine-tuning, enabling faster iteration and model flexibility while building towards more autonomous AI systems through continuous learning from human annotations.

title: Agentic AI Manufacturing Reasoner for Automated Root Cause Analysis
short_summary: Apollo Tyres developed a Manufacturing Reasoner powered by Amazon Bedrock Agents to automate root cause analysis for their tire curing processes. The solution replaced manual analysis that took 7 hours per issue with an AI-powered system that delivers insights in under 10 minutes, achieving an 88% reduction in manual effort. The multi-agent system analyzes real-time IoT data from over 250 automated curing presses to identify bottlenecks across 25+ subelements, enabling data-driven decision-making and targeting annual savings of approximately 15 million Indian rupees in their passenger car radial division.

title: AI-Powered Call Intelligence System for Multi-Location Marketing Analysis
short_summary: Netsertive, a digital marketing solutions provider for multi-location brands and franchises, implemented an AI-powered call intelligence system using Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Nova Micro to automatically analyze customer call tracking data and extract actionable insights. The solution processes real-time phone call transcripts to provide sentiment analysis, call summaries, keyword identification, coaching suggestions, and performance tracking across locations, reducing analysis time from hours or days to minutes while enabling better customer service optimization and conversion rate improvements for their franchise clients.

title: Training a 70B Japanese Large Language Model with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
short_summary: The Institute of Science Tokyo successfully developed Llama 3.3 Swallow, a 70-billion-parameter large language model with enhanced Japanese capabilities, using Amazon SageMaker HyperPod infrastructure. The project involved continual pre-training from Meta's Llama 3.3 70B model using 314 billion tokens of primarily Japanese training data over 16 days across 256 H100 GPUs. The resulting model demonstrates superior performance compared to GPT-4o-mini and other leading models on Japanese language benchmarks, showcasing effective distributed training techniques including 4D parallelism, asynchronous checkpointing, and comprehensive monitoring systems that enabled efficient large-scale model training in production.

title: Scaling Domain-Specific Model Training with Distributed Infrastructure
short_summary: Articul8, a generative AI company focused on domain-specific models (DSMs), faced challenges in training and deploying specialized LLMs across semiconductor, energy, and supply chain industries due to infrastructure complexity and computational requirements. They implemented Amazon SageMaker HyperPod to manage distributed training clusters with automated fault tolerance, achieving over 95% cluster utilization and 35% productivity improvements. The solution enabled them to reduce AI deployment time by 4x and total cost of ownership by 5x while successfully developing high-performing DSMs that outperform general-purpose LLMs by 2-3x in domain-specific tasks, with their A8-Semicon model achieving twice the accuracy of GPT-4o and Claude in Verilog code generation at 50-100x smaller model sizes.

title: Building a Centralized AI-Powered Developer Support System Using RAG
short_summary: Adobe faced challenges with developers struggling to efficiently find relevant information across vast collections of wiki pages, software guidelines, and troubleshooting guides. The company developed "Unified Support," a centralized AI-powered system using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and vector search capabilities to help thousands of internal developers get immediate answers to technical questions. By implementing a RAG-based solution with metadata filtering and optimized chunking strategies, Adobe achieved a 20% increase in retrieval accuracy compared to their existing solution, significantly improving developer productivity while reducing support costs.

title: Automated ESG Reporting with Agentic AI for Enterprise Sustainability Compliance
short_summary: Gardenia Technologies partnered with AWS to develop Report GenAI, an automated ESG reporting solution that helps organizations reduce sustainability reporting time by up to 75%. The system uses agentic AI on Amazon Bedrock to automatically pre-fill ESG disclosure reports by integrating data from corporate databases, document stores, and web searches, while maintaining human oversight for validation and refinement. Omni Helicopters International successfully reduced their CDP reporting time from one month to one week using this solution.

title: JUDE: Large-Scale LLM-Based Embedding Generation for Job Recommendations
short_summary: LinkedIn developed JUDE (Job Understanding Data Expert), a production platform that leverages fine-tuned large language models to generate high-quality embeddings for job recommendations at scale. The system addresses the computational challenges of LLM deployment through a multi-component architecture including fine-tuned representation learning, real-time embedding generation, and comprehensive serving infrastructure. JUDE replaced standardized features in job recommendation models, resulting in +2.07% qualified applications, -5.13% dismiss-to-apply ratio, and +1.91% total job applications - representing the highest metric improvement from a single model change observed by the team.

title: AI Agent for Automated Root Cause Analysis in Production Systems
short_summary: Cleric developed an AI agent system to automatically diagnose and root cause production alerts by analyzing observability data, logs, and system metrics. The agent operates asynchronously, investigating alerts when they fire in systems like PagerDuty or Slack, planning and executing diagnostic tasks through API calls, and reasoning about findings to distill information into actionable root causes. The system faces significant challenges around ground truth validation, user feedback loops, and the need to minimize human intervention while maintaining high accuracy across diverse infrastructure environments.

title: Building a Multi-Agent Research System for Complex Information Tasks
short_summary: Anthropic developed a production multi-agent system for their Claude Research feature that uses multiple specialized AI agents working in parallel to conduct complex research tasks across web and enterprise sources. The system employs an orchestrator-worker architecture where a lead agent coordinates and delegates to specialized subagents that operate simultaneously, achieving 90.2% performance improvement over single-agent systems on internal evaluations. The implementation required sophisticated prompt engineering, robust evaluation frameworks, and careful production engineering to handle the stateful, non-deterministic nature of multi-agent interactions at scale.

title: Scaling Foundation Models for Predictive Banking Applications
short_summary: Nubank integrated foundation models into their AI platform to enhance predictive modeling across critical banking decisions, moving beyond traditional tabular machine learning approaches. Through their acquisition of Hyperplane in July 2024, they developed billion-parameter transformer models that process sequential transaction data to better understand customer behavior. Over eight months, they achieved significant performance improvements (1.20% average AUC lift across benchmark tasks) while maintaining existing data governance and model deployment infrastructure, successfully deploying these models to production decision engines serving over 100 million customers.

title: Automated LLM Evaluation Framework for Customer Support Chatbots
short_summary: Instacart developed the LLM-Assisted Chatbot Evaluation (LACE) framework to systematically evaluate their AI-powered customer support chatbot performance at scale. The company faced challenges in measuring chatbot effectiveness beyond traditional metrics, needing a system that could assess nuanced aspects like query understanding, answer correctness, and customer satisfaction. LACE employs three LLM-based evaluation methods (direct prompting, agentic reflection, and agentic debate) across five key dimensions with binary scoring criteria, validated against human judgment through iterative refinement. The framework enables continuous monitoring and improvement of chatbot interactions, successfully identifying issues like context maintenance failures and inefficient responses that directly impact customer experience.

title: Building a Multi-Model LLM Marketplace and Routing Platform
short_summary: OpenRouter was founded in 2023 to address the challenge of choosing between rapidly proliferating language models by creating a unified API marketplace that aggregates over 400 models from 60+ providers. The platform solves the problem of model selection, provider heterogeneity, and high switching costs by providing normalized access, intelligent routing, caching, and real-time performance monitoring. Results include 10-100% month-over-month growth, sub-30ms latency, improved uptime through provider aggregation, and evidence that the AI inference market is becoming multi-model rather than winner-take-all.

title: Building a Digital Workforce with Multi-Agent Systems for Task Automation
short_summary: Monday.com, a work OS platform processing 1 billion tasks annually, developed a digital workforce using AI agents to automate various work tasks. The company built their agent ecosystem on LangGraph and LangSmith, focusing heavily on user experience design principles including user control over autonomy, preview capabilities, and explainability. Their approach emphasizes trust as the primary adoption barrier rather than technology, implementing guardrails and human-in-the-loop systems to ensure production readiness. The system has shown significant growth with 100% month-over-month increases in AI usage since launch.

title: Building AI Developer Tools Using LangGraph for Large-Scale Software Development
short_summary: Uber's developer platform team built a suite of AI-powered developer tools using LangGraph to improve productivity for 5,000 engineers working on hundreds of millions of lines of code. The solution included tools like Validator (for detecting code violations and security issues), AutoCover (for automated test generation), and various other AI assistants. By creating domain-expert agents and reusable primitives, they achieved significant impact including thousands of daily code fixes, 10% improvement in developer platform coverage, and an estimated 21,000 developer hours saved through automated test generation.

title: From Simple RAG to Multi-Agent Architecture for Document Data Extraction
short_summary: Box evolved their document data extraction system from a simple single-model approach to a sophisticated multi-agent architecture to handle enterprise-scale unstructured data processing. The initial straightforward approach of preprocessing documents and feeding them to an LLM worked well for basic use cases but failed when customers presented complex challenges like 300-page documents, poor OCR quality, hundreds of extraction fields, and confidence scoring requirements. By redesigning the system using an agentic approach with specialized sub-agents for different tasks, Box achieved better accuracy, easier system evolution, and improved maintainability while processing millions of pages for enterprise customers.

title: AI-Powered Code Editor with Multi-Model Integration and Agentic Workflows
short_summary: Cursor, an AI-powered code editor, has scaled to over $300 million in revenue by integrating multiple language models including Claude 3.5 Sonnet for advanced coding tasks. The platform evolved from basic tab completion to sophisticated multi-file editing capabilities, background agents, and agentic workflows. By combining intelligent retrieval systems with large language models, Cursor enables developers to work across complex codebases, automate repetitive tasks, and accelerate software development through features like real-time code completion, multi-file editing, and background task execution in isolated environments.

title: Large-Scale Deployment of On-Device and Server Foundation Models for Consumer AI Features
short_summary: Apple developed and deployed a comprehensive foundation model infrastructure consisting of a 3-billion parameter on-device model and a mixture-of-experts server model to power Apple Intelligence features across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. The implementation addresses the challenge of delivering generative AI capabilities at consumer scale while maintaining privacy, efficiency, and quality across 15 languages. The solution involved novel architectural innovations including shared KV caches, parallel track mixture-of-experts design, and extensive optimization techniques including quantization and compression, resulting in production deployment across millions of devices with measurable performance improvements in text and vision tasks.

title: Evaluation-Driven LLM Production Workflows with Morgan Stanley and Grab Case Studies
short_summary: OpenAI's applied evaluation team presented best practices for implementing LLMs in production through two case studies: Morgan Stanley's internal document search system for financial advisors and Grab's computer vision system for Southeast Asian mapping. Both companies started with simple evaluation frameworks using just 5 initial test cases, then progressively scaled their evaluation systems while maintaining CI/CD integration. Morgan Stanley improved their RAG system's document recall from 20% to 80% through iterative evaluation and optimization, while Grab developed sophisticated vision fine-tuning capabilities for recognizing road signs and lane counts in Southeast Asian contexts. The key insight was that effective evaluation systems enable rapid iteration cycles and clear communication between teams and external partners like OpenAI for model improvement.

title: Fine-tuned LLM Deployment for Automotive Customer Engagement
short_summary: Impel, an automotive retail AI company, migrated from a third-party LLM to a fine-tuned Meta Llama model deployed on Amazon SageMaker to power their Sales AI product, which provides 24/7 personalized customer engagement for dealerships. The transition addressed cost predictability concerns and customization limitations, resulting in 20% improved accuracy across core features including response personalization, conversation summarization, and follow-up generation, while achieving better security and operational control.

title: Climate Tech Foundation Models for Environmental AI Applications
short_summary: Climate tech startups are leveraging Amazon SageMaker HyperPod to build specialized foundation models that address critical environmental challenges including weather prediction, sustainable material discovery, ecosystem monitoring, and geological modeling. Companies like Orbital Materials and Hum.AI are training custom models from scratch on massive environmental datasets, achieving significant breakthroughs such as tenfold performance improvements in carbon capture materials and the ability to see underwater from satellite imagery. These startups are moving beyond traditional LLM fine-tuning to create domain-specific models with billions of parameters that process multimodal environmental data including satellite imagery, sensor networks, and atmospheric measurements at scale.

title: Autonomous SRE Agent for Cloud Infrastructure Monitoring Using FastMCP
short_summary: FuzzyLabs developed an autonomous Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) agent using Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) with FastMCP to automate the diagnosis of production incidents in cloud-native applications. The agent integrates with Kubernetes, GitHub, and Slack to automatically detect issues, analyze logs, identify root causes in source code, and post diagnostic summaries to development teams. While the proof-of-concept successfully demonstrated end-to-end incident response automation using a custom MCP client with optimizations like tool caching and filtering, the project raises important questions about effectiveness measurement, security boundaries, and cost optimization that require further research.

title: Data Flywheels for Cost-Effective AI Agent Optimization
short_summary: Nvidia developed a data flywheel approach for their internal employee support agent (NV Info Agent) to continuously improve model performance while reducing costs. The challenge was routing user queries to the correct expert agent in a multi-agent system. Starting with a 70B parameter model achieving 96% routing accuracy but high latency, they implemented a feedback loop collecting user signals, curating ground truth data (685 data points), and fine-tuning smaller models. The result demonstrated that an 8B model could match the 70B's accuracy after fine-tuning, while a 1B model achieved 94% accuracy with 98% lower inference costs and 70x lower latency, showcasing how continuous data curation and model evaluation can optimize production AI systems.

title: Scaling Agentic AI Systems for Real Estate Due Diligence: Managing Prompt Tax at Production Scale
short_summary: Orbital, a legal tech company automating real estate due diligence, shares their experience scaling an agentic LLM system from near-zero to processing 20 billion tokens monthly over 18 months. The company developed an agent that reads legal documents (deeds, leases) and extracts information traditionally done manually by real estate lawyers. Starting with GPT-3.5 and evolving through multiple OpenAI models including GPT-4 and system-2 reasoning models, they grew from zero to multiple seven figures in annual recurring revenue. Their approach deliberately prioritized prompting over fine-tuning for development speed, relied heavily on domain experts (former real estate lawyers) to write prompts, and notably chose "vibes over evals" - using human testing rather than rigorous automated evaluation systems. The presentation introduces the concept of "prompt tax" - the hidden cost of migrating prompts when upgrading to new models - and shares battle-tested tactics for managing model transitions in production.

title: Production RAG Stack Development Through 37 Iterations for Financial Services
short_summary: An independent AI engineer shares a comprehensive guide to building production-ready RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) systems based on lessons learned from 37 failed implementations. The case study walks through the complete RAG stack including orchestration (LlamaIndex), embedding models (transitioning from OpenAI closed models to open alternatives like BGE from BAI), vector databases (Qdrant), LLMs (GPT-4 for prototyping, Llama and Qwen models for production), rerankers (Cohere for prototyping, Nvidia for production), and monitoring tools (Arize Phoenix). The approach demonstrates how to move from a naive RAG implementation with poor results to a sophisticated pipeline with cross-encoders for reranking that produces accurate, contextual responses, all containerized with Docker for on-premise deployment in financial institutions.

title: Building Reliable AI Agent Systems with Effect TypeScript Framework
short_summary: 14.ai, an AI-native customer support platform, leverages the Effect TypeScript library to build robust, production-grade LLM systems that interact directly with end users. To handle the inherent challenges of unreliable APIs, non-deterministic model outputs, and complex dependencies, they built a custom domain-specific language (DSL) for agent workflows using Effect's functional composition primitives. Their architecture includes multi-provider LLM fallback mechanisms, token stream duplication for real-time delivery and analytics, and comprehensive dependency injection for testing. The approach enables predictable, resilient agentic systems with strong type safety, runtime validation, and observability via OpenTelemetry.

title: Benchmarking AI Agents for Software Bug Detection and Maintenance Tasks
short_summary: Bismuth, a startup focused on software agents, developed SM-100, a benchmark to evaluate how effectively LLM-based coding agents can find and fix bugs in production software—an area largely unexplored by existing benchmarks. Their research across 100 bugs in 84 repositories revealed that even the most popular coding agents struggle significantly with maintenance tasks, with some achieving only 1-10% true positive rates and high false positive rates (up to 97%). Bismuth's own agent led in "needle in haystack" bug detection (finding 10 bugs versus the next best at 7), while demonstrating that current agents are narrow in their reasoning, miss bugs human developers would catch immediately, and require significant improvements in cross-file reasoning and program comprehension before they can reliably handle the "back 90%" of software engineering work beyond feature development.

title: AI-Powered Automated Issue Resolution Achieving State-of-the-Art Performance on SWE-bench
short_summary: Trae, an AI-powered IDE, achieved a 70.6% resolve rate on the SWE-bench Verified benchmark by implementing a multi-stage agent architecture that combines multiple LLMs (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and OpenAI o4-mini) for code patch generation, automated regression testing for filtering, and a sophisticated voting-based selector agent for final patch selection. The system uses a Code Knowledge Graph for efficient code navigation, sequential thinking for step-by-step reasoning, and AST-based syntactic clustering to identify consensus among independently generated patches, demonstrating effective test-time scaling through intelligent ensemble methods rather than relying on a single model.

title: Text-to-Floor Plan Generation Using LLMs with Prompt Engineering and Fine-Tuning
short_summary: ZURU Tech collaborated with AWS to develop an LLM-based text-to-floor plan generator for their Dreamcatcher building design platform. The challenge was enabling non-technical users to describe buildings in natural language and receive accurate 2D floor plans. After initial success with GPT-2, the team experimented with prompt engineering using Claude 3.5 Sonnet and fine-tuning Llama 3.1 8B models. Both approaches achieved a 109% improvement in instruction adherence over the baseline, while full fine-tuning additionally improved mathematical correctness by 54%. The solution leveraged Amazon Bedrock for prompt engineering workflows and Amazon SageMaker for fine-tuning experiments, with a novel evaluation framework enabling rapid iteration cycles.

title: Scaling LLM Inference Infrastructure at Meta: From Model Runner to Production Platform
short_summary: Meta's infrastructure team addresses the complex challenges of serving LLMs at massive scale for products like Meta AI and smart glasses. The solution involves a comprehensive approach spanning model runners with continuous batching and KV caching, distributed inference using tensor and pipeline parallelism, disaggregated prefill/decode services, hierarchical KV cache management across HBM/DRAM/flash storage, and sophisticated deployment orchestration. The team processes hundreds of millions of examples during RLHF training weeks while maintaining strict latency SLOs, achieving 10x foundational performance improvements through proper runtime selection and an additional 2-4x through distributed inference, caching, and quantization techniques, though real-world production deployments commonly lose 50% of theoretical FLOPS due to workload variability and operational constraints.

title: Building ART·E: Reinforcement Learning for Email Search Agent Development
short_summary: OpenPipe developed ART·E, an email research agent trained using reinforcement learning (specifically GRPO) to answer natural-language questions by searching email inboxes. The team used the publicly available Enron email dataset to generate synthetic question-answer pairs, built a simple agentic environment with search and read tools backed by SQLite, and trained a Qwen-14B model with a multi-objective reward function optimizing for answer correctness, fewer turns, and reduced hallucinations. The resulting model outperformed OpenAI's o3 on this specific task while being faster and cheaper, with training completed in under a day on a single H100 GPU for approximately $80.

title: Revenue Intelligence Platform with Ambient AI Agents
short_summary: Tabs, a vertical AI company in B2B finance, is building ambient agents to automate revenue operations including contract extraction, invoice management, and collections. The company uses a "commercial graph" approach to hydrate customer relationship data and run intelligent workflows that operate in the background, communicating with users through Slack and email rather than traditional chat interfaces. Their approach focuses on moving from guided co-pilot experiences to fully autonomous agents that can handle tactical finance tasks while humans focus on strategic work, with key challenges around information retrieval, knowledge graph structuring, and memory for learning from human feedback.

title: Multi-Agent AI Development Assistant for Clinical Trial Data Analysis
short_summary: AstraZeneca developed an AI-powered "Development Assistant" to accelerate drug development by enabling natural language querying of clinical trial data. Built on their existing 3DP (Drug Development Data Platform), the solution evolved from a single-agent approach to a multi-agent architecture using Amazon Bedrock, featuring a supervisor agent that routes queries to specialized sub-agents for different domains (clinical, regulatory, quality). The system went from concept to production MVP in six months, with rigorous testing, controlled vocabulary augmentation, and metadata enrichment to reduce hallucinations. The tool is now being expanded to additional R&D domains while the team focuses on user adoption through change management programs and AI accreditation initiatives.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Code Generation and Agent-Based Development Tools
short_summary: This discussion from the Cursor team explores the unique challenges and opportunities in applying reinforcement learning (RL) to coding agents in production. The conversation covers the distinct nature of RL for code versus math or writing tasks, including the larger action space, multi-step tool calling requirements, and the difficulty of obtaining reliable reward signals. Key topics include optimizing inference infrastructure for RL training (including NVLink mesh parallelism and KV cache management), the trade-offs between different reward signals (tests, human feedback, reward models), novel attention mechanisms like NSA for long context handling, and the importance of real-world user feedback for model improvement. The team discusses practical approaches to memory tools, process versus outcome rewards, and the future direction of coding agents that can efficiently reuse context and amortize reasoning across sessions.

title: ML-Powered Interactive Voice Response System for Customer Support
short_summary: Airbnb transformed their traditional button-based Interactive Voice Response (IVR) system into an intelligent, conversational voice support system using machine learning. The solution combines domain-adapted Automated Speech Recognition (ASR), intent detection models, LLM-based help article retrieval and ranking, and a paraphrasing model to understand caller issues in natural language and provide relevant self-service resources. Key results include reducing ASR word error rate from 33% to approximately 10%, achieving intent detection latency under 50ms, and improving self-resolution rates through better user engagement with help articles.

title: Enhanced Agentic RAG for On-Call Engineering Support
short_summary: Uber developed "Genie," an internal on-call copilot to provide real-time support for engineering queries across Slack channels. Initial testing against a golden set of 100+ queries revealed significant accuracy gaps when using traditional RAG architecture with security and privacy policy documents. To address this, Uber transitioned to an Enhanced Agentic RAG (EAg-RAG) architecture featuring enriched document processing, LLM-powered agents for query optimization and source identification, and hybrid retrieval combining vector search with BM25. They also implemented LLM-as-Judge for automated evaluation, reducing experiment assessment time from weeks to minutes. The improvements resulted in a 27% relative increase in acceptable answers and a 60% relative reduction in incorrect advice, enabling broader deployment across critical security and privacy Slack channels.

title: AI-Powered Semantic Job Search at Scale
short_summary: LinkedIn transformed its job search experience from traditional keyword-based matching to a semantic, natural language-powered system serving 1.2 billion members. The solution leverages large language models (LLMs), embedding-based retrieval on GPU infrastructure, and a multi-stage distillation architecture that aligns retrieval and ranking models with a foundational "teacher" model. By generating synthetic training data with LLMs, implementing RAG patterns for dynamic query suggestions, and deploying exhaustive nearest neighbor search on GPUs, the team reduced pipeline complexity from nine stages to a simplified, aligned system while achieving low-latency semantic understanding at unprecedented scale.

title: Enterprise Autonomous Software Engineering with AI Droids
short_summary: Factory AI addresses the challenge of enterprise software development productivity by building autonomous "droids" that can handle complex coding tasks, migrations, and incident response without constant human supervision. Their platform integrates with enterprise tools like Jira, Slack, Notion, and GitHub to provide agents with the contextual information needed to execute multi-file tasks effectively. The company reports significant results including reducing a four-month migration project to three and a half days for a Fortune 500 customer, with enterprises seeing dramatic improvements in developer productivity through a delegation-based rather than collaboration-based workflow.

title: Agentic AI Architecture for Investment Management Platform
short_summary: Blackrock developed Aladdin Copilot, an AI-powered assistant embedded across 100 front-end applications in their investment management platform serving clients across 70 countries. The solution employs a supervisor-based agentic architecture built on LangChain/LangGraph, featuring a plugin registry that allows 50-60 engineering teams to onboard their domain-specific tools and agents. The system uses GPT-4 function calling for orchestration, with comprehensive guardrails for responsible AI including input/output moderation, PII handling, and hallucination detection. Blackrock implemented rigorous evaluation-driven development with automated testing pipelines running in CI/CD, testing every system prompt behavior and end-to-end query routing to ensure reliable performance across thousands of registered tools and agents.

title: Rebuilding an AI SDR Agent with Multi-Agent Architecture for Enterprise Sales Automation
short_summary: 11x rebuilt their AI SDR product "Alice" from scratch in three months, evolving from a button-heavy workflow to a true agentic system. The team experimented with three different agent architectures—React, workflow-based, and multi-agent systems—ultimately settling on a hierarchical multi-agent approach that combined the flexibility of React with the performance benefits of structured workflows. The production system leverages LangGraph, LangChain, and Claude models to power specialized sub-agents for research, positioning, and message writing. Results include nearly 2 million leads sourced, 3 million messages sent, and a 2% reply rate on par with human SDRs.

title: Systematic Approach to Building Reliable LLM Data Processing Pipelines Through Iterative Development
short_summary: Researchers at UC Berkeley, working on the DocETL project, investigated why LLM pipelines for processing unstructured data often fail and identified two critical gaps: data understanding and intent specification. Through human-computer interaction (HCI) research methods, they found that practitioners struggle because they don't know what questions to ask, can't specify prompts unambiguously, and face a long tail of failure modes across diverse document types. Their solution involves building tooling that helps users discover failure modes through output clustering, design targeted evaluations on the fly, and translate user notes into prompt improvements through interactive interfaces. The research emphasizes that successful LLM pipeline development requires distinct iterative stages: first understanding your data and failure modes, then achieving well-specified prompts, before applying accuracy optimization strategies.

title: Building an AI Private Banker with Agentic Systems for Customer Service and Financial Operations
short_summary: Nubank, one of the largest digital banks in Latin America with nearly 120 million users, deployed LLM-powered systems for customer service chatbots and voice/image-enabled money transfers. The customer service system handles 60% of 8.5 million monthly contacts using LLMs, while the money transfer agent reduced transaction time from 70 seconds to under 30 seconds with less than 0.5% inaccuracy and over 90% customer satisfaction. The team developed a comprehensive LLMOps infrastructure using LangChain, LangGraph, and LangSmith for tracing, evaluation, and rapid iteration. Their LLM-as-a-judge system achieved 79% F1 score (comparable to human evaluators at 80%) through six iterations of prompt engineering and fine-tuning, enabling scalable quality evaluation at production scale.

title: AI-Powered Developer Tools for Code Quality and Test Generation
short_summary: Uber's developer platform team built a suite of AI-powered developer tools using LangGraph to improve code quality and developer productivity across their massive codebase of hundreds of millions of lines of code. The solution involved creating domain-expert agents for tasks like code validation, automated test generation, and code review, composed together using LangGraph's graph-based architecture. Key products include Validator (an IDE tool that flags best practice violations and security issues) and AutoCover (an automated test generation tool). Results include thousands of daily fix interactions, 10% coverage improvement for the developer platform (equivalent to 21,000 dev hours saved), and 5,000+ tests generated weekly, with the test generation tool achieving 2-3x more coverage in half the time compared to industry alternatives.

title: Autonomous Coding Agent Evolution: From Short-Burst to Extended Runtime Operations
short_summary: Replit evolved their AI coding agent from V1 to V2, dramatically increasing autonomy from a few minutes to 10-15 minutes of continuous useful work. The solution involved rearchitecting the agent scaffold, leveraging frontier models like Claude 3.7, implementing robust evaluation and observability systems using tools like LangSmith, and optimizing for performance over latency. Results include generating approximately 1 million applications per month, with only 10% of users needing to manually edit code (down from 25%), demonstrating significant progress in autonomous software development for non-technical users.

title: Multi-Agent Investment Research Assistant with RAG and Human-in-the-Loop
short_summary: J.P. Morgan Chase's Private Bank investment research team built "Ask David" (Data Analytics Visualization Insights and Decision-making assistant), a multi-agent LLM system to automate investment research across thousands of products. The system uses a supervisor agent to orchestrate specialized sub-agents handling structured data (SQL/API translation), unstructured data (RAG over documents), and proprietary analytics. Key operational practices include evaluation-driven development with independent sub-agent testing, personalization based on user roles, reflection nodes using LLM-as-judge, and human-in-the-loop for the critical "last mile" accuracy in a domain where billions of dollars are at stake.

title: AI Agent-Driven Software Development Platform for Enterprise Engineering Teams
short_summary: Factory addresses the challenge of scaling AI-driven software development beyond incremental productivity gains (10-15%) by building a platform for fully autonomous "droids" that can handle complete engineering tasks from ticket to pull request. Their solution focuses on three core principles of agentic systems—planning, decision-making, and environmental grounding—combined with purpose-built AI-computer interfaces. The platform primarily serves enterprise organizations with 5,000-10,000+ engineers, enabling them to delegate entire software development tasks to AI agents rather than just augmenting human developers within traditional IDEs. While specific quantitative results are not provided, Factory claims the approach can achieve 5-20x performance improvements and suggests organizations should aim to delegate over 50% of engineering tasks to AI agents.

title: Production Agent Platform Architecture for Multi-Agent Systems
short_summary: LinkedIn faced challenges scaling generative AI adoption across their organization while maintaining production-grade reliability. Their initial Java-based approach for GenAI applications created friction with the Python-dominated open-source ecosystem, limiting innovation. The solution involved a strategic pivot to Python as the primary language for GenAI development, building a standardized application framework using LangChain and LangGraph, and developing custom agent infrastructure including messaging systems, layered memory, a skills registry, and custom observability. The result was LinkedIn's first production agent—the Hiring Assistant—along with over 30 GenAI services built by more than 20 teams, demonstrating successful organizational scaling of agentic AI capabilities.

title: Building and Evaluating Legal AI with Multi-Modal Evaluation Systems
short_summary: Harvey, a legal AI company, addresses the challenges of building high-quality LLM-powered products for legal professionals by implementing a comprehensive evaluation framework combining human preference judgments, automated LLM-as-judge evaluations, and step-wise workflow assessments. The company developed BigLawBench, a proprietary benchmark with complex open-ended legal tasks, and embeds domain experts (lawyers) throughout the product development lifecycle. Their approach includes side-by-side human evaluations, custom rubrics crafted by legal professionals, and extensive internal dogfooding before launching new models like GPT-4.1 to their nearly 400 law firm customers worldwide, including 8 of the top 10 largest US law firms.

title: Building and Evaluating Legal AI at Scale with Domain Expert Integration
short_summary: Harvey, a legal AI company serving nearly 400 customers including one-third of the top 100 US law firms, addresses the challenge of building high-quality AI systems for the complex legal domain. Their solution combines state-of-the-art LLMs with a "lawyer in the loop" product development approach, multi-layered evaluation strategies including human preference ratings, LLM-as-judge with domain-expert-crafted rubrics, and component-level evaluation for agentic workflows. They created their own benchmark (Big Law Bench) for realistic legal task evaluation and invested heavily in evaluation tooling including LangSmith integration. Results include successful deployment of new models like GPT-4.1 with rigorous quality assurance that caught regressions before customer release, and significantly improved iteration speed and product quality through their comprehensive evaluation infrastructure.

title: Enterprise Data Extraction Evolution from Simple RAG to Multi-Agent Architecture
short_summary: Box, an enterprise unstructured data platform serving over 115,000 companies with an exabyte of data, initially deployed a straightforward LLM-based metadata extraction system that successfully processed 10 million pages. However, as customers brought increasingly complex documents (300+ pages, 500+ fields, multilingual content, poor OCR quality), the simple architecture broke down. The team rearchitected their system from scratch using a multi-agent approach with specialized sub-agents for field grouping, intelligent extraction strategies, and quality feedback loops. This agentic architecture not only solved immediate problems but created a cleaner abstraction that was significantly easier to evolve, allowing rapid deployment of specialized agents for new document types and enabling engineers to better understand customer needs for building their own agent-powered workflows.

title: Building a Digital Workforce with Multi-Agent Systems and User-Centric Design
short_summary: Monday.com built a "digital workforce" of AI agents to handle their 1 billion annual work tasks, using LangGraph and LangSmith as their core infrastructure. They implemented a supervisor-based multi-agent architecture with specialized agents for data retrieval, board actions, and answer composition. Key learnings included the importance of user control over autonomy, preview modes before production actions, external guardrails, and careful balance of agent decomposition to avoid "compound hallucination." The system now processes millions of requests per month with reported 100% month-over-month growth in AI usage since launch.

title: Intelligent Document Processing for Mortgage Servicing Using Amazon Bedrock and Multimodal AI
short_summary: Onity Group, a mortgage servicing and origination company processing millions of document pages annually, faced challenges with traditional OCR solutions that struggled with verbose legal documents, inconsistent handwriting, and notarization verification. They built an intelligent document processing solution combining Amazon Textract with Amazon Bedrock foundation models (specifically Anthropic's Claude Sonnet), implementing a dual-model architecture that dynamically routes extraction tasks based on content complexity. The solution achieved a reported 50% reduction in document extraction costs and 20% improvement in overall accuracy compared to their previous OCR/ML approach, with specific use cases like credit report processing reaching approximately 85% accuracy.

title: Building an Autonomous AI Software Engineer with Multi-Turn RL and Codebase Understanding
short_summary: Cognition, the company behind Devon (an AI software engineer), addresses the challenge of enabling AI agents to work effectively within large, existing codebases where traditional LLMs struggle with limited context windows and complex dependencies. Their solution involves creating DeepWiki, a continuously-updated interactive knowledge graph and wiki system that indexes codebases using both code and metadata (pull requests, git history, team discussions), combined with Devon Search for deep codebase research, and custom post-training using multi-turn reinforcement learning to optimize models for specific narrow domains. Results include Devon being used by teams worldwide to autonomously go from ticket to pull request, the release of Kevin 32B (an open-source model achieving 91% correctness on CUDA kernel generation, outperforming frontier models like GPT-4), and thousands of open-source projects incorporating DeepWiki into their official documentation.

title: Multi-Agent AI Platform for Customer Experience at Scale
short_summary: Cisco's Customer Experience organization, responsible for over $26 billion in recurring revenue across 20,000 employees, implemented a multi-agent agentic AI system using LangChain and LangGraph to transform their customer lifecycle operations. The system addresses renewals, adoption, support, and delivery workflows through a supervisor-based multi-agent architecture that combines LLMs with traditional machine learning models for predictions. Key results include a 20% reduction in time spent on operational tasks within 3 weeks, 95%+ accuracy on risk recommendations, and 60% full automation of their 1.6-1.8 million annual support cases. The system runs in production across flexible deployment models including on-premises data centers, cloud, and hybrid environments.

title: Building an Agentic DevOps Copilot for Infrastructure Automation
short_summary: Qovery developed an AI-powered DevOps Copilot to automate infrastructure tasks and eliminate manual DevOps work. Starting in February 2025, the team evolved through four technical phases: from basic intent-to-tool mapping, to a dynamic agentic system with tool chaining, then adding resilience layers with retry logic, and finally implementing conversation memory for contextual understanding. The system, currently in Alpha, uses Claude Sonnet 3.7 and QDrant vector database to help developers automate deployments, optimize infrastructure, and answer configuration questions. Future improvements focus on reducing planning latency (currently up to 10 seconds), offering self-hosted model options for compliance, and implementing long-term memory across sessions.

title: Building a Structured AI Evaluation Framework for Educational Tools
short_summary: Coursera, a global online learning platform, faced challenges scaling their AI evaluation processes for their Coach chatbot and automated grading features. Their previous approach relied on fragmented spreadsheets, manual reviews, and inconsistent team scripts, making it difficult to validate AI features before production deployment. By implementing a structured four-step evaluation framework using Braintrust, they established clear success criteria, curated targeted datasets mixing real-world and synthetic examples, combined heuristic and model-based scorers, and enabled continuous iteration through online monitoring and offline testing. The results include a 90% learner satisfaction rating for their Coach chatbot, 45× more feedback in automated grading, and a 16.7% increase in course completions within a day of peer review, while enabling faster development cycles and better cross-team collaboration.

title: Fine-tuning Multimodal Models for Banking Document Processing
short_summary: Apoidea Group, a Hong Kong-based FinTech company, collaborated with AWS to enhance their document processing capabilities for banking clients by fine-tuning the Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct vision-language model using LLaMA-Factory on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod. The solution addresses inefficiencies in extracting structured data from complex financial documents such as bank statements, KYC forms, and financial reports. By leveraging QLoRA for efficient fine-tuning and vLLM for inference, the fine-tuned model achieved a TEDS score of 81.1 for table structure recognition, surpassing Claude 3 Haiku (69.9) and approaching Claude 3.5 Sonnet (86.4) while maintaining computational efficiency. The solution reportedly reduced financial spreading processes from 4-6 hours to 10 minutes and achieved over 80% ROI for banking clients.

title: Building a Comprehensive AI Platform with SageMaker and Bedrock for Experience Management
short_summary: Qualtrics built Socrates, a comprehensive internal ML/AI platform powered by Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock, to enable researchers, scientists, engineers, and knowledge workers to develop, deploy, and manage AI-powered capabilities for their Experience Management (XM) suite. The platform provides unified access to LLMs through a GenAI Gateway, streamlined model deployment infrastructure, capacity management, prompt lifecycle management, and agent orchestration frameworks built on LangGraph. By partnering closely with AWS, Qualtrics achieved significant cost reductions (up to 50% for foundation model deployment), improved latency (20% reduction on average), and faster auto-scaling (up to 40% improvement) for their generative AI workloads serving over 20,000 global clients.

title: Lessons Learned from Deploying 30+ GenAI Agents in Production
short_summary: Quic, an AI agent platform company, shares lessons learned from deploying over 30 generative AI agents for customer experience use cases across multiple industries over two years. The presentation covers the full lifecycle of LLM-based agent development, from planning and data management through development, testing, and ongoing operations. Key challenges addressed include hallucination detection, regression testing for generative systems, observability requirements unique to LLMs, model deprecation management, and the need for specialized tooling. The company reports achieving higher customer satisfaction scores, higher resolution rates, and reduced agent handling times through their AI agents, while emphasizing that humans remain essential in the loop.

title: Scaling an Autonomous AI Customer Support Agent from Demo to Production
short_summary: Intercom developed Finn, an autonomous AI customer support agent, evolving from early GPT-3.5 prototypes that couldn't reliably prevent hallucinations to a production-ready system powered by GPT-4 and Anthropic's Claude. The company faced the classic challenge of moving from impressive demos to real-world deployment, ultimately building a multi-component agent architecture with bespoke RAG, custom reranking, and extensive prompt engineering. The system now resolves 58-59% of customer support conversations autonomously across 30,000 customers, up from approximately 25% at initial launch, with continuous iteration based on production feedback and rigorous "torture testing" to ensure safe and reliable behavior.

title: Multimodal Art Collection Search Using Vector Databases and LLMs
short_summary: Actum Digital implemented a multimodal search system for an art collection containing approximately 40 million assets. The team leveraged AWS Bedrock for embedding models, OpenSearch as a vector database, and developed a hybrid search approach combining text and image similarity search. The solution enables users to search art assets by text descriptions, find similar images, and combine different search modalities. The infrastructure runs at approximately $1,000 per month per region, with significant focus on cost optimization strategies including reducing re-indexing operations and exploring fine-tuned models.

title: Building Robust Evaluation Systems for GitHub Copilot
short_summary: GitHub Copilot's development team shares their comprehensive approach to evaluating LLM-powered code completion and chat systems. The team developed a multi-layered evaluation strategy encompassing verifiable code execution tests (harness lib), A/B testing with key metrics like acceptance rate and character retention, LLM-as-judge for subjective chat quality assessment, and algorithmic tool-call validation. These evaluation frameworks enabled the team to iterate rapidly on model improvements while maintaining production quality, ultimately contributing to Copilot becoming one of the first successful commercial AI coding assistants.

title: Optimizing RAG-based Search Results for Production: A Journey from POC to Production
short_summary: Statista, a global statistics platform serving 30,000 paying customers with millions of curated statistics, developed a generative AI product called Research AI to transform how users discover and consume data insights. Starting with a proof-of-concept that made 42 LLM calls per request and had only 30% quality scores, the team implemented comprehensive traceability, established quality metrics using LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, and conducted over 100 experiments to optimize the RAG pipeline. Key techniques included multi-query rewriting and HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) to improve semantic retrieval. The optimization effort, completed in just three weeks, achieved 65% cost reduction, 10% latency improvement (with 65% savings reinvested in quality-boosting techniques), and 140% quality improvement, resulting in a production-ready system now used by a growing customer base with strong adoption metrics.

title: Building and Optimizing a RAG-based Customer Service Chatbot
short_summary: HDI, a German insurance company, partnered with AWS Professional Services to build a RAG-based chatbot that enables customer service agents to quickly find answers across multiple document sources (SharePoints, databases) containing complex insurance information. The solution uses OpenSearch as a vector store, implements hybrid search with custom reciprocal rank fusion, and went through approximately 120 experiments to optimize chunking strategies, embedding models, and HNSW indexing parameters. After one year in production, the system serves 800+ users with 88% recall rate and 6ms query latency, with plans to scale to 1,200 users.

title: Scaling AI Infrastructure: Network Architecture and Communication Optimization at Microsoft
short_summary: Microsoft's AI platform team addresses the challenges of scaling AI training clusters to hundreds of thousands of GPUs. The presentation covers network topology design (rail-optimized, multi-pod architectures), routing optimization, cluster validation frameworks (SuperBench, IB Pulse), and communication library tuning (TACCL, MSCCL). Key results include achieving #1 cloud ranking in Top 500 (rank 3 overall) and #1 cloud ranking in MLPerf (rank 2 overall), along with significant cost savings through rail-only topologies and improved reliability through smart NIC-based fault tolerance mechanisms.

title: Scaling AI Infrastructure: Managing Data Movement and Placement on Meta's Global Backbone Network
short_summary: Meta's infrastructure team describes how AI workloads, particularly those supporting generative AI and large model training, have fundamentally transformed the demands on their global backbone network. Starting around 2022, GPU demand from product groups grew over 100% year-over-year, and AI-driven traffic became significantly more volatile and harder to predict than traditional workloads. The team implemented solutions including cross-stack optimization, better data placement strategies, differentiated quality-of-service guarantees, and improved observability of data flows to "bend the demand curve" while also expanding supply through additional fiber, power, and cooling infrastructure. Key results include reducing cross-region data reads to two-thirds of original levels through caching and smarter data placement.

title: Building a Production AI Translation and Lip-Sync System at Scale
short_summary: Meta developed an AI translation system that automatically translates video content (Reels) from one language to another while generating lip-synced video to match the translated audio. The system orchestrates 10+ AI models including Meta's Seamless universal translator model, language identification, voice activity detection, and lip-sync generation. The solution addresses challenges of scale (billions of videos), quality (expressivity, sentiment preservation), and safety (hallucination detection, watermarking). Currently in alpha with a small number of creators, the system has achieved 90% eligibility rate for content translation and has shown meaningful increases in impressions due to content being available in more languages.

title: Scaling AI Infrastructure: From Training to Inference at Meta
short_summary: Meta presents their comprehensive approach to scaling AI infrastructure for production LLM workloads, addressing challenges from post-training reinforcement learning to distributed inference. The company has scaled from 256 GPUs to over 100,000 GPUs in training clusters (a 38,000% increase in two years), with plans to reach one million GPUs by end of 2025. Key solutions include building a VM vending machine for secure code execution (handling 40 billion+ instances), implementing distributed inference across multiple hosts, developing RAG techniques with vector databases to reduce hallucinations, and exploring a shift from SPMD to single-controller programming models for better fault tolerance. Infrastructure innovations span nuclear power procurement (1-4 GW RFP), new data center designs up to 2 GW capacity, and novel approaches to managing power oscillations of 10-15 MW during training jobs.

title: Human-AI Synergy in Pharmaceutical Research and Document Processing
short_summary: Merantix developed interactive AI systems for pharmaceutical clients like Boehringer Ingelheim that enable progressive automation of tedious manual tasks. For drug safety assessment, they built a system where humans describe rare rodent behaviors they're looking for in video data, and the AI learns to detect these patterns autonomously over time, shifting from fully manual annotation to AI-assisted snippets to complete automation. Similar approaches were applied to document review in legal and compliance contexts where errors are not allowed, creating semi-automated systems that combine human accuracy with AI efficiency. The case study also covers Red Tech Cortex's enterprise knowledge management platform serving 2 million users, which uses RAG-based retrieval to help companies search across their internal documents with reported productivity gains of 30% for every 100 onboarded users.

title: Cost-Effective LLM Transaction Categorization for Business Banking
short_summary: ANNA, a UK-based business banking app, deployed LLMs to categorize financial transactions for tax purposes, requiring understanding of complex business contexts across hundreds of industries. The challenge was managing costs while processing transactions through a ~50,000 token accounting rulebook system prompt. By implementing offline predictions (batch processing with 24-hour wait for 50% discount), upgrading from Claude 3.5 to 3.7 for better context utilization (reducing API calls through larger output windows), and enabling prompt caching, ANNA achieved 75% total cost savings. Key learnings included discovering that longer context windows increased hallucination rates (2-3% invalid transaction IDs), that prompt caching combined with offline predictions yielded unpredictable savings, and that quality evaluation must be maintained throughout optimization efforts.

title: Scaling Knowledge Management with LLM-powered Chatbot in Manufacturing
short_summary: OSRAM, a legacy lighting and semiconductor manufacturing company with a plant dating back to 1961, faced significant challenges with knowledge retention as experienced workers retired and product lifecycles shortened dramatically. Working with Adastra and AWS, they developed a RAG-based chatbot solution using Amazon Bedrock and Claude to consolidate scattered documentation and make institutional knowledge accessible to shop floor workers. The solution employed a hybrid search approach combining vector embeddings with keyword search to handle technical terminology, achieved over 85% accuracy at deployment with expectations to exceed 90%, and was built with a robust CI/CD pipeline for scaling across departments and plants.

title: AI Assistant Integration for Manufacturing Execution System (MES)
short_summary: 42Q, a cloud-based Manufacturing Execution System (MES) provider, developed "Arthur" - an AI chatbot to address the complexity of their software platform and reduce dependency on busy MES administrators. The solution uses RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) with Amazon Bedrock, incorporating documentation, transcribed training videos, and live database queries. Arthur provides multilingual, context-aware responses with source citations, enabling users to query both system knowledge and production data in natural language. The chatbot has been successfully deployed, with users reporting faster access to information, improved training capabilities, and reduced reliance on expert staff, though the team is still deliberating on whether to allow Arthur to take direct actions in production environments.

title: Large-Scale GPU Infrastructure for Neural Web Search Training
short_summary: The source text for this case study about Exa.ai's Exacluster was inaccessible due to a rate limiting error (HTTP 429), preventing extraction of meaningful details about the problem, solution, and results. Based on the URL path referencing "meet-the-exacluster," this appears to relate to Exa.ai's AI-powered search infrastructure, but no specific technical details, implementation approaches, or outcomes could be verified from the provided content.

title: Building a Secure Enterprise AI Assistant with RAG and Custom Infrastructure
short_summary: Hexagon's Asset Lifecycle Intelligence division developed HxGN Alix, an AI-powered digital worker to enhance how users interact with their Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) products. The challenge was to build an enterprise-grade AI assistant that could operate within high-security environments while providing accurate, multilingual responses grounded in product documentation. Using a combination of AWS services including Amazon EKS, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and Bedrock Guardrails, along with the open-source Mistral NeMo LLM, the team implemented a sophisticated RAG system to reduce hallucinations and ground responses in actual documentation. The solution streamlines information access for users who previously needed to navigate extensive PDF manuals, enhances internal workflows for customer success and support teams, and improves overall customer satisfaction through an intuitive AI interface.

title: Scaling Image Generation to 100M New Users in One Week
short_summary: OpenAI faced unprecedented scaling challenges when launching ChatGPT Images in March 2025, attracting 100 million new users and generating 700 million images in the first week—far exceeding expectations. The team had to rewrite the image generation system from synchronous to asynchronous processing on-the-fly while keeping the service running, implement system isolation to protect other OpenAI services, and perform rapid database query optimizations. Despite load surges reaching 1 million new users per hour, major outages were avoided by prioritizing availability over latency, applying rate limits strategically, and leveraging prior investments in load testing and monitoring infrastructure.

title: Implementing RAG for Call Center Operations with Hybrid Data Sources
short_summary: Manulife implemented a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system for their call center to help customer service representatives answer queries by retrieving information from both structured databases (customer policy data) and unstructured sources (policy documents, CSR notes). The solution innovatively converts structured database tables into JSON strings grouped by business concepts, vectorizes them alongside unstructured document chunks, and stores them in Azure AI Search indexes. Using GPT-3.5 for answer generation with an independent validation model (Llama 3 or GPT-4), the production system achieved response times of 7.33 seconds (reduced from an initial 21.91 seconds) and has consistently generated grounded answers without hallucinations since May 2024.

title: Vision Language Models for Large-Scale Product Classification and Understanding
short_summary: Shopify evolved its product classification system from basic TF-IDF and logistic regression models to a sophisticated Vision Language Model (VLM) architecture built on their Shopify Product Taxonomy. The system processes over 30 million predictions daily, using models like Qwen2VL 7B with FP8 quantization and in-flight batching via NVIDIA Dynamo on Kubernetes. The two-stage prediction pipeline first classifies products into categories from a 10,000+ category taxonomy, then extracts category-specific attributes. Results include an 85% merchant acceptance rate of predicted categories, doubled hierarchical precision and recall compared to earlier neural network approaches, and improved search relevance, tax calculations, and content safety across the platform.

title: Pivoting from GPU Infrastructure to Building an AI-Powered Development Environment
short_summary: Windsurf (formerly Codium/Exofunction) pivoted from GPU virtualization to building an AI-powered coding assistant, growing from 8 employees to over a million developers using their product. The company built custom inference infrastructure, trained proprietary code models with specialized capabilities like fill-in-the-middle, and developed a sophisticated retrieval system combining keyword search, RAG, AST parsing, and GPU-accelerated real-time ranking. Their agentic editor now serves hundreds of thousands of daily active users and enterprise customers including Dell and JP Morgan Chase, with codebases exceeding 100 million lines of code.

title: Building an AI Legal Assistant: From Early Testing to Production Deployment
short_summary: Casetext, a legal technology company founded in 2012, pivoted its entire 120-person company within 48 hours of gaining early access to GPT-4 to build Co-Counsel, an AI legal assistant. After a decade of incremental improvements using traditional NLP and machine learning, the transformative capabilities of GPT-4 enabled them to create a product that could perform complex legal tasks like document review and legal research in minutes rather than days. The company employed rigorous test-driven development for prompt engineering, breaking complex legal workflows into dozens of individual prompts each validated against thousands of test cases. This approach achieved production-grade accuracy required for mission-critical legal work. Two months after launching Co-Counsel publicly, acquisition discussions began with Thomson Reuters, culminating in a $650 million exit—a dramatic increase from their pre-GPT-4 valuation of approximately $100 million.

title: Building and Operating a CLI-Based LLM Coding Assistant
short_summary: Anthropic developed Claude Code, a CLI-based AI coding agent that runs in the terminal and provides raw access to Claude models for software development tasks. Born as an internal experiment, it demonstrated strong product-market fit when Anthropic engineers adopted it widely, with daily active usage growing rapidly. The tool follows Unix utility design principles, emphasizing simplicity and composability, and now writes approximately 80% of its own code. Average user cost is around $6/day with some power users spending over $1,000 daily on automated workflows, and the team reports roughly 2x productivity gains for typical engineering work.

title: Evolution of AI Agents: From Manual Workflows to End-to-End Training
short_summary: OpenAI's agents research team, led by Josh Tobin, discusses the evolution from traditional LLM workflow orchestration to end-to-end reinforcement learning trained agents. The core problem addressed is the compounding error issue in multi-step agentic workflows where small errors at each step multiply across trajectories, leading to unreliable outcomes. The solution involves training models directly via RL to succeed at complete tasks rather than designing human-specified multi-agent workflows. This approach powers OpenAI's production agentic products including Deep Research, Operator, and Codex CLI, which have achieved significant user adoption with capabilities including autonomous web research, browser automation, and code generation with contextless codebase navigation.

title: Multi-Agent RAG System for Enterprise Data Discovery
short_summary: Wix faced significant data discovery challenges in their data mesh architecture, where hundreds of tables across multiple domains made it difficult for users to locate relevant data. They developed "Anna," a multi-agent AI assistant leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Vespa as the vector database. The system uses specialized agents for intent detection, query validation, question decomposition, and structured query generation. A key innovation was embedding business questions rather than raw metadata, achieving an 83% success rate in dimension matching. The solution integrates with Cube for SQL generation and Airflow for hourly embedding updates, significantly reducing friction in data exploration and receiving positive user feedback.

title: Building a Universal Search Product with RAG and AI Agents
short_summary: Dropbox built Dash, a universal search and knowledge management product designed to help knowledge workers find information scattered across multiple applications and formats. The core challenges included handling data diversity (emails, documents, meeting notes), data fragmentation (information spread across tools), and multiple data modalities (text, images, audio, video). Dropbox implemented a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system using traditional information retrieval with on-the-fly chunking and reranking, achieving sub-2-second latency for over 95% of queries. For complex multi-step tasks, they developed AI agents using a custom Python-like domain-specific language (DSL) with a purpose-built minimal interpreter featuring static analysis and runtime type enforcement for security and reliability. The model-agnostic architecture allows flexibility in LLM selection, with rigorous evaluation conducted using public datasets and custom LLM-based judges for answer correctness and completeness.

title: Enhancing Ads Engagement with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts and Knowledge Distillation
short_summary: Pinterest's Ads Ranking team addressed the challenge of scaling recommendation models efficiently by implementing a Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts (MMoE) architecture combined with knowledge distillation techniques. The problem was that traditional DCNv2-style models could not achieve proportional metric gains simply by adding more layers and parameters, and training data retention limitations created performance gaps when deploying new experimental models. The solution involved using multiple specialized expert networks (including DCNv2, MLP variants) with lightweight gating mechanisms, combined with mixed precision inference to reduce infrastructure costs by 40%. Knowledge distillation from production models helped experimental models "learn" from deleted training data. Results showed significant improvements in both offline accuracy (where 0.1% is considered significant) and online metrics across different view types including RelatedPins and Search.

title: Using GenAI to Automatically Fix Java Resource Leaks
short_summary: Uber developed FixrLeak, a generative AI-based framework that automates the detection and repair of Java resource leaks in their extensive codebase. The system combines Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) analysis with OpenAI's GPT-4O to produce accurate fixes following Java best practices like try-with-resources. Applied to 124 resource leaks identified by SonarQube, FixrLeak successfully automated fixes for 93 out of 102 eligible cases after filtering out deprecated code and complex inter-procedural scenarios. The tool generates pull requests with validated fixes, significantly reducing manual developer effort while maintaining code quality through automated testing and human code review.

title: Improving LLM Food Tracking Accuracy through Systematic Evaluation and Few-Shot Learning
