short_summary: Taralli, a calorie tracking app, faced significant accuracy issues with its LLM-powered food analysis system, with the initial GPT-4o-mini implementation scoring only 17% on evaluation metrics due to quantity misinterpretation errors (e.g., returning 58,000 kcal for 100g of peanut butter). By implementing systematic logging with W&B Weave, building a golden dataset from real user inputs, defining clear evaluation metrics for calorie accuracy and food group classification, and applying DSPy's BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch optimization technique with Gemini 2.5 Flash, the developer improved tracking accuracy from 17% to 76% while establishing a continuous improvement flywheel for ongoing model refinement.

title: AI-Powered Accounting Automation Using Claude and Amazon Bedrock
short_summary: FloQast, an accounting software company serving over 2,800 organizations, built an AI-powered accounting transformation solution using Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet on Amazon Bedrock to automate complex financial processes. The solution addresses two key use cases: AI Transaction Matching (automating reconciliation between bank statements and ERP systems using natural language rule creation) and AI Annotations (automated document annotation for compliance and audit processes). Using Amazon Bedrock Agents for multi-step task orchestration and RAG with few-shot classification instead of fine-tuning, FloQast reported a 38% reduction in reconciliation time, 23% decrease in audit process duration and discrepancies, and 44% improvement in workload management for their accounting customers.

title: LLM-Powered Search Evaluation System for Automated Result Quality Assessment
short_summary: DoorDash faced challenges with traditional human-driven search relevance evaluation, including scalability constraints, slow feedback loops, inconsistent ratings, and limited coverage across query types. To address these issues, they built AutoEval, an LLM-powered evaluation system with human-in-the-loop oversight that assesses search result quality using a custom whole-page relevance (WPR) metric. The system leverages fine-tuned GPT-4o models, structured prompt engineering, and expert auditing to deliver near-real-time relevance judgments. Results include a 98% reduction in turnaround time, a nine-fold increase in evaluation capacity, and fine-tuned models that match or outperform external human raters in accuracy on key relevance tasks.

title: AI-Powered Marketing Compliance Automation System
short_summary: Remitly, an international money transfer company operating in 170 countries with communications in 18+ languages, developed a generative AI tool to automate marketing content compliance review. The previous manual process involved 2-4 rounds of back-and-forth between creative and legal teams, causing delays and context-switching inefficiency. The AI solution analyzes marketing text against internal compliance guidelines (derived from international regulations), identifies issues, explains which guidelines are violated, and suggests corrections. Developed in 15 days of active work spread over 3 months, the system achieved 95% accuracy and 97% issue identification rate. The tool enables marketers to self-service compliance checks before legal submission, accelerating time-to-market while reducing legal review burden.

title: Automated News Analysis and Bias Detection Platform
short_summary: AskNews, developed by Emergent Methods, addresses the challenge of news bias and information overload by building an AI-powered platform that processes 500,000 articles daily across multiple languages. The solution uses open-source LLMs like Llama at the edge to extract structured metadata (facts, entities, relationships, bias indicators) from articles, clusters them using embeddings, and builds a knowledge graph that enables users to query diverse global perspectives on any topic. The platform surfaces contradictions between sources without judgment, enforces diversity by including perspectives from multiple countries and languages, and provides transparent citations. Key customers include security risk analysts, forecasters, and journalists who use it for research, fact-checking, and identifying story angles from the meta-narrative of global coverage.

title: Enterprise-Scale LLM Deployment with Licensed Content for Business Intelligence
short_summary: Factiva, a Dow Jones-owned business intelligence platform with nearly three decades of experience aggregating licensed content from thousands of publishers, launched an AI-powered "Smart Summaries" feature in November 2024. The solution uses Google Gemini on Google Cloud to provide natural language querying and summarization across a corpus of nearly three billion articles. Critically, Factiva secured explicit generative AI licensing rights from nearly 5,000 content providers—growing from 2,000 sources in just six months—ensuring full copyright compliance and transparent royalty compensation for publishers. The implementation operates in a closed, secure environment where only licensed content feeds the generative summaries, reducing hallucination risks and maintaining the trust-based relationships Factiva has cultivated with publishers worldwide.

title: Scaling Local News Coverage with AI-Powered Newsletter Generation
short_summary: Patch, a hyperlocal news platform, deployed AI to scale its community newsletter operations from 1,100 to 30,000 communities across the US. Rather than using general-purpose LLMs like ChatGPT to generate content, Patch built a system that leverages AI to curate and summarize news from vetted local data sources, including local publishers, social media feeds, and community calendars. The AI newsletters aggregate headlines with short summaries, upcoming events, nearby news, and social media chatter while maintaining Patch's editorial voice. The result has been over 400,000 subscribers to AI-powered newsletters with a 93.6% thumbs-up rating, demonstrating that AI can effectively bridge the gap between scattered local information sources and community readers seeking to stay informed about their towns.

title: AI-Powered Content Understanding and Ad Targeting Platform
short_summary: Dotdash Meredith, one of the largest digital publishers in the US, partnered with OpenAI to develop D/Cipher, an AI-powered contextual advertising system that understands reader intent from content rather than relying on cookie-based tracking. By leveraging LLMs to analyze over a million pieces of content and correlate user behavior across 10+ billion annual visits, the company created a targeting solution that outperforms identity-based advertising. The partnership also enabled grounded AI responses that can acknowledge uncertainty ("I don't know"), improved content personalization, and positioned the publisher to monetize its content in AI search products through attribution and citations.

title: Global News Organization's AI-Powered Content Production and Verification System
short_summary: Reuters, a 174-year-old global news agency with 2,600 journalists worldwide, implemented a comprehensive generative AI strategy across its newsroom operations. Starting with proof-of-concept projects in early 2023, they developed three production tools: a fact extraction system for press releases with human-in-the-loop verification, an AI-enhanced CMS (Leon) with transcription, translation, and copy editing capabilities, and a packaging tool (LAMP) for content matching and ranking. The organization maintains strict ethical boundaries, prohibiting generative AI for images or video to preserve journalistic integrity, while exploring small language models for improved accuracy, latency, and control. Reuters has also launched the Reuters AI Suite, offering transcription and translation APIs to external news clients, effectively productizing their internal AI capabilities.

title: Journey Towards Autonomous Network Operations with AI/ML and Dark NOC
short_summary: BT, one of the UK's largest mobile network operators, is partnering with AWS to transform its network operations toward an autonomous "DarkKnock" vision where networks self-heal and self-optimize. The challenge involves managing petabytes of data from thousands of radio sites, gateways, and distributed core networks while consolidating hundreds of bespoke monitoring tools. The solution focuses on building a proper data foundation first, then layering ML models and generative AI in an "agentic AI framework" to automate data analysis, root cause analysis, anomaly detection, and predictive maintenance. While still in early stages focused on data cleaning and team upskilling, the vision includes application-aware networking and significant reduction in manual network monitoring through intelligent automation.

title: AI-Powered Shift-Left Testing Platform with Multiple LLM Agents
short_summary: QyrusAI addresses the challenge of maintaining rigorous quality standards in accelerated software development cycles by implementing an AI-driven shift-left testing approach powered by Amazon Bedrock. The solution deploys multiple specialized AI agents—including TestGenerator, VisionNova, UXtract, and API Builder—that leverage various LLMs and vision-language models (Meta's Llama, Anthropic's Claude, Cohere embeddings) to generate test cases from requirements, convert UI/UX designs to test scenarios, virtualize APIs for early frontend testing, and autonomously explore applications for issues. According to QyrusAI's claims from early adopters, this approach has resulted in an 80% reduction in defect leakage, 20% reduction in UAT effort, and 36% faster time to market, though these metrics should be considered with the caveat that they come from the vendor's own pilot programs.

title: High-Performance LLM Deployment with SageMaker AI
short_summary: Salesforce's AI Model Serving team faced challenges balancing latency, throughput, and cost-efficiency when deploying large language models and other AI models at scale across multiple AWS regions. They developed a hosting framework on AWS using Amazon SageMaker AI that leverages Deep Learning Containers, rolling-batch inference, distributed inference, and automated CI/CD pipelines with security embedded throughout. The solution resulted in substantial improvements including faster iteration cycles measured in days or hours instead of weeks, and a reported 50% reduction in model deployment time while maintaining enterprise-grade security standards.

title: Streamlining Clinical Trial Documentation Generation with RAG and LLMs
short_summary: Clario, a clinical trials endpoint data solutions provider, faced a time-consuming process of generating documentation for clinical trials that could take weeks and was prone to manual errors and inconsistencies. Working with AWS, they developed a prototype solution using Amazon Bedrock with Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless as a vector store, and Amazon S3 for storage to automate the generation of Business Requirement Specification (BRS) documents from medical imaging charter documents. The RAG-based solution demonstrated improved accuracy by minimizing translation errors, scalability through serverless architecture, and enhanced security by keeping data within the AWS ecosystem. Clario is working to productionize the solution in their Medical Imaging business during 2025.

title: Building and Deploying Enterprise-Grade LLMs: Lessons from Mistral
short_summary: Mistral, an AI company founded by former Meta researchers who worked on Llama, discusses their journey from training foundational open-source language models to building enterprise deployment solutions. The company addresses the challenge that while open-source models are freely available, most enterprises cannot effectively deploy them without significant infrastructure and expertise. Mistral's solution involves providing custom on-premise deployments, fine-tuning services, and synthetic data generation for customers in privacy-sensitive industries like finance, defense, and healthcare. Their approach emphasizes that the real value lies not in the model weights themselves but in the complete solutions that transform models into usable products, including their customer-facing application "Le Chat" which serves both as a demo and data collection mechanism for model improvement.

title: AI-Driven Digital Twins for Industrial Infrastructure Optimization
short_summary: Geminus addresses the challenge of optimizing large-scale industrial infrastructure (power plants, oil refineries, energy grids) by creating AI-driven digital twins that combine high-fidelity physics simulations with machine learning models. Traditional approaches suffered from long development cycles (12-24 months), unreliable sensor data, and operator distrust of black-box models. Geminus's solution uses synthetic data from physics simulators as training data, multi-fidelity data blending techniques, and probabilistic models with uncertainty bounds to build operator trust. The system compresses model development from months to days, runs millions of optimization scenarios in milliseconds, and integrates with existing control systems while respecting safety guardrails. Recent evolution includes using LLMs as agents to direct computational science workflows, though the company explicitly notes that LLMs are not used for direct machine control recommendations due to their non-deterministic nature.

title: Implementing RAG and RagRails for Reliable Conversational AI in Insurance
short_summary: GEICO developed a conversational chat application using LLMs to replace traditional web forms for collecting user information. The team discovered that commercial and open-source LLMs suffered from hallucinations and "overpromising" behaviors, where models incorrectly assumed capabilities they didn't have. To address these issues, they implemented Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with vector databases using HNSW indexing, developed sorting and ranking mechanisms for retrieved content, and created a novel "RagRails" approach that embeds guiding instructions within retrieved records to constrain model behavior. The implementation reduced incorrect responses from 12 out of 20 to zero in tested scenarios, demonstrating effective hallucination mitigation for customer-facing insurance applications.

title: RAG-Based System for Climate Finance Document Analysis
short_summary: ClimateAligned, an early-stage climate finance startup with a 10-person team (3 technical), built a RAG-based system to assess the "greenness" of financial instruments by processing complex corporate climate documentation. Starting with GPT-4 and hybrid search (vector similarity + BM25 keyword search), they achieved 85% model accuracy while maintaining 99% production accuracy through human-in-the-loop review. The approach reduced analysis time from 2 hours to 20 minutes per company while building labeled datasets (reaching 10,000 examples) that enabled automated review flagging and topic classification, resulting in additional order-of-magnitude throughput gains. The team is now working on topic-based document ranking, fine-tuning smaller models, and moving away from OpenAI APIs to reduce costs and improve reliability.

title: Structured LLM Conversations for Language Learning Video Calls
short_summary: Duolingo developed "Video Call with Lily," an AI-powered speaking practice feature that enables learners to have natural conversations with a virtual character. The solution required sophisticated prompt engineering to balance CEFR language proficiency levels, maintain a consistent character personality (a sarcastic teenage girl named Lily), and ensure pedagogically appropriate interactions. Key technical innovations include a multi-stage prompting architecture that separates question generation from conversation management to prevent LLM overload, a memory system that extracts and stores learner facts between sessions for personalized follow-ups, and mid-call evaluations that dynamically adjust conversation direction based on learner input. The system demonstrates how structured prompting and architectural decisions can transform general-purpose LLMs into specialized educational tools.

title: Building a Secure and Scalable LLM Gateway for Financial Services
short_summary: Wealthsimple, a Canadian FinTech company, built a comprehensive LLM platform to enable secure employee productivity and optimize client operations. Starting with an LLM gateway to address security concerns around third-party data sharing, they progressively added PII redaction, self-hosted open-source models, RAG capabilities, and a data applications platform. The journey included learnings about adoption challenges, the shift from build to buy strategies, and the importance of centralizing tools. Results include over 2,200 daily messages, one-third of the company as weekly active users, and production LLM systems that improved client experience triaging by combining Whisper transcription with classification models.

title: Automated Prompt Optimization for Intelligent Text Processing using Amazon Bedrock
short_summary: Yuewen Group, a global leader in online literature with 260 million users, transitioned from traditional NLP models to Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet on Amazon Bedrock for intelligent text analysis of web novels. Initial LLM implementations underperformed traditional NLP models due to limited prompt engineering expertise (70% vs 80% accuracy on character dialogue attribution). By adopting Amazon Bedrock's Prompt Optimization feature, which uses a fine-tuned LLM-based Prompt Analyzer and meta-prompting Prompt Rewriter, Yuewen Group achieved 90% accuracy on the same task—a 10% improvement over traditional NLP models. The automated optimization significantly reduced prompt engineering time while improving development efficiency across multiple text analysis use cases including name extraction and multi-option reasoning.

title: Evaluating Long Context Performance in Legal AI Applications
short_summary: Thomson Reuters developed a comprehensive benchmarking and evaluation framework for their CoCounsel legal AI assistant to handle long legal documents effectively. The challenge was that legal documents like deposition transcripts and M&A agreements often exceed hundreds of pages, and while modern LLMs advertise context windows up to 1M tokens, their effective performance degrades significantly with increasing input length. The solution involved a multi-LLM strategy with rigorous multi-stage testing including automated benchmarks (over 20,000 test samples), skill-specific evaluations using LLM-as-a-judge with attorney-authored criteria, and final manual review by subject matter experts. Their testing revealed that long-context LLMs generally outperformed RAG for document-based tasks, though they found that effective context windows are often much smaller than advertised limits, particularly for complex reasoning tasks requiring tracking multiple data elements.

title: GPT Integration for SQL Stored Procedure Optimization in CI/CD Pipeline
short_summary: Agoda integrated GPT into their CI/CD pipeline to automate SQL stored procedure (SP) optimization, addressing a significant manual workload that consumed approximately 366 man-days annually, with 320 of those days spent on performance test failures. The solution provides GPT with SP code, table structures, indexes, and performance test reports to generate optimized SP versions and indexing recommendations, which are presented as GitLab merge request comments with click-to-apply functionality. While the system has achieved around 25% accuracy in producing actionable optimization suggestions, it has reduced manual review time and empowered developers with self-service tuning tools. The team is working on automated logic verification to address challenges with GPT's variable code revision scope.

title: Automating Translation Workflows with LLMs for Post-Editing and Transcreation
short_summary: TransPerfect, a global language services company, faced challenges with costly and time-consuming translation workflows, particularly around machine translation post-editing and creative transcreation that required skilled human linguists. By integrating Amazon Bedrock LLMs into their GlobalLink translation management system, they implemented automated post-editing (APE) of machine-translated content and LLM-assisted transcreation. The solution uses Anthropic's Claude and Amazon Nova Pro models with style guides and approved translation examples to improve machine translation output. Results include over 95% of LLM-suggested edits showing improved quality, up to 50% cost savings on translations, 60% linguist productivity gains for transcreation, and up to 80% reduction in project turnaround times, while maintaining data security and using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for hallucination detection.

title: Enhancing Knowledge Graphs with LLMs at Netflix
short_summary: Netflix uses a large knowledge graph for entertainment data that connects various entities like movies, actors, and content relationships. While the system initially focused on entity matching at scale using traditional methods, they are now incorporating LLMs to enhance the knowledge graph by inferring new relationships and entity types. The system uses Metaflow for workflow management and implements RAG processes to combine structured data with LLM capabilities, allowing for better semantic understanding and relationship extraction from unstructured content.

title: Knowledge Graph Enhancement with LLMs for Content Understanding
short_summary: Netflix built a large-scale Knowledge Graph for entertainment data, using Metaflow to orchestrate billions of entity matching pairs across distributed infrastructure. The system enables entity matching at scale through parallel processing, achieving 10x speedups through fast data loading with Apache Arrow. More recently, the team has been exploring LLM-based approaches for inferring entity types and relationships from unstructured content, using RAG pipelines and in-context learning to extract semantic relationships that weren't explicitly available in the source data, all while maintaining production stability through Metaflow's namespacing and branching features.

title: Automated Synopsis Generation Pipeline with Human-in-the-Loop Quality Control
short_summary: Netflix faced a significant challenge in scaling the creation of synopses for their vast content catalog, as the traditional process required writers to manually gather context from multiple sources (scripts, closed captions, viewables) before drafting descriptions. The team implemented an LLM-based system using Metaflow to automate context summarization and draft synopsis generation, incorporating multiple feedback loops and an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation system with five quality criteria (precision, accuracy, tone, clarity, writing style) to ensure only high-quality drafts reach writers. The solution maintains humans in the loop while substantially reducing time spent on context gathering, enabling writers to focus on editing and quality refinement rather than starting from scratch, ultimately allowing Netflix to produce more synopses per title with the same resources.

title: Training and Deploying GPT-4.5: Scaling Challenges and System Design at the Frontier
short_summary: OpenAI's team discusses the two-year effort to train GPT-4.5, their largest pre-trained model representing a 10x compute increase over GPT-4. The project required extensive collaboration between ML researchers and systems engineers, involving large de-risking runs, multi-cluster training infrastructure, new state management approaches, and debugging challenges at unprecedented scale. Key learnings included discovering that data efficiency is becoming the primary bottleneck rather than compute, that scaling laws continue to hold with larger models showing emergent intelligence improvements, and that sophisticated fault tolerance and hardware reliability management are critical at this scale. The team also confronted novel debugging challenges, including a PyTorch sum function bug that caused intermittent failures across the entire run.

title: Multi-Agent LLM System for Logistics Planning Optimization
short_summary: Amazon Logistics faced challenges managing 10+ million data points annually for delivery planning, where human planners with tribal knowledge struggled to identify causal relationships between parameters affecting promised delivery dates. The solution employed a multi-agent AI architecture using LangChain custom agents and AWS Bedrock with Claude 3.7 to create a plan evaluation engine. Using the LACQUER algorithm to generate causal graphs from parameter heat maps, the system applies weighted formulas based on tribal knowledge to understand dependencies and optimize delivery routes. The solution enables planners to interact conversationally with complex planning data rather than manually analyzing Excel spreadsheets, potentially saving up to $150 million in losses from customer churn and missed delivery promises.

title: AI-Enhanced Body Camera and Digital Evidence Management in Law Enforcement
short_summary: An Garda Síochána (Ireland's national police service) has undertaken a comprehensive digital transformation journey deploying mobile devices to 16,000 frontline officers and implementing body-worn cameras across multiple sites. The initiative addresses challenges in evidence collection, processing, and court presentation. While currently constrained by legislation, the organization is actively researching AI capabilities including object recognition, video search, real-time translation, live transcription, and automated report generation. Early results show successful end-to-end digital evidence presentation in court, 15,000 uninsured vehicles removed from roads, and naming of all 99 individuals involved in the 2023 Dublin riots through manual video analysis—highlighting the future potential for AI-assisted processing.

title: Scaling Customer Support AI Chatbot to Production with Multiple LLM Providers
short_summary: Intercom built Finn, an AI-powered customer support chatbot that has resolved over 13 million conversations for more than 4,000 customers. Starting with a 1% error rate when migrating to Amazon Bedrock, the team implemented a comprehensive LLMOps strategy including cross-region inference, provision throughput for critical workloads, streaming optimization, custom LLM metrics (time to first token, time to sample token), and multi-model fallback strategies. Through careful attention to observability, prompt template logging, and offline evaluation using LLM-as-judge approaches, they achieved near-zero error rates in production while maintaining a cost-conscious architecture where engineering decisions directly impact revenue due to their resolution-based pricing model.

title: Scaling LLM and ML Models to 300M Monthly Requests with Self-Hosting
short_summary: StoryGraph, a book tracking and recommendation app, scaled from 1,000 to over 6 million monthly users while being managed by a single AI/DevOps engineer. The team faced critical challenges with cloud infrastructure costs and performance, ultimately migrating to self-hosted dedicated servers and deploying custom machine learning models including LLMs for book mood classification, recommendations, and personalized previews. By self-hosting their entire ML infrastructure including large language models processing approximately 1 million requests daily, they reduced potential LLM API costs from $770,000/month (if using ChatGPT-4) to a fraction of that cost, while maintaining user data privacy and achieving 300 million monthly requests.

title: Building a Low-Latency Global Code Completion Service
short_summary: GitHub Copilot faced the challenge of delivering real-time AI code completions that could compete with locally-running IDE autocomplete systems, while handling hundreds of millions of daily requests. The solution involved building a custom HTTP/2-based authenticating proxy (copilot-proxy) that enables efficient request cancellation, maintains persistent connections to minimize TCP/TLS overhead, and routes traffic globally across multiple Azure-hosted model regions. The results include serving over 400 million completion requests daily with peak loads of 8,000 requests per second and mean response times under 200 milliseconds, while enabling automatic failover between regions and reducing wasted inference by canceling approximately 45% of requests that users "type through."

title: Large-Scale Aviation Content Classification on Hacker News Using Small Language Models
short_summary: Skysight demonstrated the viability of using small language models (SLMs) for large-scale batch inference by classifying 42 million Hacker News posts to identify aviation-related content. The team built an end-to-end pipeline that processed 10.7 billion input tokens using Llama 3.1 8B, completing inference in a couple of hours and generating 1.9 billion structured JSON output tokens. The analysis found that approximately 1.13% of Hacker News stories are aviation-related, with the proportion increasing over time from 0.5% in 2007-2012 to 1.5% in recent years. While the project lacked formal statistical evaluation, it demonstrated that pre-trained SLMs can perform nuanced classification tasks cost-effectively at massive scale without requiring labeled training data or specialized ML engineering.

title: AI-Powered Account Planning Assistant for Sales Teams
short_summary: AWS Sales faced a challenge where account managers spent up to 40 hours per customer drafting in-depth, forward-looking strategy documents called account plans (APs). To address this, they built an AI-powered account planning draft assistant using Amazon Bedrock and RAG architecture, which synthesizes data from multiple internal and external sources including CRM systems, financial reports, news articles, and previous APs. Launched in October 2024, the solution enables sales teams to quickly generate comprehensive draft sections for customer overviews, industry analysis, and business priorities. The results have been significant, with account managers reporting time savings of at least 15 hours per enterprise account plan, allowing them to focus more on customer engagement and strategy development rather than research and writing.

title: Building a Next-Generation AI-Powered Code Editor
short_summary: Cursor, founded by four MIT graduates in 2022, built an AI-powered code editor that reimagines the programming interface by combining frontier models (Claude Sonnet, GPT-4, O1, DeepSeek R1) with approximately 10 custom-trained models for latency-sensitive features like next-edit prediction and autocomplete. Starting from the observation that GitHub Copilot's product experience remained static despite improving underlying models, Cursor developed a hybrid architecture where custom models handle low-latency tasks using proprietary user edit data (capturing what happens between commits), while frontier models power more complex reasoning tasks. The company reached $100 million in revenue with only 30 employees, demonstrating the value of rapid experimentation, being users of their own product, and a pragmatic approach to model selection that prioritizes product-market fit over premature GPU investment.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): A Universal Standard for AI Application Extensions
short_summary: Anthropic developed the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to solve the "M×N problem" of integrating AI applications with external tools and data sources. Born from frustration with copying data between Claude Desktop and IDEs, David and Justin designed MCP as a JSON-RPC based protocol inspired by Language Server Protocol (LSP). The protocol defines distinct primitives—tools (model-controlled actions), resources (application-controlled data), and prompts (user-initiated templates)—enabling AI applications to extend their functionality through a standardized interface. Since its November 2024 launch, MCP has been adopted across multiple IDEs, spawned numerous community-built servers, and established itself as an emerging standard for connecting LLMs to external capabilities in production environments.

title: Large Language Models for Search Relevance via Knowledge Distillation
short_summary: Pinterest developed an LLM-based search relevance system to improve how well search results align with user queries. The core challenge was that large cross-encoder language models like Llama-3-8B, while highly accurate for relevance prediction, are too computationally expensive for real-time serving at scale. The solution involved using these LLMs as teacher models to generate relevance labels on billions of rows of search data daily, then distilling this knowledge into a lightweight student model suitable for online serving. The system enriches Pin representations with multiple text features including synthetic image captions, user-curated board titles, and high-engagement query tokens. Results showed Llama-3-8B outperformed multilingual BERT-base by 12.5% in accuracy, and the production system achieved +2.18% improvement in search feed relevance (nDCG@20) and over 1.5% increase in search fulfillment rates, with strong generalization to unseen languages despite training primarily on US data.

title: Enterprise LLMOps Platform with Focus on Model Customization and API Optimization
short_summary: This podcast discussion explores IBM's WatsonX platform for enterprise AI applications, covering how Fortune 500 companies are building and deploying AI agents in production. The conversation addresses key LLMOps challenges including model selection (open source vs. proprietary), agent hosting and scaling, evaluation and observability, tool calling optimization, and the integration of protocols like MCP and GraphQL for efficient data retrieval. IBM offers both their open-source Granite model series and access to various LLMs, helping enterprises navigate the tension between legal compliance and developer innovation while deploying agents for internal workflows and customer service.

title: AI-Powered Engineering Team Management and Code Review Platform
short_summary: Entelligence addresses the growing operational overhead faced by large engineering teams by deploying AI agents for automated code review, continuous documentation updates, and engineering analytics. As AI-generated code becomes more prevalent through tools like Cursor, the need for systematic code auditing has increased. Entelligence's solution integrates with GitHub, GitLab, and IDEs to catch bugs, enforce best practices, detect PR conflicts, and maintain up-to-date documentation. The platform learns from team-specific feedback to customize review behavior, reducing noise and improving acceptance rates. Results include significant time savings for engineers who previously spent substantial time on code reviews, answering internal questions, and maintaining stale documentation.

title: Evolving Agent Architecture Through Model Capability Improvements
short_summary: Aomni has developed autonomous AI agents for revenue teams that allow sales representatives to orchestrate complex sales playbooks through simple prompts rather than navigating 5-20 different SaaS tools. The company's approach focuses on supporting human salespeople with AI-powered research and data preparation rather than replacing them with AI SDRs. A key technical insight is treating agents as workflow orchestration systems requiring the same reliability mechanisms as microservices, while maintaining a philosophy of continuously removing "scaffolding" (guardrails) as model capabilities improve. Their latest open-source deep research agent demonstrates this evolution—reducing from 20-30 different LLM calls with complex multi-agent architectures to just two LLM calls in a recursive loop, achieving better results with dramatically simpler code.

title: Systematic Analysis of Prompt Templates in Production LLM Applications
short_summary: This academic research study addresses the challenge of designing effective prompt templates for LLM-powered applications (LLMapps). Researchers from Technical University of Munich analyzed 2,163 real-world prompt templates extracted from open-source GitHub repositories, including production tools from Uber and Microsoft. Using a combination of LLM-driven analysis (llama3-70b-8192 and gpt-4o) and human review, they identified seven common template components, four placeholder categories, and key structural patterns. Sample testing revealed that well-structured templates with explicit JSON attribute names and descriptions, exclusion constraints, and strategic placeholder positioning significantly improve LLM instruction-following abilities. The findings provide actionable guidance for LLMOps practitioners on template design, with results showing that optimized templates can help weaker models achieve performance comparable to more powerful ones, offering cost optimization opportunities for production deployments.

title: Foundation Model for Large-Scale Personalized Recommendation
short_summary: Netflix faced growing maintenance costs and difficulty transferring innovations across their numerous specialized recommendation models, each trained independently despite using common data sources. They developed a foundation model inspired by LLM paradigms that centralizes member preference learning, using autoregressive next-token prediction on hundreds of billions of user interactions. The solution employs sparse attention mechanisms, sliding window sampling for training, incremental training for cold-start handling, and metadata-embedding fusion for new content. The system enables downstream applications through direct prediction, embedding generation, and fine-tuning capabilities, with experiments confirming scaling laws apply to recommendation models, showing consistent performance improvements with increased data and model size.

title: Optimizing Generative Retrieval to Reduce LLM Hallucinations in Search Systems
short_summary: Alipay addresses the challenge of hallucination in LLM-based generative retrieval (GR) for their Fund Search and Insurance Search systems. The problem centers on LLM-based GR models generating documents irrelevant to user queries, which undermines credibility in production applications. The proposed solution integrates knowledge distillation reasoning during model training and employs a decision agent for post-processing to improve retrieval precision. LLMs assess and reason over query-document pairs, with reasoning data distilled as transferred knowledge to the GR model. A decision agent extends retrieved documents through a retrieval model and selects the most relevant results from multiple perspectives. Results from offline experiments on real-world datasets and online A/B tests demonstrate improvements in search quality and conversion gains for both Fund Search and Insurance Search scenarios.

title: Enterprise-Scale LLM Deployment with Self-Evolving Models and Graph-Based RAG
short_summary: Writer, a full-stack generative AI platform for enterprises, has evolved from building custom transformer models since 2020 to deploying AI agents at scale across Fortune 500 companies in financial services, healthcare, and retail. The company addressed the challenge of moving beyond simple chatbots to production-grade "action AI" that automates complex workflows like healthcare claims processing and portfolio risk management. Their solution combines open-source Palmera models, graph-based RAG systems built on Postgres with Fusion Decoder retrieval, and hybrid no-code/code interfaces for business and IT collaboration. Key results include 30-50% workflow optimization, with enterprises now deploying hundreds of AI agents, though the company acknowledges that achieving 99%+ accuracy for multi-step tool calling remains an ongoing challenge they're addressing through self-evolving model architectures.

title: Building a Production-Grade GenAI Customer Support Assistant with Comprehensive Observability
short_summary: Elastic's Field Engineering team built comprehensive observability infrastructure for their Support Assistant, a RAG-powered customer support chatbot using GPT-4/GPT-4o through Azure OpenAI. The solution involved implementing Elastic APM for tracing, custom dashboards for monitoring usage and latency metrics, alerting systems for proactive incident response, and specialized monitoring for GenAI-specific challenges including first-generation timeouts, declined request tracking, rate limiting, and abuse mitigation. The observability stack helped identify bugs (like a data loading issue causing 100+ TPM instead of expected 1 TPM), track milestones (100th chat completion 21 hours post-launch), and resolve production issues such as HTTP 413 errors from large RAG context payloads.

title: Tuning RAG Search for Customer Support Chatbot
short_summary: Elastic's Field Engineering team developed a RAG-powered customer support chatbot that initially struggled with relevance for queries involving CVEs, product versions, and semantic matching. The team addressed these challenges through a combination of hybrid search tuning (BM25 + ELSER semantic search), conditional boosting of title and version fields, AI-generated field enrichment using GPT-4, and Elasticsearch's collapse parameter to deduplicate similar content. By implementing a systematic evaluation framework using Precision@K metrics against curated test cases, they achieved a ~75% improvement in top-3 search relevance while also generating over 300,000 AI-generated summaries for future applications.

title: UI/UX Design Considerations for Production GenAI Chatbots
short_summary: Elastic's Field Engineering team developed a generative AI customer support chatbot, facing unique UI/UX challenges including managing long LLM response latencies (5-11 seconds total), implementing custom timeout handling for streaming responses, and designing context management for multi-source RAG queries. The team built a custom chat interface using their Elastic UI component library, implemented animated loading states to maintain user engagement during response generation, created a "killswitch" mechanism to handle stalled streaming connections after 10 seconds of inactivity, and designed a prepended context menu system allowing users to control which data sources (case history, knowledge base) inform LLM responses.

title: Building a Production RAG-based Customer Support Assistant with Elasticsearch
short_summary: Elastic's Field Engineering team built a customer support chatbot called the "Support Assistant" using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach rather than fine-tuning. The solution involved creating a comprehensive knowledge library of over 300,000 documents including technical support articles, product documentation, and blogs, enriched with ELSER embeddings and AI-generated summaries. The team implemented document-level security for role-based access control, used hybrid search combining semantic and BM25 approaches, and deployed automated enrichment pipelines on Google Cloud Run. Key results included generating over 128,000 AI-generated summaries (a 10x improvement over human-written summaries) and establishing that smaller, more precise context leads to more deterministic LLM responses.

title: Building a Customer Support AI Assistant: From PoC to Production
short_summary: Elastic's Field Engineering team developed a proof of concept to integrate generative AI into customer support operations, focusing on automated case summaries and draft initial replies. Using Google Cloud Platform's Vertex AI integrated with Salesforce Service Cloud, they built a simple architecture that generated AI responses via custom prompts and delivered results through Salesforce Chatter. After 44 days of testing with 940 generated content pieces, user feedback revealed only a ~16% positive sentiment rate, primarily because the LLM lacked product-specific knowledge. This data-driven evaluation led to key insights about the need for retrieval augmented generation (RAG) with Elasticsearch and a unified chat interface, ultimately informing the decision to proceed from proof of concept to an approved project for building a Support AI Chat Assistant.

title: Building an Enterprise RAG-based AI Assistant with Vector Search and LLM Integration
short_summary: Elastic built ElasticGPT, an internal generative AI assistant leveraging their own technology stack to provide secure, scalable knowledge discovery for employees. The solution uses a RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) framework called SmartSource, which combines Elasticsearch as a vector database for storing embeddings of internal data sources with OpenAI's GPT-4o models hosted on Azure. The system is deployed on Elastic Cloud with Kubernetes orchestration, uses LangChain for RAG pipeline orchestration, and employs Elastic APM for comprehensive monitoring. The platform has reportedly reduced redundant IT queries and created employee efficiencies, while also serving as a "customer zero" testbed for Elastic's own AI capabilities.

title: Building an AI API Gateway for Streamlined GenAI Service Development
short_summary: Woowa Brothers (part of DeliveryHero) developed an AI API Gateway to address the challenges of managing multiple generative AI providers (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Imagen) across their organization. The problem stemmed from fragmented prompts and invocation logic across existing Gen AI-based services, with no centralized way to manage credentials and prompts. The solution prioritized building a gateway infrastructure that minimizes repetitive development tasks while enhancing system stability and security, serving as the foundational component before developing more advanced features like RAG pipelines, prompt experimentation, and feedback collection systems. The gateway enables faster adoption of Gen AI across various business activities, with practical applications including image enhancement features like out-painting for menu images.

title: Automating Code Sample Updates with LLMs for Technical Documentation
short_summary: Wix faced a challenge when a syntax change to their Velo development platform rendered over 2,000 code samples in their API reference documentation outdated. Rather than manually updating each sample, the technical writing team developed an automated pipeline using GPT models to classify which samples needed updating and then convert them to the new syntax. The solution involved GPT-4 for classification and GPT-3.5 Turbo for code conversion, combined with TypeScript compilation for validation. The approach reduced what would have been extensive manual work across the entire team to just six writers working for one morning, plus the upfront development investment by a smaller group.

title: Leveraging NLP and LLMs for Music Industry Royalty Recovery
short_summary: Love Without Sound, founded in 2023, addresses the multi-billion dollar music metadata problem that causes artists to lose royalties due to incorrect song attribution and unlicensed usage. The company built a modular suite of NLP tools using spaCy and Prodigy to standardize metadata across a 2 billion-row database, classify legal correspondence in real-time, extract case citations, and predict negotiation outcomes. The solution uses transformer and CNN-based models for named entity recognition, span categorization, and text classification, achieving accuracy scores between 0.90-0.99 across components. All models run locally in a data-private environment, processing emails and attachments in real-time while handling millions of tracks. The company is also developing a RAG pipeline for natural language querying and audio embedding models for content-based music matching.

title: Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Implementation Patterns and Production Case Studies
short_summary: This presentation by Nimble Gravity and Hiflylabs examines findings from a 460-respondent survey on generative AI adoption, revealing that approximately 28-30% of GenAI projects successfully reach production from assessment phase. The speakers discuss common failure reasons (tech infrastructure incompatibility, high costs), successful use cases (research summarization, automation, coding assistance, customer support), and propose multi-agent systems as a solution to accelerate time-to-value. They demonstrate a practical agentic workflow using LangGraph that orchestrates multiple specialized agents (weather, sports, market, local news) to produce a personalized morning briefing, showcasing how structured agent coordination can improve reliability and reduce hallucinations in production deployments.

title: Building and Deploying AI-Powered Visual and Semantic Search in Design Tools
short_summary: Figma developed AI-powered search capabilities to help designers find existing designs more efficiently. The problem addressed was that designers spent significant time tracking down source files, often relying on Slack channels to ask colleagues for help locating designs. The solution involved building visual search (allowing searches using screenshots, frames, or sketches) and semantic search (understanding context behind text queries) powered by embeddings and Retrieval Augmented Generation principles. The team pivoted from an initial design autocomplete concept after user research revealed that search was a more pressing need. Key challenges included determining what to index on an infinite canvas, avoiding duplicates, and establishing quality signals for designs. The team built custom evaluation tools using Figma's plugin API to grade search results and iteratively improve model quality. The feature launched at Config 2024 after months of scoping, internal beta testing, and cross-functional collaboration.

title: Building and Scaling AI-Powered Visual Search Infrastructure
short_summary: Figma faced the challenge of helping users locate specific designs and components across large organizations with complex design systems. They built an AI-powered search infrastructure using the open-source CLIP multimodal embedding model to enable semantic search across designs via text descriptions, screenshots, or layer selections. The solution required generating and indexing billions of embeddings while managing costs, leveraging AWS SageMaker for model inference, DynamoDB for metadata storage, and OpenSearch for vector search. Key optimizations included rewriting Ruby to C++, switching from GPU to CPU-based rendering, implementing indexing debouncing to reduce processing to 12% of original volume, and applying vector quantization to reduce index sizes. The features launched in early beta at Config 2024, enabling designers to find visually or semantically similar designs without manual keyword enumeration.

title: Building a Guardrail System for LLM-based Menu Transcription
short_summary: Doordash faced the challenge of manually transcribing restaurant menu photos, which was costly and time-consuming. They developed an LLM-based transcription system using OCR combined with language models to extract structured menu data from photos. However, due to inconsistent menu structures, incomplete menus, and poor photo quality, the LLM alone could not achieve the required high accuracy. To address this, they built a traditional ML guardrail model (using LightGBM) that predicts transcription quality and routes low-confidence transcriptions to human reviewers while allowing high-confidence ones to proceed automatically. This hybrid human-AI pipeline enabled automation of a significant portion of menu transcriptions without sacrificing quality, while the guardrail framework also allowed rapid adoption of new AI models including multimodal models as they became available.

title: Evolution from Monolithic to Task-Oriented LLM Pipelines in a Developer Assistant Product
short_summary: Outropy built an AI-powered Chief of Staff product for engineering leaders that scaled to 10,000 users. The team faced significant challenges with their initial monolithic inference pipelines, including context window limitations, cascading errors from chained LLM calls, and code duplication across features. They evolved from a component-oriented approach (similar to LangChain patterns) to a task-oriented design that decomposed complex inference into modular, reusable pipelines orchestrated by agents. Using Temporal for durable workflows, they achieved robust error handling, automatic retries, and the ability to iterate rapidly on individual tasks without disrupting the production system.

title: AI-Powered Chief of Staff: Scaling Agent Architecture from Monolith to Distributed System
short_summary: Outropy built an AI-powered "Chief of Staff" assistant for engineering leaders that unified information across productivity tools and tracked project developments. Starting as a Slack bot, the team evolved from simple inference pipelines to a sophisticated multi-agent architecture, learning that agents differ fundamentally from microservices and are better modeled as stateful objects. They implemented CQRS with event sourcing for agent memory, used proposition-based retrieval for natural language event handling, and scaled to 10,000 users through organization-based sharding, Python async optimizations, and migration to Temporal for workflow orchestration. The architecture ultimately led to a pivot, with the underlying technology becoming the basis for Outropy's developer platform.

title: Scaling and Operating Large Language Models at the Frontier
short_summary: This case study from Anthropic explores the operational challenges of training and deploying frontier large language models at scale. The discussion covers the evolution from GPT-3 era training to current Claude models, highlighting how engineering mega-projects require tight researcher-engineer collaboration, robust observability and monitoring systems, and sophisticated infrastructure including Kubernetes clusters pushed beyond standard specifications. Key solutions include on-call rotations with follow-the-sun coverage, defense-in-depth safety mechanisms, Constitutional AI (RLAIF) for automated alignment, and responsible scaling policies with defined AI Safety Levels. Results include 10x revenue growth in the past year, with an additional 10x growth in the coding segment over three months, while maintaining safety commitments through public Responsible Scaling Policies and Long-Term Benefit Trust governance.

title: Scaling AI-Assisted Coding Infrastructure: From Auto-Complete to Global Deployment
short_summary: Cursor, an AI-powered code editor, shares how they scaled their LLM inference infrastructure from startup to processing approximately 100 million custom model calls daily across a global fleet of around 1,000-2,000 H100 GPUs. The case study covers their three-pillar architecture (indexing systems, model inference, and streaming infrastructure), the challenges of managing multi-provider inference at scale, and detailed incident response stories including a major database outage that required a real-time migration from PostgreSQL to object storage. Key lessons include the importance of using proven databases over distributed newcomers, managing cold-start problems during incident recovery, and the operational complexity of being one of the largest frontier model API consumers globally.

title: Evaluating Product Image Integrity in AI-Generated Advertising Content
short_summary: Microsoft's ISE team worked with an advertising customer seeking 1:1 ad personalization using AI-generated backgrounds. The core challenge was ensuring that when using inpainting techniques to generate contextual backgrounds around product images, the original product remained unmodified. The team developed a multi-technique image comparison system combining Mean Squared Error (MSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Cosine Similarity using CNN feature vectors, and OpenCV template matching to detect any alterations to products in AI-generated outputs. The combined approach leverages the complementary strengths of each method—MSE and PSNR for color and scale differences, Cosine Similarity for edge and curve detection regardless of position, and template matching to locate products within generated images for scoped comparison.

title: Avoiding Unearned Complexity in Production LLM Systems
short_summary: Microsoft's ISE (Industry Solutions Engineering) team shares lessons learned from working with large enterprise customers on production LLM solutions, warning against the premature adoption of complex patterns like agentic frameworks and LangChain before simpler approaches have been exhausted. The team identifies common anti-patterns including "unearned complexity" where customers adopt sophisticated tools without validating their necessity, and highlights specific concerns around agentic solution brittleness, LangChain's pre-v1 status creating security and maintenance burdens, and the significant SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) implications of adopting dependency-heavy frameworks. The recommended approach emphasizes starting with simpler fixed-flow solutions as benchmarks before incrementally adding complexity only when justified by measurable improvements.

title: Multimodal RAG Architecture Optimization for Production
short_summary: Microsoft's ISE team developed a multimodal RAG pipeline to handle enterprise documents containing both text and images, enabling LLMs to answer domain-specific queries grounded in visual content. The solution uses GPT-4V to generate detailed image descriptions during ingestion, storing them alongside text in Azure AI Search for unified vector retrieval. Through systematic experimentation, the team optimized several pipeline components including image enrichment prompts, chunk structure, classifier thresholds, and model selection, achieving improved retrieval metrics while reducing ingestion latency by 30-50% through intelligent image filtering. Key findings included that separate image chunks outperformed inline descriptions for retrieval, GPT-4V was superior for image enrichment while GPT-4o performed better for inference, and including document metadata significantly improved source recall.

title: Large Language Models for Retail Customer Feedback Analysis
short_summary: A leading retailer faced challenges in manually processing tens of thousands of daily customer feedback comments to derive actionable insights. Microsoft's ISE team developed a solution using Azure OpenAI with GPT models to automatically extract themes, sentiments, and competitor comparisons from shopper feedback. Through iterative prompt engineering with predefined theme categories, the system generates consistent, structured JSON outputs that can be aggregated across store hierarchies for reporting and decision-making. The approach emphasizes data enrichment, prompt refinement, and the importance of evaluation before production deployment.

title: Enterprise-Scale GenAI Infrastructure Template and Starter Framework
short_summary: Microsoft's ISE team partnered with an enterprise customer facing inefficiencies from starting each GenAI project from scratch, including repetitive pipeline setup, security reviews, and resource provisioning. The solution involved creating a reusable template architecture with pre-configured LLMOps pipelines, Azure resource connections, and a "template-starter" wizard that automates project initialization. This approach eliminated duplicate approval processes, reduced team dependencies, standardized the technology stack across projects, and enabled teams to focus on innovation rather than configuration, ultimately accelerating time-to-deployment for GenAI initiatives.

title: Implementing LLMOps in Restricted Networks with Long-Running Evaluations
short_summary: Microsoft's ISE team faced challenges implementing LLMOps for an LLM chat application within a restricted bring-your-own (BYO) network environment using Azure Machine Learning. The core problems included configuring services within a private network with no public IPs, managing lengthy 6-hour end-to-end evaluation runs, and establishing reliable CI/CD/CE pipelines. The solution involved using Prompt Flow with Azure ML, implementing Git Flow branching strategy for controlled releases, and creating a PR label-based opt-out mechanism for long-running evaluations. This allowed teams to consciously decide when to skip comprehensive evaluations for simple changes while maintaining a 30-minute minimal dataset evaluation for every deployment. The approach successfully balanced thorough model validation with deployment efficiency in a highly restricted network environment.

title: Voice AI Agent Development and Production Challenges
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together voice AI practitioners from Prosus, Google DeepMind, and Canonical to explore the unique challenges of deploying voice AI agents in production. The panelists discuss critical differences between text-based and voice-based LLM applications, including latency requirements, emotional responsiveness, handling of spoken letters and dialects, and user experience considerations. Key solutions include structured prompting, asynchronous tool calling, comprehensive testing with synthetic data across languages and emotional states, and careful product definition to match voice characteristics to use cases. The discussion highlights that while voice AI models are impressive, significant craftsmanship is required to move from MVP to production-ready systems.

title: Scaling Product Categorization with Batch Inference and Prompt Engineering
short_summary: GoDaddy needed to enhance their product categorization system that assigns categories to products based on their names for over 6 million products. Their existing Llama 2 implementation produced incomplete or mislabeled categories and was cost-prohibitive at scale. Working with AWS's Generative AI Innovation Center, they developed a batch inference solution using Amazon Bedrock that processes products in batches with n-packing techniques, achieving 97% category coverage on 100,000 test products. The solution using Anthropic's Claude-Instant proved 80% faster than requirements (processing 5,000 products in 12 minutes vs. the 1-hour requirement), 8% more cost-effective than the original Llama 2 approach, and provided 79% more category coverage.

title: Scaling Open-Ended Customer Service Analysis with Foundation Models
short_summary: MaestroQA faced the challenge of analyzing millions of unstructured customer interaction transcripts (calls, chats, emails) for their enterprise clients who needed open-ended question analysis beyond simple keyword matching. They integrated Amazon Bedrock to enable their "AskAI" feature, allowing customers to run open-ended queries like "What are customers frustrated about?" across millions of transcripts. The solution uses cross-region inference for scalability, offers multiple foundation models (Claude, Mistral, Llama, Cohere), and runs on AWS infrastructure including ECS and S3. Results include a lending company achieving near 100% compliance risk detection, a medical device company ensuring FDA-required issue flagging, and an education company expanding sentiment analysis from 15% to 100% of conversations.

title: LLMs for Investigative Data Analysis in Journalism
short_summary: ProPublica, a nonprofit investigative journalism organization, has developed a methodology for using large language models to analyze large datasets and document collections in support of accountability journalism. In one notable case, reporters used an LLM to analyze over 3,400 grants flagged as "woke" by Senator Ted Cruz's office, prompting the model to identify why each grant might have been flagged and to extract supporting citations. The approach revealed that many grants were flagged for innocuous uses of words like "diversify" (referring to biodiversity) or "female" (describing a researcher). ProPublica has also used self-hosted open-source AI for transcription and classification of sensitive audio/video materials. The organization emphasizes human oversight, with all AI outputs reviewed by journalists before publication, and maintains strict guardrails including instructing models not to guess when uncertain to prevent hallucinations.

title: Large-Scale Test Framework Migration Using LLMs
short_summary: AirBnB faced the challenge of migrating nearly 3,500 React component test files from the deprecated Enzyme framework to React Testing Library (RTL). Originally estimated to require 1.5 years of manual engineering effort, the team developed an LLM-powered automation pipeline that completed the migration in just 6 weeks. The solution employed a state-machine approach with discrete validation and refactor steps, retry loops with dynamic prompting, and rich context injection (40,000-100,000 tokens per prompt). The initial bulk run achieved 75% success in 4 hours, and after 4 days of systematic prompt tuning using a "sample, tune, sweep" methodology, success rates reached 97%, with the remaining 3% completed through manual intervention guided by LLM-generated baselines.

title: RoBERTa for Large-Scale Merchant Classification
short_summary: Square faced challenges with inaccurate merchant categorization due to reliance on self-selection during onboarding, which led to inefficiencies in product targeting, business strategy, and interchange fee management. They developed a RoBERTa-based classification model trained on over 20,000 manually reviewed merchant labels, incorporating post-onboarding signals like business names, catalog items ranked by purchase frequency, and self-selected categories. The model runs daily inference on tens of millions of merchants using GPU clusters with PySpark for parallel processing, achieving approximately 30% absolute accuracy improvement over previous methods across major business categories, with some categories like retail seeing 38% gains.

title: GenAI-Powered Dual-Loop System for Automated Documentation Management
short_summary: Intuit developed a GenAI-powered dual-loop pipeline to address common challenges in technical documentation management, including inconsistent quality, outdated information, poor structure, and limited discoverability. The inner loop employs multiple LLM-based plugins to analyze, improve, standardize, and augment documents before they enter the knowledge base, while the outer loop uses embeddings and semantic search to retrieve and synthesize relevant information in response to user queries. The system features feedback-driven improvement that updates both search parameters and base documents when queries fail, enabling continuous enhancement of both content quality and retrieval accuracy. While specific quantitative results are not provided, the architecture demonstrates a systematic approach to using LLMs for intelligent document preprocessing and context-aware knowledge discovery.

title: Scaling Audio Content Generation with LLMs and TTS for Language Learning
short_summary: Duolingo faced a scaling challenge with DuoRadio, their podcast-like audio feature for language learners, where manually producing 300 episodes took nearly a year. By developing curriculum-driven generative AI pipelines that leverage existing lesson content for script generation, implementing AI-powered quality evaluators to filter outputs, and integrating automated text-to-speech audio production, they scaled from 2 to 25+ courses and from 300 to 15,000+ episodes in under two quarters. This automation reportedly reduced costs by 99% while growing daily sessions from 500K to 5M in fewer than six months, demonstrating a successful blend of AI automation with expert oversight for content quality.

title: Building a Data-Centric Multi-Agent Platform for Enterprise AI
short_summary: Alibaba presents their approach to building production-ready AI Agent systems, addressing the challenge of deploying LLMs in enterprise environments through a data-centric multi-agent architecture. Their solution leverages the Spring-AI-Alibaba framework alongside tools like Higress (AI-native API gateway), Nacos for dynamic prompt management, OpenTelemetry for observability, and Apache RocketMQ for real-time RAG data updates. The approach emphasizes a "data flywheel" concept where customer feedback continuously improves agent performance. Applied to their intelligent diagnostic system, Alibaba claims the solution resolves over 95% of consulting issues and 85% of anomalies, though specific metrics and methodology details are limited.

title: Building Production-Ready AI Agents: Lessons from BeeAI Framework Development
short_summary: IBM Research's team spent a year developing AI agents to democratize access to generative AI capabilities for everyday builders. Starting with a prototype agent that outperformed commercial search solutions using open-source Llama 3-70B with chain-of-thought prompting, they learned critical lessons about user trust, security, and enterprise requirements. This led to the creation of the open-source BeeAI Framework in TypeScript, which gained traction with developers. Key production lessons included the importance of trajectory exploration for user trust, the need for custom agent architectures rather than one-size-fits-all approaches, the critical role of evaluation and custom benchmarking, and the challenge of enforcing business rules beyond simple prompting.

title: LLM-Powered Requirements Generation and Virtual Testing for Automotive Software Development
short_summary: Capgemini developed an accelerator called "Amplifier" that uses large language models deployed on AWS Bedrock to transform whiteboard ideation sessions into structured software requirements for automotive vehicle development. The solution addresses the challenge of lengthy development cycles in automotive software (which can take months or years compared to days in web development) by extracting information from photos of whiteboard sketches, generating consistent requirements, testing for ambiguity, and creating user stories ready for development teams. Combined with virtualized ECU environments on AWS, the system enables developers to go from idea to testable prototype in hours rather than weeks, while maintaining the quality and regulatory compliance needed for automotive safety certifications.

title: Fine-tuning Custom Embedding Models for Enterprise Search
short_summary: Glean tackles the challenge of building high-quality enterprise AI search by developing custom embedding models fine-tuned for each customer's specific domain language and data. The solution involves a multi-stage training pipeline starting with masked language modeling for domain adaptation, followed by contrastive learning using synthetically generated and unsupervised training pairs from enterprise data sources. By continuously learning from user feedback and retraining models monthly, Glean reports a 20% improvement in search quality after six months. The approach emphasizes that smaller, domain-specific models often outperform larger general-purpose embedding models for enterprise RAG applications.

title: Multi-Agent Architecture for Automating Commercial Real Estate Development Workflows
short_summary: Build.inc developed a multi-agent system called "Dougie" using LangGraph to automate land diligence workflows for commercial real estate development, particularly for data centers and energy infrastructure projects. The system orchestrates over 25 sub-agents in a four-tier hierarchical architecture to perform tasks that previously required specialist consultants working over four weeks. By leveraging asynchronous execution and parallel processing, the solution reportedly completes the entire workflow in approximately 75 minutes while delivering comprehensive output that the company claims matches or exceeds human consultant quality. The system addresses the complexity of fragmented data across 30,000+ US jurisdictions and enables modular expansion without disrupting existing functionality.

title: Automating Root Cause Analysis Using Amazon Bedrock Agents
short_summary: BMW faced challenges with time-consuming root cause analysis (RCA) for service outages across their connected vehicle digital services, which span multiple teams, components, and regions serving over 23 million connected vehicles. They deployed an Amazon Bedrock Agent using the ReAct framework to automate RCA by integrating custom tools that analyze system architecture, logs, metrics, and infrastructure changes via AWS Lambda, CloudWatch, and CloudTrail. The solution correctly identifies root causes in 85% of test cases, significantly reduces diagnosis time from hours to minutes, and enables junior engineers to effectively diagnose issues by providing real-time insights and hypothesis generation that mimics experienced engineer reasoning.

title: Insurance Policy Review Automation Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Prompt Engineering
short_summary: Verisk developed Mozart companion, a generative AI-powered solution that compares insurance policy documents and summarizes changes between versions. The system uses Amazon Bedrock with Anthropic's Claude 3 Sonnet, Amazon OpenSearch Service for vector storage, and Amazon Titan Text Embeddings for document processing. Through iterative prompt engineering, RAG implementation, and hybrid FM/non-FM approaches, Verisk achieved over 90% acceptable summary quality as rated by domain experts, reducing policy change adoption time from days or weeks to minutes.

title: Improving Error Handling for AI Agents in Production
short_summary: fewsats encountered a critical issue when deploying AI agents that interact with their Sherlock Domains SDK: agents would enter "doom loops" when encountering HTTP errors because they only saw generic error codes (e.g., "HTTP Error 422") rather than detailed response bodies explaining what went wrong. By modifying their SDK to surface complete error details including response payloads, the agents could immediately self-correct—for example, understanding they needed to use "first_name" and "last_name" fields instead of a combined "name" field. This simple fix enabled AI agents across different model sizes (Claude, Llama 3, Replit Agent) to recover from errors autonomously without human intervention.

title: Building and Scaling AI-Powered Password Detection in Production
short_summary: GitHub faced the challenge of detecting generic passwords in codebases, a task where traditional regular expression approaches produced excessive false positives due to the varied and nuanced structures of passwords. They developed Copilot secret scanning, leveraging LLMs (initially GPT-3.5-Turbo, later GPT-4 variants) to analyze contextual information around potential secrets. Through iterative prompt engineering using techniques like few-shot prompting, Chain-of-Thought, and MetaReflection, along with a robust offline evaluation framework and mirror testing against real repositories, they achieved significant improvements in precision—up to 94% reduction in false positives in some organizations—while maintaining recall. The solution now runs on nearly 35% of all GitHub Secret Protection repositories, with custom workload-aware capacity management enabling efficient LLM resource utilization at scale.

title: Building Internal LLM Tools with Security and Privacy Focus
short_summary: Wealthsimple, a Canadian fintech company, built an internal LLM Gateway and suite of generative AI tools to enable secure, accessible use of LLMs across the organization. The solution includes PII redaction before sending data to external models, self-hosted open-source LLMs, multimodal input support, and a RAG-based knowledge retrieval system. Over half the company now uses the Gateway, with adoption driving productivity gains particularly in programming support, content generation, and information retrieval. The platform also extended into production use cases for operations optimization, including client ticket triaging using both traditional ML and LLM capabilities.

title: Enterprise-Scale LLM Platform with Multi-Model Support and Copilot Customization
short_summary: Telus developed FuelEx, a centralized generative AI management platform that enables the creation and deployment of customized AI co-pilots across their organization. The platform addresses key enterprise challenges around model selection flexibility, centralized management, and security by providing a multi-cloud, multi-model architecture with configurable guardrails. Results include over 30,000 custom co-pilots built, 35,000+ active users, and significant operational improvements including a 46% resolution rate for their internal IT support bot and a 21% month-over-month decrease in agent interactions.

title: AI-Powered Chatbot Automation with Hybrid NLU and LLM Approach
short_summary: Scotiabank developed an "AI for AI" system to optimize their NLU-based chatbot by automating the human review process that previously required two AI trainers spending an hour each per day reviewing customer queries. They built three machine learning models (nicknamed Luigi, Eva, and Peach) that replaced manual reviewers: a binary classifier to identify misclassified queries, a multiclass classifier to suggest better intents, and a similarity algorithm to help trainers add valuable training phrases. Additionally, they implemented an LLM-powered summarization feature using Google's text-bison (later Gemini) that condenses chatbot-to-customer conversations by 80% before handoff to live agents, reducing average handle time. The system saves approximately 1,000 hours annually and represents the bank's first generative AI feature in production.

title: RAG System for Investment Policy Search and Advisory at RBC
short_summary: RBC developed "Arcane," an internal RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system to help investment advisors quickly access and understand complex investment policies. The problem addressed was the significant bottleneck created when highly specialized financial advisors needed to search through semi-structured internal documents to answer client questions, with every second of delay having multiplicative productivity impacts worth millions in bottom line impact. The solution involved building a RAG system with careful parsing of semi-structured data (HTML, PDFs, internal websites), proper chunking strategies, and robust evaluation using RAGAS metrics alongside traditional information retrieval measures. The pilot was tested in production, with plans for scaling by their partner Borealis AI. Key learnings included the critical importance of document parsing quality, managing cumulative probability errors in multi-turn conversations, and implementing proper security measures for proprietary financial information.

title: Building a Video Q&A System with RAG and Speaker Detection
short_summary: Vimeo developed a video Q&A system that enables viewers to converse with video content in natural language using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). The system addresses the challenge of extracting information from lengthy videos by processing video transcripts through a multi-level chunking approach, storing them in a vector database, and using LLMs to generate contextually grounded answers.
