Key innovations include a speaker detection algorithm that identifies speakers without facial recognition, a bottom-up processing approach for handling various context lengths, and automated generation of related questions to keep viewers engaged. The system provides textual answers along with playable video moments as references.

title: Building Modular and Scalable RAG Systems with Hybrid Batch/Incremental Processing
short_summary: Bell Canada's ML engineering team built a modular, productionized solution for managing dynamic knowledge bases in RAG systems. The challenge was handling constantly changing document sources (like HR policies and Confluence pages) while maintaining efficient vector database synchronization. Their solution combines batch and incremental processing pipelines using Apache Beam, Airflow, and GCP services, with a structured knowledge base design inspired by TensorFlow Extended. The hybrid architecture allows both scheduled batch rebuilds and real-time document updates, with all components configurable via YAML files, enabling rapid deployment of new RAG use cases without custom development.

title: Building and Deploying a Pokemon-Playing LLM Agent at Anthropic
short_summary: David Hershey from Anthropic's Applied team built an autonomous agent that plays Pokemon as both a personal learning project and a novel evaluation method for long-horizon model capabilities. The agent uses Claude with a simple architecture consisting of button press tools, a self-managed knowledge base for persistent memory, and a navigation helper. The project evolved from an internal experiment started in June 2024 to a public release, demonstrating significant improvements across model versions and serving as an unconventional but effective benchmark for testing how well models can maintain coherence over thousands of prompts and actions while adapting to new information in real-time.

title: Building and Automating Comprehensive LLM Evaluation Framework for SNAP Benefits
short_summary: Propel, a company focused on helping SNAP (food stamp) benefit recipients, developed a comprehensive LLM evaluation framework to assess how well various AI models perform on SNAP-related questions. The problem addressed was the need to both benchmark existing models for public benefit and guide internal product development for a SNAP-specific assistant. Their solution involved creating automated evaluation pipelines using Promptfoo, testing factual knowledge across multiple models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.0 Flash), and implementing LLM-as-judge techniques for more nuanced criteria like reading level accessibility. Initial results showed significant variance between models, with Claude passing approximately 73% of factual tests compared to around 45% for other models, and identified critical gaps like outdated income limit information that would need to be addressed through techniques like RAG.

title: AI-Powered Ecommerce Content Optimization Platform
short_summary: Pattern, an e-commerce acceleration company, developed Content Brief, an AI-driven tool that processes over 38 trillion proprietary e-commerce data points to help brands optimize product listings across online marketplaces. Using Amazon Bedrock for LLM capabilities, Amazon DynamoDB for data storage, Amazon ECS with GPU support for scaling, and Amazon Textract for image analysis, the solution delivers actionable insights including attribute importance ranking, image archetype analysis, sentiment analysis of customer reviews, and competitive benchmarking. A case study with Select Brands demonstrated a 21% month-over-month revenue increase, 14.5% traffic growth, and improved conversion rates after implementing Content Brief's recommendations for their Amazon product listings.

title: Large-Scale Video Content Processing with Multimodal LLMs on AWS Inferentia2
short_summary: ByteDance faced the challenge of processing billions of daily videos for content moderation and understanding across their platforms including TikTok. They deployed multimodal large language models (LLMs) on AWS Inferentia2 chips across multiple regions, implementing various optimization techniques including tensor parallelism, static batching, INT8 quantization, and model replication. The solution achieved 50% cost reduction compared to comparable EC2 instances while maintaining the ability to process billions of videos daily for content that violates community guidelines.

title: Optimizing Production LLM Chatbot Performance Through Multi-Model Classification
short_summary: Applus+ IDIADA developed AIDA, an Amazon Bedrock-powered intelligent chatbot serving their automotive workforce, but faced challenges in efficiently routing diverse user requests to appropriate processing pipelines. The team experimented with multiple classification approaches including pure LLM-based classifiers, LLM with example augmentation (RAG), and traditional ML algorithms (k-NN, SVM, ANN) using embeddings from Amazon Titan and Cohere's multilingual model. The embedding-based approaches with classical ML classifiers significantly outperformed the LLM-based methods, with SVM using Cohere embeddings achieving 0.99 F1 for Conversation, 0.80 for Services, and 0.93 for Document Translation, while also being 4-60x faster than LLM inference. The optimized system now handles over 1,000 daily interactions with 95% accuracy, driving a reported 20% increase in team productivity.

title: Building Production Web Agents for Food Ordering
short_summary: Prosus, a large tech company operating platforms like iFood, OLX, and others serving nearly two billion consumers, developed a custom web agent framework for automating food ordering tasks. After evaluating existing frameworks like Multion and Web Voyager and finding them insufficient for production use cases (with unpredictable success rates and agents getting stuck in loops), the team built their own modular system separating planning from execution. They implemented three operational modes—traditional (with screenshots), fast (without screenshots for familiar pages), and reflex (deterministic automation)—achieving an 80% target success rate while learning that treating the project as a software engineering problem rather than a data science one was essential for production reliability.

title: SQL Query Agent for Data Democratization
short_summary: Prosus, a technology investment group with approximately 30,000 employees across multiple portfolio companies, developed the Token Data Analyst—an AI agent designed to democratize data access by allowing non-technical users to query databases using natural language. The agent integrates with Slack, connects to enterprise data warehouses like Snowflake and BigQuery, and works alongside human data analysts rather than replacing them. Results include a 74% reduction in time-to-answer for data queries and a doubling or tripling of insights generated due to reduced bottlenecks, with the system now deployed across multiple portfolio companies including iFood and OLX.

title: Evolving LLMOps Architecture for Enterprise Supplier Discovery
short_summary: Scoutbee, a supply chain intelligence company, embarked on an 18-month journey to integrate LLMs into their supplier discovery platform. Starting with a simple ChatGPT API integration that suffered from hallucinations and lack of domain knowledge, they progressively evolved their architecture through four stages: enabling open-source LLMs for data privacy, implementing domain adaptation with agents and guardrails using Graphs of Thought, reducing hallucinations through RAG with Chain of Thought prompting, and scaling data operations using knowledge graphs and a universal compute framework (Ray). The result was a production system that provides trusted, citation-backed supplier recommendations while maintaining enterprise security requirements.

title: Building a Multi-Agent LLM Platform for Customer Service Automation
short_summary: Deutsche Telekom's AI Competence Center developed LMOS (Language Models Operating System), an open-source multi-agent platform to deploy GenAI-powered customer service automation across 10 European countries and multiple channels (chat, voice). The platform addresses the challenge of scaling LLM applications across diverse business processes, languages, and APIs by providing a Kotlin-based DSL framework (ARC) for rapid agent development, a Kubernetes-native control plane for agent lifecycle management, and intent-based routing. Results include over 1 million questions answered with 89% acceptable answer rate, 300,000+ human-agent conversations deflected with under 2% risk rate, 38% better performance than vendor products in A/B testing, and agent development time reduced from 2 months to 10 days.

title: Modernizing DevOps with Generative AI: Challenges and Best Practices in Production
short_summary: This roundtable discussion explores how organizations are integrating generative AI into DevOps workflows to enhance developer productivity and experience. The panelists, representing companies including Bundesliga, Harness, and Trice, discuss current adoption patterns, challenges around compliance and code confidentiality, the non-deterministic nature of AI outputs, and practical strategies for implementation. Key outcomes include guidance on starting with IDE-integrated AI assistants, treating AI as a collaborative tool rather than a replacement, maintaining human oversight through "human in the lead" approaches, and acknowledging that productivity gains require an initial learning investment and may manifest in unexpected areas beyond code generation.

title: Optimizing Copilot Latency with NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM Integration
short_summary: Moveworks addressed the challenge of LLM inference latency in their enterprise AI Copilot by integrating NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM optimization engine. The solution leveraged optimized CUDA kernels, multi-GPU model parallelism, and techniques like Flash-Decoding and SmoothQuant quantization to dramatically improve performance. Results showed a 2.3x improvement in token throughput (from 19 to 44 tokens per second), a 2.35x reduction in average request latency (from 3.4 seconds to 1.5 seconds), and a 2.7x improvement in time-to-first-token (from 0.8 seconds to 0.3 seconds), enabling more natural conversational experiences and better resource utilization for their employee support platform.

title: Scaling Order Processing Automation Using Modular LLM Architecture
short_summary: Choco developed an AI system to automate order intake for food and beverage distributors, processing unstructured orders from multiple channels (email, voicemail, SMS, WhatsApp, fax) and integrating them into ERP systems. The solution uses a modular architecture with multiple LLMs and ML models for specific tasks like transcription, information extraction, and product matching. The system achieved over 95% prediction accuracy and helped one distributor reduce manual order entry time by 60% while processing 50% more orders daily. Key to their success was treating LLMs as narrow task executors, building comprehensive evaluation pipelines, investing heavily in human labeling, and designing user interactions that generate training data for continuous improvement.

title: Using Token Log-Probabilities to Detect and Filter LLM Hallucinations in Customer Support
short_summary: Gusto, an HR and payroll software company, developed a method to detect and filter low-quality LLM outputs in their customer support FAQ service by leveraging token log-probabilities as a confidence score. By analyzing sequence log-probability (Seq-Logprob) scores from their LLM-generated responses and correlating them with human quality labels, they demonstrated a 69% relative difference in accuracy between the most confident and least confident responses (76% vs 45% accuracy). This approach enables them to construct precision-recall curves for their LLM system, allowing automated rejection of poor-quality responses or routing low-confidence outputs to human experts for verification.

title: Building a Multi-Provider GenAI Gateway for Enterprise-Scale LLM Access
short_summary: Grab developed an AI Gateway to address the challenges of providing enterprise-wide access to multiple GenAI providers (OpenAI, Azure, AWS Bedrock, Google VertexAI) while maintaining security, cost efficiency, and governance. The solution is a centralized reverse proxy architecture that handles authentication, authorization, rate limiting, cost attribution, and auditing across all LLM requests. Since its inception in 2023, the gateway has onboarded over 300 unique use cases, with more than 3,000 employees using exploration keys for experimentation. The platform powers production applications including ride safety audio analysis, content moderation, and internal productivity tools like text-to-SQL and incident management automation.

title: Building a RAG-Based Premium Audit Assistant for Insurance Workflows
short_summary: Verisk, a data analytics partner for the global insurance industry, faced challenges with their Premium Audit Advisory Service (PAAS) platform where premium auditors struggled to efficiently search through over 40,000 classification guides, 500+ bulletins, and other documents. To address this, they built PAAS AI, a RAG-based conversational AI assistant using Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude models), Amazon OpenSearch Service for semantic search, and Amazon ElastiCache for chat history. The solution implements hybrid search combining sparse BM25 and dense vector search, custom evaluation APIs measuring answer relevancy, context relevancy, and faithfulness scores, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for safety. Early results from beta testing showed a 96-98% reduction in processing time per specialist, transforming hours of manual review into minutes of AI-assisted research.

title: Building a Hybrid Cloud AI Infrastructure for Large-Scale ML Inference
short_summary: Roblox faced challenges scaling AI inference to support their growing platform of 79.5 million daily active users, starting from fewer than 50 ML pipelines in early 2023 to approximately 250 pipelines today. They implemented a three-phase approach: building a unified ML foundation with Kubeflow, optimizing inference with Ray for batch processing and a custom feature store, and operationalizing massive inference through an ML gateway and vLLM-based LLMOps platform. The results include processing approximately 4 billion tokens per week with nearly 2x improvements in latency and throughput, serving 1 billion personalization requests daily, and supporting 1.5 billion tokens per week for their Roblox Assistant feature alone.

title: Building a Scalable Chatbot Platform with Edge Computing and Multi-Layer Security
short_summary: Fastmind developed a chatbot builder platform that focuses on scalability, security, and performance. The solution combines edge computing via Cloudflare Workers, multi-layer rate limiting, and a distributed architecture using Next.js, Hono, and Convex. The platform uses Cohere's AI models and implements various security measures to prevent abuse while maintaining cost efficiency for thousands of users.

title: Building Scalable LLM Evaluation Systems for Healthcare Prior Authorization
short_summary: Anterior, a healthcare AI company processing prior authorization decisions for insurance providers covering 50 million American lives, built a real-time reference-free evaluation system to handle mission-critical medical decisions at scale. The challenge was that traditional human review approaches don't scale—reviewing even 5% of 100,000 daily decisions would require 50 clinicians. Their solution combines LLM-as-judge techniques with confidence estimation and contextual prioritization to dynamically identify which cases need human review, estimate system performance in real-time, and maintain quality without proportionally scaling review staff. The result is a team of fewer than 10 clinical experts reviewing tens of thousands of cases, achieving an F1 score of nearly 96% on prior authorization decisions, with alignment between AI and human reviews comparable to inter-human agreement.

title: Practical Lessons Learned from Building and Deploying GenAI Applications
short_summary: This presentation by Juan Pero, a seasoned consultant and developer from Bolbeck, shares practical lessons learned from 18 months of building generative AI applications. The talk covers critical LLMOps challenges including model selection and hosting, ensuring output quality through techniques like prompt engineering, guardrails, and RAG, managing costs and latency in agentic systems, and the importance of observability. Key takeaways include externalizing prompts for collaboration and future-proofing, understanding the significant cost differences between models (demonstrating how switching from OpenAI o1 to Llama 3.3 could reduce monthly costs from $300,000 to $50,000 for a call center use case), and implementing robust tracing for debugging non-deterministic agent behavior.

title: Building and Deploying Production AI Agents for Enterprise Data Analysis
short_summary: Asterrave, founded by Patrick (co-founder and CTO), rebuilt their entire product around AI agents to enable enterprise users to search and query data warehouses using natural language. The team learned that focusing on agent reasoning over model knowledge was critical, implementing discrete tool calls for retrieval instead of RAG approaches. Key insights included optimizing the Agent Computer Interface (ACI) with format-specific responses (JSON for GPT-4, XML for Claude), avoiding fine-tuning in favor of reasoning-focused architectures, and designing multi-agent systems with manager-worker hierarchies limited to 5-8 agents. The company ultimately concluded that custom implementation was preferable to frameworks like LangGraph for production deployments due to requirements like cascading user security credentials.

title: Building a Production AI Agent System for Customer Support
short_summary: Decagon, a Series B startup, has built an AI agent engine for enterprise customer support that handles conversations across chat, email, SMS, and voice channels. The solution addresses the traditionally poor customer support experience by deploying LLM-powered agents that can understand unstructured knowledge bases, execute complex workflows, and take actions like issuing refunds. The system includes routing capabilities to human agents, co-pilot features for human support staff, an admin dashboard for configuration and monitoring, and QA interfaces for continuous improvement. Key metrics tracked include deflection/automation rates and customer satisfaction scores, with enterprises reporting improved support experiences while maintaining brand consistency and security compliance.

title: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Sales Proposal Generation
short_summary: Fujitsu addressed inefficiencies in sales proposal creation by developing an AI-powered agent using Azure AI Agent Service and Semantic Kernel to orchestrate multiple specialized AI agents. The solution integrates with Azure AI Search to retrieve knowledge from scattered internal sources and generates tailored, data-driven proposals. The implementation resulted in a 67% productivity improvement in sales proposal creation, enabling approximately 38,000 employees to redirect time toward customer engagement and strategic planning. The project also serves as a foundation for broader AI-driven transformation across the organization.

title: Building Deep Research: A Production AI Research Assistant Agent
short_summary: Google DeepMind's Deep Research team built an agentic research assistant that can autonomously browse the web for 5-10 minutes to produce comprehensive research reports. The system addresses the challenge of multi-faceted queries that traditionally require users to open 50-60 browser tabs. Key innovations include an editable research plan that provides transparency and user control, iterative planning that adapts based on discovered information, parallel and sequential web browsing with intelligent source selection, and an asynchronous execution platform that maintains state across long-running jobs. The product has been well-received by users who value the depth of research over speed, contrary to typical Google product metrics where lower latency correlates with higher satisfaction.

title: Scaling Financial Research and Analysis with Multi-Model LLM Architecture
short_summary: Rogo, an enterprise AI finance platform, addressed the challenge of time-consuming manual financial research by building a multi-model architecture using OpenAI's models (GPT-4o, o1-mini, o1) integrated with major financial datasets like S&P Global, Crunchbase, and FactSet. The solution enables real-time insights from over 50 million financial documents, automated due diligence, and collaborative workflows for investment banks and asset managers. The platform reportedly saves analysts 10+ hours per week, serves over 5,000 bankers, and achieved 27x ARR growth since emerging from stealth in 2024.

title: AI-Powered Root Cause Analysis Assistant for Race Day Operations
short_summary: Formula 1 faced significant challenges with operational IT issues during live race events, where triaging and resolving critical problems across network, API, and downstream services could take up to three weeks and required cross-team investigations. In partnership with AWS, F1 developed a generative AI-powered Root Cause Analysis (RCA) assistant using Amazon Bedrock, implementing an agentic RAG architecture that connects to internal systems, databases, CloudWatch logs, and third-party tools like Jira and Datadog. The solution enables engineers to query issues using natural language, receiving responses within 5-10 seconds and reducing initial triage time from over a day to less than 20 minutes. The end-to-end resolution time was reportedly reduced by up to 86%, with one recurring issue that previously took 15 engineer days now resolved within 3 days including testing and deployment.

title: AI-Powered SNAP Benefits Notice Interpretation System
short_summary: Propel is developing an AI-powered tool to help SNAP (food stamp) recipients understand complex government notices they receive about their benefits. The problem stems from notices being confusing due to legal language, cognitive overload from required information, and difficulty distinguishing critical action items from informational content. Using LLMs like Claude 3.5 Sonnet with carefully crafted prompts, the prototype extracts two key outputs: the importance level of a notice and what action (if any) the user needs to take. The tool is still in alpha testing with program experts before deployment to users, with early results showing promising improvements in clarity compared to raw notices. Safety considerations include hallucination mitigation through grounding outputs to notice content, PII redaction strategies, and careful evaluation before production deployment.

title: Building a Systematic SNAP Benefits LLM Evaluation Framework
short_summary: Propel, a company building tools for SNAP (food stamp) program participants, shares their approach to building domain-specific LLM evaluations to assess how well AI models perform on safety net benefits questions. The problem addressed is the lack of reliable, specialized evaluations for niche domains like government benefits programs, where general-purpose AI models may provide inaccurate or unhelpful information to vulnerable users. Their solution involves a test-driven development approach: starting with domain expert exploration of models, documenting nuanced failure modes (such as the asset limit example where technically correct answers miss practically important information), and building automated eval test cases. The work aims to enable model comparison across providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), inform cost-latency tradeoffs through intelligent routing, and establish safety guardrails for production deployment. While results are preliminary (this is part 1 of a series), the methodology demonstrates how domain expertise can be codified into reproducible evaluations for high-stakes AI applications.

title: Collaborative Prompt Engineering Platform for Production LLM Development
short_summary: LinkedIn developed a collaborative prompt engineering environment using Jupyter Notebooks to accelerate the development of LLM-powered features for Sales Navigator. The challenge was bridging the gap between technical engineers and non-technical domain experts while maintaining rapid iteration cycles for prompt development. By creating reusable notebook-based playgrounds with containerized environments, standardized test datasets, and integrated prompt template management using LangChain and Jinja, they enabled cross-functional teams to collaborate seamlessly on prompt engineering. The approach resulted in AccountIQ, a feature that reduced company research time from two hours to five minutes, and established a framework for rapid prototyping and continuous improvement of GenAI features.

title: Automated GPU Kernel Generation Using LLMs and Inference-Time Scaling
short_summary: NVIDIA engineers developed a novel approach to automatically generate optimized GPU attention kernels using the DeepSeek-R1 model combined with inference-time scaling. The problem addressed was the labor-intensive and skill-demanding task of creating efficient GPU kernels for various attention mechanisms used in LLMs and multimodal models. The solution involved a closed-loop workflow where DeepSeek-R1 generated kernel code, which was then verified on H100 GPUs, with feedback guiding subsequent generation attempts over a 15-minute iteration window. The results demonstrated 100% numerical correctness for Level-1 problems and 96% for Level-2 problems on Stanford's KernelBench benchmark, with some automatically generated kernels outperforming those created by skilled engineers.

title: Building Voice-Enabled AI Assistants with Real-Time Processing
short_summary: This meetup-style presentation covers multiple approaches to building personal AI assistants that can capture, transcribe, and intelligently respond to users throughout their daily lives. Speakers from Deepgram, Bee (formerly Owl), Friend, and LangChain demonstrate real-time voice bot architectures achieving sub-second latency using speech-to-text, LLMs, and text-to-speech pipelines, alongside wearable hardware devices for continuous audio/video capture. The discussions cover critical production considerations including latency optimization (targeting under 1.5 seconds end-to-end), cost management (achieving approximately 6.5 cents per 5-minute call), memory architectures for personalization, and the challenges of building always-on AI companions that can perform autonomous actions across apps.

title: AI SRE Agents for Production System Diagnostics
short_summary: Cleric, a San Francisco-based startup, is building an AI SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) agent that helps engineering teams diagnose and root cause production incidents. The system leverages knowledge graphs to map complex production environments including Kubernetes clusters, cloud infrastructure, and organizational knowledge from Slack threads and runbooks. The agent uses a layered memory architecture combining episodic and procedural memory, confidence scoring to reduce alert fatigue, and progressive trust-building with human engineers. Key challenges include the unsupervised nature of production debugging, rapidly changing system states, and the need for agents to work with fuzzy, incomplete information while maintaining high reliability standards akin to self-driving cars.

title: AI Lab: A Pre-Production Framework for ML Performance Testing and Optimization
short_summary: Meta developed AI Lab, a pre-production testing framework designed to minimize Time to First Batch (TTFB) for machine learning engineers. The problem addressed was the overhead delay between submitting a training workflow and when the first batch of data enters the model for processing—a critical bottleneck affecting ML iteration speed at scale. The solution involves continuous A/B testing of ML workflows in a controlled environment, enabling both proactive improvements and automatic regression prevention. Notable results include up to 40% reduction in TTFB during the rollout of Python Cinder runtime, with iterative testing yielding a 2x increase on original improvements. The framework uses auto-shrinking techniques to minimize GPU resource consumption while maintaining regression detection capability.

title: Scaling AI-Generated Image Animation with Optimized Deployment Strategies
short_summary: Meta tackled the challenge of deploying an AI-powered image animation feature at massive scale, requiring optimization of both model performance and infrastructure. Through a combination of model optimizations including halving floating-point precision, improving temporal-attention expansion, and leveraging DPM-Solver, along with sophisticated traffic management and deployment strategies, they successfully deployed a system capable of serving billions of users while maintaining low latency and high reliability.

title: AI-Assisted Root Cause Analysis System for Incident Response
short_summary: Meta developed an AI-assisted root cause analysis system to streamline incident investigations in their large-scale infrastructure. The system combines heuristic-based retrieval to reduce the search space from thousands of code changes to hundreds, followed by a fine-tuned Llama 2 (7B) model that ranks and identifies the most likely root causes. Using an election-based ranking algorithm with structured prompts, the system achieved 42% accuracy in identifying root causes within the top five suggested code changes during backtesting for investigations related to their web monorepo.

title: RAG-Powered Terraform Support Slackbot
short_summary: Benchling's infrastructure team built an internal Slackbot to help engineers quickly find answers to Terraform Cloud questions without manually searching through a 20-page FAQ or numerous Slack threads. Using Amazon Bedrock's RAG capabilities with Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2, they created a knowledge base that ingests documentation from Confluence, public Hashicorp documentation, and historical Slack threads. The solution leverages AWS Lambda, API Gateway, and OpenSearch Serverless for the vector database, providing a familiar Slack interface for approximately 50 engineers who make infrastructure changes monthly. While the prototype successfully demonstrated rapid deployment of LLM-powered tools, the team identified limitations including lack of image processing support and the need for manual data synchronization.

title: High-Performance GPU Memory Transfer Optimization for Large Language Models
short_summary: Perplexity explored achieving 3200 Gbps GPU memory transfer rates on AWS SageMaker HyperPod infrastructure. While the source text is extremely limited, it suggests a focus on optimizing high-performance computing infrastructure for large-scale AI/ML workloads, specifically targeting GPU memory bandwidth optimization to support demanding LLM training and inference operations on AWS managed infrastructure.

title: Data Quality Assessment and Enhancement Framework for GenAI Applications
short_summary: QuantumBlack Labs developed AI4DQ Unstructured, a toolkit designed to assess and remediate data quality issues in unstructured data that underpin generative AI applications like RAG pipelines. The solution addresses common problems such as diverse document formats, lack of metadata, duplicate documents, and conflicting information that can cause hallucinations and inconsistent results. In a case study with an international health organization, the toolkit processed 2.5 GB of data across 1,500+ files, identifying over ten high-priority data quality issues, removing 100+ irrelevant or duplicated documents (saving 10-15% in storage costs), and preserving critical information that would otherwise be lost for 5% of policy documents. The tool claims a 20% increase in RAG pipeline accuracy through metadata enrichment.

title: Advanced Embedding-Based Retrieval for Personalized Content Discovery
short_summary: Pinterest's engineering team tackled the challenge of delivering highly personalized, engaging, and diverse content to users on their Homefeed by advancing their embedding-based retrieval system. They implemented sophisticated feature crossing techniques using MaskNet and DHEN frameworks, integrated pre-trained ID embeddings with contrastive learning, upgraded their serving corpus with time-decay scoring, and developed novel multi-embedding and conditional retrieval techniques. These improvements yielded measurable gains including 0.15-0.35% improvement in engaged sessions from MaskNet, additional 0.1-0.2% from DHEN scaling, 0.6-1.2% increases in repins and clicks from ID embeddings, and significant engagement improvements from multi-embedding and conditional retrieval approaches.

title: Scaling Search Query Understanding with LLMs: From POC to Production
short_summary: Yelp faced the challenge of improving search query understanding across millions of daily searches, where traditional NLU techniques were fragmented and lacked intelligence for tasks like spelling correction, segmentation, and review highlighting. They developed a systematic approach leveraging LLMs that involves formulation with powerful models like GPT-4, proof of concept validation through caching head queries, and scaling via fine-tuning progressively smaller models (GPT-4o-mini, BERT, T5) for cost efficiency. Using RAG with business names and categories, combined with strategic caching that exploits power-law query distributions, they achieved significant improvements in search CTR, with up to 100x cost savings compared to direct GPT-4 usage, while covering 95% of traffic through pre-computed signals.

title: Building a Secure and Scalable LLM Gateway for Enterprise GenAI Adoption
short_summary: Wealthsimple, a Canadian financial services platform, built a comprehensive LLM gateway and internal tooling ecosystem to enable employee productivity while maintaining data security. The solution included an audit-trail-enabled gateway proxying requests to multiple LLM providers, a custom PII redaction model, self-hosted open-source LLMs using llama.cpp, and RAG capabilities. The initiative achieved significant adoption with over 2,200 daily messages, nearly one-third of employees as weekly active users, and over half as monthly active users, with employees reporting significant productivity improvements in programming, content generation, and information retrieval tasks.

title: Building a Secure AI Assistant for Visual Effects Artists Using Amazon Bedrock
short_summary: Untold Studios, a visual effects and animation company, built an AI assistant called "Untold Assistant" using Amazon Bedrock with Claude 3.5 Sonnet to help artists access internal resources through natural language queries in Slack. The solution leverages RAG with pre-built connectors for Confluence and Salesforce, function calling for extensibility, and Stable Diffusion for image generation. The system handles up to 120 queries per day, reducing information retrieval time from minutes to seconds, while maintaining strict data security within the AWS ecosystem. The modular architecture reduced development time from months to weeks and allows rapid integration of new capabilities.

title: Scientific Intent Translation System for Healthcare Analytics Using Amazon Bedrock
short_summary: Aetion, a provider of real-world evidence software for biopharma and healthcare organizations, developed "Measures Assistant" — a generative AI feature that translates natural language scientific queries into complex patient variable algorithms. The solution uses Amazon Bedrock with Anthropic's Claude 3 Haiku, deployed as a microservice on Kubernetes, and incorporates a local knowledge base with RAG-like patterns for improved accuracy. The system enables scientists and analysts without data science expertise to implement complex studies in minutes rather than days, eliminating the need for specialized support staff while maintaining decision-grade evidence standards.

title: Optimizing Security Threat Investigation with Multi-Model LLM Strategy
short_summary: Trellix, a cybersecurity company, sought to optimize the cost and speed of their AI-powered threat investigation platform, Trellix Wise, which automates security event analysis and risk scoring. By adopting Amazon Nova Micro alongside Anthropic's Claude Sonnet in a multi-model strategy on Amazon Bedrock, they achieved inference speeds three times faster and costs nearly 100-fold lower for specific workflow stages. The solution leverages RAG with Amazon OpenSearch Service and multiple inference passes with the smaller model to maximize data completeness while constraining hallucinations through proprietary prompt engineering, resulting in an estimated 30-fold cost reduction in the data collection stage while maintaining quality.

title: Improving Local Search with Multimodal LLMs and Vector Search
short_summary: OfferUp, a mobile-first online marketplace, transformed its search capabilities from traditional keyword-based lexical search to multimodal vector search using Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon OpenSearch Service. The foundational search architecture struggled with context understanding, synonym awareness, and complex multi-concept queries. By implementing multimodal embeddings that encode both text and images into the same semantic space, OfferUp achieved a 27% improvement in relevance recall, 54% reduction in geographic spread (more local results), 6.5% growth in search depth, 2.2% increase in user engagement, and 3.8% improvement in Engagement with Seller Response (EWSR). The solution leveraged neural search pipelines, k-NN vector indexing, and OpenSearch ingest pipelines integrated with Amazon Bedrock connectors.

title: Rapid Development of AI-Powered Video Interview Analysis System
short_summary: Vericant, a video interview company serving educational institutions, deployed a generative AI solution in approximately 30 days to help admissions teams process interview content more efficiently. The problem was that admissions officers had to watch 15-minute interview videos to understand each applicant, which didn't scale well. The solution involved using GPT models via OpenAI's playground to generate summaries, key points, and topics from interview transcripts, reducing processing time from 15 minutes to 20-30 seconds per interview. The CEO built the initial prompts himself without programming, using a Google Sheets-based evaluation framework to iteratively improve output quality before handing off to engineering for production integration. This first-to-market advantage opened up an entirely new business opportunity around scaling the admissions team's processing capabilities.

title: Small Specialist Agents for Semiconductor Manufacturing Optimization
short_summary: Tokyo Electron, a global semiconductor manufacturing equipment company, is developing a multi-agent LLM system called Small Specialist Agents (SSA) to address the increasingly complex challenges in semiconductor manufacturing. The solution involves orchestrating multiple specialized agents—both public (physics, chemistry, machine learning) and private (equipment specifications, process history)—managed by a General Management Agent (GMA). The approach incorporates RAG and OODA (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act) decision loops to simulate expert discussions and provide actionable insights for process optimization. To address scalability concerns with 18,000 employees potentially querying the system, they are developing domain-specific small language models, including a semiconductor foundation model called "SemiCon," which can run locally to reduce costs, improve response times, and protect confidential information.

title: Autonomous Semiconductor Manufacturing with Multi-Modal LLMs and Reinforcement Learning
short_summary: Samsung is developing autonomous semiconductor fabrication ("Autonomous Fab") capabilities using multimodal foundation models, LLMs, knowledge graphs, and reinforcement learning to enhance process control in chip manufacturing. The solution addresses challenges in monitoring thousands of process steps, detecting anomalies in sensor data, automating root cause analysis, and enabling advanced process control. By combining domain expertise with RAG-based LLM systems, time series foundation models, and knowledge graphs, Samsung has deployed production systems that help engineers diagnose equipment issues, detect defects, and predict process outcomes—though challenges remain with time series model accuracy and hallucination issues.

title: Evolution of Industrial AI: From Traditional ML to Multi-Agent Systems
short_summary: Hitachi's AI research division presents their multi-year journey of deploying industrial AI at scale, demonstrating how generative AI augments traditional machine learning solutions. Their flagship example is a truck repair recommendation system deployed at Penske, operational for 5-7 years across 700 shops serving over half a million trucks, which combined historical repair classification models with generative AI-powered service manual understanding using graph-based fault trees and RAG techniques. The presentation outlines the evolution from Industrial AI 1.0 (focused on production, installation, maintenance) to 2.0 (full value chain coverage with generative AI) and the emerging 3.0 vision featuring agentic architectures with both virtual and physical agents.

title: AI Agent for Customer Service Order Management and Training
short_summary: RHI Magnesita, a global mining and manufacturing company producing refractory products, deployed an AI agent (Industrial Virtual Advisor) developed with Itomatic to address $3 million in annual human errors in order processing, invoicing, and accounts receivable. The solution aims to standardize training for customer service representatives (CSRs) across three countries, reduce order entry errors, and serve as a bridge during their SAP digital transformation. After approximately five months of implementation, the agent demonstrates capabilities including customer order history analysis, special requirements retrieval, and order reasonableness validation, with the team seeing enthusiastic adoption particularly from their Mexico-based CSR group.

title: AI-Powered Sustainable Fishing with LLM-Enhanced Domain Knowledge Integration
short_summary: Furuno, a marine electronics company that invented the first fish finder in 1948, is developing an AI system to help fishermen identify fish species and sizes to promote sustainable fishing practices. The core challenge is severe data scarcity—with over 300 fish species in Japan and only hundreds of data points per species, traditional machine learning approaches would take over a century to build effective models. Their solution involves an ensemble of three models: an image recognition model for fish finder displays, a classifier model using swimming depth and ultrasonic signals, and a novel "knowledge model" that captures each fisherman's decades of intuitive expertise. The emergence of LLMs has enabled a more straightforward means for fishermen to input their tacit knowledge, which was previously difficult to translate into usable data. Early results show promising outcomes, with fishermen better able to predict when fish arrive at fixed nets. The system is being deployed on laptop PCs as edge devices aboard vessels, with plans to monetize as a subscription service at approximately $300/month.

title: Practical Challenges in Building Production RAG Systems
short_summary: Prolego's engineering team discusses the real-world challenges of implementing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems in production, moving beyond simple tutorials to address complex issues like document parsing, chunking strategies, retrieval optimization, and evaluation. The discussion reveals that while RAG appears straightforward in demos, production deployments require careful attention to document structure preservation, context window management, and sophisticated evaluation techniques that go far beyond basic accuracy metrics.

title: Quantitative Framework for Production LLM Evaluation in Security Applications
short_summary: Elastic developed a comprehensive evaluation framework to quantitatively assess and improve their GenAI-powered security features, including AI Assistant and Attack Discovery. The team transitioned from manual, spreadsheet-based testing to an automated framework using LangSmith and LangGraph, enabling systematic prompt tuning, LLM provider comparison, and rubric-based evaluation. The framework incorporates curated test datasets, tracing capabilities, evaluation rubrics with LLM-as-judge patterns, and scoring mechanisms with accuracy thresholds (85%), allowing the team to objectively validate that each improvement genuinely enhances product quality for enterprise users at scale.

title: Email Classification System Using Foundation Models and Prompt Engineering
short_summary: Travelers Insurance processes millions of emails annually containing agent and customer service requests. In collaboration with AWS's Generative AI Innovation Center, they developed an FM-based classifier using Anthropic's Claude models on Amazon Bedrock to categorize emails into 13 service request categories. Through prompt engineering techniques including few-shot prompting, persona definition, and detailed class definitions, the team improved classification accuracy from an initial 68% to 91% without requiring model fine-tuning. The serverless solution processes email text and PDF attachments using Amazon Textract for OCR, enabling automation that can save tens of thousands of hours of manual processing.

title: Large-Scale Learned Retrieval System with Two-Tower Architecture
short_summary: Pinterest faced the challenge of scaling their recommendation system to serve over 500 million monthly active users while moving beyond heuristic-based retrieval approaches. The solution involved building an embedding-based retrieval system using a two-tower machine learning architecture that learns from logged user engagement events. The user tower captures long-term and real-time user preferences, while the item tower generates embeddings for billions of pins. The system leverages approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search via their in-house Manas serving infrastructure, with careful model version synchronization during auto-retraining cycles to prevent embedding space mismatches. The learned retrieval candidate generator now has top user coverage and top three save rates, successfully deprecating two other candidate generators while achieving significant overall site engagement improvements.

title: Scaling LLM-Powered Financial Insights with Continuous Evaluation
short_summary: Fintool, an AI equity research assistant serving institutional investors, faced the challenge of processing over 1.5 billion tokens across 70 million document chunks daily while maintaining the high accuracy standards required in financial contexts. They implemented a comprehensive evaluation workflow using Braintrust that combines automated LLM-as-a-judge scoring, golden dataset benchmarking, rigorous citation validation, and human-in-the-loop oversight. This approach enabled them to scale to millions of LLM-generated insights daily while maintaining trust and reliability, with automated evaluations freeing human reviewers to focus on edge cases and enabling rapid intervention when quality issues arise.

title: Five Critical Lessons for LLM Production Deployment
short_summary: This talk from an experienced LLM practitioner (formerly at Apple, now at LlamaIndex) covers five critical lessons learned from deploying LLM applications in production. The speaker addresses real-world challenges including handling inappropriate user inputs through query classification, understanding model-specific prompt formatting requirements (XML for Anthropic, different formats for Llama versions), recognizing that small implementation changes can break systems (such as embedding text preprocessing), acknowledging the current limitations of function calling accuracy (around 50% even for top models), and emphasizing the importance of inspecting data quality from document parsers before feeding into RAG systems.

title: Implementing Product Comparison and Discovery Features with LLMs at Scale
short_summary: idealo, a European price comparison website with over 4 million products and 500 million offers, developed LLM-powered features to enhance user experience. The team learned that focusing on user needs rather than hype is essential, treating LLMs as language interfaces rather than knowledge databases reduces hallucination risks, and building robust evaluation frameworks is critical for production success. They deployed a product comparison feature that intelligently extracts and highlights relevant attributes from 70+ product specifications, and a guided product finder that uses expert content to generate contextual questions helping users narrow down search results. These features are live in A/B tests measuring business KPIs like conversion rates and bounce rates.

title: Building and Evaluating Production Voice Agents: From Custom Infrastructure to Platform Solutions
short_summary: A team explored building a phone agent system for handling doctor appointments in Polish primary care, initially attempting to build their own infrastructure before evaluating existing platforms. They implemented a complex system involving speech-to-text, LLMs, text-to-speech, and conversation orchestration, along with comprehensive testing approaches. After building the complete system, they ultimately decided to use a third-party platform (Vapi.ai) due to the complexities of maintaining their own infrastructure, while gaining valuable insights into voice agent architecture and testing methodologies.

title: Building and Deploying Production LLM Code Review Agents: Architecture and Best Practices
short_summary: Ellipsis, an AI software engineering tool, developed a sophisticated multi-agent system for automated code review that addresses the common challenge of high false positive rates. Their solution employs multiple specialized "Comment Generator" agents running in parallel to find different types of issues, followed by a filtering pipeline that includes deduplication, hallucination detection, and confidence thresholding. The system leverages a modular Code Search subagent with multi-step RAG combining keyword and vector search, efficient incremental repository indexing, and IDE-like tooling through language server integration. Key to their production success is an extensive evaluation framework using LLM-as-judge patterns, automated trajectory auditing for failure diagnosis, and graceful error handling at multiple levels. While specific quantitative results are not provided, the company claims significant improvements in code review accuracy and developer workflow integration.

title: Scaling LLM Inference to Serve 400M+ Monthly Search Queries
short_summary: Perplexity, an AI-powered search engine handling over 435 million queries monthly, faced the challenge of deploying multiple LLMs cost-effectively while meeting strict latency requirements. The inference team implemented a solution using NVIDIA H100 GPUs, Triton Inference Server, and TensorRT-LLM to serve over 20 AI models simultaneously, including Llama 3.1 variants (8B, 70B, 405B). By leveraging tensor parallelism across multiple GPUs, custom scheduling algorithms, and Kubernetes-based orchestration, they achieved up to 3x cost reduction per million tokens for latency-sensitive requests. The team reports approximately $1 million in annual savings for specific features by self-hosting models rather than using third-party APIs, while maintaining strict SLAs for user experience.

title: Unlocking Patient Population Insights Using Smart Subgroups and LLMs
short_summary: Aetion, a real-world evidence software provider for biopharma and healthcare, developed the Smart Subgroups Interpreter feature to enable natural language querying of patient population clusters. The solution combines unsupervised machine learning for clustering patients based on over 1,000 computed features with Amazon Bedrock and Anthropic's Claude 3 Haiku to generate descriptive cluster names and answer user queries about patient subgroups. Deployed on Kubernetes with data stored in Amazon S3 and Aurora, the system uses composite prompt engineering techniques that incorporate scientific feature descriptions and prevalence statistics. The outcome allows healthcare researchers unfamiliar with real-world data to discover patient population patterns and generate decision-grade evidence in minutes rather than days, without requiring support staff.

title: Building a Production-Grade Email AI Assistant Using RAG and Multi-Stage Retrieval
short_summary: Shortwave built an AI assistant for their email application using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to help users query and interact with their email history. The system uses a modular "tool" architecture where GPT-4 performs tool selection to determine what data sources (calendar, email history, drafts) are needed, followed by parallel data retrieval from multiple backends including vector databases, full-text search, and custom ML models. Their AI Search system combines traditional search with embedding-based semantic search using Pinecone, followed by multi-stage re-ranking using heuristics and cross-encoder models (MS Marco MiniLM) running on their own GPU cluster. The result is an assistant that can answer questions about a user's email history in 3-5 seconds despite the complex multi-step pipeline involving multiple LLM calls, vector lookups, and ML model inference.

title: Building Robust Evaluation Systems for Auto-Generated Video Titles
short_summary: Loom, a video communication platform, developed an AI feature to automatically generate video titles using LLMs. The challenge was establishing reliable quality evaluation for these generated outputs. By implementing a structured four-step process with Braintrust evals—combining custom code-based scorers for objective checks (like emoji presence) and LLM-as-a-judge scorers for subjective qualities (relevance, engagement, clarity)—Loom created a repeatable evaluation system. The result was faster, more confident feature shipping with comprehensive quality assurance at scale.

title: Enterprise GenAI Implementation Strategies Across Industries
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together executives from AstraZeneca, Adobe, and Allianz Technology to share their experiences deploying GenAI and LLMs in production across diverse enterprise contexts. Key challenges addressed include prioritizing use cases, engaging legal stakeholders early, managing cultural transformation, and scaling successful pilots. AstraZeneca's research assistant for literature search achieved viral adoption among scientists, Adobe developed a legal governance framework (A-F elements) for AI enablement, and Allianz Technology implemented Amazon Q for code modernization while building a model-agnostic architecture. Common success factors emerged around iterative development, fast experimentation with clear kill criteria, treating AI adoption as cultural transformation rather than tool rollout, and building flexible architectures that can swap models as technology evolves.

title: AI Agent Automation of Security Operations Center Analysis
short_summary: Doppel, a cybersecurity company focused on social engineering defense, faced the challenge of manually processing over 10 million daily data points (websites, social media accounts, and mobile apps) to identify phishing attacks. While traditional ML filtered obvious false positives, nuanced decisions requiring human judgment remained time-consuming. By deploying an AI agent built on OpenAI's o1 model, trained using the same methods applied to human analysts and incorporating thousands of curated historical decisions, Doppel claims to have automated 30% of their security operations center (SOC) workload within 30 days. The company reports the AI agent achieved lower false-positive rates and uncovered more genuine threats compared to human analysts, resulting in faster response times.

title: Scaling Generative AI in Gaming: From Safety to Creation Tools
short_summary: Roblox, a social 3D platform with 70 million daily active users, has deployed AI and LLMs across multiple production systems including real-time content moderation, code assistance, texture generation, and animation control. The company adopted transformer-based models (initially BERT/DistilBERT) for safety moderation across 40+ languages, developed StarCoder LLMs for code generation in their Luau programming language, and implemented ControlNet for controllable image and material generation. Their AI systems process every user communication in real-time, with the code assist feature having suggested over 300 million characters of code. Roblox maintains a hybrid architecture using both third-party APIs and proprietary backends, allowing them to iterate quickly with weekly releases while optimizing models for their specific use cases.

title: Scaling Financial Software with GenAI and Production ML
short_summary: Ramp, a fintech company valued at $7.6 billion, leverages AI and machine learning across its entire stack to automate corporate expense management, underwriting, fraud detection, and accounting. The company uses traditional ML for receipt matching, fraud prevention, and credit underwriting, while deploying generative AI through their "Ramp Intelligence" suite for price intelligence, expense categorization, and accounting automation. Internally, they've dramatically increased sales productivity through AI-augmented workflows, with SDRs reportedly booking 3-4x more meetings than competitors. Their experimental agentic AI capabilities allow users to interact with the platform through natural language commands that trigger automated actions, though these features remain in alpha testing due to reliability requirements in financial applications.

title: Agent Registry and Dynamic Prompt Management for AI Feature Development
short_summary: GitLab faced a challenge with their AI-powered issue description generation feature where prompts were hardcoded in Ruby classes, meaning any prompt changes required a full GitLab release cycle. This was particularly problematic for self-managed customers who don't update frequently. The solution involved building an Agent Registry within an AI Gateway that abstracts prompts, parameters, and provider configurations into a centralized, dynamically configurable system. This architecture allows GitLab to update prompts, switch between LLM providers (demonstrated with Claude and Vertex/Gemini), and modify agent behavior without touching the main application codebase, enabling rapid delivery of AI improvements to all customers transparently.

title: Building a Systematic LLM Evaluation Framework from Scratch
short_summary: Coda, an all-in-one workspace platform, faced significant challenges when OpenAI released GPT-3.5 Turbo and prompt behaviors changed dramatically, breaking their existing AI features. To address the non-deterministic nature of LLMs and external model changes, they built a systematic evaluation framework that evolved through four phases: from manual OpenAI Playground testing, to using Coda's own platform, to adopting Vellum for prompt iteration, and finally integrating Braintrust for automated evaluation at scale. The journey took them from supporting one feature with 25 benchmark examples and one engineer to over 15 features with 5,000+ data points, 50+ automated checks, and 500+ weekly evaluation runs across five engineers—enabling confident model upgrades and prompt changes in production.

title: Production AI Agents with Dynamic Planning and Reactive Evaluation
short_summary: Hex, a data science notebook platform, successfully deployed AI agents to automate multi-step data analysis workflows. The team overcame common agent failure modes by constraining plan diversity, building a DAG-based reactive agent architecture, aggressively minimizing context window usage for latency optimization, and keeping humans close to agent outputs for course correction. Their approach involved bootstrapping agent capabilities from existing human-facing features, careful prompt engineering via function calling, and building comprehensive evaluation suites with domain-specific assertions rather than generic metrics.

title: Building an AI Agent for Real Estate with Systematic Evaluation Framework
short_summary: Rechat, a real estate technology company, built an AI agent called Lucy for real estate professionals but struggled to move from prototype to production without knowing success rates or detecting regressions. By implementing a systematic evaluation framework including unit tests, assertions, trace logging, human review workflows, synthetic data generation, and eventually LLM-as-a-judge, they were able to rapidly improve their success rates and ultimately required fine-tuning to handle complex use cases like mixing structured and unstructured outputs, user feedback loops, and multi-tool command execution that couldn't be achieved through prompt engineering alone.

title: Comprehensive LLM Evaluation Framework for Production AI Code Assistants
short_summary: GitHub's Copilot team shares their rigorous approach to evaluating AI models before integrating them into their production code assistance tool. The challenge involves assessing multiple foundation models (including those from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google) for performance, quality, and safety. Their solution combines automated testing with over 4,000 offline tests, including containerized repository testing where models must fix deliberately broken code, alongside LLM-as-judge evaluation for chat capabilities. The infrastructure leverages a proxy server architecture enabling rapid model iteration without code changes, with results processed through GitHub Actions, Apache Kafka, and Azure dashboards. This comprehensive evaluation pipeline ensures that only models meeting their quality and responsible AI standards reach production users.

title: AI-Powered Hyper-Personalized Email Marketing System
short_summary: HubSpot's marketing team transformed their first conversion nurturing email flow from cohort-based personalization to true one-to-one personalization using GPT-4 and a vector database. By scraping company websites, analyzing user behavior, and inferring individual "jobs to be done," the LLM generates personalized course recommendations and custom email copy for each lead. The system achieved an 82% increase in conversion rates, approximately 30% improvement in open rates, and over 50% improvement in click-through rates compared to their previous segment-based approach.

title: Evaluation Driven Development for LLM Reliability at Scale
short_summary: Dosu, an AI teammate for software project maintenance, faced the challenge of ensuring reliability when scaling their LLM-powered product from manual log inspection to thousands of repository installations. They adopted Evaluation-Driven Development (EDD) as a methodology to systematically improve LLM performance, treating prompts as code and creating evaluation datasets from production failures. By implementing LangSmith for monitoring and tracing, they gained visibility into Dosu's activity at scale, enabling them to identify failure modes, search production traces by various criteria, and continuously iterate on their models and prompts with confidence that changes wouldn't cause regressions.

title: Optimizing LLM Token Usage with Production Monitoring in Natural Language to SQL System
short_summary: Dataherald, an open-source natural language-to-SQL engine company, faced escalating LLM costs due to inefficient token usage in their production RAG agent built with LangChain. Their manual monitoring approach using TikToken and MongoDB failed to identify a critical bug where their few-shot retriever's token usage grew uncapped over time, reaching approximately 150,000 tokens per query. After implementing LangSmith for production monitoring, they identified the issue within hours and deployed fixes that reduced token usage to approximately 25,500 tokens per query—an 83% cost reduction. The case demonstrates how proper observability tooling is essential for managing LLM applications in production, particularly when using expensive models like GPT-4-32K.

title: Evaluations Driven Development for Production LLM Applications
short_summary: Anaconda developed an Evaluations Driven Development (EDD) methodology to improve their AI coding assistant for data scientists. The problem was that initial LLM-based error handling had very low success rates (0-13%) across different models. Their solution involved creating an in-house "llm-eval" framework for systematic testing, combined with prompt engineering techniques like few-shot learning and chain-of-thought prompting, plus an innovative "Agentic Feedback Iteration" process where LLMs analyze evaluation results to suggest prompt improvements. The results were dramatic: success rates improved to 63-100% across models, with Mistral 7B achieving 100% accuracy at temperature 1, demonstrating that rigorous evaluation-driven prompt optimization can substantially improve LLM reliability without model retraining.

title: Eval-Driven Development for AI Applications
short_summary: Vercel addresses the challenge of testing probabilistic AI systems by introducing "eval-driven development," a methodology that replaces traditional deterministic testing with continuous evaluations. Their flagship product v0, an AI-powered UI generator, uses a multi-faceted evaluation strategy combining code-based grading, human feedback, and LLM-based grading to catch errors early, prevent regressions, and drive continuous improvement. The approach integrates with their "AI-native flywheel" concept, creating a positive feedback loop between evals, data quality, model strategies, and user feedback. While they claim significant improvements in development iteration speed and maintain a 100% pass rate on safety evals, the article acknowledges ongoing challenges in maintaining and scaling the eval suite.

title: Building an AI-Powered Software Development Platform with Multiple LLM Integration
short_summary: Lovable (formerly GPT Engineer) developed an AI-powered platform that enables non-programmers to build full-stack web applications through natural language prompts. The company addressed the challenge of making LLM-based code generation reliable and fast by implementing an opinionated, multi-model architecture that combines OpenAI's smaller models for speed with Anthropic's Claude Sonnet for more complex reasoning. The platform uses intelligent file selection, optimized prompting strategies, and a focus on speed over complex agentic workflows. Results include over 1,000 products built per day, doubling of paying users month-over-month, and commercial products being launched that were built entirely through prompting without writing code.

title: Natural Language Interface to Business Intelligence Using RAG
short_summary: Volvo Car Mobility faced the challenge of data analysts being frequently interrupted by business stakeholders asking ad-hoc questions about operational metrics via Slack. To solve this, an AI engineer built a Slack bot that uses ChatGPT to translate natural language questions into BigQuery SQL queries, returning results directly in Slack. The solution leverages the expanded context window of GPT-4 Turbo (128K tokens) to include the entire database schema and DBT metadata as context, eliminating the need for vector database semantic search. The system is now in production, automating routine data queries and freeing up the data team for higher-value work.

title: Multi-Agent LLM System for Business Process Automation
short_summary: Cognizant developed Neuro AI, a multi-agent LLM-based system that enables business users to create and deploy AI-powered decision-making workflows without requiring deep technical expertise. The platform allows agents to communicate with each other to handle complex business processes, from intranet search to process automation, with the ability to deploy either in the cloud or on-premises. The system includes features for opportunity identification, use case scoping, synthetic data generation, and automated workflow creation, all while maintaining explainability and human oversight.

title: Building a Comprehensive LLM Evaluation Framework with BrainTrust Integration
short_summary: Hostinger's AI team developed a comprehensive LLM evaluation framework to assess and improve their customer support chatbots. The framework addresses three key goals: offline evaluation of changes against predefined datasets during development, continuous assessment of live chatbot performance, and identification of emerging issues to drive iterative improvements. They implemented this using a combination of automated metrics (including factuality and directional accuracy), human review, and user feedback, leveraging the third-party tool Braintrust to orchestrate the evaluation pipeline. The approach enables programmatic evaluation through GitHub Actions, comparison between experiments, and organic growth of golden example datasets across multiple teams.

title: Iterative Development Process for Production AI Features
short_summary: Zapier, a leading workflow automation platform, developed a systematic approach to building production-ready AI products by combining rapid prototyping, user feedback collection, and rigorous evaluation practices. Starting with frontier models like GPT-4 Turbo and Claude Opus for initial validation, the team ships early versions with sub-50% accuracy while mitigating risks through beta labels and opt-in features. By obsessively collecting explicit and implicit user feedback and establishing comprehensive evaluation datasets, Zapier improved many of their AI products from sub-50% accuracy to over 90% within 2-3 months. The process concludes with cost and latency optimization once robust evals are in place to benchmark cheaper model alternatives.

title: Building a Scalable AI Feature Evaluation System
short_summary: Notion, a connected workspace platform, faced challenges with their manual and intensive AI evaluation workflow as they expanded their generative AI features including Q&A, writing assistance, and document generation. Their original process relied on JSONL files stored in git repositories and human evaluators scoring individual responses, which was time-consuming and difficult to scale. By partnering with Braintrust, Notion transformed their evaluation workflow to include curated versioned datasets, custom scoring functions combining heuristics with LLM-as-a-judge approaches, and systematic experiment comparison. The results were significant: the team increased their issue triage and fix rate from 3 per day to 30 per day, enabling faster iteration and higher quality AI features in production.

title: Migrating LLM Fine-tuning Workflows from Slurm to Kubernetes Using Metaflow and Argo
short_summary: Adept.ai, a company building AI agents that can interact with computer interfaces, faced challenges scaling their LLM fine-tuning and training infrastructure. Their original Slurm-based setup had become complex with multiple config files, inconsistent entry points, and difficult onboarding for new team members. The solution involved adopting Metaflow with Argo Workflows on Kubernetes to orchestrate self-serve fine-tuning pipelines, while maintaining backward compatibility with existing Slurm workloads through a hybrid approach. The results include enabling data scientists to launch fine-tuning jobs in a self-serve manner, automated nightly training and evaluation workflows, integrated CI/CD for workflow updates, and infrastructure monitoring—all orchestrated through Metaflow and Argo on Kubernetes.

title: Building a Scalable ML Platform with Metaflow for Distributed LLM Training
short_summary: Autodesk built a unified machine learning platform (AMP) from scratch using Metaflow as the core orchestration tool to enable data scientists to train and fine-tune large language models at scale. The platform integrates with AWS services including SageMaker Studio, AWS Batch, and Step Functions, providing security-hardened infrastructure for distributed training across multiple GPU nodes. The team successfully demonstrated fine-tuning of 3-6 billion parameter models using DeepSpeed, Ray Train, and PyTorch Lightning, with benchmarks showing efficient scaling across 16 A10 GPUs. Key achievements include a custom Ray parallel decorator for Metaflow, GitOps-based production deployment workflows, and integration of high-performance computing features like Elastic Fabric Adapter and FSx for Lustre for improved inter-node communication and data access.

title: Building Production LLM Pipelines for Insurance Risk Assessment and Document Processing
short_summary: Vouch Insurance, a provider of business insurance for technology startups, built LLM-powered pipelines using Metaflow for risk classification and document AI processing. The solution integrates OpenAI APIs via LangChain, runs on AWS Batch infrastructure, and serves predictions through a FastAPI instance with a custom SDK for product engineers. The pipelines handle structured, semi-structured, and document data (primarily PDFs), running hourly for risk classification and on-demand for document processing, with careful cost management through prediction caching and token management.

title: Evolving ML Infrastructure for Production Systems: From Traditional ML to LLMs
short_summary: This fireside chat features Faras Hammad, an ML leader at Doordash with experience at Netflix, Meta, Uber, and Yahoo, discussing the integration of LLMs into production ML systems. The discussion covers how companies should approach LLM adoption with realistic expectations about error rates, the coexistence of LLMs with traditional ML models, and the significant infrastructure changes required to support generative AI workloads. Key insights include using LLMs for low-risk use cases like product labeling while maintaining guard rails, leveraging traditional models as validation layers for LLM outputs, and designing flexible infrastructure that can adapt to rapidly evolving AI capabilities.

title: Evolution of ML Model Deployment Infrastructure at Scale
short_summary: Faire's ML Platform team evolved their model serving infrastructure over two years, moving from a fragmented manual process requiring multiple PRs and 3+ days for deployment to a unified internal tool called "mmm" (Machine Learning Model Management). The original system embedded ML models directly in a backend monolith, creating bottlenecks around varying workloads, library versioning, and slow deployment cycles. By adopting Amazon SageMaker for real-time inference and Comet for experiment tracking, then building a custom UI-based management layer on top, they reduced deployment time from days to approximately 4 hours (with only 10 minutes of human effort), enabled zero-code deployments, implemented automated testing and shadow rollouts, and achieved comprehensive observability across their ML stack—including support for deploying LLMs and large vision models.

title: Human-AI Co-Annotation System for Efficient Data Labeling
short_summary: Appen addressed the growing challenge of data annotation quality and cost for generative AI projects by developing a human-AI co-annotation strategy. The solution combines LLM-powered pre-annotations with human review, using model uncertainty (entropy) as a routing mechanism to determine when human intervention is needed. In a case study for a leading US electronics company, this approach improved annotation accuracy by 3-4 percentage points across task components, achieving up to 94% accuracy (up from 90% without AI assistance), while reducing annotation time by 63% and costs by 62%. The system used GPT-4o multimodal capabilities to analyze search queries, product titles, and images, with the notable finding that human accuracy remained unaffected even when LLM predictions were incorrect.

title: MLOps Platform for Airline Operations with LLM Integration
short_summary: LATAM Airlines, South America's largest airline, developed an in-house MLOps framework called Cosmos to standardize ML development and deployment across their organization. The platform reduced model development-to-production time from 3-4 months to under a week, enabling use cases including fuel optimization (saving millions of dollars and 4 kilotons of CO2 annually), personalized web recommendations using LLM-generated destination features combined with traditional ML, and inventory forecasting with approximately 60,000 models. The framework integrates traditional machine learning with generative AI capabilities while maintaining vendor independence through custom wrappers around GCP services.

title: Evolution of ML Platform to Support GenAI Infrastructure
short_summary: Lyft faced the challenge of integrating LLM capabilities into their existing ML platform, which already supported over 1,000 unique models across 50+ engineering teams. Their solution involved evolving their unified model serving infrastructure to accommodate LLM API proxies, building custom client libraries that route traffic through centralized infrastructure, and developing a lightweight evaluation framework for online and offline analysis. The results include standardized LLM access across the company with full observability, PII filtering capabilities, quality evaluations using LLM-as-judge patterns, and production use cases including RAG-based customer support that provides faster first response times and better agent context.

title: From Pilot to Profit: Three Enterprise GenAI Case Studies in Manufacturing, Aviation, and Telecommunications
short_summary: This presentation covers three enterprise GenAI implementations across automotive manufacturing, in-flight entertainment, and telecommunications, exploring the journey from pilot to profitability. The speaker identifies three critical "hidden levers" for success: adoption triggers (getting expert buy-in and integrating with existing workflows), lean workflows (using GenAI only where necessary and combining with classical AI), and revenue accelerators (capturing sales, enabling upsells, and dynamic discounting). Each case study illustrates different challenges—from pilot paralysis caused by theoretical vs. practical knowledge gaps, to token cost bloat from processing excessive log data, to inadvertently educating customers who then bought from competitors. The cases demonstrate realistic ROI timelines of 14-24 months and initial investment ranges of $200K-$1M, challenging optimistic industry predictions of sub-12-month returns.

title: Automated Product Classification and Attribute Extraction Using Vision LLMs
