short_summary: Shopify faced the challenge of extracting structured product information (categories, attributes like color, size, material) from unstructured merchant product listings to support critical business functions like tax calculation, search, and recommendations. They developed a two-step vision LLM pipeline that first predicts product categories, then extracts relevant attributes based on that category. To manage costs at scale (tens of millions of predictions daily), they fine-tuned smaller models using synthetic golden datasets generated through multi-LLM agreement (GPT, Claude, Gemini) and human validation. The system now serves both real-time merchant-facing predictions and high-throughput batch processing, with merchants providing feedback that feeds into continuous model improvement.

title: Optimizing LLM Training with Efficient GPU Kernels
short_summary: LinkedIn developed Liger Kernels, a set of custom GPU primitives written in Triton, to address memory consumption bottlenecks in LLM training. The problem was that standard kernel implementations caused excessive memory transfers between GPU HBM and compute units, leaving expensive GPU resources idle. By rewriting fundamental operations like RMSNorm, LayerNorm, RoPE, and fused linear cross-entropy, LinkedIn achieved up to 3x reduction in peak memory allocation and 20% throughput improvements for large batch sizes. The kernels are open-sourced on GitHub and have been ported to AMD GPUs, enabling more efficient training of models powering LinkedIn's various AI features including profile summaries, learning platform enhancements, and recruiter messaging tools.

title: Comprehensive Debugging and Observability Framework for Production Agent AI Systems
short_summary: This presentation by Valohai's CEO introduces a rubric for assessing agentic AI and MLOps maturity in production environments. The problem addressed is the significant productivity plateau organizations face when scaling AI/ML operations—where adding more resources doesn't yield expected returns due to excessive time spent on debugging, maintenance, onboarding, and troubleshooting multi-agent systems. The proposed solution is a comprehensive checklist covering environment reproducibility, system logs, model versioning, prompt tracking, RAG lineage, and fine-tuning pipelines. While no specific results are shared, the framework aims to reduce the 3-4 weeks organizations typically spend identifying issues in complex agentic AI systems.

title: Incremental LLM Adoption Strategy in Email Processing API Platform
short_summary: Nylas, an API provider for email, calendar, and contact data, implemented a three-month phased strategy to integrate generative AI into their Extract AI product. They developed a multi-agent system for automating development tasks (opening 200+ PRs, merging ~50), replaced their blind annotation system with GPT-4 (achieving 20x cost savings and 60x speed improvement), and implemented an LLM fallback strategy for email processing that reduced bug tickets by over 90%. The team also built self-hosting infrastructure using Llama CPP on GCP with L4 GPUs, calculating break-even points for API costs versus self-hosted solutions at around 10,000 API calls per month.

title: Enterprise-Wide LLM Framework for Manufacturing and Knowledge Management
short_summary: Toyota's Enterprise AI team developed a comprehensive agentic RAG framework to address multiple manufacturing and knowledge management challenges. The solution tackles complex data ingestion from diverse document formats (PDFs, videos, Excel, OneNote with nested tables and images), implements hybrid search with multilingual support, and includes a Prompt Guardian security layer. Key applications include Battery Brain for reducing scrappage rates at a new battery manufacturing plant, Gear Pal for minimizing manufacturing line downtime (projected seven-figure savings per quarter), and Project Cura for enterprise knowledge capture and retrieval. The framework combines LangChain and LlamaIndex capabilities with custom components, golden query evaluation sets, and LLM-as-judge testing to ensure quality in production deployments.

title: Converting Natural Language to Structured GraphQL Queries Using LLMs
short_summary: Cato Networks, a secure access service edge (SASE) provider, faced the challenge of making their event management console more accessible to users unfamiliar with product-specific terminology. Their Events page required manual filter configuration using a complex query syntax, which was time-consuming and required deep product knowledge. They implemented a natural language search capability using Amazon Bedrock's foundation models (specifically Claude 3.5 Sonnet) to convert free text queries into structured JSON that could be validated against a schema and transformed into GraphQL API requests. The solution employed prompt engineering with detailed JSON schema instructions, enabling schema-based validation of model outputs. Results included significantly reduced query time (from minutes to near-instant), positive customer feedback, multi-language support, and near-zero time to value for users, with the system maintaining an error rate below 0.05.

title: Healthcare Conversational AI and Multi-Model Cost Management in Production
short_summary: This panel discussion explores LLMOps challenges across healthcare conversational AI (Interactly.ai) and enterprise cost tracking (Amberflo), alongside perspectives from Inflection AI, Google Vertex AI, and Databricks. Key topics include model selection trade-offs between accuracy and latency, the importance of custom evaluation benchmarks over public benchmarks, multi-model architectures for cost optimization, usage-based billing for LLM applications, ethical AI deployment with safety filters, and the emerging pattern of compound AI systems. The discussion highlights practical approaches to deploying LLMs in production, including using GPT-4 for evaluation and synthetic data generation while using smaller models for latency-sensitive inference, implementing proper metering and observability for multi-model deployments, and fine-tuning models for specific cultural and organizational contexts.

title: Building Production-Ready AI Agents and Monitoring Systems
short_summary: This panel discussion at Airbyte's headquarters brought together practitioners from Portkey, Airbyte, and Comet to discuss the challenges of putting LLMs into production. Key topics covered included the importance of monitoring and observability for AI systems, the challenges of logging LLM outputs without incurring excessive costs, the need for forward compatibility as models rapidly evolve, the role of AI gateways in handling failures and implementing guard rails, and the critical importance of data quality over model sophistication. The panelists shared practical experiences including building auto-generating data connectors from documentation, implementing vision models for document processing at scale, and the need for proper evaluation frameworks before production deployment.

title: Optimizing GPU Memory Usage in LLM Training with Liger-Kernel
short_summary: LinkedIn faced significant resource bottlenecks during LLM training, including heavy GPU memory access and excessive per-operation overhead, which slowed training for features like job matching and content recommendations. To address these challenges, they developed Liger-Kernel, an open-source Python library built on Triton that leverages FlashAttention and operator fusion techniques to optimize GPU performance. The solution merges operations that previously required multiple GPUs to run on single GPUs and computes attention scores more efficiently in SRAM. The reported results include a 60% reduction in GPU memory usage, 20% improvement in multi-GPU training throughput, and 3x reduction in end-to-end training time.

title: Integrating LLMs and Diffusion Models for Website Design Automation
short_summary: Wix developed a Diffusion Layout Transformer (DLT) to automate the creation of custom website layouts, addressing the challenge that designing professional-looking layouts requires significant design expertise and time. The solution combines a joint discrete-continuous diffusion process with a Transformer encoder architecture that allows flexible conditioning on component attributes like position, size, and category. Presented at ICCV 2023, the DLT framework outperformed existing solutions on layout synthesis and editing tasks across multiple benchmark datasets including PubLayNet, RICO, and Magazine, while maintaining comparable computational complexity to previous approaches.

title: Domain Adaptation of LLMs for Enterprise Use Through Multi-Task Fine-Tuning
short_summary: Wix faced limitations with standard LLM customization techniques (prompt engineering, RAG, task-specific fine-tuning) for their customer service domain, experiencing high costs, latency, and hallucination issues. They implemented a comprehensive domain adaptation approach combining multi-task supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with adapters and domain adaptation using full weights fine-tuning (DAPT). This required extensive custom data collection, synthetic data generation, custom evaluation benchmarks including an LLM-as-a-judge approach, and training on AWS P5 GPU infrastructure with LLaMA2 7B. Their resulting smaller, customized LLM outperformed GPT-3.5 on Wix-specific tasks including intent classification, sentiment analysis, customer segmentation, and question answering.

title: Dynamic Knowledge and Instruction RAG System for Production Chatbots
short_summary: Wix developed an AI Site-Chat system to help website visitors interact with sites more effectively while allowing site owners to customize chatbot responses through feedback. The solution addresses the challenge that traditional chatbots struggle to adapt to business-specific preferences and "unwritten knowledge." Wix implemented two key technical innovations: a hybrid LLM-ML framework that uses LLMs for feature extraction through yes/no questions combined with CatBoost classifiers for text classification, and a Dynamic Domain Knowledge and Instruction RAG (DDKI-RAG) system that dynamically updates knowledge bases and system prompts based on owner feedback. This approach enables real-time learning and adaptability, producing more accurate and context-aware chatbot responses while avoiding the limitations of static RAG systems.

title: Automated Search Quality Evaluation Using LLMs for Typeahead Suggestions
short_summary: LinkedIn faced challenges scaling human-based quality evaluation for their typeahead search suggestions serving over 1 billion members. They developed a GenAI Typeahead Quality Evaluator using OpenAI's GPT model (served through Azure) to automate the assessment of search suggestion quality. The solution involved creating comprehensive quality measurement guidelines, building a golden test set from platform traffic, and developing specialized prompt engineering templates for different suggestion types. The automated system reduced evaluation time from days or weeks to just hours while achieving measurable quality improvements, with one experiment showing a 6.8% absolute improvement in typeahead quality scores and a 20% reduction in low-quality suggestions.

title: Domain-Adapted Foundation Models for Enterprise-Scale LLM Deployment
short_summary: LinkedIn faced challenges with latency, cost, and domain-specific performance when using proprietary LLMs like GPT-4 for their 1B+ member platform. They developed EON (Economic Opportunity Network) models—domain-adapted foundation models built on open-source architectures like Llama—using multi-task instruction tuning with reasoning traces, preference alignment via RLHF and DPO, and integration with their Economic Graph data. The EON-8B model achieved 75x cost efficiency compared to GPT-4, while the domain-adapted model powering their Hiring Assistant's evaluation agent improved candidate-job-requirements matching accuracy by 4% over GPT-4o mini and 30% over Llama-3-8B-instruct, demonstrating that targeted domain adaptation can outperform larger proprietary models on specialized tasks.

title: Optimizing LLM Training with Triton Kernels and Infrastructure Stack
short_summary: LinkedIn developed and open-sourced Liger-Kernel to address GPU memory and throughput bottlenecks in LLM training. The library provides optimized Triton kernels that can be integrated with a single line of code, achieving up to 20% improvement in training throughput and 60% reduction in memory usage for popular models like Llama, Gemma, and Qwen. At LinkedIn's internal production scale, the team observed a 3X reduction in end-to-end training time for a ~70B parameter model and 10-20% throughput gains for models at ~100B and ~10B scales. The library has been widely adopted, with 3,000+ GitHub stars and 200k+ downloads since its August 2024 release, and integrates with major training frameworks including HuggingFace, Axolotl, and DeepSpeed.

title: Multi-Track Approach to Developer Productivity Using LLMs
short_summary: eBay tackled the challenge of enhancing developer productivity by implementing a three-track approach to generative AI: deploying GitHub Copilot as a commercial offering, fine-tuning Code Llama 13B on their internal codebase (creating "eBayCoder"), and building an internal RAG-based GPT for knowledge retrieval. Their controlled A/B test of Copilot with 300 developers showed a 27% code acceptance rate, 17% decrease in PR merge time, and 12% decrease in Lead Time for Change. The fine-tuned LLM addressed large-scale code migration tasks and reduced code duplication, while the internal knowledge base GPT helped developers quickly find answers to organizational questions that previously required multiple meetings to resolve.

title: Developing and Deploying Domain-Adapted LLMs for E-commerce Through Continued Pre-training
short_summary: eBay faced the challenge of needing domain-specific LLMs that could handle e-commerce tasks at scale while maintaining cost-effectiveness and data security, which third-party models like GPT-4 could not provide. The solution involved continued pretraining of Meta's Llama 3.1 models (8B and 70B parameters) on a balanced mixture of e-commerce and general domain data to create "e-Llama" models. Training utilized 480 NVIDIA H100 GPUs with Megatron-LM for 3D parallelism, processing 1 trillion tokens. The resulting models demonstrated approximately 25% improvement on English e-commerce benchmarks and 30% improvement on non-English benchmarks, with only 1% degradation on general domain tasks, enabling eBay to leverage AI across the company more efficiently.

title: Using RAG to Improve Industry Classification Accuracy
short_summary: Ramp, a corporate finance and expense management company, has developed multiple LLM-powered production systems spanning agentic data analysis, merchant matching, expense approval automation, industry classification via RAG, and MCP server integration. Their solutions address diverse problems including answering over 1,000 data questions monthly via an AI agent, resolving merchant matching issues in under 10 seconds using smart RAG and LLMs, automating expense approvals with trustworthy agents, and building infrastructure to allow LLMs to interact with company resources through an MCP server.

title: Building a Unified Data Platform with Gen AI and ODL Integration
short_summary: This case study from TCS and MongoDB presents an architectural approach for modernizing enterprise data platforms to support generative AI workloads. The problem addressed is that organizations struggle with fragmented legacy systems that deliver stale, batch-processed data, hindering real-time decision-making and AI adoption. The proposed solution combines Operational Data Layers (ODLs) with MongoDB as the operational database, integrating vector search and generative AI capabilities through Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) patterns. The architecture enables real-time data access, enhanced customer interactions, automated compliance reporting, and AI-enriched applications. While presented as a conceptual framework rather than a specific deployment case study, the approach claims to deliver benefits including improved operational efficiency, personalized customer experiences, and the ability to rapidly develop AI-driven applications across industries like telecommunications, banking, and healthcare.

title: Multi-Agent Financial Analysis System for Equity Research
short_summary: Captide addresses the challenge of inefficient financial analysis workflows by building an NLP-powered platform that automates the extraction of insights from regulatory filings and investor relations documents. Using LangGraph for agentic workflows with parallel processing and structured outputs, and LangSmith for real-time monitoring and feedback collection, they deployed production-ready agents on LangGraph Platform. The solution allows investment analysts to define complex analysis tasks in natural language, with agents orchestrating document retrieval and processing pipelines, reportedly compressing research that previously took days into seconds while maintaining the precision required for financial industry standards.

title: Multi-Agent Customer Support System for E-commerce
short_summary: Minimal, a Dutch e-commerce support automation startup, built a multi-agent customer support system using LangGraph and LangSmith to handle customer service tickets autonomously. The system addresses the challenge of efficiently resolving both basic and complex support issues (T1-T3) by splitting tasks across specialized agents—a Planner Agent, Research Agents, and a Tool-Calling Agent—that work together to generate responses and execute actions like order cancellations and refunds. The company reports 80%+ efficiency gains and expects 90% of tickets to be handled autonomously with only 10% escalated to humans, though these figures should be viewed with appropriate skepticism given the promotional nature of the source.

title: Automated Carrier Claims Management Using AI Agents
short_summary: FIEGE, a major German logistics provider with 22,000 employees and €2 billion turnover, deployed an AI agent in September 2024 to handle carrier claims management from end to end. The system processes customer emails, communicates with carriers, checks contractual obligations, and resolves claims with 70-90% full automation. By sandboxing generative AI within deterministic workflows and using templates rather than free-form generation, the solution avoids hallucination issues while processing claims in under 60 seconds. The implementation resulted in eight-digit revenue improvements from increased refund recovery, demonstrating practical enterprise AI agent deployment.

title: Mission-Critical LLM Inference Platform Architecture
short_summary: Baseten, an LLM inference platform, discusses the challenges and solutions for running mission-critical inference workloads in production. The case study focuses on their deployment of DeepSeek V3 (a 671 billion parameter MoE model), integration with SGLang as a serving framework, and the three pillars required for production LLM serving: model-level performance optimization, horizontal scaling infrastructure, and developer experience for multi-model workflows. They highlight how they serve customers with strict latency requirements (including AI phone call applications requiring sub-400ms response times), custom model deployments, and multi-cloud scaling capabilities.

title: Lessons from Red Teaming 100+ Generative AI Products
short_summary: Microsoft's AI Red Team (AIRT) shares comprehensive lessons learned from red teaming over 100 generative AI products since 2018, addressing both security vulnerabilities and responsible AI harms. The team developed a threat model ontology covering actors, TTPs, weaknesses, and impacts, and created PyRIT, an open-source Python framework for automated AI red teaming. Key findings include that simple attacks often outperform gradient-based methods, the importance of system-level rather than model-only testing, the need for human expertise in assessing novel harms, and that AI security requires continuous improvement rather than one-time solutions. The work demonstrates that effective AI red teaming requires combining automation with human judgment, considering both adversarial and benign user scenarios, and understanding that securing AI systems is an ongoing process rather than a solvable problem.

title: Building and Managing Production Agents with Testing and Evaluation Infrastructure
short_summary: Nearpod, a K-12 EdTech company, built a multi-agent system to automate question generation for teachers, reducing development time from months to hours. The team developed specialized agents for input validation, question generation, and orchestration, supported by a custom evaluation framework with thousands of test cases achieving 98-100% accuracy. By leveraging a data platform foundation with DBT and Redshift, they created an agent registry enabling cross-departmental collaboration and cost-optimized deployments using cheaper models while maintaining quality through prompt engineering and token optimization.

title: Multi-Agent GenAI System for Developer Support and Documentation
short_summary: Northwestern Mutual faced challenges with their internal developer support system, including long response times (especially during weekends and holidays), repetitive basic questions that already had documentation, and requests for automatable tasks like unlocking user accounts. They built a multi-agent AI support bot using Amazon Bedrock, moving from experimentation to production in approximately three months (June to September 2024). The solution uses multiple specialized agents for documentation, user management, repository management, pipeline failure analysis, and response evaluation. Key results include answering support requests within minutes without engineer engagement, freeing support engineers to focus on complex issues, and establishing a foundation for more complex business-facing applications in their regulated financial services environment.

title: Building and Orchestrating Multi-Agent Systems at Scale with CrewAI
short_summary: CrewAI developed a production-ready framework for building and orchestrating multi-AI agent automations, processing over 10 million agent executions monthly. The company used its own framework to automate internal operations including marketing content creation, lead qualification, and code documentation. The solution addresses the complexity of deploying AI agents at scale by providing shared memory, caching layers, guardrails, and tool integration, while also offering an enterprise platform (CrewAI Plus) that converts local agent crews into production-ready APIs with autoscaling and private VPC capabilities.

title: Production Evolution of an AI-Powered Medical Consultation Assistant
short_summary: Doctolib developed an AI-powered Consultation Assistant to help healthcare professionals by converting speech to text, summarizing medical consultations, and mapping content to medical ontologies like ICD-10. The team addressed the classic "chicken and egg" problem of needing user feedback to improve AI while requiring functional AI to generate engagement by creating simulated consultations with fake patient personas. They implemented a comprehensive feedback collection system combining explicit ratings and implicit usage signals, used LLM-as-judge for automated quality evaluation, and established A/B testing as the gold standard for validating changes. The solution employed dual improvement loops: a short-term prompt engineering cycle (days to weeks) and a long-term model fine-tuning cycle (weeks to months). The product launched to widespread adoption and positive feedback after over a year of continuous improvement with beta testers and medical experts.

title: Unified Healthcare Data Platform with LLMOps Integration
short_summary: Doctolib, a European healthcare technology company, outlines their architectural transformation from a monolithic data platform to a unified healthcare data platform designed to support AI and ML use cases at scale. The company addresses limitations of their centralized approach—including complex CI pipelines, shared permissions, and inflexible orchestration—by designing a modular architecture that incorporates dedicated LLMOps tooling, vector databases, model serving infrastructure, and a GenAI assistant for natural language data exploration. While primarily an architectural blueprint rather than a post-implementation case study, the plan demonstrates how healthcare organizations can structure their platforms to operationalize LLMs in production with proper governance, security, and team ownership boundaries.

title: Implementing Multi-Agent RAG Architecture for Customer Care Automation
short_summary: Doctolib, a healthcare technology company, evolved their customer care system from a basic RAG implementation to a sophisticated multi-agent architecture using LangGraph. The solution addresses limitations of traditional RAG by implementing specialized LLM agents that can handle complex multi-step reasoning, execute API calls, and perform back-end actions on behalf of users. While the system shows promise for automating customer support tasks (such as granting agenda access permissions), the team acknowledges ongoing challenges with agent behavior variance, prompt size limitations, and the need for robust evaluation frameworks before achieving production-ready deployment.

title: Implementing RAG for Enhanced Customer Care at Scale
short_summary: Doctolib, a leading European e-health company, implemented a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to improve their customer care services. The team built a production pipeline using GPT-4o hosted on Azure OpenAI, OpenSearch as a vector database, and implemented re-ranking along with a dedicated evaluation framework using Ragas metrics. After extensive optimization including latency reduction from 1 minute to under 5 seconds, prompt engineering, and the development of an ML classifier to predict answerable queries, the system achieved a 20% reduction in customer care case deflection, allowing agents to focus on more complex cases. The team acknowledges limitations with complex queries and is exploring agentic architectures for future improvements.

title: Implementing LLM Fallback Mechanisms for Production Incident Response System
short_summary: The source content from Vespper regarding LLM fallback mechanisms is no longer available (404 error). Based on the URL title alone, this case study appears to have addressed implementing fallback mechanisms for LLM systems in production, a critical LLMOps pattern for ensuring reliability when primary LLM services fail or become unavailable. Without access to the actual content, no specific details about the problem, solution, or results can be verified.

title: Building State-of-the-Art AI Programming Agents with OpenAI's o1 Model
short_summary: Weights & Biases developed an autonomous AI programming agent using OpenAI's o1 model that achieved state-of-the-art results on SWE-Bench-Verified, resolving 64.6% of software engineering issues. The solution combined o1 with a GPT-4o memory component, custom code editing tools, auto-command capabilities, parallel rollouts with cross-check selection, and was developed using extensive experimentation tracked through W&B's Weave toolkit. The team ran 977 evaluations over two months to refine the agent, discovering key insights about prompt engineering for o1 and developing new tooling including "Eval Studio" and "Phaseshift" for agent composition.

Zillow investigated whether real estate listing descriptions could function as proxies for protected classes (specifically race) by analyzing semantic differences in listings from neighborhoods with different racial demographics. Using a combination of text statistics, key phrase analysis, and LDA topic modeling enhanced by LLM-generated topic labels, the team discovered significant disparities: listings in majority non-Hispanic white areas emphasized luxury features and upscale amenities, while listings in majority Black areas disproportionately featured investment opportunities, auctions, and renovation themes. This analysis demonstrates how AI can be used to understand potential bias in unstructured data before it is incorporated into production ML systems.

title: LLM Observability for Enhanced Audience Segmentation Systems
short_summary: Acxiom, a global leader in customer intelligence and data-driven marketing, faced significant challenges scaling their LLM-based audience segmentation application. Their initial lightweight logging system couldn't handle the growing user base, and complex debugging of multi-step LLM reasoning chains proved difficult. By adopting LangSmith as their observability platform, they gained visibility into nested LLM calls involving up to 60 calls and 200k tokens per interaction. The solution integrated seamlessly with their existing LangChain-based RAG architecture and hybrid model ecosystem (including vLLM, Claude via AWS Bedrock, and Databricks endpoints), enabling streamlined debugging, improved audience reach through more accurate segment creation, scalable growth without re-engineering the observability layer, and optimized token usage for cost management.

title: Intelligent Document Processing for Education Quality Assessment Reports
short_summary: The Education and Training Quality Authority (BQA) in Bahrain faced challenges with manual review of self-evaluation reports from educational institutions, including incomplete submissions, missing evidence, and time-consuming verification processes. Working with AWS through the Cloud Innovation Center program, BQA developed a proof of concept solution using Amazon Bedrock with the Titan Express model and SageMaker JumpStart with Meta Llama for intelligent document processing. The system automates text extraction via Amazon Textract, summarizes lengthy submissions, and evaluates institutional evidence against quality standards using carefully engineered prompts. Anticipated results include 70% accurate standards-compliant report generation, 30% reduction in evidence analysis time, and 30% reduced operational costs, though these metrics remain projections from the proof of concept stage.

title: Semantic Caching for E-commerce Search Optimization
short_summary: Walmart implemented semantic caching to enhance their e-commerce search functions, addressing the limitations of traditional exact-match caching when handling the nuances of natural language queries. By leveraging embeddings and vector search to understand query intent rather than requiring exact matches, Walmart achieved a cache hit rate of approximately 50% for tail queries—significantly exceeding their initial expectations of 10-20%. The solution also improved search relevance by enabling generative AI to understand customer intent (e.g., "football watch party" returning snacks, party drinks, apparel, and TVs), though the implementation required balancing performance trade-offs related to latency and the increased computational costs of vector-based caching.

title: Federal Government AI Platform Adoption and Scalability Initiatives
short_summary: This panel discussion explores the challenges and strategies U.S. federal government agencies face when transitioning AI applications from pilot testing to full-scale production. Key challenges include budget cycle misalignment, scaling access across organizations, cybersecurity compliance, and data governance at different classification levels. Solutions discussed include leveraging White House policy frameworks as implementation roadmaps, establishing Chief AI Officers and governance councils, building auditability into platforms systematically, and reusing foundation models across multiple use cases. Practical success stories mentioned include the Department of Energy's "Energy GPT" chatbot, NEPA policy document analysis, OPM's COBOL code modernization using LLMs, State Department's diplomatic cable summarization, and the Navy's Project AMMO which reduced model retraining time from six months to one week using Domino Data Lab's MLOps platform.

title: Production LLM Systems at Scale - Lessons from Financial Services, Legal Tech, and ML Infrastructure
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together ML engineering leaders from Nubank, Harvey AI, Galileo, and Convirza to share practical experiences productionizing LLMs. Key themes include the shift from experimentation to production-grade systems in 2024, the strategic use of small language models (SLMs) for cost and latency optimization, modular system architecture for complex workflows, evaluation challenges at scale, and the importance of human-in-the-loop feedback mechanisms. The panelists discuss how they approach model selection based on quality, throughput, latency, and cost trade-offs, with multiple organizations reporting success in replacing or augmenting large proprietary models with fine-tuned smaller models that match or exceed performance for narrow tasks.

title: Building and Scaling Production-Ready AI Agents: Lessons from Agent Force
short_summary: Salesforce shares lessons learned from building their AgentForce platform, highlighting the challenges of moving LLM-based applications from initial demos (60% accuracy) to production-ready systems (80-90% accuracy). The solution involves implementing robust evaluation frameworks, automated batch testing, RAG pipeline monitoring, and strategic fine-tuning of smaller language models to balance speed, accuracy, and cost. Key outcomes include faster iteration cycles (30-minute test feedback loops), improved brand voice alignment, and reduced cost-to-serve through fine-tuned smaller models rather than large base models.

title: Optimizing Call Center Analytics with Small Language Models and Multi-Adapter Serving
short_summary: Convirza, a company specializing in phone conversation analytics, faced challenges scaling their AI infrastructure to handle millions of monthly calls while extracting hundreds of custom data points ("indicators"). Their legacy approach using separately deployed models for each indicator was costly and complex. By transitioning from OpenAI GPT models and custom Longformer models to fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B with LoRA adapters served via Predibase, they achieved 10x cost reduction compared to OpenAI, 8% higher F1 scores, 80% higher throughput, and sub-0.1 second inference times—enabling near real-time insights at scale with the ability to run 60+ adapters on a single GPU.

title: Enterprise-Wide LLM Assistant Deployment and Evolution Towards Fine-Tuned Models
short_summary: Marsh McLennan, a global professional services firm with 90,000 employees, deployed an LLM-based assistant across their entire organization starting in 2023, processing approximately 25 million requests per year. Their approach prioritized making experimentation cheap by renting models by the call rather than hosting infrastructure themselves. After initial skepticism about fine-tuning due to cost and operational complexity concerns, they adopted a LoRA-based approach (via Predibase) that dramatically changed the economics, enabling them to run training cycles for approximately $20 and achieve accuracy exceeding GPT-4. The organization reports conservatively saving over one million hours annually, with plans to expand from productivity augmentation to process automation through specialized fine-tuned models in 2025.

title: Enterprise-Wide RAG Implementation with Amazon Q Business
short_summary: Principal Financial, a 145-year-old financial services company, implemented Amazon Q Business as an enterprise AI assistant to address fragmented knowledge management across over 9,000 pages of work instructions. Their team of 300+ employees processing 680,000+ annual customer cases faced a 1.5-year training period due to scattered documentation across legacy systems. By integrating Amazon Q Business with QnABot on AWS and implementing custom metadata enrichment via Amazon Bedrock, they achieved 84% document retrieval accuracy (up from 67% baseline), with 97% of user queries receiving positive or neutral feedback. The solution reduced some workloads by 50% while maintaining a human-in-the-loop approach for customer interactions.

title: Observability Platform's Journey to Production GenAI Integration
short_summary: New Relic, processing seven petabytes of observability data daily, implemented generative AI both internally to improve developer productivity and externally within their product platform. Internally, they achieved approximately 15% productivity gains across engineering levels through AI-assisted code reviews, test generation, and code refactoring. They built a multi-agent architecture for workflow automation, incident management with automated RCA generation, and cloud cost optimization that saved $4-5 million annually through intelligent convertible RI management. On the product side, they integrated AI monitoring capabilities, natural language query translation for their NRQL database language, automated alert optimization, and change tracking—all while maintaining a balanced approach between classical machine learning for forecasting and generative AI for appropriate use cases.

title: GenAI Transformation of Manufacturing and Supply Chain Operations
short_summary: Jabil, a $29 billion contract manufacturing company with 140,000 employees across 100 locations in 35 countries, deployed Amazon Q Business to create intelligent assistants across their manufacturing shop floors and supply chain operations. The company implemented three key use cases: "Ask Me How" for manufacturing floor assistance with multilingual support, a Procurement Intelligence Platform (PIP) for commodity insights, and V-Command for supply chain services. These solutions help operators quickly resolve equipment errors, provide procurement teams with market intelligence for buying decisions, and enable supply chain practitioners to identify risks and optimize logistics. Early results show reduced downtime on manufacturing floors, faster sales cycles for supply chain services, and improved decision-making through consolidated internal and external data insights.

title: Automated Email Triage System Using Amazon Bedrock Flows
short_summary: Parameta, a data solutions provider for the financial services industry, faced challenges managing thousands of client service requests via email, with a manual process involving reading emails, understanding technical issues, gathering data, routing requests, and verifying information. They implemented an automated email triage system using Amazon Bedrock Flows that orchestrates a sequence of specialized LLM prompts for classification, entity extraction, and validation, combined with an Amazon Bedrock agent that queries both a knowledge base and enterprise databases (Snowflake/Athena) to generate contextual responses. The solution reduced resolution times from weeks to days while maintaining high accuracy, was developed in just two weeks, and enabled non-technical team members to understand and adjust the response process.

title: AI-Powered Client Services Assistant for Post-Trade Services
short_summary: London Stock Exchange Group's LCH division faced challenges with their client services team needing to quickly retrieve accurate information from complex documentation to answer member queries about post-trade products and services. They implemented Amazon Q Business with RAG capabilities to create a conversational AI assistant that indexes internal documents, FAQs, CRM data, and public rulebooks. The solution includes a custom validation system using Anthropic's Claude v2 to verify response accuracy against a "golden answers" benchmark. Results demonstrated high factual accuracy with responses delivered within seconds, reducing the time agents spend on each query while improving customer experience in a regulated financial services environment.

title: Field AI Assistant for Sales Team Automation
short_summary: Databricks developed an internal "Field AI Assistant" to transform their sales experience by addressing the challenge of sellers being overwhelmed with information scattered across multiple siloed applications. The solution, built on Databricks' Mosaic AI agentic framework, integrates structured and unstructured data from their Lakehouse, CRM system (Salesforce), and collaboration platforms to provide conversational AI interactions for information retrieval, customer insights, and automated actions like CRM updates and email drafting. The assistant leverages Azure OpenAI GPT-4, vector search, function calling, and Unity Catalog governance. While specific quantitative results are not disclosed, Databricks reports that the solution empowers sellers to focus on strategic, high-value activities by streamlining workflows and automating repetitive administrative tasks.

title: Panel Discussion on LLMOps Challenges: Model Selection, Ethics, and Production Deployment
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together practitioners from various companies including Interact (healthcare AI), Inflection AI, Google Vertex AI, Amberflow, and Databricks to discuss practical LLMOps challenges in production. Key topics covered include model selection for healthcare conversational AI with strict latency and accuracy requirements, multi-model cost tracking and metering strategies, responsible AI deployment with safety filters and bias mitigation, the emergence of compound AI systems, and the trade-offs between model size, cost, and performance. The discussion emphasizes building custom evaluation benchmarks over public ones, implementing proper data governance, and the importance of tuning models to specific use cases and cultural contexts rather than relying on generic foundation models.

title: Autonomous Software Development Using Multi-Model LLM System with Advanced Planning and Tool Integration
short_summary: Factory.ai developed Code Droid, an autonomous AI system designed to automate software engineering tasks using natural language instructions. The system addresses the challenge of accelerating software development velocity by combining multi-model LLM orchestration, sophisticated planning and task decomposition, codebase understanding through their HyperCode representation system, and integrated developer tooling. On the SWE-bench benchmark, Code Droid achieved 19.27% on the full benchmark and 31.67% on SWE-bench Lite, outperforming competitors like Devin and Aider. The system operates in sandboxed production environments with extensive safety protocols, explainability logging, and security certifications including ISO 42001, SOC 2, and ISO 27001.

title: Autonomous Software Development Agent for Production Code Generation
short_summary: Cognition AI developed Devin, an autonomous AI software engineer that can complete end-to-end software development tasks using the same tools human engineers use. The system addresses the challenge of software engineering being labor-intensive by enabling engineers to delegate implementation tasks through natural language instructions. Devin can create projects from scratch, debug production codebases, make pull requests, and iterate based on feedback—all while running autonomously. The company uses Devin internally to build Devin itself, with the AI agent creating features like search bars, API integrations, and internal dashboards. The result is a workflow shift where engineers become more like engineering managers, running multiple Devin instances in parallel and focusing on higher-level problem-solving rather than implementation details.

title: Advanced Context-Aware Code Generation with Custom Infrastructure and Parallel LLM Processing
short_summary: Codeium, an AI-powered developer tools company, faced limitations with traditional embedding-based retrieval for code generation, finding that vector embeddings hit a performance ceiling when retrieving multi-document context from large codebases. Their solution, called "M Query," leverages vertical integration—owning their own models and custom infrastructure—to run thousands of parallel LLM calls for context reasoning at 1/100th the cost of competitors. This approach enables high-quality, multi-document retrieval that considers active files, recent commits, and project context. The system was rolled out to a subset of their 1.5+ million users, resulting in measurably higher user satisfaction (more thumbs up on chat messages), increased code generation acceptance rates, and ultimately more code written for users.

title: Building a Voice Assistant from Open Source LLMs: A Home Project Case Study
short_summary: This case study from Weights & Biases demonstrates the journey of productionizing LLM applications through a practical example of building a custom voice assistant (an "Alexa alternative"). Starting with 0% accuracy using default prompts, the project iterated through prompt engineering, model switching (Llama 2 to Mistral), and fine-tuning with QLoRA to achieve 98% accuracy. The talk emphasizes that while AI is easy to demo, it's significantly harder to productionize, and presents key lessons including the critical importance of building evaluation frameworks, tracking all experiments for reproducibility, starting with lightweight prototypes, and incorporating end-user feedback for iterative improvement.

title: Automated LLM Evaluation and Quality Monitoring in Customer Support Analytics
short_summary: Echo AI, a customer conversation analytics platform, partnered with Log10 to build a production LLM system that analyzes 100% of customer interactions across support, sales, and success teams. The challenge was moving beyond manual sampling (typically 5%) to real-time, comprehensive analysis while maintaining enterprise-grade accuracy. Using Log10's Auto Feedback system, Echo AI implemented automated evaluation of LLM outputs, enabling human-in-the-loop feedback collection from solution engineers, detection of model drift and hallucinations, and continuous improvement of fine-tuned models. The solution achieved a reported 20 F1-point improvement in accuracy for specific use cases and reduced the time to deliver trusted insights to new customers to within seven days.

title: Large-Scale AI Assistant Deployment with Safety-First Evaluation Approach
short_summary: Discord deployed Clyde AI, an LLM-powered chatbot with RAG capabilities, to over 200 million users, facing significant challenges around safety, security, and content moderation rather than model performance. The team developed a rigorous evaluation culture treating evals as unit tests, implemented deterministic metrics over complex LLM-graded approaches, built open-source tooling (promptfoo) for local evaluation and red teaming, and created systematic processes for identifying jailbreaks and harmful outputs. Key learnings included keeping evals simple and fast, resisting prompt bloat, using existing observability tools like Datadog rather than specialized LLM solutions, and implementing creative solutions like randomly injecting GPT-4 responses to prevent model drift in long conversations.

title: Scaling Trust and Safety Using LLMs at Tinder
short_summary: Tinder, the world's largest dating app, addresses the challenge of detecting trust and safety violations at scale by fine-tuning open-source LLMs using LoRA adapters. The solution involves creating high-quality training datasets with GPT-4 assistance, fine-tuning models on hundreds to thousands of examples, and serving multiple adapters efficiently using LoRAX on a small number of GPUs. This approach enables real-time inference at tens of QPS with ~100ms latency, achieving near 100% recall on simpler tasks like social handle detection while providing significantly better generalization against adversarial behavior compared to traditional ML models.

title: LLMOps Best Practices and Success Patterns Across Multiple Companies
short_summary: This talk from HumanLoop, an LLMOps platform provider, synthesizes lessons learned from helping hundreds of companies deploy LLMs in production. The speaker identifies three fundamental pillars for success: team composition (emphasizing domain experts over ML specialists), rigorous evaluation at every stage of development, and comprehensive logging/tooling infrastructure. Multiple customer examples are cited, including Filevine (legal tech) which roughly doubled revenue after launching six AI products, Duolingo where linguists do all prompt engineering, and Ironclad which achieved 50% auto-negotiation of contracts after building proper debugging infrastructure. The core message is that LLM applications are now generating real ROI, and success comes from centering domain experts in the development process, building evaluation criteria upfront, and ensuring proper tooling for collaboration and debugging.

title: Building and Scaling Enterprise LLMOps Platforms: From Team Topology to Production
short_summary: This presentation by Patrick Debois, founder of DevOps Days, explores how enterprises can build internal AI platforms to scale generative AI adoption across development teams. Drawing from two years of building GenAI applications and 15 years of DevOps experience, the talk addresses the organizational friction between data science and engineering teams, proposes a platform-based approach with centralized model access, vector databases, observability, and governance, and discusses the challenges of testing LLM outputs, managing model changes, and enabling traditional developers to build AI applications. The solution involves creating dedicated platform teams that provide infrastructure, enablement, and governance services, following patterns similar to the evolution of DevOps platform engineering.

title: Document Processing Automation with LLMs: Evolution of Evaluation Strategies
short_summary: Klarity, an AI company automating back-office document workflows for finance and accounting teams, shares their journey of building evaluation systems for production LLMs. After pivoting from traditional ML to generative AI, they developed a pragmatic approach to evals that prioritizes user experience over abstract benchmarks. Their solution involves frontloading UX testing, building customer-specific accuracy metrics, developing custom synthetic data generation, and strategically reducing degrees of freedom in their multi-LLM architecture. The company now processes over 500,000 documents across 15+ unique LLM use cases, demonstrating that thoughtful evaluation strategies can enable rapid feature development while maintaining production reliability.

title: Building an AI Innovation Team and Platform with Safeguards at Scale
short_summary: Twilio's Emerging Tech and Innovation team shares their journey of exploring disruptive AI innovation within an enterprise context. The team faced challenges around quality expectations, cost considerations, and the tension between rapid prototyping and enterprise-grade reliability. Their solutions included creating a separate sub-brand (Twilio Alpha) for early-stage products, implementing RAG-based personalization and perception engines for customer engagement, building an AI assistant/agent builder, and establishing principles around shipping early, hiring for curiosity, and maintaining roadmap flexibility. Key learnings emphasized customer obsession, setting appropriate expectations through sub-branding, internal dogfooding with low-risk use cases, and sharing knowledge both internally and externally to drive adoption.

title: Comprehensive Security and Risk Management Framework for Enterprise LLM Deployments
short_summary: PredictionGuard presents a comprehensive framework for deploying secure and accurate LLM systems in enterprise environments. The talk addresses five key challenges: hallucination detection using factual consistency models, supply chain vulnerabilities through trusted model registries, vulnerable model servers requiring endpoint monitoring, data breach prevention via PII filtering and confidential computing, and prompt injection attacks using ensemble classification models. The solution combines traditional NLP techniques with modern LLM safeguards, emphasizing visibility and configurability while maintaining low latency by avoiding chained LLM calls in favor of smaller, CPU-efficient models for validation tasks.

title: Responsible LLM Adoption for Fraud Detection with RAG Architecture
short_summary: Mastercard shares their journey of adopting LLMs in production, transitioning from structured data AI to leveraging unstructured data through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The company addressed challenges around hallucination, access controls, and scalable ML infrastructure while maintaining responsible AI principles. Their approach resulted in boosting fraud detection by up to 300% in some cases. The presentation emphasizes that LLM code represents less than 5% of the work in building end-to-end systems, with the remaining 95% involving infrastructure, data pipelines, safeguards, and governance frameworks.

title: Building Production-Grade RAG Systems for Financial Document Analysis
short_summary: Microsoft development teams share their experiences building a production RAG system for financial document analysis, handling analyst reports and SEC filings. The presentation addresses key challenges including metadata extraction for document filtering, multimodal processing of charts and graphs, and the critical importance of evaluation-driven development. They demonstrate how seemingly simple changes can dramatically affect system accuracy, and emphasize that while RAG appears easy in demos, real-world implementation requires careful attention to document parsing, image classification, and robust evaluation pipelines to handle tens of thousands of complex financial documents.

title: Evolution of Code Assistant Integration in a Cloud Development Platform
short_summary: Val Town, a code hosting service, faced the challenge of integrating state-of-the-art LLM code generation capabilities to meet user demands. Through a series of "fast-follow" iterations from 2022-2024, they evolved their AI assistant "Townie" from simple ChatGPT-based copy-paste automation to a sophisticated fullstack app generator powered by Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Key innovations included integrating Codeium for faster autocomplete, developing automatic error detection and prompting, and experimenting with diff-based code generation for faster iteration cycles. While acknowledging they are primarily copying innovations from competitors like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Windsurf, Val Town has created a functional integrated AI code editor that can generate deployed fullstack applications with frontend, backend, and database in minutes.

title: Building and Deploying Repository-Specific AI Assistants for GitHub
short_summary: PeterCat.ai addresses the inefficiency of finding answers and getting support on GitHub repositories by creating custom AI assistants tailored to specific codebases. The solution combines LLM-powered agents with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to enable assistants that understand repository documentation, code, and historical issues. Using LangChain for agent orchestration, OpenAI embeddings for vectorization, and Supabase for vector storage, the system provides automated PR code reviews and intelligent issue responses. The project was open-sourced in September 2024, gaining over 850 GitHub stars and adoption by 178 open-source projects within three months, demonstrating practical value in reducing developer friction when interacting with open-source repositories.

title: Fine-tuned LLM for Message Content Moderation and Trust & Safety
short_summary: Thumbtack, a home services marketplace, needed to enhance their message review system to detect policy violations like abusive language, job seeking, and partnership requests between customers and service professionals. Their existing CNN-based model struggled with nuanced language and subtle violations. After finding that prompt engineering with off-the-shelf LLMs yielded poor results (AUC of only 0.56), they fine-tuned an LLM on tens of thousands of labeled samples, achieving an AUC of 0.93. To optimize costs, they repurposed their legacy CNN model as a pre-filter, reducing LLM processing to only 20% of messages. The production deployment used LangChain for centralized LLM service management. Results showed precision improved by 3.7x and recall by 1.5x compared to the previous system, having processed tens of millions of messages successfully.

title: Implementing Effective Safety Filters in a Game-Based LLM Application
short_summary: JOBifAI, an LLM-powered game featuring AI-generated gameplay mechanics, encountered significant challenges with LLM safety filters and output reliability in production. The developers faced three main failure modes: invalid JSON responses, schema non-conformance, and safety filter rejections—all returning similar error codes. Their solution involved implementing a retry mechanism (up to 3 attempts) achieving roughly 99% success rates, while also designing in-game consequences for inappropriate player inputs. The case study highlights fundamental LLMOps challenges around error handling, cost unpredictability, and the lack of granular API error codes, which the developers argue makes LLMs "defective tools" for production applications despite the proof-of-concept's success.

title: Using LLMs to Enhance Search Discovery and Recommendations
short_summary: Instacart faced limitations in their search experience where users found highly relevant results but lacked inspirational, discovery-driven content for product exploration. Their pre-LLM approach to the "Related Items" section often returned poorly matched alternatives when exact matches weren't available. By integrating LLMs into their search stack, combining world knowledge with Instacart-specific domain data (query understanding signals, historical conversion data, and search logs), they developed both basic and advanced content generation techniques to produce complementary and substitute product recommendations. The system uses offline batch processing for prompt generation and product mapping, stores results in a key-value store, and employs a "Whole Page Ranker" model for optimal content positioning. They also implemented "LLM as a Judge" for scalable content evaluation. The results included substantial improvements in user engagement (18% improvement in engagement rate with inspirational content) and incremental revenue generation.

title: Building an AI-Generated Movie Quiz Game with RAG and Real-Time Multiplayer
short_summary: Datastax's Langflow team built a custom AI workflow to automate the repetitive task of gathering and organizing content for their AI++ developer newsletter. The solution uses Langflow to ingest URLs, leverage an LLM to generate summaries and categorizations, and save results directly to Notion. A browser bookmarklet was created to trigger the entire workflow with a single click from any webpage, significantly streamlining the content curation process for newsletter production.

title: Agentic RAG Implementation for Retail Personalization and Customer Support
short_summary: Retail and e-commerce companies face challenges in connecting operational data with unstructured information to deliver personalized customer experiences. MongoDB Atlas and Dataworkz offer an agentic RAG-as-a-service solution that combines real-time operational data (customer purchases, inventory, product descriptions) with unstructured data sources (wikis, PDFs, documents) to power intelligent chatbots, personalized recommendations, dynamic marketing, and enhanced site search. The solution uses vector embeddings stored in MongoDB Atlas with multistep agentic RAG pipelines to retrieve context-aware responses in real time, promising improved customer engagement, optimized inventory management, and scalable AI capabilities for retail operations.

title: Exploring RAG Limitations with Movie Scripts: The Copernicus Challenge
short_summary: This case study from OpenGPA explores the limitations of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) when applied to context-rich documents. While the original source content is unavailable due to a DNS resolution error, the title suggests an investigation into scenarios where standard RAG approaches may struggle, particularly when documents require deep contextual understanding rather than simple keyword-based retrieval. The study appears to focus on identifying edge cases and challenges in production RAG systems.

title: Enterprise-Scale Healthcare LLM System for Unified Patient Journeys
short_summary: John Snow Labs presents an enterprise platform for integrating multimodal medical data (EHR, unstructured clinical notes, FHIR resources, and imaging) into unified patient journeys using healthcare-specific LLMs. The system addresses the challenge of fragmented, messy patient data across multiple sources by extracting, normalizing, and deduplicating information from various modalities, storing it in an OMOP-compliant relational database, and enabling natural language querying for clinical decision support, cohort building, and patient risk assessment. The platform runs entirely on-premises within customer infrastructure, uses proprietary medical LLMs that outperform GPT-4 on clinical tasks, and is designed to scale to millions of patients with billions of documents while maintaining accuracy, consistency, and explainability.

title: Scaling Document Processing with LLMs and Human Review
short_summary: Vendr, a company that helps customers optimize SaaS purchasing, partnered with Extend to build an LLM-powered document processing system capable of extracting structured data from over 100,000 order forms and contracts. The challenge was converting unstructured PDF documents into usable structured data for pricing comparisons and customer recommendations. Using a hybrid approach combining LLMs with human-in-the-loop review, traditional OCR preprocessing, document embeddings for similarity detection, and careful entity mapping workflows, they achieved significantly faster document processing than prior manual coding approaches while maintaining high accuracy through targeted human review rather than reviewing every document.

title: Automated Medical Literature Review System Using Domain-Specific LLMs
short_summary: John Snow Labs developed a medical chatbot that automates literature review processes for academic research, addressing the significant time and effort traditionally required (weeks to months). The solution combines proprietary domain-tuned LLMs with a RAG architecture that indexes major medical publication databases (PubMed, arXiv, bioRxiv, MDPI) updated daily. Users can define search keywords, data extraction points, and inclusion/exclusion criteria in plain English, with the system automatically processing hundreds of documents and extracting structured data with evidence citations. A demonstrated example processed 271 documents in approximately 7 minutes, providing color-coded results indicating which studies met criteria, along with exportable structured data and reasoning explanations for each extraction decision.

title: Building and Evaluating a RAG-based Menopause Information Chatbot
short_summary: Vira Health, a digital health company focused on menopause care, developed and evaluated an AI chatbot using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide reliable menopause information. The challenge was that general-purpose LLMs like ChatGPT could not guarantee clinically verified responses with traceable sources. The solution involved building a RAG system that exclusively used peer-reviewed position statements from The Menopause Society as trusted documents, constraining the LLM's responses to clinically accurate content. Evaluation using both AI judges (Claude 2.1) and manual clinical review across 40 open-ended questions showed 95% faithfulness to source documents, consistently high relevance scores, near-zero harmful responses, and strong clinical correctness, demonstrating a viable foundation for healthcare AI applications while acknowledging further research is needed before clinical deployment.

title: AI-Powered Neurosurgery: From Brain Tumor Classification to Surgical Planning
short_summary: This presentation from Cedars Sinai's NLP Summit covers the comprehensive application of machine learning and AI in neurosurgery, addressing challenges in brain tumor classification (where traditional radiologists achieve only 69-77% accuracy), surgical planning optimization, hematoma prediction, and intraoperative surgical assistance. The solutions presented include convolutional neural networks achieving 95%+ accuracy for brain tumor classification, graph neural networks for brain bleed symptom prediction (80%+ accuracy), deep learning models for predicting surgical revision needs and hematoma expansion, and real-time AI systems for surgical instrument tracking and smoke removal during procedures. These implementations demonstrate significant improvements in patient outcomes, surgical precision, and hospital operational efficiency.

title: Developing a Multilingual Ayurvedic Medical LLM: Challenges and Learnings
short_summary: Trigent Software attempted to build "IRGPT," a fine-tuned medical LLM for multilingual Ayurveda consultations, combining ancient Indian holistic medicine with modern AI. The team faced significant challenges with regional language data, cultural nuances, and contextual accuracy that led to pivoting from multilingual support to English-only. Using GPT-2 Medium with 347 million parameters trained on approximately 150,000 validated samples, they achieved a working prototype but acknowledged the project as a learning experience rather than a success story. Key lessons included the need for more targeted regional data and cultural context, with plans to continue development through academic partnerships.

title: Implementing LLMs for Patient Education and Healthcare Communication
short_summary: National Healthcare Group is implementing large language models to transform patient education by creating 24/7 accessible, personalized, multilingual health information chatbots. The problem addressed is the traditional limitations of patient education—time-constrained consultations, inconsistent information across providers, literacy barriers, and resource-intensive translation processes. The solution involves integrating LLM-powered chatbots into existing healthcare apps and messaging platforms like WhatsApp, enabling patients to query health information on demand. Current projects include eczema education and lung function test preparation guidance. While specific quantitative results are not yet reported, the anticipated benefits include improved health outcomes through better-informed patients, reduced healthcare costs, enhanced patient satisfaction, and more efficient use of clinician time by offloading routine educational queries to AI systems.

title: MultiCare: A Large-Scale Medical Case Report Dataset for AI Model Training
short_summary: The MultiCare project addresses the challenge of training medical AI models by creating a comprehensive, open-access dataset of over 75,000 clinical case reports spanning 1990 to 2023. The dataset includes 135,000 medical images with labels and captions, covering diverse medical specialties like oncology, cardiology, and surgery. The solution involved extracting and processing data from PubMed Central's open-access articles, implementing image preprocessing to split compound images, and creating normalized image labels from captions using NLP techniques. The resulting 8.8GB dataset is available on Zenodo and Hugging Face, with a GitHub repository providing tools for creating custom subsets based on specific use cases for training language models, computer vision models, or multimodal models.

title: Natural Language Interface for Healthcare Data Analytics using LLMs
short_summary: NLQ (Natural Language Query) company developed an AI-powered interface for Aachen University Clinic to make Intensive Care Unit databases accessible to non-technical healthcare staff. The system uses a hybrid architecture combining vector databases with metadata embeddings, fine-tuned large language models for intent detection and slot filling, and structured query generation to transform natural language questions into SQL queries. This enables physicians and department heads to quickly retrieve patient data analytics, generate visualizations, and calculate downstream complications without requiring SQL expertise, ultimately supporting faster clinical decision-making.

title: LLM-Powered Information Extraction from Pediatric Cardiac MRI Reports
short_summary: Great Ormond Street Hospital (part of the NHS) faced the challenge of extracting valuable clinical data from 15,000 heterogeneous cardiac MRI reports accumulated over 10 years, which were locked in unstructured PDF format. The team developed an LLM-based information extraction pipeline using smaller language models (due to GPU constraints) for question-answering to extract patient identifiers, combined with a few-shot learning approach (SetFit) for table classification. They built a custom infrastructure called GRID with separate development and staging servers to handle information governance requirements. Results showed that prompt engineering significantly improved entity extraction performance, with Flan-T5 Large providing the best results, while the SetFit-based classifier achieved strong performance on table row classification with only 280 training examples.

title: NLP and Machine Learning for Early Sepsis Detection in Neonatal Care
short_summary: Wroclaw Medical University is developing a clinical decision support system for neonatal intensive care units that uses natural language processing to extract and structure unstructured medical data from electronic health records, combined with machine learning models to detect early signs of sepsis in newborns. The project addresses the challenge of sepsis—a life-threatening condition that causes 3 million deaths annually and requires rapid diagnosis—by analyzing vital signs, lab results, and clinical observations in real-time. Early results from similar systems cited in the presentation show potential to reduce diagnosis time from 24 hours to 2 hours, with high sensitivity and specificity, while also potentially reducing unnecessary antibiotic use through pattern recognition.

title: Automating Radiology Report Generation with Fine-tuned LLMs
short_summary: Researchers at Heidelberg University's Department of Radiology developed a system to automate radiology report generation using fine-tuned large language models. Facing increasing CT procedure volumes and radiologist burnout, the team created an architecture combining Vision Transformers for image encoding with a fine-tuned Llama 3 8B model for text generation. Using quantization (4-bit), LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and the Alpaca prompt format, they achieved training on a single RTX 5000 GPU. The system generates detailed radiologist reports from impressions, achieving a training loss of 0.72, validation loss of 1.36, and BLEU scores of 0.69 (training) and 0.33 (validation), with human evaluation by senior radiologists also being conducted.

title: Healthcare NLP Pipeline for HIPAA-Compliant Patient Data De-identification
short_summary: Dandelion Health developed a comprehensive pipeline for de-identifying free text patient notes to maintain HIPAA compliance while preserving high-fidelity clinical data for researchers. The solution combines John Snow Labs Healthcare NLP with custom pre-processing (categorizing notes by modality, extracting embedded tables, handling edge cases like ASCII tables) and post-processing techniques including "Hiding in Plain Sight" (HIPS) token replacement. The system operates in an air-gapped AWS environment with no internet access, uses SQS queuing and Lambda for scalable processing, and achieves effective PHI detection recall upwards of 99% when combining the base NLP recall of ~95% with the HIPS approach that reduces re-identification risk by approximately 90%.

title: Multimodal Healthcare Data Integration with Specialized LLMs
short_summary: John Snow Labs developed an end-to-end generative AI system for healthcare data integration that transforms raw, multi-modal patient data (structured EHR data, unstructured clinical notes, FHIR resources, PDFs, HL7 messages) into unified, queryable patient journeys. The solution addresses the challenge of fragmented healthcare data by using healthcare-specific LLMs for information extraction, semantic modeling, terminology mapping, and natural language querying. The system enables clinicians to ask complex questions about individual patients or population cohorts in natural language, with consistent and explainable answers. Key results include dramatically more complete patient histories (studies cited show 40% of important diagnoses exist only in free text), support for millions of patients with billions of documents, and production-ready deployment in air-gapped, PHI-compliant environments using commodity infrastructure and the OMOP standard data model.

title: Building Healthcare-Specific LLM Pipelines for Oncology Patient Timelines
short_summary: Roche Diagnostics, in partnership with John Snow Labs, developed an AI-assisted data abstraction solution for oncology care that leverages healthcare-specific large language models to extract chemotherapy treatment timelines from unstructured EHR data. The system addresses the challenge of fragmented, unstructured healthcare data by using NLP and machine learning to auto-detect medical concepts, extract temporal relations between chemotherapy events and time expressions, and translate free text into structured data. Their approach utilized prompt engineering with zero-shot techniques on models like JSL Med Llama 3, achieving high precision in relation extraction while reducing manual data entry burden. The solution integrates with Roche's navify oncology clinical hub to provide patient-specific NCCN guideline recommendations and support evidence-based care decisions.

title: Automated HCC Code Extraction from Clinical Notes Using Healthcare NLP
short_summary: WVU Medicine, a comprehensive health system spanning 25 hospitals, implemented John Snow Labs' Healthcare NLP to automate the extraction of Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) codes from radiology notes. The system addresses the challenge of providers missing critical chronic condition codes during patient documentation by using NLP to analyze unstructured clinical notes and suggest relevant codes via real-time best practice alerts in their EMR system. Since going live in December 2023, the model has extracted over 27,000 HCC codes, with 18.4% accepted by providers, positively impacting over 5,000 patients through more accurate health status documentation and improved care coordination.

title: Medical Transcript Summarization Using Multiple LLM Models: An Evaluation Study
short_summary: Oracle's research team evaluated multiple large language models (Claude, GPT-4, Llama 3.1, and Phi 3.1) for summarizing medical transcripts to reduce administrative burden on healthcare care coordinators. Using a dataset of medical transcripts scraped from MT Samples, the team compared models using ROUGE scores and cosine similarity metrics, with Claude serving as the ground truth baseline. Results showed GPT-4 performed best across quantitative metrics (ROUGE-1: 0.821, cosine similarity: 0.879), while Phi 3.1 offered a good balance between accuracy and conciseness with the advantage of being lightweight enough for edge deployment on devices like iPads. The research demonstrated potential to reduce care coordinator preparation time by over 50%, though challenges including hallucinations, medical terminology complexity, and context understanding remain areas for future improvement.

title: Building and Evaluating a Financial Earnings Call Summarization System
short_summary: Aiera, an investor intelligence platform covering over 45,000 financial events per year, developed a comprehensive dataset and evaluation framework for LLM-powered summarization of earnings call transcripts. The team faced challenges with publicly available financial NLP datasets not meeting their specific needs, leading them to build their own using Claude 3 Opus for generating reference insights. They conducted extensive evaluation comparing ROUGE and BERT scoring metrics across multiple LLM providers, ultimately finding Claude 3.5 Sonnet performed best on their summarization task. The case study highlights the complexity of evaluating abstractive summarization in domain-specific contexts and the importance of semantic similarity metrics over traditional n-gram overlap measures.

title: Smart Business Analyst: Automating Competitor Analysis in Medical Device Procurement
short_summary: Philips developed a GenAI-powered "Smart Business Analyst" tool to automate competitor analysis and procurement insights gathering. The solution addresses the time-consuming manual process of collecting competitive intelligence across market analysis, supplier evaluation, and price benchmarking. By leveraging a multi-agent architecture with subquery generation, web scraping, and report generation agents, the system can automatically populate complex feature comparison matrices (e.g., 25 features across 8 competitors) in seconds rather than hours. The tool integrates with internal databases, external data sources, and includes Google Search API for real-time information, providing more precise numerical outputs than generic ChatGPT while supporting multilingual queries and conversational memory.

title: Healthcare Patient Journey Analysis Platform with Multimodal LLMs
short_summary: John Snow Labs presents their enterprise platform for integrating multimodal medical data (structured EHR data, unstructured clinical notes, FHIR resources, and imaging) into unified patient journeys. The system uses healthcare-specific LLMs to extract, normalize, and deduplicate information from diverse sources, enabling natural language queries across millions of patients and billions of documents. The platform is designed for on-premise deployment within healthcare organizations' security perimeters, uses the OMOP common data model for interoperability, and demonstrates superior accuracy compared to general-purpose LLMs like GPT-4 on clinical tasks. Key use cases include patient cohort building, clinical decision support, HCC coding, and risk score calculation, with the system addressing the fundamental challenge that 30-50% of clinical codes are typically missing from structured data alone.

title: Text-to-SQL System with RAG-Enhanced Table Selection
short_summary: Pinterest developed a Text-to-SQL feature to help data analysts convert natural language questions directly into SQL queries, addressing the challenge of navigating a large data warehouse with hundreds of thousands of tables.
