Working with a cross-functional team including computational linguists and data scientists (in collaboration with Inovex), they developed a Gradio-based interface using LangChain and OpenAI's GPT models that integrates prompt libraries, AI-aided prompt engineering, constitutional AI evaluation, and human-in-the-loop editing. The tool enables scalable content generation while maintaining Babbel's quality standards, achieving over 85% acceptance rate from content editors on generated items, and supports localization into eight languages while preserving cultural relevance and educational value.

title: Scaling an AI-Powered Search and Research Assistant from Prototype to Production
short_summary: Perplexity AI built an AI-powered research assistant that combines LLMs with real-time web search to provide direct answers to complex queries. Starting as a Slack bot for internal use, the product evolved into a full consumer search platform. Key technical achievements include orchestrating search indices with LLMs, fine-tuning GPT-3.5 to match GPT-4 quality at 6x lower cost, building custom inference infrastructure for Llama models achieving best-in-class latency, and developing "generative UI" for dynamic clarifying questions. The company differentiated itself through fast iteration, achieving superior citation accuracy and perceived utility scores compared to competitors in Stanford evaluations.

title: Implementing Generative AI in Manufacturing: A Multi-Use Case Study
short_summary: Accenture's Industry X practice developed and validated multiple generative AI use cases for manufacturing industries through a structured experimentation methodology. The team addressed challenges around test case generation, technical publication creation, operational copilots, and requirements quality checking by integrating LLMs into existing workflows and tools like PTC Codebeamer. Results showed 40-50% effort reduction in document generation tasks and up to 80% reduction in time for converting functional requirements into MBSE models, though Accenture emphasizes that results vary significantly by industry, maturity level, and specific use case.

title: Building and Testing Production AI Applications at CircleCI
short_summary: CircleCI's engineering team discusses their experience building AI-powered developer tools, particularly an error summarizer that uses LLMs to analyze stack traces and provide actionable recommendations. The conversation explores the unique challenges of testing non-deterministic LLM outputs in production, including the use of model-graded evaluations, strategies for managing costs through routing and fine-tuning, and the importance of building feedback loops from user behavior. The discussion emphasizes that while LLM-powered applications are easy to prototype, ensuring they work reliably in production requires adapting traditional software testing philosophies to handle probabilistic outputs and subjective quality criteria.

title: AI Error Summarizer Implementation: A Tiger Team Approach
short_summary: CircleCI formed a tiger team to explore generative AI opportunities and built an AI Error Summarizer feature that sends build errors to an LLM for summarization. The team spent 6-7 weeks in discovery mode, interviewing product managers across the company to identify pain points, then rapidly prototyped using OpenAI's API and LangChain. The project demonstrated that regular software engineers can quickly build AI-enabled features without specialized ML expertise, and that high-value AI features can be subtle additions to existing products rather than revolutionary overhauls.

title: Scaling LLM Applications in Telecommunications: Learnings from Verizon and Industry Partners
short_summary: This panel discussion featuring executives from Verizon, Anthropic, and Infosys explores the challenges and best practices of deploying generative AI in telecommunications. Key use cases discussed include content generation and knowledge management (such as processing complex lease documents), software development lifecycle optimization, and co-pilot implementations for productivity enhancement. The panelists emphasize the importance of ROI justification (suggesting a $50M problem threshold to justify $6M AI investments), establishing centers of excellence with governance tollgates, maintaining model-agnostic architectures through wrapper layers, and achieving high accuracy rates (95%+) before production deployment. They also discuss the critical role of evaluation frameworks, user adoption challenges, and the evolving nature of foundation models that requires rapid re-evaluation capabilities.

title: Building a Voice Assistant with Open Source LLMs: From Demo to Production
short_summary: This case study from Weights & Biases demonstrates the journey of productionizing LLM applications through a practical example of building a custom voice assistant (an "Alexa alternative"). Starting with 0% accuracy using default prompts, the project iteratively improved through prompt engineering (reaching 75%), model switching from Llama 2 to Mistral (79%), and finally fine-tuning with QLoRA (98% accuracy). The presentation emphasizes that while AI is easy to demo, it is hard to productionize, and highlights the critical importance of building robust evaluation frameworks, tracking all experiments for reproducibility, and iterating quickly to bridge the gap between compelling demos and production-ready applications.

title: Security Learnings from LLM Production Deployments
short_summary: This case study presents insights from NVIDIA's AI Red Team on securing LLM-enabled applications in production environments. The talk covers common vulnerabilities discovered during 18 months of security assessments, focusing on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, plugin architectures, and prompt injection attacks. Key findings include the risks of improper access controls on RAG data stores, data exfiltration through active content rendering, and remote code execution vulnerabilities in poorly sandboxed plugins. The recommendations emphasize treating all LLM inputs as potentially adversarial, applying traditional application security principles, and designing systems that assume external data sources are internet-facing attack surfaces.

title: Lessons from Enterprise LLM Deployment: Cross-functional Teams, Experimentation, and Security
short_summary: A team of Microsoft Industry Solutions Engineers shares practical lessons learned from helping strategic enterprise customers in Australia deploy LLM solutions throughout 2024. The presentation covers the critical importance of cross-functional teams, the need for continuous experimentation and evaluation in LLMOps, the complexities of implementing RAG solutions safely, and the essential role of guardrails in enterprise deployments. Key takeaways include treating LLM applications like "raising a puppy" requiring constant attention, starting simple without agentic frameworks, implementing robust feedback loops and observability, and building comprehensive guardrails to prevent jailbreaking, prompt injection, and data exfiltration attacks in production systems.

title: T-RAG: Tree-Based RAG Architecture for Question Answering Over Organizational Documents
short_summary: Qatar Computing Research Institute developed T-RAG (Tree-RAG), a production LLM application for question answering over private organizational governance documents for a large non-profit organization. The system addressed challenges of data security requiring on-premise deployment, limited computational resources, and the need for reliable responses. T-RAG combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation with a finetuned Llama-2 7B model and introduces a novel tree structure to represent organizational entity hierarchies, generating textual context for entity-related queries. Using QLoRA for parameter-efficient finetuning on 1,614 Q&A pairs generated from the source document, the system achieved 73% accuracy compared to 56.8% for standard RAG and 54.1% for finetuning alone. Evaluations including Needle in a Haystack tests demonstrated that the tree context significantly improved entity-related question accuracy, with T-RAG maintaining 64.1% accuracy even with relevant context buried among 10 unrelated chunks, versus 33.3% for standard RAG.

title: Challenges in Building Enterprise Chatbots with LLMs: A Banking Case Study
short_summary: This case study examines the significant challenges encountered when building production-grade enterprise chatbots using LLMs like GPT-4 and RAG pipelines. Drawing from a real banking customer support project that initially projected a 3-month proof of concept timeline but ultimately stalled, the article identifies key technical hurdles including knowledge base generation, retrieval optimization, conversation flow design, memory management, promise containment, latency issues, and regulatory compliance. Despite the apparent simplicity of combining tools like Pinecone with GPT-4, the author demonstrates that even leading AI companies like Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI have struggled to deploy effective customer-facing chatbots, with many reverting to predefined response options rather than free-flowing AI conversations.

title: From SMS to AI: Lessons from 5 Years of Chatbot Development for Social Impact
short_summary: ONE, a campaigning and advocacy organization fighting extreme poverty in Africa, developed rule-based chatbots on Messenger and WhatsApp to engage supporters across six African countries. Starting in 2019, they built iterative prototypes using RapidPro for chat-flow building, Turn as a WhatsApp Business Provider, ActionKit for CRM, and Tableau with Google BigQuery for analytics. The chatbots now reach over 38,000 unique users in English and French, enabling petition signing, quizzes, and activist group connections, with over 17,000 actions taken. Key learnings included the importance of starting small with focused MVPs, prioritizing user testing, anticipating significant marketing costs (with Messenger acquisition at $0.17 versus $1.77 for WhatsApp users), planning re-engagement strategies within Meta's messaging constraints, and ensuring cross-organizational value. While not yet AI-powered, ONE considers these lessons foundational for future generative AI implementations.

title: Four Critical Lessons from Building 50+ Global Chatbots: A Practitioner's Guide to Real-World Implementation
short_summary: Campfire AI shares practical lessons from building over 50 chatbots across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas. The case study addresses common failure patterns in conversational AI deployments, including handling out-of-scope queries (false positives and true negatives), organizing NLP intents hierarchically for specific responses, anticipating unusual user expressions, and designing graceful fallback flows instead of dead-end error messages. The key insights focus on treating chatbot development as an AI project rather than a traditional IT project, targeting 90% intent recognition rates through iterative testing and NLP model optimization, and implementing comprehensive safety nets to ensure users always receive value from interactions.

title: Building a Financial Data RAG System: Lessons from Search-First Architecture
short_summary: A consulting engagement developed a generative AI chatbot for a major financial services client to enable executives and investor relations teams to query proprietary data including SEC filings, earnings transcripts, and analyst reports. The initial RAG implementation using Azure's OpenAI accelerator delivered quick wins but suffered from critical issues including incorrect context attribution, poor financial table retrieval, and irrelevant search results. Through iterative improvements—including page-based chunking, GPT-4 generated summaries as searchable index fields, context-aware search agents, and custom scoring profiles for recency—the team achieved significant quality improvements. The solution transformed hours of manual research into seconds of conversational AI interaction, though the project highlighted that RAG success depends more on search optimization than LLM capabilities.

title: Production RAG Best Practices: Implementation Lessons at Scale
short_summary: This case study from Kapa.ai synthesizes lessons learned from implementing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems across 100+ technical teams including Docker, CircleCI, Reddit, and Monday.com. The core problem addressed is that over 80% of in-house generative AI projects fail to move beyond the proof-of-concept stage. The solution involves a comprehensive framework covering five key areas: careful data source curation, robust refresh pipelines for keeping knowledge current, comprehensive evaluation frameworks, optimized prompting strategies, and security best practices. The results include production-ready AI assistants that can accurately answer technical product questions while avoiding hallucinations and staying current with rapidly evolving documentation.

title: Enterprise AI Adoption Journey: From Experimentation to Core Operations
short_summary: Credal, an enterprise AI platform provider, shares observations from multiple enterprise customers navigating AI adoption in regulated industries. The case study outlines a four-stage adoption curve from early experimentation through core operations workflows, identifies key challenges including data security, RAG debugging difficulties, and access control management, and presents strategic decisions around build-vs-buy, platform-vs-point-solutions, and multi-LLM strategies. Results indicate that in tech companies, approximately 50% of organizations adopt AI tooling within 8 weeks, reaching 75% after one year when implementation goes well.

title: Optimizing RAG Systems: Lessons from Production
short_summary: AWS GenAIIC shares lessons learned from building RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) solutions across multiple industries since May 2023. The team addresses common challenges in deploying LLM-based chatbots that extract information from heterogeneous knowledge bases, presenting a comprehensive guide covering retrieval optimization techniques (hybrid search, metadata filtering, query rewriting), evaluation strategies (retrieval metrics, LLM-as-a-judge), and methods to reduce hallucinations (prompt engineering guardrails, quote verification). The solutions leverage Amazon Bedrock, OpenSearch Serverless, and custom implementations to improve retrieval accuracy and answer reliability in production RAG systems.

title: Building Production-Grade Heterogeneous RAG Systems
short_summary: AWS GenAIIC presents a comprehensive technical guide for building RAG systems that handle heterogeneous data formats in production environments. The article addresses common challenges when dealing with mixed data sources (text, tabular, images) by introducing routing mechanisms, LLM-powered code generation for structured data analysis, and multimodal embeddings. The solutions described include real-world implementations across multiple industries—oil and gas data analysis, financial analysis, industrial maintenance, ecommerce search, and technical assistance systems—with practical code examples using Amazon Bedrock, OpenSearch, and Anthropic's Claude models.

title: Production Lessons from Building and Deploying AI Agents
short_summary: Rasgo shares practical lessons from a year of building and deploying AI agents for enterprise data analysis. The company developed a platform enabling Fortune 500 customers to analyze internal data using natural language, connecting to databases like Snowflake and BigQuery. Key insights include prioritizing reasoning over knowledge, the critical importance of the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI) design, avoiding abstractions like LangChain for production systems, the limitations of fine-tuning for agent reasoning, and the necessity of building robust evaluation frameworks. The team found that model selection significantly impacts agent performance, with GPT-4 substantially outperforming GPT-3.5-turbo in reasoning tasks, and emphasized that competitive differentiation comes from the surrounding infrastructure (security, data connectors, UI, memory systems) rather than the agent itself.

title: Custom RAG Implementation for Enterprise Technology Research and Knowledge Management
short_summary: Trace3's Innovation Team built "Innovation-GPT," a custom generative AI solution to streamline research on emerging enterprise technology companies and manage institutional knowledge. The system uses web scraping to automatically gather information on newly funded tech companies, processes unstructured data into structured JSON profiles with metadata annotations, vectorizes the content, and integrates it into a RAG architecture with a chatbot interface. The solution addresses the team's challenge of manually researching companies and recalling information from a growing database of enterprise solutions. Risk management practices including multi-shot in-context learning and human-in-the-loop validation were implemented to mitigate hallucination risks, with all AI outputs serving as starting points that require human fact-checking.

title: GenAI-Powered Work Order Management System POC
short_summary: An international infrastructure company managing housing complexes across the U.S. partnered with NTT Data to explore whether GenAI could improve their work order management system, which processes over 500,000 annual maintenance requests. In under two weeks, NTT Data developed a proof of concept using a privately-hosted LLM that classified work orders by expertise required, urgency level, and special handling requirements. The solution demonstrated improved accuracy, consistency, and transparency compared to the largely manual process handled by 70 employees, while also providing explainable reasoning for each classification decision. The client plans to use insights from the POC to optimize their current team's performance before moving to full deployment.

title: Generative AI-Powered Knowledge Sharing System for Travel Expertise
short_summary: Hotelplan Suisse, Switzerland's largest tour operator, faced a challenge where travel experts had deep but specialized knowledge about specific destinations, requiring time-consuming consultations when customers asked about areas outside an individual expert's expertise. Working with Datatonic on Google Cloud, they developed a Generative AI-powered chatbot that ingests data from 10+ internal and external sources using semantic search, enabling sales staff to instantly access the collective knowledge of 500+ travel experts. The solution includes guardrails to prevent hallucinations, automated CI/CD pipelines, comprehensive logging to BigQuery, and chat history management. The result accelerated expert recommendations from hours to minutes, improving customer service speed and quality.

title: Enterprise LLM Playground Development for Internal AI Experimentation
short_summary: Thomson Reuters needed to enable enterprise-wide experimentation with large language models in a safe, controlled environment to foster AI innovation and identify use cases across their global workforce. They developed Open Arena, an LLM playground built on AWS serverless architecture in under 6 weeks, featuring multiple open-source and fine-tuned models deployed via Amazon SageMaker with Hugging Face containers, RAG pipelines for content-based experiences, and a user-friendly tile-based interface. The platform achieved over 1,000 monthly active users within a month, averaging 5-minute interaction times, and successfully generated numerous production use cases while democratizing AI experimentation for non-technical employees.

title: Leveraging Amazon Q for Integrated Cloud Operations Data Access and Automation
short_summary: First Orion, a telecom software company specializing in caller ID and spam protection, implemented Amazon Q to solve the challenge of cloud operations teams spending excessive time tracking down information across siloed data sources. By deploying Amazon Q as a conversational interface integrated with multiple data sources including S3, web crawlers, Confluence, and their ServiceNow CMDB, cloud operators can now use natural language to query operational data and even create tickets in systems like Jira and Zendesk without leaving the Q application. The solution reduces friction in troubleshooting workflows by consolidating data access and actions into a single chat-based interface, allowing operators to focus on solving problems rather than hunting for information.

title: Generative AI Contact Center Solution with Amazon Bedrock and Claude
short_summary: DoorDash faced challenges handling hundreds of thousands of daily support calls from delivery drivers (Dashers), with most calls still requiring live agent intervention despite existing IVR solutions. Working with AWS's Generative AI Innovation Center over 8 weeks, DoorDash built a voice-based generative AI self-service solution using Amazon Bedrock with Anthropic's Claude 3 Haiku, Amazon Connect, and RAG-based knowledge retrieval. The solution achieved response latencies of 2.5 seconds or less, increased testing capacity by 50x through automated evaluation frameworks, reduced development time by 50%, and now handles hundreds of thousands of calls daily while significantly reducing escalations to live agents by thousands per day.

title: Large-Scale Enterprise Copilot Deployment: Lessons from Einstein Copilot Implementation
short_summary: Salesforce deployed Einstein Copilot, their LLM-powered conversational AI assistant, across their internal CRM org used by thousands of employees. The team navigated challenges including testing against billions of records, developing custom actions beyond standard capabilities, and establishing robust feedback loops. Starting with 100 sellers and progressively scaling, they achieved measurable time savings by focusing on high-value use cases like record summarization, email drafting, and task prioritization. Key learnings included the importance of starting simple with standard actions, developing comprehensive query test sets (250+ queries with 80% success rate targets), ensuring proper user enablement through demo videos and multi-channel communication, and treating the deployment as a continuous improvement project rather than a one-time rollout.

title: Lessons from Deploying an HR-Aware AI Assistant: Five Key Implementation Insights
short_summary: Applaud shares lessons learned from deploying generative AI assistants for HR service delivery, addressing challenges including knowledge content quality management, personalization based on employee context, testing methodologies for conversational AI, managing accuracy expectations with temperature settings and prompt engineering, and establishing continuous monitoring processes. The company developed an HR-aware AI assistant that integrates with enterprise knowledge sources like SharePoint and ServiceNow, allowing HR teams to provide personalized answers based on employee attributes while avoiding outdated or irrelevant content.

title: Building Personalized Financial and Gardening Experiences with LLMs
short_summary: This case study features two companies—Bud Financial (fintech) and Scotts Miracle-Gro (consumer goods)—using Google Cloud's AI stack to deliver hyper-personalized customer experiences. Bud Financial built an AI agent called "YZ" that understands customers through transactional data to provide personalized financial guidance in a regulated environment. Scotts Miracle-Gro developed "My Scotty," an AI assistant using Vertex AI Conversations, Gen AI Playbooks (now Agents), and custom image recognition to offer personalized gardening advice and product recommendations. Both companies leverage GKE for model training and deployment, Gemini through Vertex AI APIs, and semantic search capabilities. Key results include accelerated product development, improved customer trust through personalization, and more intuitive customer interactions through natural language interfaces.

title: Data and AI Governance Integration in Enterprise GenAI Adoption
short_summary: This panel discussion at Google Cloud Next brings together data governance leaders from Collibra (AI partner), Mercado Libre (e-commerce), ATB Financial (banking), and Loblaw (retail) to explore how generative AI is transforming data governance practices. The participants discuss how GenAI creates both demand for well-governed data (as foundation for AI models) and opportunities to automate traditionally manual governance tasks like metadata description generation. Key solutions discussed include using Gemini for automated data cataloging, building RAG-based internal assistants grounded in business knowledge, implementing semantic search for natural language data discovery, and developing integrated data and AI governance frameworks. Results include accelerated data product development, improved data quality for AI applications, and the evolution from data governance as a roadblock to an enabler for AI initiatives.

title: AI-Powered Personalized Content Recommendations for Sports and Entertainment Venue
short_summary: The Golden State Warriors faced the challenge of delivering personalized content to millions of fans across multiple channels from a massive volume of game previews, recaps, photos, videos, and event information. Working with Google Cloud and implementation partner SADA, they built a Vertex AI-powered recommendation engine that ingests content from their CMS, user analytics from BigQuery, and event data to deliver personalized recommendations across their mobile app, website, and CRM systems. The solution uses a "build once, deploy everywhere" API abstraction layer, enabling a small technology team (under 600 employees total) to deliver tailored experiences to fans while focusing resources on customer experience rather than infrastructure management.

title: Generative AI Implementation in Banking Customer Service and Knowledge Management
short_summary: This panel discussion featuring executives from Discover Financial Services, Macquarie Bank, Scotia Bank, and Intesa Sanpaolo explores how major banks are implementing AI and generative AI in production. The primary case study focuses on Discover's deployment of a RAG-based generative AI system to help customer service agents find relevant procedures and information faster. By implementing Vertex AI with Gemini on Google Cloud, Discover reduced agent search time by approximately 70% (from minutes to seconds), enabling agents to stay in conversation flow with customers. The solution involved establishing an AI governance council, iterative model tuning with knowledge workers, human-in-the-loop evaluation using thumbs up/down feedback from agents, and a phased risk-based rollout approach across different skill groups.

title: Responsible AI Implementation for Healthcare Form Automation
short_summary: WellSky, a healthcare technology company serving over 2,000 hospitals and 130,000 providers, partnered with Google Cloud to address the "pajama time" problem—where 75% of home health nurses complete documentation after hours rather than spending time with their families. By leveraging Google's Vertex AI platform and healthcare-specific models like MedPalm, WellSky built an AI-powered forms automation solution with strong responsible AI governance. The solution includes evidence citations for all AI-generated content, comprehensive monitoring, and tooling for model updates. The implementation focused on reducing administrative burden while maintaining quality of care, using a cross-functional incubation team approach and establishing reusable building blocks for future AI use cases.

title: Enhancing E-commerce Search with Vector Embeddings and Generative AI
short_summary: Mercado Libre, Latin America's largest e-commerce platform with 144 million unique users, faced challenges with their traditional word-matching search engine failing to understand complex natural language queries like "I want a gift for my daughter who loves soccer and is a fan of Lionel Messi." They implemented a vector embedding approach using Google Cloud's Vector Search to represent items and match them semantically with user queries, moving beyond simple keyword matching. This solution significantly improved search quality for complex longtail queries, leading to increased click rates and conversion rates, while helping both buyers find what they need and sellers connect more efficiently with buyer needs.

title: Enterprise-Wide Generative AI Implementation for Marketing Content Generation and Translation
short_summary: Bosch, a global manufacturing conglomerate with over 427,000 employees and operations spanning mobility, consumer goods, energy, and industrial technology, faced significant challenges managing marketing content across 3,500+ websites and hundreds of social media channels. To democratize generative AI capabilities across the enterprise, Bosch partnered with Google Cloud to build a centralized "Gen AI Playground" that empowers employees to create marketing content, generate images, and translate materials themselves. Using Google's Imagen 2 model with custom brand guardrails (colors, tonality, composition), the solution reduced dependency on external agencies, cut translation costs (previously consuming 50% of marketing budgets), and accelerated campaign creation from 6-12 weeks to near-real-time. The platform was developed in approximately one month and is designed to serve all 430,000+ Bosch associates with use-case-driven interfaces that abstract away technical complexity.

title: LLM Testing Framework Using LLMs as Quality Assurance Agents
short_summary: Alaska Airlines, in partnership with Bitra (a Google Cloud services partner), developed CARL (QA Response Liaison), an LLM-powered testing framework designed to evaluate conversational AI chatbots at scale. The problem stemmed from the inherent risks of deploying customer-facing chatbots—users may attempt to manipulate bots into saying offensive things, making unauthorized promises, or deviating from intended behavior (as seen in publicized incidents with Chevrolet and Air Canada). CARL addresses this by using one LLM to simulate diverse user personas—from benign travelers to malicious hackers—and systematically test chatbot responses across hundreds of conversational paths. The solution runs on GCP infrastructure using Vertex AI, Cloud Composer for orchestration, AlloyDB for storage, and supports multiple LLM backends. Results showed improved customer satisfaction scores (NPS lift) in beta testing, with the framework successfully catching edge cases like getting the bot to "talk like a pirate" before production deployment.

title: Large Bank LLMOps Implementation: Lessons from Deutsche Bank and Others
short_summary: This panel discussion featuring technology leaders from Deutsche Bank and Discover Financial Services explores the practical implementation of generative AI in banking operations. The banks are tackling challenges including processing hundreds of thousands of unstructured documents daily using Google's Document AI enhanced with banking-specific controls, automating research report generation where 80% of analyst time is spent on data collection, improving engineering productivity through code assistance, and enhancing risk models with expanded data capabilities. Both organizations have established Centers of Excellence and governance frameworks, working under model risk management protocols while navigating regulatory requirements. Early production deployments include compliance monitoring for state regulations and procedure summarization using RAG, with plans to expand toward customer-facing applications as the technology matures and regulatory clarity improves.

title: Enterprise LLM Implementation Panel: Lessons from Box, Glean, Tyace, Security AI and Citibank
short_summary: This panel discussion at a Google Cloud conference brings together leaders from Box, Glean, Typeface, Security AI, and Citibank to share their experiences implementing generative AI in enterprise production environments. The panelists address common challenges including data security, permissions-aware RAG systems, content personalization, regulatory compliance, and organizational transformation. Key solutions discussed include enterprise-grade security controls, permissions-aware search indexing, magic prompts for user accessibility, knowledge graphs for data governance, and a "lab to factory floor" mentality for scaling AI adoption. Results shared include a telecommunications company resolving customer cases 47% faster, a software company saving 40 engineering years, and insurance providers achieving 2-5% sales improvements through personalized content generation.

title: Scaling Email Content Extraction Using LLMs in Production
short_summary: Yahoo Mail faced a coverage ceiling with their traditional sequence-to-sequence ML models for email extraction, achieving only 80% coverage from top senders while struggling with long-tail senders. They implemented LLMs via Google Cloud's Vertex AI to extract package tracking and receipt information from billions of daily emails. After overcoming challenges with hybrid on-premise/cloud infrastructure, GPU availability, and privacy compliance, Yahoo achieved 3.5 million new purchase receipt extractions daily with 94% standard domain coverage, 5.5 million package extractions with 99% tail domain coverage, 51% increase in extraction richness, and 16% reduction in tracking API errors—all deployed to 100% of US daily active users by December 2023.

title: Domain-Specific LLMs for Drug Discovery Biomarker Identification
short_summary: BenchSci developed an AI assistant platform called ASCEND to accelerate preclinical drug discovery by helping scientists understand disease biology, generate hypotheses, and design experiments. The platform uses a RAG architecture combining decade-old structured biomedical evidence data with domain-specific LLMs, including Google's Med-LM foundation model trained on medical data. By applying this to biomarker identification, scientists at major pharmaceutical companies reported a 40% increase in productivity, reducing processes that previously took months to just a few days.

title: Video Content Summarization and Metadata Enrichment for Streaming Platform
short_summary: Paramount+ partnered with Google Cloud Consulting to develop two generative AI use cases—video summarization and metadata extraction—to enhance content personalization and discovery on their streaming platform. The challenge was automating the processing of over 50,000 videos that previously required thousands of hours of manual labor for summaries and metadata tagging, while also reducing dependency on costly third-party metadata providers. Through an iterative "GenAI Jump Start" engagement, they developed MVP prototypes using Google's LLMs with techniques including few-shot prompting, function calling, prompt chaining, and LoRA fine-tuning for embeddings. The solution architecture includes transcription creation (with Whisper distill as fallback), generation pipelines with event triggers, and integration with personalization systems. Results validated their hypothesis that clear context with specific examples improves output quality, and established a roadmap for genre-specific prompt templates, summary scoring classifiers for A/B testing, and reinforcement learning fine-tuning.

title: Enterprise-Wide Virtual Assistant for Employee Knowledge Access
short_summary: BNY Mellon, a 250-year-old global financial services company, deployed an LLM-based virtual assistant to help 50,000 employees find information across the organization's vast knowledge base. The solution moved beyond traditional search by providing direct answers rather than returning lengthy documents. Built on Google Cloud's Vertex AI, the system evolved through iterative learning—addressing chunking strategy challenges, implementing Document AI for complex documents like cafeteria menus, and refining metadata tagging with content owners. The bank successfully rolled out the assistant enterprise-wide after starting with pilot departments, and is now focusing on automated evaluation of assistant performance, expanding to structured data, and building comprehensive metrics dashboards.

title: Scaling Voice AI with GPU-Accelerated Infrastructure
short_summary: ElevenLabs, a fast-growing voice AI company, leverages Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) with NVIDIA GPUs to power their generative voice technology at scale. The company faced the challenge of running computationally demanding AI workloads for text-to-speech, voice cloning, and real-time speech-to-speech translation across 29 languages. By utilizing GKE's GPU sharing strategies, autopilot features with NVIDIA H100 GPUs, and NVIDIA's NIM inference microservices, ElevenLabs achieved the ability to generate 600 hours of audio for every hour in a day, serving 41% of Fortune 500 companies with use cases spanning audiobooks, article narration, AI tutors, and dubbing studios.

title: Integrating Gemini for Natural Language Analytics in IoT Fleet Management
short_summary: Cox 2M, the commercial IoT division of Cox Communications, faced challenges with a lean analytics team spending excessive time on ad hoc internal requests, taking up to a week to answer single business questions. By implementing ThoughtSpot's Sage platform integrated with Google BigQuery and powered by Gemini LLM, they reduced time-to-insight by 88%, from over a week to under an hour. The solution enables non-technical business users to query data using natural language, with Gemini providing automatic change analysis, natural language narrations of insights, and the ability to summarize dashboard changes. The production system handles massive IoT scale (200+ sensor messages per hour, 11.4 billion assets tracked) while enabling self-service analytics that allows the analytics team to focus on high-value customer-facing outcomes.

title: Network Operations Transformation with GenAI and AIOps
short_summary: Vodafone is leveraging GenAI and traditional AI/ML approaches on Google Cloud Platform to transform its network operations lifecycle. The company faced challenges with legacy OSS (Operational Support Systems), siloed data across performance management tools, and difficulty correlating network data with customer experience insights. Their solution involves migrating network data sources to GCP (over 2 petabytes), building unified performance management systems to replace 100+ proprietary tools, and deploying GenAI copilots for complex incident management. Key outcomes include a planned 50% reduction in OSS tools (600 applications), improved cross-functional collaboration, faster insight-to-action cycles for network engineers, and the development of "smart CapEx" GenAI-powered network investment planning that combines commercial, customer experience, and network data.

title: AI-Powered Natural Language Flight Search Implementation
short_summary: Alaska Airlines partnered with Google Cloud to develop a natural language destination search feature powered by Gemini, addressing the challenge of travel planning when guests have flexible destinations. The solution transforms the traditional transactional flight booking experience into an immersive, conversational interface where travelers can describe their ideal trip in natural language (e.g., "woodsy cabin getaway" or "mountain biking with family, under $200"). The system uses Gemini for understanding natural language queries, coordinates with Alaska Airlines' flight APIs through function calling for real-time availability and pricing, integrates Google Maps for visualization, and generates personalized destination copy dynamically. The team went from inception to production-quality implementation in weeks, leveraging their modernized cloud-native infrastructure and existing Google partnerships.

title: LLM-Powered Multi-Tool Architecture for Oil & Gas Data Exploration
short_summary: DXC Technology collaborated with AWS to build an AI assistant for the oil and gas industry that enables users to explore and analyze diverse data types through natural language queries. The solution uses Anthropic's Claude models on Amazon Bedrock with an intelligent router that directs queries to specialized tools optimized for different data types including text documents, tabular production data, and industry-specific LAS (Log ASCII Standard) files. By implementing query rewriting for conversational context, Retrieval-Augmented Generation for semantic search, and custom code-generating agents for data analysis, the solution transforms data exploration workflows that previously took hours into minutes, helping reduce time to first oil for DXC's customers in the energy sector.

title: Text-to-SQL System for Complex Healthcare Database Queries
short_summary: MSD, a global pharmaceutical company, collaborated with AWS Generative AI Innovation Center to implement a text-to-SQL solution that translates natural language questions into SQL queries for complex healthcare databases. The solution uses Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet on Amazon Bedrock, featuring custom lookup tools for coded columns, detailed column descriptions, and few-shot learning. This approach enables analysts to extract insights from databases like DE-SynPUF without writing complex SQL manually, reportedly reducing query time from hours to minutes and democratizing data access across technical and non-technical staff.

title: Transforming Insurance Agent Support with RAG-Powered Chat Assistant
short_summary: InsuranceDekho, an Indian InsurTech platform working with over 150,000 insurance agents and 49 insurance companies, faced significant delays in responding to customer queries as agents frequently needed to consult subject matter experts (SMEs) for policy-specific questions. They implemented a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) chat assistant using Amazon Bedrock with Anthropic's Claude Haiku, combined with Amazon OpenSearch Service as a vector database and Redis on Amazon ElastiCache for caching. The solution enables agents to autonomously answer customer queries about policy coverages, exclusions, and plan features without SME involvement, resulting in an 80% reduction in response time and improved sales and customer service experience.

title: Building Goal-Oriented Retrieval Agents for Low-Latency Recommendations at Scale
short_summary: Faber Labs developed GORA (Goal Oriented Retrieval Agents), a specialized agent system designed to optimize subjective relevance ranking for various business KPIs. The system addresses the challenge of personalizing user experiences in real-time across e-commerce, healthcare, and financial services. By combining large event models trained from scratch with open-source LLMs, implementing a Rust-based backend for ultra-low latency, and using end-to-end reinforcement learning for unified goal optimization, they achieved response times suitable for conversational AI while reporting over 200% improvements in conversion rates and average order values for their clients.

title: Building a Tool Calling Platform for LLM Agents
short_summary: Arcade AI addresses a critical gap in the LLM agent ecosystem: the inability for agents to take authenticated actions on behalf of users. The problem is that current agent frameworks conflate tool execution with orchestration, limiting scalability and capability. Most tools are restricted to simple HTTP requests protected by API keys, preventing agents from performing truly useful tasks like sending emails or managing documents as users. Arcade AI's solution is a dedicated tool calling platform that separates tool execution from agent orchestration, provides a robust authentication/authorization layer for user-delegated actions, and treats tools as first-class software artifacts requiring proper versioning, testing, and CI/CD. The platform includes a Tool SDK for building tools, an engine for serving them, and an OpenAI-compatible API that handles tool injection and execution automatically. While still early stage, the platform enables demonstrations like sending Twilio messages and creating Notion documents through conversational AI interfaces.

title: Building a Knowledge as a Service Platform with LLMs and Developer Community Data
short_summary: Stack Overflow addresses the challenge of LLM accuracy and trust in AI-assisted development by positioning its massive repository of 60 million questions and answers (approximately 40 billion tokens) as a critical data infrastructure layer for LLM training and fine-tuning. The company developed the Overflow API product to provide structured, real-time access to curated developer knowledge for major AI partners including Google Gemini, OpenAI, and GitHub Copilot, while also integrating generative AI capabilities into their enterprise products. Their approach reportedly demonstrates approximately 20 percentage point improvements in open-source LLM accuracy when fine-tuned with Stack Overflow data, creating a symbiotic ecosystem where AI companies gain high-quality training data while the developer community benefits from AI-enhanced tools across multiple interfaces.

title: Agent-Based AI Assistants for Enterprise and E-commerce Applications
short_summary: Prosus, a global technology group operating e-commerce platforms across 100 countries, developed two agent-based AI systems: Tokan, an internal enterprise assistant deployed to over 20,000 employees across 24 companies, and OLX Magic, a consumer-facing e-commerce discovery assistant. Starting in 2022 before ChatGPT's release, they pursued a "collective discovery" approach where employees could experiment with LLMs. Through iterative improvements including the introduction of agents in January 2024, they reduced hallucination rates from 10% to 1%, achieved approximately 48 minutes of time saved per employee per day, and scaled to nearly 1 million requests per month. The cost per interaction stabilized around 25 cents despite increased complexity, with token costs dropping 98% while tokens per question increased due to agentic workflows. For iFood (their Brazil-based food delivery company), the data exploration agent automated 21% of data requests and reduced time-to-insight by 75%.

title: AI-Powered SRE Agent for Production Infrastructure Management
short_summary: Cleric AI has built an AI-powered Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) agent designed to free engineers from the operational burden of production environments. The system addresses the growing complexity of distributed infrastructure (particularly Kubernetes clusters) by using an LLM-based reasoning engine that can automatically respond to alerts, investigate potential root causes across hundreds of systems, and present concise diagnoses to engineers. The agent maintains a knowledge graph of infrastructure relationships, learns from past investigations, and uses confidence scoring to determine when to surface findings. While the product is live with enterprise customers, full autonomous remediation remains guarded behind human approval, with the roadmap progressing from diagnosis to remediation to preventative actions.

title: Building Production-Grade AI Agents: Overcoming Reasoning and Tool Challenges
short_summary: Kentauros AI is developing GUI navigation agents capable of performing complex, open-ended tasks through visual interfaces. The team has identified three core problem categories—"big brain" (strategic reasoning), "little brain" (tactical decisions), and "tool brain" (precision of interfaces)—that cause cascading errors in agentic systems. Their solution involves a multi-component architecture with specialized models for different cognitive functions, a sophisticated memory system for learning from both successes and failures, fine-tuned click accuracy models achieving up to 90% precision, and a roadmap toward hot-swappable skills and reinforcement learning. While still iterating through agent generations (G2, G3, working toward G4-G5), they demonstrate practical lessons for production LLM agents including the critical importance of retrieval mechanisms over simple data storage and the value of domain-specific tooling.

title: Leveraging Vector Embeddings for Financial Fraud Detection
short_summary: NICE Actimize, a leader in financial crime prevention, is exploring vector embeddings as a scalable approach to enhance fraud detection systems. The team converts tabular transaction data into text representations, then uses embedding models (such as RoBERTa variants) to generate semantic vectors that capture the essence of fraud patterns. This approach enables similarity detection between different fraud schemes (like Nigerian prince scams and Ponzi schemes) despite surface-level text differences, while maintaining the low-latency requirements essential for real-time transaction processing. The research demonstrates promising results in identifying semantic similarities between fraud narratives with minimal code, though challenges remain in converting structured data to meaningful text and handling numerical representations.

title: Generative AI Integration in Financial Crime Detection Platform
short_summary: NICE Actimize embedded generative AI into their cloud-native financial crime detection platform (Excite) to address the challenge of creating complex analytical artifacts for fraud, money laundering, and market abuse detection. By implementing GPT-based agents with extensive prompt engineering and guardrails, they enabled analysts to use free text to create aggregations, features, and models directly in production without requiring deep knowledge of data schemas or SPEL expressions. The solution also extends to MLOps with AI co-pilots that help operations teams understand ML features and autonomous agents that can diagnose and fix issues in production ML models. While the outputs still require validation through testing pipelines due to reliability concerns, the approach significantly reduces time-to-market and enables frictionless self-service analytics.

title: Natural Language to SQL System with Production Safeguards for Contact Center Analytics
short_summary: NICE implemented a text-to-SQL solution enabling users to query their contact center metadata database using natural language. The system translates user questions into SQL queries, handles multi-tenant security by adding tenant filters post-query generation, applies intelligent defaults for time ranges and record limits, and provides visualization recommendations along with textual explanations of the results. The solution addresses real-world production challenges beyond basic demos, including follow-up question handling, relevancy guardrails, and query caching for refreshed data scenarios.

title: Troubleshooting and Optimizing RAG Pipelines: Lessons from Production
short_summary: Lemonade, a technology-oriented insurance company serving millions of customers globally, shared lessons learned from building and optimizing RAG pipelines in production. The presentation covered common pain points in RAG systems including missing content, retriever failures, re-ranker issues, and output formatting problems, along with practical solutions such as data cleaning, hyperparameter tuning, embedding fine-tuning, query rewriting, and various advanced retrieval strategies. The company notably processes 50% of insurance claims fully automatically and has used a chat interface for customer interactions since 2015, making RAG a critical component of their customer-facing systems.

title: Implementing Question-Answering Over Sales Conversations with Deal Me at Gong
short_summary: Gong developed "Ask Me" (or "D Me"), a natural language Q&A feature that allows sales managers and representatives to query complex B2B deal data containing hundreds of emails and thousands of calls. The system aggregates information from multiple sources (calls, emails, CRM metadata) and uses LLMs to provide real-time answers within a 5-second latency target. Key challenges addressed included handling long context windows, reducing hallucinations through validation layers, managing costs at scale (4,000+ companies with thousands of users each), and adding citation capabilities to link answers back to source materials. Notably, analysis of user queries revealed that 70% of questions could be answered by existing specialized features with better accuracy, leading to a hybrid approach combining free-form Q&A with intelligent routing to purpose-built tools.

title: Building Price Prediction and Similar Item Search Models for E-commerce
short_summary: eBay developed a machine learning system to help sellers price their products, particularly sports trading cards, by using embedding-based retrieval to find similar historically-sold items. The solution addresses the challenge of pricing second-hand and niche products where traditional text search fails due to abbreviations, slang, and domain-specific terminology. The team trained custom BERT-based embedding models using click-through data from user searches, implemented both semantic similarity and direct price prediction approaches, and discovered an inherent trade-off between retrieval quality and pricing accuracy, ultimately developing a multi-task learning approach that allows tuning the balance between these objectives.

title: Automated Sign Language Translation Using Large Language Models
short_summary: VSL Labs addresses the critical accessibility gap for the 500 million deaf and hard-of-hearing people worldwide by building an automated English-to-American Sign Language (ASL) translation platform. Their solution uses generative AI models including GPT-4 and T5 to translate text into sign language glosses with "stage directions" that control a 3D avatar's movements, facial expressions, and body positioning. The platform serves various use cases including airport announcements, video content, and real-time communication, addressing the shortage and high cost of human interpreters while maintaining high-quality translations that include the crucial non-manual markers (facial expressions, body movements) that make sign language comprehensible.

title: Automated Sports Commentary Generation using LLMs
short_summary: WSC Sport developed an automated sports commentary system that generates complete game recaps with AI-powered narration in multiple languages. The system reduces production time from 3-4 hours to just 1-2 minutes by combining highlight detection, LLM-based script generation with dynamic prompt engineering, and text-to-speech synthesis. The solution addresses challenges including hallucination prevention, maintaining synchronization with video, avoiding repetitive language, and handling sport-specific terminology across leagues like NBA, NFL, NHL, and European football leagues.

title: Vector Search and RAG Implementation for Enhanced User Search Experience
short_summary: This presentation by a Couchbase developer advocate explores how vector search integrates with generative AI to improve user experiences. The talk covers the fundamentals of vector embeddings, similarity measurements, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), then showcases two production case studies: Revolut's fraud detection system "Sherlock" that uses vector search to identify dissimilar (anomalous) transactions, saving customers over $3 million annually and catching 96% of fraudulent transactions in under 50 milliseconds; and Scen.it's multimedia search platform that enables text-based search across 500,000+ video clips for marketing campaigns. The presentation emphasizes when to use vector search versus traditional keyword search based on use case requirements.

title: LLM-Powered 3D Model Generation for 3D Printing
short_summary: Build Great AI developed a prototype application called DesignBench that uses multiple LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 3.5, Llama 3.1) to generate 3D-printable objects from natural language descriptions. The system addresses the challenge of making 3D design accessible to non-experts by having LLMs generate CAD code (OpenSCAD) that renders into STL files for 3D printing. While spatial reasoning remains challenging for current LLMs (August 2024), the application compensates by running multiple models simultaneously with different prompting strategies, allowing users to iterate quickly on designs. Early results show significant time savings compared to traditional CAD software—reducing hours of work to minutes—though the complexity ceiling remains lower than professional CAD tools.

title: Training and Deploying MPT: Lessons Learned in Large Scale LLM Development
short_summary: MosaicML (now part of Databricks) shares practical lessons learned from training their open-source MPT (MosaicML Pretrained Transformer) models at scale. The case study addresses common misconceptions about LLM training costs, demonstrating that a GPT-3 quality 7B parameter model can be trained for approximately $250,000 rather than the $1M+ most practitioners expect. Key insights cover the full LLMOps lifecycle including planning and evaluation criteria, compute budgeting using scaling laws, data preparation best practices, distributed training infrastructure, fault tolerance at scale, and organizational processes for managing expensive training runs.

title: Enhancing E-commerce Search with LLMs at Scale
short_summary: Instacart faced challenges with traditional NLP-based search including handling tail queries (20+ million), extracting product attributes across thousands of categories, and understanding complex user intents like "breakfast ideas to lose weight." By integrating LLMs into their search stack, they improved query understanding, product attribute extraction, query tagging, and merchandising personalization. The solution involves both online and offline LLM processing, with careful attention to cost, latency, prompt engineering, and content moderation. Key results include better handling of tail queries, automated product attribute extraction that previously required manual domain experts, enhanced new product discovery, and the ability to understand broad conceptual queries without building complex knowledge graphs.

title: Panel Discussion: Scaling Generative AI in Enterprise - Challenges and Best Practices
short_summary: This panel discussion brought together AI leaders from Google Cloud, Symbol AI, Chain ML, and Deloitte to explore generative AI adoption across industries. Panelists discussed key use cases including customer service automation, summarization of communication data, self-service analytics, and developer productivity tools. They identified barriers to production deployment such as regulatory constraints in healthcare and finance, organizational AI literacy gaps, data platform maturity issues, and the need for robust evaluation frameworks. The experts emphasized value-driven approaches to AI adoption, the importance of choosing appropriate foundational models, building experimentation cultures, and the emerging trend toward domain-specific models and autonomous agents.

title: Systematic LLM Evaluation Framework for Content Generation
short_summary: Canva's machine learning team developed a systematic LLM evaluation framework to ensure quality when transforming diverse and messy user design inputs into "delightful" content formats like summaries, emails, and songs. The solution involved defining quality criteria upfront, converting them into measurable metrics (information score, intent score, semantic order score, tone score, and format score), and using both rule-based evaluators and LLM-as-a-judge approaches to score outputs. The evaluation system enabled effective prompt engineering with regression testing capabilities, ensuring prompt improvements for specific metrics didn't negatively impact other quality dimensions.

title: Production LLM Implementation for Customer Support Response Generation
short_summary: Stripe developed an LLM-based system to help support agents respond more efficiently to customer inquiries by prompting them with relevant, accurate responses. The team discovered that out-of-the-box GPT models produced factually incorrect answers for domain-specific questions, leading them to build a sequential pipeline of fine-tuned GPT models including trigger classification, topic classification, answer generation, and tone adjustment, combined with a RAG-like approach. While offline evaluations showed strong performance, the team encountered significant challenges with agent adoption and learned critical lessons about the gap between offline metrics and online performance. Key takeaways included the importance of breaking complex problems into ML-manageable steps, prioritizing online monitoring from the start, and recognizing that data quality improvements consistently outperformed model architecture upgrades for domain-specific problems.

title: Cost Reduction Through Fine-tuning: Healthcare Chatbot and E-commerce Product Classification
short_summary: Airtrain presents two case studies demonstrating how fine-tuning smaller open-source models (Mistral 7B) can match the performance of larger models like GPT-3.5/GPT-4 while reducing inference costs by up to 94%. A healthcare chatbot company needed on-premise deployment for privacy compliance and achieved comparable quality metrics to GPT-3.5 after fine-tuning. An e-commerce unicorn improved product category classification accuracy from 47% (untuned) to 94% (fine-tuned), exceeding both human accuracy (76%) and enabling cost-effective processing at scale. The key success factors included establishing robust evaluation harnesses, curating high-quality training datasets, and following a structured approach: prototype with best-in-class APIs first, validate the use case works, then fine-tune for production cost optimization.

title: Scaling Self-Hosted LLMs with GPU Optimization and Load Testing
short_summary: Fuzzy Labs, an MLOps consultancy based in Manchester, UK, built a self-hosted RAG-based LLM system for a technology company selling developer tools. The customer needed to improve developer experience by making their complex product documentation more navigable through an LLM-powered assistant. The initial architecture using FastAPI and Hugging Face pipelines with Mistral 7B showed poor performance (11+ second latency, breaking under minimal load). By implementing vLLM for optimized inference (achieving 10x throughput improvement through paged attention) and Ray Serve for horizontal autoscaling across GPU instances, they achieved sub-second inference times capable of supporting hundreds of concurrent users in production.

title: Improving LLM Accuracy and Evaluation in Enterprise Customer Analytics
short_summary: Echo AI, an LLM-native customer analytics platform, partnered with Log10 to deploy reliable AI systems for enterprise customers processing millions of customer conversations. The challenge was achieving high accuracy in multi-step LLM analysis pipelines where each conversation could be analyzed 50 different ways by 20 different models, while signing six and seven-figure enterprise contracts. Log10 provided an LLMOps infrastructure layer including logging, observability, auto-feedback systems that bootstrap with as few as 25-50 labeled examples, and auto-tuning capabilities. The partnership enabled Echo AI to achieve a 20-point F1 score improvement in their LLM applications, reduce prompt optimization time from weeks to hours, and successfully deploy to some of the largest LLM-native enterprise contracts in the market.

title: Production Agents: Real-world Implementations of LLM-powered Autonomous Systems
short_summary: This panel discussion features three practitioners sharing their experiences deploying LLM-powered agents in production. Sam discusses building a personal assistant with real-time user feedback loops and router-based multi-agent architectures. Div demonstrates MultiOn, a browser automation agent that uses compressed DOM parsing to control web interfaces. Devin presents a GitHub bot that navigates codebases to help with feature requests. Key themes include the importance of routing layers to constrain agent behavior, checkpointing for reliability, streaming outputs for better UX, and strategic use of GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 based on task complexity. All presenters emphasize that production agents are systems, not just models, requiring careful architecture around planning, execution, and human-in-the-loop interventions.

title: Production LLM Systems: Document Processing and Real Estate Agent Co-pilot Case Studies
short_summary: This webinar presents two distinct LLMOps case studies: Docugami, a document engineering company that uses hierarchical chunking, XML knowledge graphs, and custom fine-tuned models for document understanding and RAG; and Rehat, a real estate SaaS platform building "Lucy," an AI copilot using OpenAI function calling. Both teams share practical lessons on debugging complex chains with LangSmith, creating evaluation pipelines, managing the transition from prototype to production, handling cost and latency constraints, and establishing continuous improvement workflows using human feedback and synthetic test cases.

title: Building a Production-Ready Multi-Agent Coding Assistant
short_summary: Replit developed an AI coding agent ("Replit Agent") to enable users to build web applications from natural language prompts without writing code. The solution employs a multi-agent architecture with specialized sub-agents (manager, editors, verifier), uses Claude 3.5 Sonnet as the primary model, and generates tool calls as code rather than using function calling APIs for improved reliability. Since launching in September 2024, the system has processed hundreds of thousands of runs in production, with users spending hours on single projects and seeing working prototypes within 90 seconds.

title: Dark Vessel Detection System Using SAR Imagery and ML
short_summary: The Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) developed an ML-based system to detect illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing by identifying "dark vessels" that disable their tracking transponders. Using synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery from satellites, the team created a large annotated dataset (243,000 annotations across 82 million square kilometers) and ran public challenges to develop detection models. The resulting system was deployed to SeaVision, a maritime domain awareness platform used by over 100 countries, enabling detection of vessels that would otherwise be invisible to traditional monitoring systems. This addressed a significant environmental and economic problem where one in five fish caught globally originates from illegal fishing.

title: Automating Enterprise Workflows with Foundation Models in Healthcare
short_summary: The researchers present aCLAr (Demonstrate, Execute, Validate framework), a system that uses multimodal foundation models to automate enterprise workflows, particularly in healthcare settings. The system addresses limitations of traditional RPA by enabling passive learning from demonstrations, human-like UI navigation, and self-monitoring capabilities. They successfully demonstrated the system automating a real healthcare workflow in Epic EHR, showing how foundation models can be leveraged for complex enterprise automation without requiring API integration.

title: Panel Discussion: Best Practices for LLMs in Production
short_summary: This panel discussion brought together six industry experts to share practical insights on deploying generative AI solutions in production environments. The panelists addressed key challenges including the ease of prototyping versus the difficulty of production deployment, the critical importance of observability and evaluation pipelines, hardware constraints and GPU availability, and the distinction between RAG and fine-tuning approaches. Key recommendations included starting with API providers like OpenAI for rapid prototyping, implementing comprehensive observability from day one, focusing on user feedback as the primary evaluation metric, and treating production as the starting point rather than the end goal of ML development.

title: Production Intent Recognition System for Enterprise Chatbots
short_summary: This case study covers two presentations from a machine learning meetup focusing on chatbot development in production environments. FeedYou, a chatbot platform company, shared their journey using NLP.js for intent matching, discovering that lightweight JavaScript-based models outperformed more complex solutions like FastText for their use case of short user inputs and per-chatbot model training. They developed validation strategies to detect overlapping intents and leveraged named entity recognition to simplify model complexity. Prometeus AI presented their Flowstorm conversational AI platform, which evolved from their Alexa Prize-winning chatbot experience, implementing hierarchical sub-dialog structures with multi-level intent recognition (local, global, and out-of-domain) and GPT-2 generative models for handling out-of-domain responses. Both presentations emphasized the practical challenges of building production chatbots with rapid model training, modular dialog design, and handling the reality that most user inputs are very short (1-2 words) while longer inputs have significantly lower match rates.

title: LLM Production Case Studies: Consulting Database Search, Automotive Showroom Assistant, and Banking Development Tools
short_summary: This presentation from Globant covers five real-world LLMOps case studies across consulting, automotive, banking, and enterprise AI platforms, highlighting common production challenges including retrieval accuracy issues, hallucinations from cloud provider services, non-canonical data sources, and premature technology adoption. Key workarounds involved layering LLMs for metadata generation and filtering, using text-to-SQL approaches when vector similarity proved inadequate, implementing stage-by-stage evaluation to isolate failure points, and learning to challenge client assumptions early rather than inheriting technical debt from poorly scoped POCs.

title: Building and Testing a Production LLM-Powered Quiz Application
short_summary: This case study documents the journey of building "Quizaic," a trivia quiz application that evolved from a limited static-content prototype to a fully dynamic, generative AI-powered system using Google's Gemini models. The original 2016 concept was constrained by the Open Trivia Database's limited topics, questions, and English-only format. After the March 2023 LLM explosion, the developers integrated Gemini for unlimited quiz generation on any topic in any language, plus Imagen for dynamic image generation. The solution uses Flutter for cross-platform UI, Cloud Run for hosting, Firestore for real-time data, and Vertex AI for LLM integration. Key lessons learned include the importance of defensive coding against inconsistent LLM outputs, prompt engineering specificity, model version pinning, and developing automated validation pipelines using LLMs to assess quiz accuracy—achieving 91% accuracy with Gemini Ultra compared to 70% with Gemini Pro.

title: Scaling LLM Infrastructure: Building and Operating 24K GPU Clusters for LLaMA Training
short_summary: Meta's production engineering team presents the infrastructure challenges and solutions for training LLaMA 3, a generative AI model requiring 24,000 GPUs operating for months. The problem involved a fundamental shift from training numerous small recommendation models (8-500 GPUs each) to training a single massive model on 15 trillion tokens. The solution required full-stack optimizations across hardware (adapting chassis from 500W to 700W GPUs, managing thermal throttling), networking (building parallel RoCE and InfiniBand clusters with custom load balancing), and software (implementing tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism with network topology-aware scheduling). The team achieved 95% training efficiency on a 24-hour rolling window basis, overcoming challenges like GPU failures, thermal issues, and synchronization bottlenecks that could halt thousands of GPUs simultaneously.

title: Best Practices for LLM Production Deployments: Evaluation, Prompt Management, and Fine-tuning
short_summary: This talk by a HumanLoop co-founder distills lessons learned from working with companies ranging from large enterprises like Duolingo to cutting-edge startups on deploying LLMs in production. The speaker identifies three critical success factors: systematic evaluation frameworks (citing GitHub Copilot's acceptance rate and code retention metrics as exemplary), proper prompt management with versioning and collaboration capabilities, and leveraging fine-tuning to improve cost, latency, and domain-specific performance. Companies that neglect these areas often fail to achieve results or conclude that LLMs cannot solve their problems, while those who invest in evaluation infrastructure consistently outperform. The talk emphasizes that evaluation should be designed into the product from the start, combining implicit and explicit user feedback with automated metrics.

title: Automated Software Development Insights and Communication Platform
short_summary: Blueprint AI, a startup founded in late 2022, addresses the challenge of bridging business-technical communication gaps and providing real-time visibility into software development progress. By connecting to tools like Jira and GitHub, their system continuously ingests and analyzes development data using LLMs to generate intelligent reports that surface what happened, identify related conversations and blockers, and notify stakeholders of relevant updates. The founder shares extensive insights on prompt engineering practices, the challenges of LLM reliability and performance in production, and practical approaches to building AI-native applications from his experience since the GPT-3 private beta in 2020.

title: Building Production-Ready LLM Agents with State Management and Workflow Engineering
short_summary: This technical session presented by Gal Peretz, VP R&D at Renovai and co-host of the Lang Talks podcast, demonstrates hands-on approaches to building LLM agents for production environments. The presentation addresses key challenges including the limitations of standalone LLMs (such as hallucinations and inability to perform certain tasks like counting), the need for tool integration to fill knowledge gaps, state and memory management for multi-turn conversations, and workflow engineering for complex multi-agent systems. The solution involves using LangChain and LangGraph frameworks to build agent executors with checkpointing for state persistence, implementing different routing strategies (prompt-based React vs. fine-tuned OpenAI functions), and constructing multi-agent architectures with supervisor-researcher-blogger patterns. The session also explores multimodal agents using GPT-4 Vision for web navigation, emphasizing the importance of tracing tools like LangSmith for debugging production agent systems.

title: Building Production AI Agents with Vector Databases and Automated Data Collection
short_summary: Devin Kearns shares 18 months of experience building autonomous AI agents for business automation. The problem addressed is the high cost of scaling businesses through hiring, particularly for repetitive tasks like inbox management, lead qualification, and customer follow-up. The solution involves architecting multi-agent systems using n8n as a workflow platform, Pinecone for vector databases, and structured prompt engineering with extensive examples. The approach emphasizes treating agents as virtual employees with proper onboarding (data), access to tools, and clear job functions. Results include reduced operational costs, automated lead generation workflows, and a scalable framework where specialized agents handle distinct workflows within job functions rather than requiring complex multi-agent coordination.

title: LLM Applications in Education: Personalized Learning and Assessment Systems
short_summary: This panel discussion, organized by Schmidt Futures and featuring LangChain's founder Harrison Chase, explored how LLMs are being deployed in educational technology. Three case studies were presented: Podzi, a nonprofit using GPT-3.5 Turbo for question generation and tutoring chatbots with spaced repetition learning; ITEL (Intelligent Textbooks for Enhanced Lifelong Learning), a Vanderbilt research project using LangChain for question generation, output parsing, and vector store embeddings for summary evaluation; and The Learning Agency Lab, which creates open datasets and runs Kaggle competitions to crowdsource LLM-based solutions for automated writing evaluation. Key challenges discussed include math accuracy limitations, hallucination concerns, personalization at scale, and the need for teacher oversight. The panel emphasized LangChain's role in connecting LLMs to external data sources, enabling personalization, and providing developer tooling for production-ready educational applications.

title: Production Agents: Routing, Testing and Browser Automation Case Studies
short_summary: This panel discussion features three practitioners sharing their experiences building LLM-powered agents for production use cases. Sam discusses building a personal assistant with real-time user feedback mechanisms and router-based agent architectures to manage tool complexity. Div presents MultiOn, a browser automation agent that can control web interfaces to complete tasks like ordering food or posting on social media, using DOM parsing and compressed representations to stay within token limits. Devin shares work on using LLMs' code understanding capabilities for non-coding engineering tasks like documentation and issue triage. Key themes include the importance of routing layers to simplify agent complexity, checkpointing for graceful degradation, human-in-the-loop interventions, caching strategies for speed optimization, and the challenges of testing non-deterministic agent outputs in production environments.

title: Practical LLM Deployment: From Evaluation to Fine-tuning
short_summary: This case study explores practical lessons learned from deploying LLMs in production across multiple industries, drawing from Hamill Hussein's experience at Parlance Labs, a research and consultancy focused on helping companies operationalize LLMs. The discussion covers the critical importance of data-centric approaches, robust evaluation strategies that go beyond "vibe checks," the iterative nature of LLM development, and practical fine-tuning techniques. Key insights include the finding that traditional data science skills (data cleaning, metric design, evaluation) are highly transferable to LLMOps work, that developer velocity and rapid iteration cycles are crucial for success, and that most production LLM work involves looking at data and building custom evaluation tools rather than training models from scratch. Specific examples from clients like ReChat (a real estate CRM) demonstrate how these principles apply in practice.

title: Rapid Development and Deployment of Enterprise LLM Features Through Centralized LLM Service Architecture
