short_summary: PagerDuty faced the challenge of rapidly developing and deploying generative AI features into their incident management platform within just two months following the release of ChatGPT. They built a centralized LLM API service that abstracted LLM complexity, enabled standardized access across teams, and supported multiple providers including OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and AWS Bedrock. The solution featured Kubernetes-based microservices architecture, robust security controls, and comprehensive monitoring via Datadog and Sumo Logic. The team successfully released multiple GenAI features including AI-generated runbooks, automated status updates, postmortem report generation, a Slack-based chatbot assistant, and automation digest summaries—all deployed to production within the aggressive two-month timeline through cross-functional collaboration between applied scientists, ML engineers, and product teams.

title: Building Robust Enterprise Search with LLMs and Traditional IR
short_summary: Glean, founded in 2019 by ex-Google engineers, built an AI-powered enterprise search platform that indexes content across SaaS applications to help employees find information. Rather than relying solely on modern vector search techniques, they employ a hybrid approach combining traditional information retrieval with semantic search, layered with personalization signals based on organizational structure and user interactions. The platform evolved from pure search to an employee portal with features like aggregated notifications, trending documents, and Go links. Their approach emphasizes rigorous ranking algorithm tuning over chasing cutting-edge AI buzzwords, resulting in a billion-dollar valuation and adoption by Fortune 50 companies including Databricks, Canva, and Duolingo.

title: Building a Foundation Model Operations Platform
short_summary: Humanloop pivoted from automated labeling to become an LLMOps platform helping engineers manage, version, and evaluate prompts in production LLM applications. The company addressed the challenge that engineers face when moving from prototype to production with LLMs, providing tools for prompt engineering, versioning, collaboration between technical and non-technical team members, and comprehensive evaluation across development, monitoring, and regression testing phases. The platform now serves enterprise customers like Duolingo and Gusto, with features for collecting three types of user feedback (votes, actions, and corrections), running evaluations using code or LLMs, and supporting fine-tuning workflows.

title: Building a Silicon Brain for Universal Enterprise Search
short_summary: Dropbox, traditionally a file syncing company, is undergoing a strategic transformation to become an AI-first productivity platform. CEO Drew Houston, who has personally spent over 400 hours coding with LLMs, led the company's pivot starting in early 2023 to leverage AI for solving knowledge work challenges. The company developed Dropbox Dash, a universal search product that uses RAG and semantic search to help users find content across multiple platforms (including competitors like Google Drive and OneDrive). The solution addresses the fragmented nature of modern knowledge work where users have multiple disconnected search boxes across various tools. By focusing on the application layer rather than competing in the commoditizing LLM space, Dropbox aims to become the trusted interface for organizing, finding, and sharing content across the entire digital workspace.

title: Building a Horizontal Enterprise Agent Platform with Infrastructure-First Approach
short_summary: Dust.tt evolved from a developer framework competing with LangChain to an enterprise agent infrastructure platform. The company addressed the challenge of deploying AI agents within organizations by building maintained integrations to internal data sources (Notion, Slack, Salesforce, etc.), providing a model-agnostic interface supporting GPT-4, Claude, and other frontier models, and creating accessible tooling for non-technical users to build agents. The platform reports exceptional adoption metrics with 60-70% weekly active users across entire companies and up to 88% daily active users in some deployments, demonstrating the value of horizontal agent platforms that emerge use cases organically rather than prescribing vertical solutions.

title: Evolution from Open-Ended LLM Agents to Guided Workflows
short_summary: Lindy.ai evolved from an open-ended LLM-powered agent approach to a structured, workflow-based platform that constrains AI agents to improve reliability. The company found that giving agents "rails" through visual workflow builders with explicit triggers, required actions, and structured outputs dramatically improved reliability compared to their original approach of just providing a large prompt field and tools. With Claude 3.5 Sonnet, the model is no longer the bottleneck—instead, integration quality, workflow design, and user experience are the primary challenges. The platform now supports complex multi-step automations for meeting scheduling, customer support, email processing, and more, with features like memory management, cross-agent collaboration, and a "poor man's RLHF" system for continuous improvement from user feedback.

title: Pitfalls and Best Practices for Production LLM Applications
short_summary: This presentation from Humanloop shares lessons learned from observing hundreds of LLM projects succeed and fail in production over more than a year of operating their developer platform. The talk identifies four key pitfalls: lack of objective evaluation, inadequate prompt management infrastructure, premature optimization with chains and agents, and underestimating fine-tuning. Best practices include implementing systematic evaluation with user feedback signals, proper versioning and collaboration tools for prompts, starting with the best available models before optimizing, and leveraging fine-tuning for improved performance, cost, and latency. Case studies from GitHub Copilot and Phind demonstrate successful implementations of these principles.

title: Large Language Models in Production Round Table Discussion: Latency, Cost and Trust Considerations
short_summary: This roundtable discussion brings together practitioners from finance (Digits), venture capital (Unusual Ventures), research (Facebook AI Research), and tooling (Bountiful) to explore the practical realities of deploying large language models in production. The conversation covers the spectrum from simple API-wrapper applications to complex agentic workflows, examining key trade-offs between cost, latency, and quality. Specific production experiences are shared, including Digits' approach to self-hosting open-source models for financial data processing, with techniques like quantization, pruning, and teacher-student distillation to reduce latency. The discussion also addresses trust and hallucination mitigation through human-in-the-loop validation, content filtering, and retrieval-augmented generation patterns.

title: Cost Optimization and Performance Panel Discussion: Strategies for Running LLMs in Production
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together practitioners from Neeva (search), Intercom (chatbots), Prompt Layer (LLM monitoring), and OctoML (model deployment) to share real-world strategies for managing the cost and latency challenges of running large language models in production. Key solutions discussed include moving from foundational APIs to self-hosted smaller models through knowledge distillation and structured pruning, achieving dramatic cost reductions (from $40/hour on A100 GPUs to $0.30 on A10 spot instances) and latency improvements (from 3+ seconds to 400ms). The panelists also cover practical monitoring approaches including synthetic evaluation with critic models, simple pre-filtering classifiers to reduce API calls, and the importance of understanding your use case before over-engineering optimization solutions.

title: Building a Generic Recommender System API with Privacy-First Design
short_summary: Slack's ML engineering team built a generic recommender API to serve multiple internal use cases for recommending users and channels across the platform. The solution addressed the challenge of repeatedly solving similar recommendation problems by creating a simple, reusable API that product managers and engineers could easily integrate with, while maintaining strict data privacy requirements. The team developed a feature engineering pipeline using logged online features, employed hand-tuned models for cold-start scenarios that could later be replaced by ML models showing 10%+ improvement, and built the system to scale across hundreds of different recommendation contexts while ensuring zero data leakage between customer organizations.

title: Domain-Specific Small Language Models for Call Center Intelligence
short_summary: Deepgram addresses the challenge of deploying language AI for call center applications by advocating for small, domain-specific language models (SLMs) over large foundational models. The problem stems from the fact that large language models (100B+ parameters) are too slow, expensive, and poorly suited for the highly specific, messy nature of real call center conversations. Their solution involves transfer learning a 500M parameter model on call center transcript data, resulting in dramatically improved metrics for next-token prediction and perplexity. The system combines ASR with diarization and the domain-adapted SLM for summarization, processing calls in approximately 8.4 seconds with accurate transcripts and human-readable summaries.

title: Overcoming LLM Production Deployment Challenges
short_summary: This talk by a machine learning practitioner from Neeva (a search AI startup) addresses why impressive LLM demos rarely make it to production. The speaker identifies two major categories of challenges: infrastructural issues (latency, buy vs. build decisions, API reliability, evaluation) and output-related issues (format variability, lack of reproducibility, adversarial attacks). Solutions discussed include streaming outputs, multi-cloud fallback strategies, setting temperature to zero for reproducibility, few-shot prompting for format consistency, and strategically targeting non-critical workflows with higher latency tolerance. The key recommendation is to "buy while you build" - start with API access for quick market validation while simultaneously developing in-house fine-tuned models for long-term cost sustainability.

title: Using LLMs to Scale Insurance Operations at a Small Company
short_summary: Anzen, a small insurtech startup with under 20 employees, deployed LLMs to automate insurance underwriting processes and build a document compliance review feature. For underwriting, they built a BERT-based classifier to identify insurance applications from inbox attachments (achieving 95% accuracy with just 300 labeled samples) and used AWS Textract for information extraction, reducing what would traditionally require a dedicated team to an automated pipeline completed in under a week. For compliance document review, they combined sentence embeddings with question-answering models to extract features from offer letters and separation agreements, enabling automated compliance issue detection. The solutions allowed the small team to compete with larger insurance companies by dramatically reducing manual processing time while maintaining accuracy.

title: Enterprise-Scale LLM Integration into CRM Platform
short_summary: Salesforce addresses the challenge of deploying generative AI in enterprise CRM environments where 76% of executives report struggling with production deployment. Their solution, Einstein GPT, integrates large language models across sales, service, marketing, and developer workflows to provide intelligent assistance while maintaining strict data privacy through tenant-isolated architecture. The platform enables sales teams to auto-generate personalized emails, service agents to receive AI-recommended responses grounded in knowledge articles, marketers to create landing pages with generated content and images, and developers to get code autocomplete with test scaffolding. Key architectural decisions include a trust-first approach with data masking, toxicity detection, and ensuring customer data never trains shared models—maintaining the principle that "your data is yours."

title: Panel Discussion on LLM Evaluation and Production Deployment Best Practices
short_summary: This panel discussion brought together experts from Gantry, Structured.io, and NVIDIA to explore the fundamental challenges of evaluating large language models in production environments. The panelists discussed how LLM evaluation differs from traditional ML evaluation due to the lack of clear objective functions and pre-built datasets, the shift from technical to non-technical stakeholders driving LLM projects, and the critical importance of domain-specific evaluation over public benchmarks. Key solutions discussed included building observability systems, leveraging human feedback loops, using guardrails frameworks like NVIDIA's Nemo Guardrails, and focusing on outcome-based metrics rather than traditional accuracy measures.

title: Integrating Foundation Models into the Modern Data Stack: Challenges and Solutions
short_summary: Numbers Station addresses the challenge of manual, time-consuming data engineering work in the modern data stack by leveraging foundation models for tasks like SQL generation, data cleaning, and data linkage. Their approach uses in-context learning and prompt engineering to automate traditionally rule-based processes, while addressing production challenges such as scale through model distillation, prompt brittleness through aggregation techniques, and domain knowledge gaps through continual pre-training and retrieval-augmented generation. The solution enables business users to generate SQL from natural language, automate data cleaning without extensive rule development, and link records across disparate data sources more efficiently.

title: Panel Discussion on Building Production LLM Applications
short_summary: This expert panel discussion brings together practitioners from Stripe, Prompt Ops, Meta, and Insight Partners to explore the practical challenges of deploying LLMs in production. The panelists address key LLMOps concerns including hallucination mitigation strategies, prompt engineering best practices, model selection trade-offs between open-source and commercial models, evaluation frameworks, cost optimization, and building continuous feedback loops. Real-world examples from companies like Honeycomb demonstrate how organizations are successfully integrating LLM features into products, while the discussion emphasizes that proper evaluation infrastructure remains a significant gap in the industry despite rapid deployment of LLM-based applications.

title: Linguistic-Informed Approach to Production LLM Systems
short_summary: Chris Brousseau, a lead data scientist at Mastercard, presents a framework for improving LLM performance by applying linguistic principles across five dimensions: syntax, morphology, semantics, pragmatics, and phonetics. The talk demonstrates how pragmatic instruction through tools like Guidance can dramatically improve both accuracy (from 7/20 to 17/20 on biology questions) and speed (from ~1 minute to ~2 seconds) compared to vanilla ChatGPT queries. The presentation addresses common tokenization problems, the importance of goal-setting over pure metric optimization, and considerations for model longevity in production environments, particularly for specialized domains like financial language at Mastercard.

title: Building an LLM-Powered Support Response System
short_summary: Stripe built an LLM-powered system to help support agents respond to customer questions more efficiently. The team discovered that out-of-the-box GPT models produced inaccurate answers due to outdated or incomplete training data, leading them to develop a sequential fine-tuned GPT framework with classification and generation stages. Key lessons included the importance of breaking down complex problems into manageable ML steps, prioritizing online monitoring and feedback loops, and recognizing that data quality outweighs model sophistication. While offline testing showed positive results, initial production deployment revealed low agent adoption rates, highlighting the critical role of UX considerations and the gap between offline metrics and real-world usage.

title: Kubernetes as a Platform for LLM Operations: Practical Experiences and Trade-offs
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together infrastructure experts, investors, and practitioners to explore the challenges and opportunities of running large language models on Kubernetes. The conversation covers training, fine-tuning, and inference workloads, addressing key concerns around GPU costs and availability, container size challenges with large models, auto-scaling limitations, and the trade-offs between cloud-agnostic platforms and specialized solutions. While no definitive best practices exist yet due to the rapidly evolving landscape, panelists agree that Kubernetes offers valuable abstractions for composability and vendor independence, though significant optimization work remains needed for LLM-specific workloads.

title: Challenges in Designing Human-in-the-Loop Systems for LLMs in Production
short_summary: V7, a training data platform company, shares insights from their experience building human-in-the-loop systems for LLMs in production. The talk highlights the gap between LLM capabilities and practical industry deployment, noting that most production implementations remain simplistic (using basic thumbs up/down feedback) despite the potential for more sophisticated learning systems. Key challenges identified include automation being overrated, people being poor teachers for models, information asymmetry issues, and the mismatch between LLMs' elaborate reasoning capabilities and industry's need for discrete, well-defined outcomes. V7's "Auto Label" feature demonstrates multimodal co-pilot functionality but reveals that truly automating expert knowledge remains difficult.

title: Building Production-Scale Code Completion Tools with Continuous Evaluation and Prompt Engineering
short_summary: GitLab's Model Ops team built code completion tools (GitLab Suggestions) over a 6-7 month journey, developing a comprehensive LLMOps architecture that combines multiple open-source and third-party LLMs. Their solution involves continuous evaluation at scale using historical code commits to determine "agreeable developer output," a prompt engine with version-controlled prompt templates, and a reinforcement learning loop that continuously improves acceptance rates. The architecture includes microservices for tokenization, similarity scoring, and prompt validation, enabling them to move beyond manual spreadsheet-based prompt evaluation to automated, scaled continuous improvement of their code completion accuracy.

title: Scaling AI Systems for Unstructured Data Processing: Logical Data Models and Embedding Optimization
short_summary: CoActive AI shares lessons learned from three years of building AI-first systems for unstructured data. The presentation addresses two major pitfalls in production AI: the impedance mismatch between physical and logical data models that creates bottlenecks, and the cost explosion when running multiple foundation models. Their solutions include creating hybrid data-AI teams to manage logical data model transformations and using embeddings as a caching mechanism to reduce redundant compute across multiple downstream tasks, ultimately enabling more cost-effective and scalable AI deployments.

title: Framework for Evaluating LLM Production Use Cases
short_summary: This podcast discussion features Barak Turovsky, a former Google product leader who helped launch Google Translate with deep neural networks, sharing his framework for evaluating LLM use cases in production. The framework plots use cases on a grid of accuracy vs. fluency requirements and stakes level, arguing that creative and workplace productivity tasks (writing emails, presentations, content) are better near-term fits for LLMs than high-stakes information/decision support use cases like search. The discussion covers production challenges including hallucination management, latency, cost, and the critical importance of human feedback loops, while predicting that customer-facing interactions across industries will be the biggest disruption area in the next 3-5 years.

title: Best Practices for Implementing LLMs in High-Stakes Applications
short_summary: This conference talk by Yada from Moonhub explores the challenges and best practices for incorporating large language models into high-stakes use cases such as healthcare and mental health applications. Using a hypothetical therapy bot as an example, the presentation addresses key concerns including controllability, bias and fairness, robustness, and the importance of human-in-the-loop systems. The talk provides practical recommendations such as breaking tasks into smaller components, maintaining prompt databases with fine-tuned embeddings, using ensemble methods, implementing cohort-based evaluation, and considering when traditional ML approaches may be more appropriate than LLMs. The emphasis is on risk mitigation and careful deployment strategies rather than rushing to adopt new technologies.

title: Natural Language Query Interface with Production LLM Integration
short_summary: Honeycomb, an observability company, built a natural language query assistant that translates user input into executable queries against their data analysis platform. The problem was that while SREs and platform engineers thrived with their query interface, average developers and product managers struggled with the unfamiliar tooling, leading to high drop-off rates. Using OpenAI's GPT-3.5 API, they shipped a production feature in one month that converts natural language into JSON query specifications. Results showed the success rate improved from 75% to 94% through iterative prompt engineering based on real production data, and teams using the query assistant were more than twice as likely to create complex queries and nearly three times more likely to add queries to boards—key activation metrics that correlate with paying customers.

title: LLM-Powered Investment Document Analysis and Processing
short_summary: AngelList transitioned from traditional ML approaches (AWS Comprehend for news classification) to OpenAI-powered solutions, dramatically reducing development time from months to a single day while improving accuracy. The team built an internal document extraction system for investment documents that evolved into a public product called Relay, which automatically parses investment terms, company updates, and legal documents. By leveraging GPT-4 with carefully engineered prompts and LangChain for orchestration, they achieved 99% accuracy on document extraction tasks while reducing costs compared to both manual contractor work and previous AWS-based ML infrastructure.

title: Building a Production-Grade LLM Orchestration System for Conversational Search
short_summary: Perplexity AI built a conversational search engine that combines LLMs with search indexes, Wolfram Alpha, and other tools to provide instant, citation-backed answers to any question. The company tackled key challenges including latency optimization (reducing query time from 6-7 seconds to sub-second), hallucination mitigation through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and multi-model orchestration. By avoiding high-level tooling libraries and building end-to-end engineering themselves, they achieved significant performance gains while supporting features like personalized AI profiles, follow-up question generation, and query reformulation across multiple specialized LLMs.

title: Optimizing LLM Server Startup Times for Preemptable GPU Infrastructure
short_summary: Replit faced the challenge of serving self-hosted LLMs at low latency while managing expensive GPU costs. By optimizing for preemptable (spot) GPU instances in Google Cloud, they reduced costs by approximately two-thirds compared to on-demand pricing. The key technical challenge was reducing server startup time from 18 minutes to under 2 minutes to handle the frequent node preemptions inherent to spot instances. This was achieved through container size optimization, GKE image streaming, switching to local NVMe SSDs, and fixing a hidden multiprocessing bug in the gsutil tool that was throttling model download speeds.

title: LLM Feature Extraction for Content Categorization and Search Query Understanding
short_summary: Canva's engineering team evaluated LLMs as a feature extraction method for two key use cases: user search query categorization and content page categorization. By replacing traditional single-purpose ML classifiers and multi-step NLP pipelines with LLM APIs (specifically OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002), they achieved significant operational improvements—reducing development time from weeks to days, lowering operational costs by 95% in one case, and improving accuracy metrics. The approach leveraged few-shot learning without fine-tuning for text classification and LLM embeddings for semantic similarity clustering, demonstrating that LLMs can serve as an effective middle layer for downstream ML tasks rather than just end-user applications.

title: Scaling Chatbot Platform with Hybrid LLM and Custom Model Approach
short_summary: Voiceflow, a conversational AI platform provider, integrated large language models into their existing chatbot and voice assistant building platform while maintaining their custom-built language models for core NLU tasks. They faced challenges with JSON parsing from LLM outputs, latency inconsistencies across providers (finding Azure OpenAI nearly three times faster than standard OpenAI), and cost trade-offs between fine-tuning smaller models versus using larger models with few-shot learning. Their solution involved building an ML Gateway service for unified model access, implementing prompt engineering and regex-based error handling, and making strategic decisions about when to use third-party LLM APIs versus self-hosted custom models. The results showed their custom NLU model still outperforms GPT-4 on their specific intent/entity detection tasks while costing 1000x less for inference, demonstrating that LLMs are not always the optimal solution for production workloads.

title: LLM Integration in EdTech: Lessons from Duolingo, Brainly, and SoloLearn
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together AI and product leaders from three major EdTech companies—Duolingo, Brainly, and SoloLearn—serving nearly a billion learners globally. The discussion covers practical lessons learned from deploying LLMs in educational products, including the challenges of factual accuracy, cost management at scale, and the distinction between generating content versus generating content that actually teaches effectively. Key solutions discussed include retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), using LLMs to generate cheap rules and detectors rather than running expensive inference at scale, training custom models for cost efficiency, and constraining LLM outputs with domain-specific data rather than relying on models as knowledge sources. Results are nuanced, with panelists emphasizing that successful implementations require tight constraints, domain expertise, and iterative refinement rather than naive LLM deployment.

title: Implementing LLM Observability for Natural Language Querying Interface
short_summary: Honeycomb built a natural language querying interface for their observability product, allowing users to query data using plain language instead of learning the UI. While the initial release solved 80% of use cases, the remaining 20% represented a challenging long tail of edge cases important to paying customers. By applying comprehensive observability practices—capturing everything from user inputs to full RAG pipeline decisions across 48 spans per request—they established a flywheel of continuous improvement. This approach enabled them to isolate specific problems, deploy fixes daily, and validate improvements against real user behavior, ultimately achieving higher product retention, improved conversion rates to paid tiers, and significant value for their sales team.

title: Plus One: Internal LLM Platform for Cross-Company AI Adoption
short_summary: Prosus, a large conglomerate serving approximately two billion users across education, food delivery, finance, and other sectors, developed "Plus One," a Slack-integrated AI assistant to help teams across their portfolio companies explore and adopt generative AI. The tool aggregates multiple LLM and generative models under one interface, allowing thousands of users to experiment with capabilities like image generation, transcription, code review, and document summarization. Over a year of deployment with half a million queries, they reduced hallucination rates from 10% to under 2% through RAG implementations, prompt engineering, and intelligent model routing. Key learnings include the importance of balancing cost, quality, and latency through model routing, the challenges of multilingual tokenization economics, and the brittleness of agent-based systems in production environments.

title: Building a RAG System for Cybersecurity Research and Reporting
short_summary: Trainingracademy, a cloud security training startup, built Stinkbait.io, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) application for cybersecurity research and reporting. The team faced significant challenges including fragmented knowledge across cybersecurity subcommunities, LLM content censorship for security topics, and data quality issues with PDFs and web scraping. They navigated vector database selection, embedding model choices, and context chunking strategies, ultimately learning that preprocessing and data quality are critical to RAG system performance. The presentation shares practical lessons on handling diverse file formats, choosing between indexing algorithms like IVF-flat and HNSW, and strategies for future-proofing vector storage.

title: Pragmatic Product-Led Approach to LLM Integration and Prompt Engineering
short_summary: This case study explores how a senior product manager at LinkedIn approaches building generative AI products and features at scale. The discussion covers the philosophy of treating LLMs as tools rather than solutions, the importance of starting with simple implementations before adding ML complexity, strategies for prompt engineering and evaluation, and the critical role of trust in AI-powered user experiences. Key insights include using off-the-shelf LLM APIs for rapid go-to-market testing before transitioning to narrower, specialized models, building "push" experiences that abstract complexity from users rather than "pull" assistant-style interactions, and establishing robust evaluation criteria and feedback loops for production AI systems.

title: Multi-Model LLM Orchestration with Rate Limit Management
short_summary: Bito, an AI coding assistant startup, faced significant challenges scaling their LLM-powered developer tools due to rate limits across multiple API providers. They built a custom load balancer and model orchestration system that routes requests across OpenAI (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4), Azure OpenAI, and Anthropic (Claude) based on context size, request type, cost, and availability. The solution includes graceful degradation when limits are hit, model-specific prompt engineering for each LLM provider, and a homegrown vector database for code indexing that keeps data local to user machines. Their approach prioritizes user experience through intelligent routing while managing costs and handling the operational complexity of maintaining separate prompts for each model.

title: LLMs and Protein Engineering: Building a Sustainable Materials Platform
short_summary: Cambrium, a Berlin-based biotech startup, leverages generative AI and LLMs to design novel proteins for sustainable materials production. The company uses a custom protein programming language and machine learning models to generate protein sequences with specific properties, enabling them to bring their first product—a vegan human collagen for cosmetics—to market in under two years. Their LLMOps implementation includes a RAG-based Slack assistant for internal research queries and experimental data retrieval, while their core protein design pipeline uses diffusion models to generate proteins with mathematically-defined loss functions, significantly de-risking expensive biological experiments and increasing success rates from ~1% to potentially 50-75%.

title: Debating the Value and Future of LLMOps: Industry Perspectives
short_summary: This podcast discussion features two practitioners with opposing views on whether LLMOps represents a fundamentally new discipline or is merely a marketing buzzword built on MLOps foundations. Patrick Barker, CTO of Kentos (building AI agents), argues that LLMOps requires an entirely different skillset from traditional MLOps, pointing to the new user personas (JavaScript developers with OpenAI API keys) and different tooling requirements. Farood, an MLOps engineer from Iran working at an advertising company, counters that the core MLOps mindset—delivering data transparently, securely, and reproducibly—remains unchanged regardless of whether the model is an LLM or a simple classifier. The discussion explores practical implications including data pipeline similarities, the challenge of deploying LLM applications to production, agent-based systems potentially automating ML 1.0 workflows, and concerns about environmental sustainability of foundation models at scale.

title: Panel Discussion: Real-World LLM Production Use Cases
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together practitioners from different domains—customer service automation, AI consulting, and sales intelligence—to share real-world LLM production experiences. Key use cases include Resides' RAG-based property knowledge system that increased question resolution rates from 50% to 95-99% while doubling associate productivity, structured extraction from transcripts for executive coaches generating thousands of dollars in value from 50-cent API calls, and sales call argument analysis that improved sales by 30%. The panelists emphasize prioritizing product thinking over engineering optimization, shipping quickly then iterating based on production feedback, using LLMs to evaluate LLM outputs, and focusing on customer value rather than technical capabilities.

title: Data Engineering Challenges and Best Practices in LLM Production
short_summary: This podcast discussion from QuantumBlack explores the critical but often overlooked data engineering challenges when deploying LLMs in production, particularly in financial services and insurance. The speakers highlight how moving from MVP to production requires addressing unstructured data quality, document versioning in RAG systems, PII handling, and cost management. Key insights include the need for three-layer data quality checks (input, prompt, output), the importance of vector databases and proper data cataloging, and strategies for balancing innovation with risk through controlled rollouts and limited intent scoping for chatbots.

title: MLOps Maturity Levels and Enterprise Implementation Challenges
short_summary: This podcast discussion between ML platform leaders and consultants explores the three maturity levels of MLOps (zero through two), examining how organizations can progress from manual, ad-hoc ML deployments to fully automated continuous integration and delivery pipelines. The speakers from Klaviyo, IBM, and the MLOps Community discuss the practical challenges of operationalizing machine learning, including the differences between traditional ML and LLM deployments, how to translate technical improvements into business metrics, and the various personas (data engineers, data scientists, DevOps engineers) that must collaborate to achieve ML maturity. Key insights include the importance of standardized templates, model versioning through registries, continuous monitoring, and the unique challenges of LLM deployments such as GPU costs and compliance considerations.

title: Optimizing Production Vision Pipelines for Planet Image Generation
short_summary: Prem AI demonstrates how to deploy vision-based diffusion models in production for generating realistic planet images at scale. The problem involved generating millions of images following specific constraints including aspect ratios, controlled attributes (colors, atmosphere, nebulae), and consistent positioning. The solution combined fine-tuning Stable Diffusion XL with a curated high-quality dataset, custom upscaling pipelines, and various optimization techniques including LoRA fusion, torch.compile, and model quantization. Results showed significant quality improvements through custom upscaling workflows and notable latency reductions through optimization techniques, enabling efficient serving at scale using frameworks like Ray Serve.

title: State of Production Machine Learning and LLMOps in 2024
short_summary: This keynote presentation by Alejandro Saucedo, Director of Engineering Science and Product at Zalando and scientific adviser at The Institute for Ethical AI, provides a comprehensive overview of the state of production machine learning in 2024. The talk addresses the challenges of deploying ML systems at scale, including specialized hardware requirements, complex data flows, compliance needs, and security considerations. It covers technological trends across frameworks, architecture, monitoring, and security, while also exploring organizational shifts from project-based to product-based thinking, the convergence of MLOps and DataOps, and the evolution of team structures to include cross-functional squads. The presentation emphasizes that LLMs have accelerated and reinforced existing MLOps challenges rather than creating entirely new paradigms, and stresses the importance of proportionate risk assessment when deploying AI systems.

title: From MVP to Production: LLM Application Evaluation and Deployment Challenges
short_summary: This panel discussion brings together practitioners from Databricks, Honeycomb, Last Mile AI, and a venture capital firm to explore the challenges of moving LLM applications from proof-of-concept to production. The panelists discuss how user behavior in production often differs dramatically from internal testing expectations, the critical importance of evaluation frameworks (including human annotation, heuristic-based methods, and LLM-as-judge approaches), industry-specific challenges in evaluation metrics, and the ongoing struggle with keeping knowledge bases and retrieval systems up to date. Key takeaways include the need for staged rollouts to intermediate user groups, comprehensive logging and feedback capture, and the recognition that many LLMOps challenges mirror traditional MLOps problems but with added complexity due to non-deterministic outputs and unbounded inputs.

title: Building an On-Premise Health Insurance Appeals Generation System
short_summary: This personal project tackles the challenge of health insurance claim denials in America by building an LLM-based system to generate appeal letters. The solution involves fine-tuning a language model on synthetic data derived from California's independent medical review board records, deploying it on a self-hosted Kubernetes cluster with consumer GPU hardware (RTX 3090), and serving it via vLLM. While still in early development and explicitly not production-ready, the project demonstrates a low-budget approach to LLMOps with fine-tuning costs around $12 using Lambda Labs and inference running on personal hardware costing approximately $748.

title: Managing Model Updates and Robustness in Production Voice Assistants
short_summary: This case study explores the LLMOps practices at Amazon Alexa, focusing on the challenges of maintaining and updating natural language understanding models in production. The team tackled key problems including preventing negative flips during model retraining (where previously correct predictions become incorrect), improving model robustness to input variations, and managing synthetic data generation for training. Solutions included implementing positive congruent training techniques to minimize regression, using T5 models to generate augmented training data with utterance variations, and establishing rigorous quality control processes for synthetic data. The results enabled continuous model updates while maintaining consistent user experience for high-frequency utterances.

title: LLM Applications in Drug Discovery and Call Center Analytics
short_summary: A banking client partnered with QuantumBlack to build a batch processing pipeline that transforms historical call center audio files into structured, analyzable data. The solution addressed regulatory constraints requiring on-premises production deployment with limited GPU resources. By implementing a multi-stage pipeline including diarization, transcription, PII recognition, and LLM-based analysis using open-source models like Mistral 7B and OpenAI Whisper, the team achieved significant performance improvements—including a 60x speedup in diarization through domain-specific optimizations and near-100% GPU utilization through batching and parallelization with Horovod.

title: Productionizing Generative AI Applications: From Exploration to Scale
short_summary: A LinkedIn senior product manager shares practical insights on bringing generative AI features to production at scale, covering the journey from user research and prototyping through prompt engineering optimization and evaluation frameworks. The talk addresses key challenges including GPU resource management, the prompt engineering vs. fine-tuning decision, building systematic prompt evaluation pipelines, and establishing user trust in AI-generated content. Key learnings include that prompt engineering often outperforms fine-tuning for most use cases, the importance of treating prompts like ML models with proper evaluation frameworks, and prioritizing user experience before optimizing for GPU costs as foundational models continue to improve.

title: Building Production-Ready Conversational AI Voice Agents: Latency, Voice Quality, and Integration Challenges
short_summary: Deepgram, a leader in speech transcription services working with clients like Spotify and NASA, presents their approach to building conversational AI voice agents. The presentation addresses key challenges including achieving sub-300ms latency for natural conversation flow, endpoint detection to determine when users stop speaking, voice quality optimization for conversational contexts, and handling LLM output formatting to sound natural in speech. Their solution involves combining speech-to-text and text-to-speech capabilities with LLMs, using techniques like output chunking, prompt engineering for conversational tone, and adding filler words and pauses to make AI-generated speech more human-like. The company is launching Aura, a text-to-speech product targeting under 250ms latency optimized for conversational voice applications.

title: Enterprise Challenges and Opportunities in Large-Scale LLM Deployment
short_summary: This case study presents insights from a senior leader at West Group (a large enterprise with 500 data scientists and engineers) on the challenges of deploying LLMs and generative AI at enterprise scale. The speaker addresses the fundamental differences between traditional MLOps and LLMOps, highlighting that while many organizations are using generative AI, few have successfully deployed it at scale. Key challenges discussed include the emerging technology stack, cost estimation complexities, new data layer requirements (vector databases, prompt hubs), monitoring with human-in-the-loop evaluation, and organizational restructuring needs. The proposed solutions emphasize avoiding pre-training unless core to business proposition, using scalable frameworks for fine-tuning, leveraging off-the-shelf optimization techniques, building centers of excellence, and treating LLMOps as additive to existing MLOps practices rather than a complete reinvention.

title: Deploying LLM-Based Recommendation Systems in Private Equity
short_summary: A data scientist at a private equity company shares their journey of deploying LLM-based recommendation systems, highlighting the challenges of transitioning from traditional ML to LLMOps. The team uses LLMs throughout the data science lifecycle—from cleaning scraped text data to engineering features and creating similarity searches—while grappling with production concerns like API rate limits, compute costs, evaluation strategies, and data quality. The presentation emphasizes that while cloud services like AWS SageMaker and Bedrock offer integration pathways, deploying LLMs in production is more complex than marketing materials suggest, requiring careful consideration of user experience, processing time, and automation challenges.

title: Building an AI-Powered Email Writing Assistant with Personalized Style Matching
short_summary: Shortwave, an AI-first email client, built Ghost Rider, an AI writing feature that learns from users' past emails to generate drafts and autocomplete suggestions that match their personal writing style while incorporating factually accurate information. The system uses a RAG architecture with email embeddings stored in a vector database to find semantically similar past emails, which are then used as examples for the LLM to mimic both style and content. Fine-tuning was employed for the autocomplete feature to handle specific formatting requirements like cursor position and whitespace. The solution addresses two key problems with generic AI email writing: sounding authentically like the user and including correct contextual information rather than hallucinations or boilerplate text.

title: Building a Scalable LLM Gateway for E-commerce Recommendations
short_summary: Mercado Libre, Latin America's largest e-commerce platform with over 50,000 employees, built a centralized LLM Gateway to democratize access to generative AI across the organization. The gateway addresses challenges of scale (handling large request volumes exceeding model limits), multi-provider integration, security, monitoring, and cost management. A key production use case involves using LLMs to generate personalized product recommendations and push notifications in real-time, handling multiple Spanish dialects and Portuguese across Latin American markets. By 2023, the system supported over 16,000 unique users and more than 150 use cases, with improvements observed in recommendation quality and expected positive impact on NPS metrics.

title: Automated Evaluation Framework for LLM-Powered Features
short_summary: Slack's machine learning team developed an automated evaluation framework to measure and improve the quality of their generative AI products, specifically message summarization and natural language search. The solution addresses the challenge of evaluating subjective LLM outputs at scale by breaking down broad quality concepts into smaller, measurable metrics including hallucination detection, format validation, and relevance scoring. They implemented a staged evaluation process with golden sets, validation sets, and A/B testing to enable rapid prototyping and confident product improvements. The approach demonstrated measurable quality improvements when introducing techniques like extractive summarization as a preprocessing step.

title: Building an Enterprise LLMOps Stack: Lessons from Doordash
short_summary: This presentation by the ML Platform team lead at Doordash explores the challenges and architectural considerations for building an enterprise LLMOps stack. The speaker examines the unique challenges of deploying LLM applications at scale across five dimensions including inference and serving, discusses the need to support both proprietary and open-source LLMs, and reviews reference architectures from companies like LinkedIn and Uber. The presentation emphasizes that use cases should drive stack development, with a focus on velocity, friction reduction, and cost management as key success metrics.

title: Multimodal Feature Stores and Research-Engineering Collaboration
short_summary: Runway, a generative AI company known for video generation models like Stable Diffusion and Gen-1, tackles the challenge of managing training data for multimodal AI systems. The problem centers on how to efficiently store, query, and serve diverse data types (video, images, text, embeddings) for large-scale distributed training jobs. Their solution involves building what they call a "multimodal feature store" that enables semantic search over unstructured data, pre-computation of features like embeddings and depth maps, and efficient streaming of data batches to distributed training infrastructure. The approach also emphasizes shared codebases between researchers and engineers, using Python/Pydantic instead of YAML configurations, and creating tooling that abstracts away cloud infrastructure complexity while maintaining Docker-based workflows.

title: Building a Production-Ready AI Phone Call Assistant with Multi-Modal Processing
short_summary: RealChar, founded by a former Google Assistant and self-driving car engineer, is building an AI assistant called Revia that makes phone calls on behalf of consumers to handle customer service interactions. The system uses a robotics-inspired parallel processing architecture with an event bus for handling multimodal inputs (audio, text, DTMF tones) in real-time. Drawing from self-driving car engineering practices, they've built a virtual simulation environment for testing, implemented multi-tier fallback mechanisms to handle slow or inconsistent LLM responses, and created real-time observability tools to monitor AI behavior at millisecond granularity. The product is in beta testing and aims to relieve consumers of tedious customer service phone calls.

title: Blueprint for Scalable and Reliable Enterprise LLM Systems
short_summary: This panel discussion at an AI quality conference brought together enterprise AI leaders from Bank of America, Nvidia, Microsoft, and IBM to share their experiences building scalable and reliable AI/ML systems in production. The panelists discussed key challenges including aligning AI initiatives with business objectives, managing data silos, navigating the differences between traditional MLOps and LLMOps, deploying models through rigorous testing frameworks, implementing responsible AI governance, and the emerging trend toward agentic workflows. Key insights included the importance of consistent platforms and governance standards across organizations, the unique challenges of evaluating subjective natural language outputs from generative AI, and the extended timelines (6-8 weeks to build, 3+ months to deploy) required when dealing with sensitive enterprise data.

title: MLOps Evolution and LLM Integration at a Major Bank
short_summary: Andy McMahan, Principal AI and MLOps Engineer at Barclays, discusses the challenges and strategies of implementing MLOps and LLMOps in a heavily regulated financial institution. The conversation covers how traditional ML workflows can be adapted for generative AI use cases, the importance of treating LLMs as commodities or services rather than training custom models, building an ecosystem of tools rather than a rigid platform, and the critical role of ROI-focused metrics and strong leadership in driving successful AI initiatives. Key themes include the balance between innovation and regulatory compliance, the need for horizontal scaling of parallel initiatives in large organizations, and the importance of speaking the language of business value rather than focusing on vanity metrics.

title: Scaling and Optimizing Self-Hosted LLMs for Developer Documentation
short_summary: This multi-speaker session covers three complementary approaches to improving LLM production systems. Fuzzy Labs presented a case study on scaling a self-hosted RAG-based developer documentation assistant, achieving significant latency improvements using vLLM for inference optimization and Ray Serve for horizontal autoscaling. Boundary demonstrated BAML, an open-source domain-specific language that improves structured output accuracy and reduces token usage by 20-25% through custom parsing algorithms. SAS showcased combining traditional NLP techniques with LLMs for public comment analysis, reducing manual processing time from 4,500 to 600 hours by using text analytics to filter and bucket statements before LLM summarization.

title: MLflow's Production-Ready Agent Framework and LLM Tracing
short_summary: This case study explores MLflow's approach to bridging the gap between demo-stage GenAI agents and production-ready deployments. The MLflow team identified key challenges in productionizing LLM-based agents including debugging black-box systems, retrieval relevance optimization, prompt engineering complexity, and tracking rapid iterations. Their solution introduces MLflow Tracing for visibility into agent execution, enhanced evaluation capabilities for RAG systems, and automatic integrations with popular agentic frameworks like AutoGen, LlamaIndex, and LangGraph. The result is a unified platform that allows teams to track experiments, evaluate agent performance, visualize traces, and deploy agents with confidence.

title: Real-time Data Streaming Architecture for AI Customer Support
short_summary: This case study presents a fictional airline scenario (Bited Airlines) to illustrate how shifting from batch-processed ETL systems to real-time streaming data architecture can dramatically improve AI customer support agents. The problem centered on AI agents providing outdated, incomplete, or hallucinated responses due to data silos and delayed batch processing. By implementing "shift left" data architecture using Kafka and Flink for real-time streaming directly into vector stores, the AI agents gained access to unified, up-to-date customer context from all channels. The results included improved first-contact resolution, reduced hallucinations, better customer satisfaction, and lower operational costs compared to human agents.

title: Best Practices for AI Agent Development and Deployment
short_summary: This case study explores the foundational principles and practical patterns for deploying AI agents in production environments. Raj Ricky, a Principal Product Manager at Microsoft Azure Data, discusses how organizations should approach agentic AI development by defining clear success criteria upfront, constraining the environment appropriately, starting simple with off-the-shelf tools before customizing, and keeping humans in the loop during early iterations. The discussion covers key considerations around orchestration frameworks (like LangChain, Semantic Kernel, AutoGPT), the inherent stochastic nature of LLMs, and the tradeoffs between reliability and complexity. Practical applications discussed include fraud detection, supply chain optimization, patient monitoring in healthcare, agricultural automation, and personal shopping assistants.

title: AWS Trainium & Metaflow: Democratizing Large-Scale ML Training Through Infrastructure Evolution
short_summary: Outerbounds and AWS collaborated to integrate Metaflow, an open-source ML orchestration framework, with AWS Trainium custom ML chips to enable cost-efficient large language model training and deployment. The integration allows data scientists to leverage AWS's custom silicon (Trainium for training, Inferentia for inference) through familiar Python workflows while achieving up to 50% cost savings on training compared to traditional GPU instances. The solution provides a complete MLOps stack including orchestration, versioning, monitoring, and deployment capabilities, with customer testimonials reporting 80% cost reductions and improved energy efficiency.

title: Generative AI Assistant for Agricultural Field Trial Analysis
short_summary: Agmatix, an agricultural technology company, faced the challenge of helping agronomists analyze complex field trial data with hundreds of parameters and multiple visualization options. They developed "Leafy," a generative AI assistant powered by Amazon Bedrock and Anthropic Claude, enabling agronomists to query trial data using natural language instead of manually creating analytical dashboards. The solution integrates with their existing AWS-based data pipeline (Amazon S3, AWS Glue, Lambda) and uses prompt engineering to combine user questions with trial data and contextual instructions. According to reported results, the implementation led to over 20% improved efficiency, more than 25% improvement in data integrity, and a three-fold increase in analysis potential throughput, though these specific metrics should be considered with appropriate caution as they come from the company itself.

title: SQL Generation and RAG for Financial Data Q&A Chatbot
short_summary: Q4, a capital markets access platform company, faced challenges building a Q&A chatbot for Investor Relations Officers due to the numerical and structured nature of their financial datasets. Traditional RAG approaches using semantic search and embeddings failed to accurately retrieve context from numerical data like stock quotes and transaction histories. The team developed a solution using Amazon Bedrock and SQLDatabaseChain that generates SQL queries from natural language questions, which then retrieve precise context from the database for LLM-powered summarization. By selecting optimal LLMs for different tasks (Claude V2 for SQL generation, Titan Text Express for summarization), optimizing prompts with XML tags, and eliminating unnecessary validation steps, they achieved single-digit second response times while maintaining high accuracy for their regulated financial use case.

title: LLM-Powered Data Discovery and Documentation Platform
short_summary: Grab faced a significant data discovery challenge with over 200,000 tables in their data lake, where 51% of data consumers took multiple days to find needed datasets due to poor semantic search capabilities and only 20% documentation coverage. They built HubbleIQ, an LLM-powered chatbot leveraging GPT-4 for documentation generation and Glean for enterprise search integration, deployed through both their Hubble UI and Slack. The solution increased documentation coverage from 20% to 90% for critical tables, improved search click-through rates from 82% to 94%, and achieved a 17 percentage point increase in users finding it easy to discover datasets, while reaching all-time high monthly active users.

title: Enhancing Vector Similarity Search with LLM-Based Reranking
short_summary: Grab's engineering team developed an LLM-assisted vector similarity search approach to address limitations in traditional vector search when handling complex, nuanced queries involving negations or contextual constraints. The solution combines FAISS-based vector similarity search for efficient initial shortlisting with GPT-4o for re-ranking results based on contextual understanding. Experiments on synthetic datasets showed that while both approaches performed comparably on straightforward queries, the LLM-assisted method significantly outperformed raw vector search on complex queries involving negations (e.g., "food with no fish or shrimp") or conceptual requirements. The approach has been deployed internally at Grab for datasets exceeding 4,500 rows, demonstrating practical applicability despite the added latency from LLM queries.

title: Productionizing LLM-Powered Data Governance with LangChain and LangSmith
short_summary: Grab developed Metasense, an LLM-powered system to automate data classification and governance metadata generation across their data lake. The system addressed challenges with third-party classification services and resource constraints for training custom models. Through prompt engineering improvements—including splitting the model into PII and non-PII classification tasks, reducing prompt complexity, and chunking large tables—along with adopting LangChain and LangSmith frameworks for collaboration and rapid experimentation, the team achieved low misclassification rates and scaled coverage to the vast majority of their data lake tables, significantly reducing manual workload for data owners.

title: RAG-Powered LLM System for Automated Analytics and Fraud Investigation
short_summary: Grab's Integrity Analytics team built a RAG-powered LLM solution to automate repetitive analytical tasks including regular metric report generation and fraud investigations. The system integrates an internal LLM platform (Spellvault) with a custom Python-based API middleware (Data-Arks) that serves structured data from SQL queries to LLM agents. By using RAG instead of fine-tuning, the team achieved cost efficiency and the ability to respond with real-time data without model retraining. The solution delivers summarized reports through Slack, saving an estimated 3-4 hours per report, and enables fraud investigations that previously took significant time to be completed in minutes.

title: Production-Ready LLM Integration Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Custom ReAct Implementation
short_summary: Buzzfeed faced challenges deploying LLMs in production for chatbots and content experimentation, particularly around dataset recency limitations (OpenAI's training data only covered events up to October 2021) and limited context windows (4k tokens). After exploring and abandoning self-hosted fine-tuned models like FLAN-T5 due to unfavorable economics, they implemented a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture using semantic search with embeddings. The team built an event-driven Nearest Neighbor Search system using NSQ, migrated from Google's Matching Engine to Pinecone for cost savings, and ultimately replaced LangChain with a custom "native ReAct" implementation for better control over error handling, instrumentation, and API call management. This allowed their products like chatbots and ChatGPT Plugins to answer questions about current events using up-to-date content from their article and recipe corpus.

title: Building an AI Tutor with Enhanced LLM Accuracy Through Knowledge Base Integration
short_summary: Clipping, a Brazilian edtech startup, addressed the challenge of LLM hallucinations and misinformation in educational contexts by building ClippingGPT, an AI tutor trained on a proprietary external knowledge base using embeddings and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The system was designed to help students prepare for Brazil's notoriously difficult Diplomatic Career Entrance Examination. By chunking documents, creating embeddings via OpenAI's API, storing them in Redis as a vector database, and retrieving relevant context before generating answers, ClippingGPT achieved a 23rd place finish in the 2022 exam simulation—outperforming GPT-4 by 26% and passing the exam threshold that GPT-4 alone could not reach. The results demonstrate that domain-specific knowledge augmentation can significantly improve LLM accuracy for high-stakes educational applications.

title: Building an AI Co-Pilot Application: Patterns and Best Practices
short_summary: Thoughtworks developed Boba, an experimental AI co-pilot for product strategy and generative ideation, to explore how to build LLM-powered applications beyond simple chat interfaces. The project identified eight key patterns for mediating conversations between users and LLMs, including Templated Prompts, Structured Responses, Real-Time Progress streaming, Select and Carry Context, Contextual Conversation, Out-Loud Thinking, Iterative Response, and Embedded External Knowledge using RAG techniques. Built on GPT-3.5/4 with LangChain, the application demonstrated practical approaches to prompt engineering, JSON response parsing, streaming responses for UX improvement, and integrating external data sources via vector stores to overcome LLM knowledge cutoff limitations.

title: AI-Powered Insurance Claims Chatbot with Continuous Feedback Loop
short_summary: Allianz Benelux faced the challenge of helping customers navigate their complex insurance product portfolio with numerous variations, claim forms, and support numbers. Using Landbot's no-code chatbot platform, their Business Transformation Unit and Customer Care Center teams developed and deployed a conversational chatbot in just three weeks. The solution leveraged 92,000+ unique search terms collected over years to categorize keywords and link them to appropriate insurance products and destinations. The chatbot was scaled across the Benelux region with Dutch and German language versions through a 48-hour hackathon. Results included over 18,000 customers served with 90% positive feedback ratings, real-time feedback integration via Slack and Trello for continuous improvement, and the ability to convert feedback into improvements within 24 hours.

title: Enterprise Knowledge Management with LLMs: Morgan Stanley's GPT-4 Implementation
short_summary: Morgan Stanley faced the challenge of enabling their financial advisors to efficiently access vast knowledge bases and automate repetitive tasks while maintaining strict quality and compliance standards required in financial services. They partnered with OpenAI to deploy GPT-4-powered tools including an internal chatbot (AI @ Morgan Stanley Assistant) for information retrieval and a meeting summarization tool (AI @ Morgan Stanley Debrief) using Whisper and GPT-4. The foundation of their success was a comprehensive evaluation framework that tested AI performance against real-world use cases before deployment, with continuous refinement based on expert feedback. The results include 98% adoption among advisor teams, document access increasing from 20% to 80%, and dramatically reduced time for client follow-ups from days to hours.

title: Retrieval Augmented LLMs for Real-time CRM Account Linking
short_summary: Schneider Electric faced the challenge of manually linking customer accounts across CRM systems to identify parent-subsidiary relationships, a process requiring up-to-date knowledge of corporate acquisitions and restructuring. By partnering with AWS Machine Learning Solutions Lab, they deployed a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) system using Flan-T5-XXL on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, augmented with Google Search API via LangChain to overcome LLM knowledge cutoff limitations. The solution also incorporated SEC 10K filings for reliable corporate structure data. Domain-specific prompt engineering improved accuracy from 55% to 71%, significantly reducing manual effort in account linking workflows and enabling faster data access for downstream analytics teams.

title: LLM-Based Agents for User Story Quality Enhancement in Agile Development
short_summary: Austrian Post Group IT developed an Autonomous LLM-based Agent System (ALAS) to automatically improve user story quality in their agile software development teams. The system uses GPT models configured as specialized agents (Product Owner and Requirements Engineer) that collaborate through structured prompts to analyze and enhance user stories. Evaluated by 11 professionals across six agile teams using 25 synthetic user stories from a mobile delivery application project, the system demonstrated significant improvements in clarity, comprehensibility, and business value articulation. While GPT-4 produced more comprehensive improvements, it also generated longer stories that raised practical concerns. The study highlights both the potential of LLMs in requirements engineering and the continued need for human oversight to ensure contextual relevance and accuracy.

title: Scaling Game Content Production with LLMs and Data Augmentation
short_summary: Ubisoft faced challenges with the tedious and time-consuming process of creating diverse NPC dialogue variations (bark trees) for their narrative-driven games. By partnering with AI21 Labs, they implemented an LLM-powered solution for data augmentation that allows writers to generate training data for internal paraphrasing models. The solution uses AI21's API to generate diverse dialogue variations based on character motivations, which writers then curate and edit. This human-in-the-loop approach enabled rapid scaling of content production, transforming work that was previously too tedious to attempt into an efficient workflow where writers can focus on editing rather than generating content from scratch.

title: Real-time Question-Answering System with Two-Stage LLM Architecture for Sales Content Recommendations
short_summary: Microsoft developed a real-time question-answering content recommendation system for their internal MSX Sales Copilot to help sellers quickly find relevant sales documentation from the Seismic content repository. The solution uses a two-stage LLM architecture combining a bi-encoder for fast document retrieval with a cross-encoder for re-ranking, leveraging metadata prompt engineering since document content was not programmatically accessible. Deployed as an Azure Machine Learning endpoint integrated with Semantic Kernel, the system returns top-5 relevant documents in seconds. Human evaluation showed that most queries (15 out of 31) were rated as returning relevant results, with seller satisfaction surveys rating relevancy at 3.7 out of 5 and task relevance at 4 out of 5.

title: GPT-4 Visit Notes System
short_summary: Summer Health, a text-based pediatric telehealth service, faced the challenge of time-consuming and often unclear medical visit note documentation that burdened pediatricians and frustrated parents. They implemented GPT-4 to automatically generate clear, jargon-free visit notes from doctors' detailed written observations, with a clinical review process ensuring accuracy. The results included a 5x reduction in documentation time (from 10 minutes to 2 minutes per note), a 400% reduction in delays completing visit notes, and significantly improved parent satisfaction with note clarity and comprehensiveness.

title: Fine-tuning LLMs for Toxic Speech Classification in Gaming
short_summary: A large gaming company sought to automate the detection of toxic language in player communications to promote a healthier gaming environment. AWS Professional Services addressed the challenge of limited labeled training data (initially ~100 samples) by fine-tuning BERT-based foundation models pre-trained on Twitter data (BERTweet). After experimenting with a two-stage binary-then-multi-class classification approach during proof of concept, the production solution was simplified to a single-stage multi-class classifier trained on approximately 10,000 samples. The final bertweet-base-offensive model achieved 88% precision, 83% recall, and 86% F1 score while reducing maintenance complexity and operational costs compared to the two-stage architecture.

title: Enterprise AI Transformation: Holiday Extras' ChatGPT Enterprise Implementation Case Study
short_summary: Holiday Extras, a European leader in travel extras, faced challenges with multilingual content creation, data fluency across non-technical staff, and scaling customer support. They deployed ChatGPT Enterprise across their entire organization, achieving 95% weekly adoption and saving over 500 hours per week (equivalent to $500k annual savings). Key results include 30% of customer inquiries handled by AI bots, NPS scores rising from 60% to 70%, code debugging times reduced by 75%, and translation tasks that previously took weeks now completed in hours. The company also developed custom GPTs for UX scoring and deployed a customer-facing AI bot (Syd AI) for travel insurance queries.

title: AI-Powered Customer Support Automation for Global Transportation Service
short_summary: Lime, a global micromobility company operating electric bikes and scooters across 200+ cities, faced challenges scaling customer support operations manually across multiple languages and priority levels. By implementing Forethought's AI-powered suite including Triage (for intelligent routing), Solve (for automated responses), and Workflow Builder (for RPA-guided processes), Lime achieved 27% case automation, 98% automatic ticket tagging with 2.5 million predicted tags, and a 77% reduction in time to first response, enabling them to handle over 1.7 million annual tickets more efficiently while improving customer satisfaction.

title: Building an AI Teaching Assistant: ChatLTV at Harvard Business School
short_summary: Harvard Business School professor Jeffrey Bussgang developed ChatLTV, a RAG-based Slack chatbot trained on 13 years of course materials (200 documents, 15 million words) to serve as an AI faculty co-pilot for his MBA entrepreneurship course. The system used OpenAI's GPT-4 via Azure for privacy compliance, Pinecone for vector storage, and LangChain for middleware. Over the Fall 2023 semester, approximately 170 of 250 students made over 3,000 queries, with nearly 40% rating the chatbot quality as 4 or 5 out of 5. The system enhanced both student preparation and faculty insight, allowing the professor to understand student knowledge gaps before class by reviewing query logs. A supplementary custom GPT was later created for providing feedback on final papers, demonstrating the expanding role of LLMs in educational contexts.

title: Practical Implementation of LLMs for Automated Test Case Generation
short_summary: Researchers at Cesar investigated using GPT-3.5 Turbo with LangChain to automate test case construction for a real-world web application (Da.tes). They developed a multi-step prompt engineering approach with structured templates to generate software requirements, test conditions, and test cases. The generated test cases were evaluated by QA engineers against human-written test cases across documentation quality factors (correctness, consistency, completeness). Results showed AI-generated test cases achieved comparable quality scores (average 4.31 vs 4.18 for human-written), with 58.6% preference in A/B testing. While promising, the study identified limitations including the need for feature-by-feature input and challenges with integration tests across multiple features.

title: Building a Custom LLM for Automated Documentation Generation
short_summary: Databricks developed a custom fine-tuned LLM to automatically generate documentation for tables and columns in Unity Catalog after encountering quality, performance, and cost challenges with off-the-shelf SaaS LLMs. Starting as a hackathon prototype, a team of two engineers spent one month and less than $1,000 in compute to fine-tune an MPT-7B model on approximately 3,600 synthetically generated examples. The resulting bespoke model achieved quality comparable to expensive SaaS alternatives while delivering a 10x reduction in inference costs and improved throughput scalability. The feature now powers over 80% of table metadata updates on the Databricks platform.

title: HIPAA-Compliant LLM-Based Chatbot for Pharmacy Customer Service
short_summary: Amazon Pharmacy built a generative AI question-and-answering chatbot to assist customer care agents in retrieving accurate pharmacy information in real time. The solution employs the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pattern using Amazon SageMaker JumpStart foundation models, with embeddings for similarity search and an LLM for response generation. The HIPAA-compliant system augments human agents rather than replacing them, allowing them to validate and edit responses before sending to customers, while a feedback loop enables continuous model improvement.

title: Automated Unit Test Improvement Using LLMs for Android Applications
short_summary: Meta developed TestGen-LLM, an LLM-based tool to automatically improve unit test coverage for Android applications written in Kotlin. The system addresses the challenge of enhancing existing test suites by generating additional test cases that cover neglected edge cases. Through a rigorous filtration process that validates buildability, reliability, and novel coverage contribution, TestGen-LLM was able to improve 10% of the classes it was applied to during deployment on Instagram and Facebook platforms, with most recommendations being accepted by engineers for production use.

title: Lessons from Building a Production RAG System: Data Formatting and Prompt Engineering
short_summary: Credal, an enterprise AI platform company, shares practical lessons learned from processing over 250,000 LLM calls on 100,000+ corporate documents. The core challenges addressed include handling complex document structures in RAG systems, managing LLM attention limitations, and optimizing prompt engineering for production reliability. Key solutions involved developing custom data formatting pipelines that inline footnotes and convert tables to CSV format, implementing LLM-generated metadata tagging for improved retrieval, and restructuring prompts to focus model attention on the most critical task components. The company found that standard libraries like LangChain were insufficient for production-grade enterprise use cases, requiring custom implementations for document parsing, output formatting, and multi-step reasoning chains to achieve the 95%+ accuracy needed for customer-facing applications.

title: Building a Production-Ready Business Analytics Assistant with ChatGPT
short_summary: This case study from Microsoft presents a methodology for transforming ChatGPT into a business analytics assistant capable of answering complex analytical questions from structured SQL databases. The approach addresses LLMs' known limitations with quantitative reasoning by using a multi-agent architecture with specialized "Data Engineer" and "Data Scientist" agents that leverage tools (Python, SQL queries, visualization libraries) rather than performing calculations directly. The solution implements the ReAct (Reasoning and Acting) framework for iterative problem-solving, with agents breaking down complex questions into intermediate steps, observing results, and adjusting their approach. While the implementation demonstrates promising capabilities for automating data analytics workflows, the author acknowledges significant challenges including output format consistency, hallucination risks, token limit constraints, and the need for multiple validation mechanisms to ensure reliability in production scenarios.

title: Building Analytics Applications with LLMs for E-commerce Review Analysis
short_summary: This case study from Microsoft's Data Science team demonstrates how Large Language Models can replace traditional machine learning pipelines for analyzing e-commerce product reviews. The solution uses OpenAI's API with carefully engineered prompts to perform sentiment analysis, product aspect extraction, and topic clustering in a single model rather than training and maintaining multiple separate models.
