By setting temperature to 0 for deterministic outputs and using few-shot prompting techniques, the approach achieves improved explainability over traditional "black box" models while significantly reducing development time and operational complexity.

title: Building AI Assist: LLM Integration for E-commerce Product Listings
short_summary: Mercari's Generative AI/LLM team built Mercari AI Assist, a feature that leverages GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-turbo to help sellers improve their listing titles on the marketplace platform. The team employed prompt engineering with simple retrieval-augmented generation, using GPT-4 for offline extraction of key title attributes and GPT-3.5-turbo for real-time suggestion generation to balance cost and quality. Through rigorous offline and online evaluation, including preliminary partial releases, they discovered significant output inconsistencies from the LLM APIs at scale, requiring robust pre- and post-processing logic. The case study highlights practical lessons in LLMOps including model selection, cost optimization, handling API errors specific to LLMs, and managing hallucinations and content moderation challenges when deploying commercial LLM APIs in production.

title: Scaling AI-Powered File Understanding with Efficient Embedding and LLM Architecture
short_summary: Dropbox developed AI-powered summarization and question-answering features for file previews on the web, addressing the challenge of information overload for knowledge workers. The solution leverages their existing file conversion framework (Riviera) to extract text from 300+ file types and generate embeddings, which are then processed using k-means clustering for summarization and similarity matching for Q&A. Key innovations include treating embeddings as cacheable file conversions, using k-means clustering to identify diverse topics while reducing hallucinations, and implementing a power-law-based algorithm to dynamically determine context size for multi-file queries. Results include a 93% reduction in cost-per-summary, 64% reduction in cost-per-query, and dramatic latency improvements (p75 summary latency dropped from 115 seconds to 4 seconds, Q&A from 25 seconds to 5 seconds).

title: Hybrid AI System for Large-Scale Product Categorization
short_summary: Walmart developed Ghotok, an AI system that combines predictive and generative AI models in an ensemble approach to improve product categorization across over 400 million SKUs. The system addresses the challenge of mapping categories to product types by first using predictive AI models to filter millions of candidate pairs down to thousands based on confidence thresholds, then applying generative AI with chain-of-thought prompting for semantic understanding to further reduce false positives. The solution is deployed with a two-tier LRU caching system to meet millisecond-level latency requirements, and includes an exception handling tool with both ML and human intervention for edge cases in production.

title: LLM-Based Dasher Support Automation with RAG and Quality Controls
short_summary: Doordash faced challenges with their flow-based Dasher (delivery driver) support system, which could only resolve a limited subset of issues and relied on English-only knowledge base articles that were difficult to navigate. They implemented a RAG-based LLM chatbot that retrieves relevant information from knowledge base articles and generates contextual responses. To address hallucination and quality concerns inherent in LLMs, they developed a two-tier LLM Guardrail system combining semantic similarity checks with an LLM-powered evaluator, plus an LLM Judge system for continuous quality monitoring. The solution reportedly reduced hallucinations by 90% and compliance issues by 99%, enabling the system to autonomously assist thousands of Dashers daily while allowing human agents to focus on complex problems.

title: Error Handling in LLM Systems
short_summary: Uber developed QueryGPT, a natural language to SQL generation system, to address the challenge of efficiently authoring SQL queries across their data platform that handles approximately 1.2 million interactive queries monthly. The solution leverages LLMs, vector databases, and a multi-agent architecture with specialized agents for intent classification, table selection, and column pruning to generate SQL from English prompts. After evolving through 20+ iterations from a hackathon concept to production, the system reduced query authoring time from approximately 10 minutes to 3 minutes. In limited release to Operations and Support teams, QueryGPT achieved around 300 daily active users, with 78% reporting that generated queries reduced time compared to writing from scratch.

title: Fine-Tuning and Quantizing LLMs for Dynamic Attribute Extraction
short_summary: Mercari's AI/LLM team tackled the challenge of extracting dynamically specified attributes from user-generated marketplace listing descriptions, where conventional ML models struggled with the variety of content and changing attribute requirements. They fine-tuned Google's gemma-2b-it model using QLoRA on a single A100 GPU, then applied post-training quantization with llama.cpp to reduce model size by approximately 95%. The resulting 4-bit quantized model outperformed GPT-3.5 Turbo by more than five percentage points on BLEU score while being significantly smaller and an estimated 14 times less costly to operate, demonstrating that fine-tuned smaller models can surpass larger commercial APIs for specific extraction tasks.

title: Automating Test Generation with LLMs at Scale
short_summary: Assembled, a workforce management software company, faced the common engineering challenge of maintaining comprehensive test coverage while shipping features quickly. Their solution was to leverage large language models (specifically OpenAI's o1-preview and Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet) to generate unit tests automatically. By crafting precise prompts that include the function to test, relevant struct definitions, and example tests from their codebase, engineers can generate comprehensive test suites in minutes rather than hours. The company reports saving hundreds of engineering hours collectively, with individual engineers who previously wrote few tests now consistently writing them, and thorough testers saving weeks of time. The approach has been extended to frontend component testing and integration testing with mocked services.

title: LLM Integration for Customer Support Automation and Enhancement
short_summary: Airbnb faced challenges in scaling their customer support operations, dealing with long-tail corner cases, and reducing costly data labeling requirements. They implemented text generation models across three key use cases: content recommendation for their Help Center, a real-time agent assistance system using a QA model, and a chatbot paraphrasing capability. By leveraging models like MT5 and T5 with prompt engineering, they achieved significant improvements in document ranking relevance, agent efficiency through higher engagement rates, and better user trust in chatbot interactions. The solutions utilized historical agent-user conversation data for training, DeepSpeed for multi-GPU training acceleration, and Sentence-Transformers for data quality improvements.

title: Building a RAG-Based Documentation Chatbot: Lessons from Fiddler's LLMOps Journey
short_summary: Fiddler developed a RAG-based documentation chatbot using OpenAI's GPT-3.5 to help users find answers from their documentation. The project involved integrating LangChain for efficient development, implementing sophisticated query processing to handle natural language complexity, developing document chunking strategies to work within LLM context windows, and using multiple retrieval strategies for accurate responses. Key outcomes included iterative improvements through prompt engineering, human feedback integration, hallucination reduction techniques, and the importance of UI/UX design in building user trust. The company leveraged their own LLM Observability solutions to continuously evaluate and monitor chatbot performance.

title: Two-Stage Fine-Tuning of Language Models for Hyperlocal Food Search
short_summary: Swiggy, an Indian food delivery platform, addressed the challenge of understanding complex, multi-intent search queries across diverse regional cuisines and languages by implementing a two-stage fine-tuning approach for small language models. The solution involved first performing unsupervised domain adaptation using TSDAE on historical order data, followed by supervised fine-tuning with manually curated query-item pairs augmented by LLMs. Using the all-mpnet-base-v2 model with latency constraints of 100ms, they achieved improved Mean Average Precision and Precision@5 metrics across both dense and sparse hyperlocal regions. The approach successfully retrieves contextually relevant items for complex queries like "gym snacks" or "Karnataka famous sweets." As of the publication, this feature was in experimental phase being tested with a small user cohort.

title: Automating Post Incident Review Summaries with GPT-4
short_summary: Canva's reliability engineering team faced challenges with inconsistent and time-consuming Post Incident Review (PIR) summaries that were manually written by engineers. They implemented GPT-4-chat to automatically generate blameless, structured summaries from Confluence-stored incident reports. The solution involved parsing HTML reports, sanitizing sensitive data, and using carefully crafted prompts with few-shot examples. After evaluating GPT fine-tuning, GPT completion, and GPT chat approaches, they selected GPT-4-chat for its superior ability to correlate incident phases and maintain consistent output formatting. After approximately two months in production, most AI-generated summaries remained unaltered by engineers, demonstrating both quality approval and significant reduction in operational toil for reliability engineers.

title: Healthcare Data Analytics Democratization with MapAI and LLM Integration
short_summary: Komodo Health developed MapAI, an NLP-based generative AI assistant embedded in their MapLab enterprise platform, to democratize healthcare data analytics. The solution addresses the problem of non-technical pharmaceutical team members (brand leads, Medical Affairs managers, clinical researchers) waiting weeks or months for data insights. By enabling natural language queries against their comprehensive Healthcare Map database, MapAI allows users of all technical skill levels to generate insights and visualizations quickly. The system uses an intelligence agent architecture with specialized GenAI agents, experimented with multiple foundational models (Llama 3.1, Mistral 7B, Phi-3), and leverages LangChain and LangGraph for orchestration, with an automated LLM lifecycle to facilitate future model adoption.

title: Building Production-Grade Conversational Analytics with LangGraph and Waii
short_summary: This case study explores Waii's text-to-SQL capabilities integrated with LangGraph to create conversational analytics applications that can handle complex database queries through natural language. The solution addresses the challenge of translating natural language questions into accurate SQL queries, particularly focusing on complex join handling across multiple tables. By combining Waii's specialized text-to-SQL engine with LangGraph's multi-agent orchestration framework, the system enables non-technical users to perform sophisticated data analysis through natural conversation, with demonstrated capabilities including 14-table joins, bridge table handling, and automatic query optimization.

title: Building and Deploying AI Agents for Account Qualification
short_summary: Unify, a go-to-market AI company, developed an agent-based system for account qualification—determining whether companies fit a user's ideal customer profile. Using LangGraph for agent state machine orchestration and LangSmith for experimentation and tracing, the team iterated through multiple agent versions, evolving from a barebones implementation to a sophisticated plan-reflect-tools architecture. Key challenges included balancing agent accuracy with speed (particularly when using OpenAI's o1-preview model for planning), implementing parallel tool calls for web scraping, and redesigning the UI to show real-time agent decision-making rather than hiding execution behind a spinner. The team leveraged LangSmith's versioned datasets and experiment comparison features to run systematic evaluations across hundreds of test cases with minimal custom infrastructure.

title: Autonomous AI Agent for Enhanced Customer Service Chatbots
short_summary: Salesforce developed Einstein Service Agent (now Agentforce Service Agent), an autonomous AI-powered customer service agent designed to replace traditional rule-based chatbots. The solution addresses the problem that 81% of customers prefer waiting for human agents over interacting with conventional chatbots that lack contextual understanding. By leveraging LLMs integrated with CRM and business data through the Einstein 1 Platform, the agent can understand natural language, reason about customer intent, and autonomously resolve service issues across multiple channels 24/7. The system includes built-in guardrails via the Einstein Trust Layer, supports multimodal inputs (text, images, video, audio), and provides seamless handoffs to human agents for complex cases. Early customer feedback from OpenTable indicates promising results in handling inquiries with human-like accuracy while adhering to diverse country-specific guidelines.

title: Integrating Live-Staffed AI Chat with LLM-Powered Customer Service
short_summary: Smith.ai, a virtual receptionist and customer engagement company, developed a next-generation AI-powered web chat system using large language models to handle customer conversations more naturally and autonomously. The previous AI technology could only manage simple, linear Q&A interactions without understanding conversational context. By implementing generative AI trained on business-specific data (website content, CRM data, product documentation), the new system can engage in free-flowing natural language conversations while seamlessly switching to structured workflows for lead capture. Human agents remain in the loop to supervise AI responses, handle complex situations requiring empathy, and validate lead qualification, creating a hybrid approach that claims to deliver more meaningful customer interactions with reduced agent workload.

title: Leveraging LangSmith for Debugging Tools & Actions in Production LLM Applications
short_summary: Mendable, a platform helping enterprise teams answer technical questions with AI, faced significant challenges in debugging their new Tools & Actions feature that enables LLM-powered agents to take automated actions via API calls. The lack of observability into agent execution, combined with complex just-in-time AI inputs/outputs, led to messy debugging processes with console.logs and high latency runs. By integrating LangSmith's tracing and debugging tools, Mendable gained visibility into agent decision-making, identified performance bottlenecks (such as a 7.23-second delay caused by concatenated prompts), optimized tool schemas, and built datasets for evaluation. The solution enabled them to deploy their Tools & Actions feature to enterprise customers, with one deployment reportedly achieving $1.3 million in savings over five months.

As a result, no specific problem, solution, or results can be identified from the Five Sigma case study.
