title: Scaling Parallel Agent Operations with LangChain and LangSmith Monitoring
short_summary: Paradigm, a Y Combinator 2024 startup, built an AI-powered intelligent spreadsheet that orchestrates thousands of task-specific agents in parallel for data processing. Using LangChain for rapid iteration and agent development, and LangSmith for monitoring and observability, Paradigm was able to track agent execution flows, optimize token usage, refine their dependency systems for column generation, and implement a precise usage-based pricing model. The LangSmith observability platform provided granular insights into agent thought processes and LLM usage, enabling the team to keep compute costs low while maintaining accuracy across complex multi-step reasoning tasks.

title: Optimizing Research Report Generation with LangChain Stack and LLM Observability
short_summary: Athena Intelligence, an AI-powered enterprise analytics platform, faced the challenge of building a production-ready system for generating complex research reports with proper source citations. They adopted LangChain for LLM-agnostic model management, LangGraph for orchestrating multi-agent workflows with hundreds of LLM calls, and LangSmith for development iteration and production monitoring. The solution enabled rapid prompt engineering through playground-based debugging, comprehensive observability across their agentic architecture, and out-of-the-box production monitoring including error rates, latency, and time-to-first-token metrics. According to the company, this toolchain significantly accelerated their development velocity and made previously unfeasible debugging tasks possible.

title: Smart Ticket Routing and Support Agent Copilot using LLMs
short_summary: Adyen, a global financial technology platform serving major clients like Meta, Uber, and Microsoft, faced scaling challenges with their support team as transaction volumes grew. They deployed two LLM-powered applications: a smart ticket routing system that analyzes theme and sentiment to direct tickets to appropriate specialists, and a support agent copilot using RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to suggest responses. Built with LangChain and LangSmith on a Kubernetes-based microservice architecture, the system was developed in just 4 months and resulted in more efficient ticket routing, faster response times, and improved agent satisfaction.

title: Enhancing Memory Retrieval Systems Using LangSmith Testing and Evaluation
short_summary: New Computer, the company behind the personal AI assistant "Dot," faced challenges in optimizing their agentic memory retrieval system that dynamically creates and retrieves memories to understand users over time. Using LangSmith for experimentation and evaluation, they created synthetic user datasets to test various retrieval methods including semantic search, keyword matching, BM25, and meta-field filtering while preserving user privacy. By leveraging LangSmith's experiment comparison view and prompt playground, they achieved 50% higher recall and 40% higher precision compared to their baseline implementation, enabling rapid iteration on both retrieval techniques and conversational prompts.

title: LangSmith Implementation for Full Product Lifecycle Development and Monitoring
short_summary: Wordsmith, an AI assistant for in-house legal teams, faced challenges with visibility into LLM performance as their product grew in complexity with multi-stage inference chains across heterogeneous data sources. By implementing LangSmith across their entire product lifecycle—from prototyping to production monitoring—they achieved faster debugging through hierarchical tracing, established reproducible evaluation baselines that enabled same-day deployment of new models like Claude 3.5, reduced time to debug production issues from minutes to seconds, and enabled systematic A/B experimentation through tag-based exposure tracking with Statsig integration. The approach reportedly reduced costs on particular tasks by up to 10x through model optimization guided by well-defined evaluation sets.

title: Building Enterprise-Scale AI Applications with LangChain and LangSmith
short_summary: Rakuten, operator of Japan's largest online shopping mall with 70+ businesses, built a comprehensive AI platform called "Rakuten AI for Business" to support business clients with market analysis, customer support, and productivity tools. The company leveraged LangChain and LangSmith to rapidly develop multiple LLM-powered products including an AI Analyst, AI Agent, and AI Librarian. Additionally, using LangChain's OpenGPTs package, a team of three engineers deployed an internal employee chatbot platform in just one week, intended to scale to 32,000 employees. LangSmith provided critical capabilities for prompt management via Hub, experimentation with custom evaluation metrics, and enterprise-grade data security with environment separation between development and production.

title: Evolving Quality Control AI Agents with LangGraph
short_summary: Rexera, a real estate transaction automation company, evolved their quality control AI system through three iterations—from single-prompt LLMs to CrewAI multi-agent systems to LangGraph—to improve accuracy in reviewing thousands of real estate workflows daily. The initial single-prompt approach struggled with complex multi-step workflows, showing 35% false positives and 10% false negatives. After migrating to CrewAI's multi-agent framework, they reduced false positives to 8% and false negatives to 5%, but agents still lacked precise control in decision-making. The final migration to LangGraph enabled custom decision paths with tree-like branching structures, further reducing false positives to 2% and false negatives to 2%, providing more deterministic quality control checks for tasks like rush order verification, document accuracy, and SLA compliance.

title: Advanced Agent Monitoring and Debugging with LangSmith Integration
short_summary: Replit, a coding platform serving over 30 million developers, built Replit Agent—a sophisticated AI-powered tool for writing, running, and deploying code. The complexity of their agentic workflows, which involved hundreds of steps including planning, environment setup, dependency installation, and application deployment, pushed the limits of existing LLMOps observability solutions. By integrating LangSmith and working closely with LangChain, Replit gained deep visibility into agent interactions through improved large trace handling, intra-trace search capabilities, and thread views for human-in-the-loop workflows. This collaboration enabled faster debugging, improved trace visibility, and better handling of parallel tasks in production.

title: LangSmith Integration for Automated Feedback and Improved Iteration in SDLC
short_summary: Factory, an enterprise AI company building autonomous "Droids" for software development lifecycle automation, faced challenges with observability and debugging in complex LLM pipelines operating in secure customer environments. By implementing self-hosted LangSmith, they established robust tracing infrastructure integrated with AWS CloudWatch, enabling precise tracking of data flow through agentic stages. They leveraged LangSmith's Feedback API to automate the collection and analysis of user feedback on LLM outputs, linking feedback directly to specific LLM calls to quickly identify issues like hallucinations. This automated feedback loop enabled prompt optimization based on real customer data, resulting in a claimed 2x improvement in iteration speed compared to manual methods, along with reported customer benefits including approximately 20% reduction in open-to-merge time and 3x reduction in code churn.

title: Building a Scalable Conversational Video Agent with LangGraph and Twelve Labs APIs
short_summary: Jockey is an open-source conversational video agent that combines LangGraph's multi-agent framework with Twelve Labs' video understanding APIs to enable intelligent video processing and manipulation. The system evolved from LangChain's legacy AgentExecutor to LangGraph v1.1, implementing a sophisticated multi-agent architecture with Supervisor, Planner, and Worker nodes to handle complex video workflows including search, editing, and text generation. The architecture provides granular control over workflow execution, optimizes token usage, and enables both local development and scalable production deployments via LangGraph Cloud.

title: Optimizing Agent Behavior and Support Operations with LangSmith Testing and Observability
short_summary: Podium, a communication platform for small businesses, faced challenges with their AI Employee agent making 20-30 LLM calls per interaction without clear visibility into agent behavior. By implementing LangSmith for observability, dataset curation, and fine-tuning, they established a comprehensive testing lifecycle that improved their agent's F1 response quality from 91.7% to 98.6%. Additionally, by empowering their Technical Product Specialists with trace visibility, they reduced engineering intervention for troubleshooting by 90%, allowing engineers to focus on development rather than support tasks.

title: Multi-Agent System for Prediction Market Resolution Using LangChain and LangGraph
short_summary: Chaos Labs developed Edge AI Oracle, a multi-agent system built on LangChain and LangGraph to resolve queries in prediction markets. The system addresses challenges of single-model bias and truth-seeking by orchestrating a council of AI agents powered by diverse LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta) through a sequential workflow including research, web scraping, bias filtering, report writing, and classification. The architecture enables configurable consensus requirements, with the initial deployment requiring unanimous agreement with over 95% confidence from each agent, though quantitative results on accuracy improvements are not provided in the case study.

title: Building Reliable AI Agents for Application Development with Multi-Agent Architecture
short_summary: Replit developed Replit Agent, an AI-powered coding assistant that helps users build complete applications from scratch using natural language prompts. To address the challenge of "blank page syndrome" and the complexity of multi-step software development, Replit implemented a multi-agent architecture with specialized agents (manager, editor, and verifier) that emphasize human-in-the-loop collaboration rather than full autonomy. The team employed advanced prompt engineering techniques including few-shot examples, dynamic prompt construction with memory compression, and a custom Python-based DSL for tool calling across 30+ tools. They used LangGraph for their agent framework and LangSmith for observability, enabling them to trace and debug complex multi-turn conversations during their alpha testing phase with AI-first developers, ultimately delivering a product that lowers barriers to software creation for both novice and experienced developers.

title: Building a Complex AI Answer Engine with Multi-Step Reasoning
short_summary: Perplexity developed Pro Search, an AI-powered "answer engine" that handles complex, multi-step queries by separating planning from execution. The system breaks down nuanced questions into manageable steps, generates and executes search queries sequentially, filters results to the most relevant documents, and synthesizes final answers using LLMs. Through careful prompt engineering, model-specific customization, and extensive evaluation using LLM-as-a-Judge alongside manual testing and A/B experiments, the team achieved both speed and accuracy. The result was a 50% increase in query search volume as users discovered the capability to answer complex research questions efficiently.

title: AI-Powered Email Search Assistant with Advanced Cognitive Architecture
short_summary: Superhuman developed Ask AI, an AI-powered search assistant to help users navigate their inboxes and calendars more efficiently. The original single-prompt RAG approach had limitations with task-specific instructions, date reasoning, and complex queries. The team transitioned to a parallel multi-agent architecture with query classification, metadata extraction, task-specific tool use, and tailored response generation. Through careful prompt engineering techniques like "double dipping" instructions and a rigorous staged evaluation process, they achieved sub-2-second response times with reduced hallucinations. The result was a 14% reduction in search time (5 minutes saved per week) for users who previously spent up to 35 minutes weekly on email searches.

title: AI-Powered Tour Guide for Financial Platform Navigation
short_summary: Ramp developed an AI-powered "Tour Guide" agent to help users navigate their financial operations platform, reducing the learning curve and decreasing reliance on customer support. The solution uses an iterative action-taking architecture where the agent generates one UI interaction (scroll, click, or text fill) at a time based on the current app state, rather than planning entire workflows upfront. The team optimized for latency by consolidating multi-step LLM calls into a single prompt, simplified DOM inputs to constrain the decision space, and implemented guardrails to prevent the agent from operating on high-risk pages. The result is a human-agent collaborative experience where users can observe, pause, and override the AI's actions while receiving contextual explanations at each step.

title: Building and Operating Production LLM Agents: Lessons from the Trenches
short_summary: The source content for this case study is unavailable due to a 404 error, indicating that the original blog post titled "Lessons from 15 Months of LLM Agents" from Ellipsis has been removed or relocated. Based on the URL and title alone, this appears to have been a retrospective on building and operating LLM-based agents in production over an extended period, though specific details about the problem, solution, and results cannot be verified from the provided content.

title: Building Production-Grade AI Agents with Distributed Architecture and Error Recovery
short_summary: Parcha developed enterprise-grade AI agents to automate manual compliance workflows, particularly Know Your Business (KYB) processes. Starting with a naive approach using LangChain agents and websockets, they encountered significant production challenges including context window pollution, unreliable connections, lack of recovery mechanisms, and LLM hallucinations. Through iterative improvements, they evolved to an asynchronous architecture with pub/sub communication, a coordinator-worker agent model for task decomposition, separation of extraction from judgment tasks, Redis-based memory management, and robust error handling with self-correction prompts. These changes significantly improved reliability, reduced token usage, and enabled agents to complete complex multi-step compliance tasks with fewer catastrophic failures.

title: Enterprise LLMOps: Development, Operations and Security Framework
short_summary: Cisco's engineering team addressed the challenges of deploying LLM-powered applications in large enterprise environments by developing an end-to-end LLMOps model. The presentation highlighted how traditional DevOps workflows struggle to accommodate the unique characteristics of LLMs, and proposed solutions for continuous delivery, monitoring, security, and on-call operations for AI-powered applications. Drawing from recent AI product launches at Cisco, the talk outlined a comprehensive framework for managing the full lifecycle of LLMs in production enterprise settings.

title: Optimizing Email Engagement Using LLMs and Rejection Sampling
short_summary: Nextdoor faced the challenge that off-the-shelf generative AI (ChatGPT API) produced email subject lines that were less engaging than user-generated ones, with initial tests showing only 56% of the clicks compared to baseline. They developed a two-model system combining a subject line generator (OpenAI API with prompt engineering to extract rather than rewrite content) and a fine-tuned reward model that predicts which subject line will generate more engagement. The reward model uses rejection sampling to accept AI-generated subjects only when predicted to outperform user-generated alternatives. Key engineering optimizations included caching (reducing costs by 600x), daily performance monitoring, and retry mechanisms with fallbacks. A/B testing showed the final system achieved a 1% lift in sessions, 0.4% increase in Weekly Active Users, and 1% increase in ad revenue compared to user-generated subject lines.

title: Dutch YouTube Interface Localization and Content Management
short_summary: Tastewise, a food and beverage trend intelligence platform, built "TasteGPT" - a production RAG chatbot that translates natural language queries into structured API requests against their proprietary data platform. The team evolved from a naive single-prompt approach to a parallelized multi-prompt architecture where each prompt handles specific responsibilities (page navigation, query extraction, location filtering, etc.). Key innovations included using intermediate output layers to handle hallucination issues with location filtering and leveraging GPT's self-explanations in few-shot examples to improve prompt effectiveness. The system went from concept to production in approximately 4 months (February to June 2023), significantly impacting how users engage with the platform. The company also explored generative AI for image generation for their content agency offering.

title: Building Production-Grade LLM Applications: An Architectural Guide
short_summary: This GitHub technical guide provides a comprehensive framework for building LLM applications in production, covering the five major steps from problem identification to online evaluation. The guide addresses key architectural decisions including LLM selection (considering licensing, model size, and performance), customization techniques (in-context learning, RLHF, and fine-tuning), and the essential tooling stack comprising user input handling, input enrichment with embeddings and vector databases, prompt optimization, and responsible AI components like content classifiers and telemetry services. Using a hypothetical ISP customer service assistant as an illustrative example, the guide demonstrates how these components work together to create effective LLM-powered applications.

title: Medical AI Assistant for Battlefield Care Using LLMs
short_summary: Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) developed CPG-AI (Clinical Practice Guideline-driven AI), a proof-of-concept conversational AI agent designed to provide medical guidance to untrained soldiers on the battlefield. The system leverages large language models (LLMs) combined with structured care algorithms from Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) guidelines. Using their internally-developed RALF (Reconfigurable APL Language model Framework) software ecosystem, researchers created a prototype capable of inferring patient conditions from conversational input, answering medical questions without jargon, and guiding users through tactical field care procedures. While explicitly described as not yet "battle-ready," the project demonstrates significant progress in adapting LLMs for high-stakes, real-time medical decision support in operational environments.

title: GitHub Copilot Integration for Enhanced Developer Productivity
short_summary: Duolingo, the world's most popular language learning platform with over 500 million users, faced challenges with inconsistent development standards and workflows that limited developer mobility and efficiency. The company implemented GitHub Copilot as an AI-powered pair programming assistant alongside GitHub Codespaces and custom API integrations to enforce code consistency and accelerate development. Results include a 25% increase in developer speed for those unfamiliar with repositories, 67% decrease in median code review turnaround time, 70% increase in pull requests, and reduced environment setup time from hours to just one minute for their largest repository. The solution enables their 300 developers to focus on complex business challenges rather than routine tasks, supporting Duolingo's mission to build the best education platform in the world.

title: GitHub Copilot Deployment at Scale: Enhancing Developer Productivity
short_summary: Mercado Libre, Latin America's largest e-commerce and digital payments ecosystem with over 10,000 developers, faced challenges in maintaining developer productivity while ensuring security across their massive codebase. The company deployed GitHub Copilot to its entire developer organization of 9,000+ users, resulting in approximately 50% reduction in time spent writing code. Combined with GitHub Enterprise and GitHub Advanced Security for automated security scanning, this integration enabled the team to merge and deploy around 100,000 pull requests per day while maintaining security standards. The AI coding assistant reportedly helped developers automate repetitive tasks, accelerate onboarding for new hires, and focus more on high-value feature development.

title: Evaluation-Driven Refactoring: How W&B Improved Their LLM Documentation Assistant Through Systematic Testing
short_summary: Weights & Biases refactored their LLM-powered documentation assistant, Wandbot, to address inefficiencies in document parsing, slow retrieval speeds, and redundant LLM calls. Through systematic evaluation-driven development, they transitioned from FAISS to ChromaDB for vector storage, implemented asynchronous processing using LangChain Expression Language (LECL), optimized chunk sizes, and parallelized API calls. The refactoring effort, which involved approximately 50 evaluations and significant debugging, improved answer correctness from 72% to 81% while reducing response latency by 84% (from ~492 seconds to ~80 seconds per response).

title: LLMOps Lessons from W&B's Wandbot: Manual Evaluation & Quality Assurance of Production LLM Systems
short_summary: Weights & Biases developed Wandbot, an LLM-powered documentation assistant, and implemented a manual evaluation framework to assess its performance. The case study focuses on the evaluation methodology for their RAG-based chatbot system, addressing the challenge of measuring LLM output quality in production documentation assistance scenarios. While specific results are not available from the source text, the work demonstrates Weights & Biases' approach to systematic LLM evaluation practices.

title: LLMOps Evolution: Scaling Wandbot from Monolith to Production-Ready Microservices
short_summary: Weights & Biases faced challenges with their initial monolithic Wandbot documentation assistant, including maintenance difficulties, duplicated code across Discord and Slack deployments, and scalability limitations. They re-architected the system into a microservices-based solution with distinct ingestion, chat, database, and API modules. The new architecture enabled multilingual support (English and Japanese), LLM fallback mechanisms for reliability, conversation history persistence, and cost optimization through embedding caching. Key improvements included migrating from LangChain to LlamaIndex for better control, integrating Cohere's rerank-v2 for improved retrieval relevance, and deploying on Replit for auto-scaling and improved uptime. The team conducted both manual and automated evaluations to measure retrieval accuracy and response relevance.

title: Building Robust LLM Evaluation Frameworks: W&B's Evaluation-Driven Development Approach
short_summary: Weights & Biases developed Wandbot, an LLM-powered documentation assistant, and improved its performance through evaluation-driven development. The team faced challenges with misalignment between automated and manual evaluations, suboptimal retrieval performance, and incomplete knowledge bases. They built a GPT-4 powered auto-evaluation framework aligned with human annotations using few-shot prompting and Argilla for curation. Enhancements included improved data ingestion for Markdown parsing, a query enhancer using Cohere for language detection and intent classification, and a hybrid retriever combining FAISS, BM25, and web search via you.com API. The v1.1 release with GPT-4-1106-preview demonstrated improved Answer Correctness, Answer Relevancy, and Context Recall compared to previous versions, while maintaining comparable Answer Faithfulness metrics.

title: Building and Scaling a Production Generative AI Assistant for Professional Networking
short_summary: LinkedIn developed a generative AI-powered assistant to help members with job searches and content browsing by enabling them to get faster information, assess job fit, and receive career advice. The solution employed a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with a multi-agent architecture, where a router directs queries to specialized agents (job assessment, knowledge sharing, etc.), which then retrieve data from internal APIs and Bing before generating contextual responses. Key challenges included achieving consistent quality (reaching 80% quickly but struggling to push past 95%), developing robust evaluation pipelines with up to 500 daily annotated conversations, handling LLM structured output errors with a custom defensive YAML parser, and managing capacity/latency tradeoffs with streaming and async non-blocking pipelines. The team successfully launched the product while continuing to work on fine-tuning models and automated evaluation.

title: LLM-as-Judge Framework for Production LLM Evaluation and Improvement
short_summary: Twilio Segment faced the challenge of evaluating their LLM-powered audience generation system where multiple valid outputs could exist for the same prompt. They implemented an "LLM-as-Judge" architecture that uses a separate LLM to evaluate and score generated Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) against ground truth examples. To address the lack of natural language prompts in their training data, they built a synthetic evaluation generation pipeline where an LLM generates prompts from existing ASTs. The system achieved over 90% alignment with human evaluation, with GPT-4 models scoring highest (4.55/5.0). This evaluation framework enabled the team to systematically compare models, optimize prompts, and test architectural changes, contributing to a 3x improvement in median time-to-audience creation and 95% feature retention rate for their CustomerAI audiences product.

title: Dogfooding AI Features in GitLab's Development Workflow
short_summary: GitLab describes how they internally dogfood their AI-powered feature suite called GitLab Duo across their engineering and product teams. The company aimed to demonstrate real-world efficiency gains from integrating AI throughout the software development lifecycle, from code review and documentation to incident response and testing. Key solutions include Code Suggestions for multi-language development, Duo Chat for answering coding questions and drafting content, and automated summarization for merge requests and incident reviews. While GitLab reports benefits such as reduced manual effort, faster documentation, higher code quality, and streamlined administrative tasks, the case study is primarily promotional in nature and lacks specific quantitative metrics to substantiate these claims.

title: Building a Comprehensive LLM Platform for Food Delivery Services
short_summary: Swiggy, India's leading food delivery platform, embarked on a comprehensive generative AI initiative in 2023 to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency. The company deployed multiple AI solutions including Stable Diffusion-based image generation for catalog enrichment (with LoRA fine-tuning for Indian dishes), GPT-4 powered review summarization, RAG-based WhatsApp bots for restaurant partner support, and neural search capabilities. Key challenges addressed included hallucination mitigation, latency optimization (100ms for search vs 3 seconds for chatbots), and data governance. Results included improved funnel metrics and reduced cancellations in A/B testing for review summarization, though the team acknowledged that many initiatives required 3-4 months of iteration before achieving viable ROI, and customer-facing conversational interfaces showed limited traction.

title: Building and Deploying an AI-Powered Incident Summary Generator
short_summary: Incident.io built an AI feature that automatically suggests incident summaries using OpenAI's models to help responders keep incident documentation fresh without interrupting their mitigation work. By analyzing Slack conversations, incident updates, and metadata, the system proposes summaries that users can accept, edit, or reject. The team invested heavily in prompt engineering tooling, structured JSON output requirements, and explicit feedback mechanisms. Results showed that half of all summary updates are now written by AI, with 63% of actioned suggestions being accepted as-is and only 11% being rejected, though the majority of suggestions still go unused, leading the team to maintain human-in-the-loop approval rather than auto-setting summaries.

title: AI-Powered Co-pilot System for Digital Sales Agents
short_summary: Wayfair developed Agent Co-pilot, a generative AI assistant that works alongside digital sales agents to provide real-time, contextually relevant chat response recommendations. The system addresses the challenge of efficiently supporting customers while reducing agent workload by leveraging LLMs with carefully constructed prompts that include task descriptions, company policies, product information, and conversation history. Initial testing demonstrated a 10% reduction in average handle time, enabling faster customer service while maintaining quality through comprehensive monitoring including factuality checks, instruction adherence tracking, and a secondary QA LLM for automated quality assessment.

title: Multi-Track Approach to Developer Productivity Using LLMs
short_summary: eBay implemented a three-track approach to enhance developer productivity using LLMs: utilizing GitHub Copilot as a commercial offering, developing eBayCoder (a fine-tuned version of Code Llama 13B), and creating an internal GPT-powered knowledge base using RAG. The implementation showed significant improvements, including a 27% code acceptance rate with Copilot, enhanced software upkeep capabilities with eBayCoder, and increased efficiency in accessing internal documentation through their RAG system.

title: DragonCrawl: Uber's Journey to AI-Powered Mobile Testing Using Small Language Models
short_summary: Uber's Developer Platform team developed DragonCrawl, an LLM-based system for autonomous mobile application testing that addresses the challenges of scale, maintenance overhead, and cross-language/cross-city testing requirements. Traditional script-based testing required 30-40% of engineering time for maintenance and struggled with UI changes. DragonCrawl uses a fine-tuned MPNet model (110M parameters) to interpret screen content and make human-like decisions about UI interactions. Since launching in late 2023, the system achieved 99%+ stability, successfully tested flows in 85 of 89 top cities worldwide without code changes, blocked 10 high-priority bugs, and eliminated maintenance requirements that previously cost thousands of developer hours.

title: Building Production-Ready LLMs for Automated Code Repair: A Scalable IDE Integration Case Study
short_summary: Replit developed a specialized 7B parameter LLM for automated code repair that leverages Language Server Protocol (LSP) diagnostics. The problem addressed was that while LSP identifies errors in code, it only provides fixes in about 10% of Python diagnostic cases. Replit created a data pipeline using operational transformations and session events to generate 100K+ training examples, synthesized high-quality diffs using larger LLMs with DSPy, and fine-tuned DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct-v1.5 using MosaicML infrastructure. The resulting Replit Code Repair 7B model achieved competitive performance against much larger models like GPT-4 Turbo and Claude-3-Opus on both their custom real-world benchmark and LeetCode-based evaluations, while maintaining inference efficiency suitable for production deployment in their IDE.

title: Building Fair Housing Guardrails for Real Estate LLMs: Zillow's Multi-Strategy Approach to Preventing Discrimination
short_summary: Zillow developed a comprehensive LLM guardrails system to ensure fair housing compliance in real estate conversational AI applications. The problem addressed was preventing discriminatory responses (steering) based on protected classes like race, religion, familial status, and disability when deploying LLMs for real estate search and transactions. The solution combined three strategies: prompt engineering for baseline compliance awareness, stop lists for catching explicit violations, and a fine-tuned BERT-based classifier for nuanced detection. The resulting system operates as both a pre-processing filter on user inputs and post-processing validator on LLM outputs, enabling Zillow to deploy conversational AI while maintaining legal compliance with the Fair Housing Act and related regulations.

title: Fine-tuning and Scaling LLMs for Search Relevance Prediction
short_summary: Faire, a global wholesale marketplace, faced challenges in measuring and improving the semantic relevance of search results at scale. Manual human labeling was expensive and slow, while initial GPT-based solutions were costly for high-throughput inference. The team fine-tuned open-source Llama models (Llama2-7b, Llama2-13b, and Llama3-8b) using Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (LoRA) on labeled datasets of up to 250k examples. The best-performing Llama3-8b model achieved a 28% improvement in Krippendorff's Alpha accuracy compared to the fine-tuned GPT model. By leveraging quantization, batching, DeepSpeed, and horizontal scaling across 16 GPUs, the team achieved throughput of 70 million predictions per day at significantly reduced costs, enabling daily relevance measurement and unlocking downstream use cases for search optimization.

title: Building a Food Delivery Product Knowledge Graph with LLMs
short_summary: Doordash developed a product knowledge graph leveraging large language models to better understand and organize their extensive catalog of products from restaurants and merchants. The solution aimed to improve product discovery, search relevance, and recommendations across their platform by using LLMs to extract, normalize, and connect product information at scale. While specific quantitative results are not provided in the available text, this represents a significant application of LLMs for structured data extraction and knowledge representation in a food delivery e-commerce context.

title: Optimizing Security Incident Response with LLMs at Google
short_summary: Google's Security Workflow Automation team deployed LLMs to accelerate incident response communications, addressing the time-consuming process of writing incident summaries for executives and stakeholders. By implementing structured input processing, iterative prompt engineering with few-shot examples, and human-in-the-loop workflows, they achieved a 51% reduction in time to draft incident summaries while improving quality ratings by 10% compared to human-written summaries. The solution was expanded to executive communications, achieving 53% time savings on more complex multi-section documents.

title: Automated CVE Analysis and Remediation Using Event-Driven RAG and AI Agents
short_summary: Nvidia developed Agent Morpheus, an AI-powered system that automates the analysis of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in enterprise software containers. The solution combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with AI agents using four Llama3 LLMs (three LoRA fine-tuned) to determine if vulnerabilities are actually exploitable, rather than just present. The system generates investigation checklists, executes tasks autonomously, and produces standardized VEX documents for security analysts. By leveraging NVIDIA NIM microservices and the Morpheus cybersecurity framework for parallel processing, Agent Morpheus achieved a 9.3x speedup (from 2842 seconds to 305 seconds for 20 CVEs), reducing vulnerability triage time from hours or days to seconds while maintaining human oversight for final decisions.

title: Automating Job Role Extraction Using Prosus AI Assistant in Production
short_summary: OLX faced a challenge where job roles were buried within job ad titles and descriptions, creating barriers to efficient search. They implemented a solution using Prosus AI Assistant (an LLM powered by OpenAI) to extract job roles from unstructured text and build normalized job-role taxonomies. The production pipeline processes approximately 2,000 new or updated ads daily, generating around 4,000 API requests. Initial A/B testing showed positive uplift in successful event metrics and a significant decrease in search extensions when results were limited, indicating improved search relevance. However, the solution costs approximately $15K per month, prompting the team to consider transitioning to self-hosted models for long-term sustainability.

title: Building a Delicate Text Detection System for Content Safety
short_summary: Grammarly developed DeTexD, a benchmark dataset and baseline model for detecting "delicate" text—emotionally charged or potentially triggering content that goes beyond traditional toxicity detection. The problem addressed was that existing toxic text detection methods fail to capture broader categories of sensitive content that could harm users or AI agents. The team created a 40,000-sample training dataset and 1,023-sample benchmark through targeted domain specification and keyword matching, then fine-tuned a RoBERTa-based classifier. Results showed their baseline model achieved 79.3% F1 score, significantly outperforming existing methods like Google's Perspective API (42.3% F1) and OpenAI's moderation API (31.1% F1), demonstrating that delicate text detection requires specialized approaches distinct from toxicity classification.

title: LLM Security: Discovering and Mitigating Repeated Token Attacks in Production Models
short_summary: Dropbox's security research team discovered vulnerabilities in OpenAI's ChatGPT models (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) where repeated token sequences in prompts could bypass alignment guardrails and extract memorized training data, including PII. The team identified that OpenAI's initial mitigation—filtering single-token repeats—could be circumvented using multi-token repeated sequences. Dropbox demonstrated successful training data extraction from both GPT-3.5 (extracting jq documentation) and GPT-4 (extracting Bible passages), and also identified potential denial-of-service vectors through expensive long-running requests. After responsible disclosure in January 2024, OpenAI confirmed the vulnerabilities and implemented broader filtering for multi-token repeats along with server-side timeouts. Dropbox plans to release an open-source, LangChain-compatible repeated tokens detector to help other organizations protect their LLM deployments.

title: Building a Commonsense Knowledge Graph for E-commerce Product Recommendations
short_summary: Amazon developed COSMO, a framework that uses large language models to build commonsense knowledge graphs from customer behavior data (query-purchase and co-purchase pairs) to improve product recommendations. The system employs a recursive human-in-the-loop process where LLMs generate hypotheses about commonsense relationships, which are then filtered through heuristics and human annotation before being used to prompt the LLM with refined instructions. When evaluated on the Shopping Queries Data Set, models augmented with COSMO knowledge graph data achieved up to 60% improvement in macro F1 score with frozen encoders and maintained a 22-28% edge over baselines even after fine-tuning, demonstrating significant improvements in matching products to customer queries requiring commonsense reasoning.

title: LLMs for Cloud Incident Management and Root Cause Analysis
short_summary: Microsoft Research developed an LLM-based system for automating cloud incident management at hyperscale, addressing the challenge of quickly diagnosing production incidents in services like Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams. The solution uses fine-tuned GPT-3 and GPT-3.5 models to generate root cause analysis and mitigation recommendations from incident titles and summaries. Evaluated on over 40,000 real production incidents across more than 1,000 services, the fine-tuned GPT-3.5 (Davinci-002) model showed significant improvements over baseline models, with gains of at least 15% for root cause recommendations. Human evaluation by on-call engineers showed over 70% rated the recommendations as useful (3 out of 5 or better), demonstrating practical applicability in production incident resolution workflows.

title: Evolution of LLM Integration in GitHub Copilot Development
short_summary: GitHub developed Copilot, an AI-powered code generation tool, by iteratively working with OpenAI's large language models starting with GPT-3 in 2020. The team overcame challenges in code completion quality through prompt crafting techniques (such as incorporating file paths and neighboring editor tabs for context) and fine-tuning approaches. Key innovations included pulling similar code from open editor tabs to improve suggestion relevance and adding language disambiguation through file metadata. The result was a production AI coding assistant that evolved from solving 50% of test problems to over 90%, with continuous model improvements enabling multi-language support and increasingly contextual code suggestions that developers could tangibly feel in their daily workflows.

title: The Hidden Complexities of Building Production LLM Features: Lessons from Honeycomb's Query Assistant
short_summary: Honeycomb built Query Assistant, a natural language interface that translates user queries into structured observability queries using LLMs. The team faced significant challenges including context window limitations with large customer schemas, LLM latency making chaining impractical, prompt engineering trade-offs between correctness and usability, prompt injection security concerns, and legal/compliance requirements. They addressed these through creative schema trimming, few-shot prompting, output validation, and extensive security controls, ultimately shipping the feature within a month while acknowledging that LLMs are engines for features rather than complete products.

title: LLM-Powered Data Classification System for Enterprise-Scale Metadata Generation
short_summary: Grab, Southeast Asia's leading superapp, faced challenges in classifying petabyte-scale data entities for sensitive information and PII detection. Manual classification campaigns were insufficient due to data volume, velocity, and inconsistent policy interpretation across teams. The company built an orchestration service called Gemini that integrates GPT-3.5 for automated column-level tag classification using prompt engineering techniques. The LLM-based approach allowed data governance personnel to express requirements through natural language prompts without needing dedicated ML teams or custom model training. Within a month of rollout, the system scanned over 20,000 data entities (300-400 daily), with 80% of users reporting the new process helped with tagging. The solution achieved significant time savings (approximately 360 man-days per year) at an affordable cost, enabling downstream applications like Attribute-based Access Control and Dynamic Data Masking.

title: Enterprise LLM Application Development: GitHub Copilot's Journey
short_summary: GitHub shares its three-year journey building GitHub Copilot, an LLM-powered code assistant that went from concept to production through a "find it, nail it, scale it" framework. The team focused on a specific problem (IDE-based code suggestions), implemented robust A/B testing and experimentation infrastructure, used techniques like neighboring tabs to improve suggestion acceptance rates by 5%, and scaled from OpenAI's API to Microsoft Azure infrastructure for enterprise reliability. Results showed developers coding up to 55% faster with 74% reporting improved satisfaction, demonstrating successful production deployment of LLMs at scale.

title: Neural Search and Conversational AI for Food Delivery and Restaurant Discovery
short_summary: Swiggy, India's leading food and grocery delivery platform, developed an in-house neural search capability powered by a fine-tuned Large Language Model to enable conversational, open-ended queries for food discovery across their 50 million-plus item catalog. The solution addresses the challenge of overwhelming choice by allowing users to search naturally (e.g., "I just finished my workout. Show me healthy lunch options") and receive personalized recommendations. The company extended this approach across their ecosystem, building conversational bots for restaurant discovery (Dineout), grocery shopping (Instamart), and partner support tools, while also collaborating with a third party on a GPT-4 powered customer service chatbot.

title: Strategic Framework for Generative AI Implementation in Food Delivery Platform
short_summary: Doordash outlines a strategic framework for implementing Generative AI across five key areas of their food delivery platform: customer task assistance, personalized discovery, content generation, structured information extraction, and employee productivity enhancement. The company identifies potential use cases ranging from automated cart building and voice-powered ordering to OCR-based receipt processing and SQL query generation. While the blog post presents an aspirational roadmap rather than documented production implementations, it acknowledges key challenges including data privacy, security considerations, and ethical implications of AI bias that must be addressed in deployment.

title: Building an AI Co-pilot for Product Strategy with LLM Integration Patterns
short_summary: Thoughtworks built Boba, an experimental AI co-pilot for product strategy and ideation, to explore effective patterns for LLM-powered applications beyond simple chat interfaces. The team developed and documented key patterns including templated prompts, structured responses, real-time progress streaming, context management, and external knowledge integration. The case study provides detailed implementation insights for building sophisticated LLM applications with better user experiences.

title: LLM-Enhanced Trust and Safety Platform for E-commerce Content Moderation
short_summary: Whatnot, a fast-growing livestream shopping marketplace, faced challenges with scam detection and content moderation as their platform scaled. Traditional rule engines and single-message ML models could not capture the contextual patterns of fraudulent conversations. By integrating LLMs (specifically leveraging GPT-4 capabilities) into their trust and safety stack, they analyze entire conversation threads alongside user signals to detect scams with high accuracy. The system uses zero-shot and few-shot prompting to classify scam likelihood, returning structured JSON outputs that feed into their existing rule engine for automated enforcement. Results reported include proactive detection of over 95% of scam attempts within minutes, with 96% precision and high recall. The approach has been extended to detect off-platform transactions and harassment.

title: AI-Powered Slack Conversation Summarization System
short_summary: Salesforce AI Research developed AI Summarist, a conversational AI tool that addresses the cognitive overload experienced by Slack users who must monitor multiple channels. The solution uses state-of-the-art NLP models to automatically disentangle conversations from message streams and generate concise summaries on demand. Users can request ad-hoc summaries of threads or entire channels, schedule recurring daily or weekly summaries, and click through to original messages for context. The system prioritizes data privacy by not storing chat content or generated summaries, only retaining metadata and optional user feedback for model improvement. While specific performance metrics are not disclosed, the tool aims to help users optimize time spent on Slack, personalize information consumption, and catch up quickly after time away.

title: Building and Scaling an Enterprise AI Assistant with GPT Models
short_summary: Instacart developed Ava, an internal AI assistant powered by OpenAI's GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 models, to boost employee productivity across the organization. Starting as a hackathon project focused on engineering use cases, Ava evolved into a company-wide tool with over half of Instacart's employees using it monthly and 900+ using it weekly. The solution includes a web interface similar to ChatGPT with features like conversation search, automatic model upgrades, a "Prompt Exchange" for sharing reusable prompts, and Slack integration for thread summarization and conversational AI. The case study demonstrates how to scale an internal LLM-powered tool from an engineering prototype to enterprise-wide deployment while managing user experience, adoption, and cross-functional accessibility.

title: Building an AI-Powered Help Desk with RAG and Model Evaluation
short_summary: Vimeo developed an AI-powered help desk chat prototype to address limitations in their traditional customer support systems, which struggled with search relevance and immediate query resolution. The solution uses a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, indexing Zendesk Help Center articles into a vector store (HNSWLib) and leveraging LangChain to orchestrate conversational retrieval with multiple LLM providers including Google Vertex AI Chat Bison, OpenAI GPT-3.5 Turbo, and GPT-4. After comparative testing across models for performance, cost, and response quality, they selected Google Vertex AI Chat Bison for its concise responses, faster processing, and seamless GCP authentication. The prototype demonstrated the ability to provide immediate, accurate, and contextually relevant answers to customer inquiries, though the team encountered challenges around outdated training data in LLMs and quality assurance for generated responses.

title: Building and Deploying Large Language Models for Skills Extraction at Scale
short_summary: LinkedIn developed a multi-stage AI pipeline to extract and map skills from unstructured content across its platform (job postings, member profiles, resumes, LinkedIn Learning courses, and feeds) to power their Skills Graph. The solution combines trie-based token matching with semantic skill tagging using a two-tower model based on Multilingual BERT, followed by skill expansion and multitask cross-domain scoring. To meet stringent latency requirements (under 100ms for ~200 profile edits per second), they employed Knowledge Distillation to reduce model size by 80% without sacrificing performance. The system incorporates feedback loops from recruiters and job seekers for continuous model improvement. Results included improvements across job recommendations (+0.14% applicants, +0.46% confirmed hires), job search engagement (+0.23%), and qualified applications (+0.87%).

title: Improving Contextual Understanding in GitHub Copilot Through Advanced Prompt Engineering
short_summary: GitHub's engineering teams have continuously improved GitHub Copilot's ability to understand code context through several key innovations. The core challenge was that transformer LLMs could only process about 6,000 characters at a time, limiting how much developer code could inform suggestions. Solutions included prompt engineering to optimize data prioritization, the "neighboring tabs" technique that considers all open IDE files (yielding 5% relative improvement in suggestion acceptance), the Fill-in-the-Middle paradigm that considers code both before and after the cursor (yielding 10% relative improvement), and experimentation with vector databases and embeddings for semantic code matching across entire repositories. These improvements help GitHub Copilot provide more contextually relevant code suggestions while maintaining low latency.

title: Building and Scaling an LLM-Powered Query Assistant in Production
short_summary: Honeycomb faced a challenge with new users struggling to learn their data querying interface, impacting product activation and retention. They built Query Assistant, an LLM-powered natural language to query translation feature using GPT-3.5-turbo and text-embedding-ada-002. After rapid iteration informed by production data, the feature showed strong positive correlations with key activation metrics: teams using Query Assistant had 26.5% manual querying retention at week 6 versus 4.5% for non-users, and showed higher rates of complex query creation (33% vs 15.7%) and Board creation (11% vs 3.6%). Operating costs remained remarkably low at approximately $30/month for OpenAI API calls, though adoption among free-tier users was lower than hoped at 39%. The team emphasized that LLMs require a "ship to learn" approach since traditional debugging and unit testing don't apply to nondeterministic systems.

title: Detecting and Mitigating Prompt Injection via Control Characters in ChatGPT
short_summary: Dropbox's security team discovered a novel prompt injection technique using control characters (such as backspace and carriage return) that can circumvent system instructions in OpenAI's GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 models. By prepending large quantities of encoded control characters to user input, researchers were able to cause the models to ignore their original instructions, forget provided context, and even hallucinate responses to completely different questions. This research highlights important security considerations for production LLM applications and emphasizes the need for proper input sanitization strategies when deploying LLM-powered products.

title: Strategic Implementation of Generative AI at Scale
short_summary: TomTom, facing the need to stay competitive in location technology, implemented a comprehensive GenAI strategy using a hub-and-spoke organizational model to democratize AI innovation across the company. The solution involved a central Innovation Hub team overseeing strategic direction while local "spoke" teams identified domain-specific opportunities, resulting in multiple production applications including a ChatGPT location plugin, an in-car AI assistant (Tommy), and developer documentation chatbots. The company achieved these outcomes without significant additional investment or hiring by leveraging Azure OpenAI partnerships, deploying internal tools like GitHub Copilot and an open-source ChatGPT alternative called "Chatty," and implementing extensive upskilling programs including hackathons and training initiatives.

title: AI-Powered Lesson Generation System for Language Learning
short_summary: Duolingo faced the challenge of creating and maintaining language learning content for over 21 million daily users with fewer than 1,000 employees, resulting in new course content being released only a few times per year. The company implemented a Large Language Model system that generates lesson exercises based on structured prompts created by their learning designers, incorporating parameters like target language, CEFR difficulty level, grammar focus, and thematic elements. This human-in-the-loop approach allows teaching experts to generate multiple exercise options with a single click, then review, edit, and select the best outputs before publication. The solution aims to increase content production speed, enabling deeper curriculum development, expansion of ancillary features, and broader support for smaller language courses.

title: LLM Evaluation Framework for Financial Crime Report Generation
short_summary: Sumup, a financial technology company, developed an LLM-powered system to generate financial crime reports (Reason for Suspicion narratives) for Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance. The core challenge was evaluating these free-text narratives, as traditional NLP metrics like ROUGE scores failed to capture meaningful quality differences. Their solution employed an LLM-driven evaluator with custom benchmark checks covering topic coverage, customer profile data, supporting facts, avoiding hallucinations, and conclusion quality. The evaluator produces numerical scores (0-5) with explanations, successfully differentiating between high-quality (4.67 average) and poor-quality (2.5 average) generated texts. Testing with real compliance agents showed the automated evaluation closely matched human assessments and identified similar areas for improvement, enabling data scientists to iterate on model improvements without requiring constant human review.

title: Enhancing E-commerce Search with GPT-based Query Expansion
short_summary: Whatnot, a livestream shopping platform, faced challenges with misspelled queries and abbreviations degrading their search experience, leading users to incorrectly assume the platform lacked relevant content. They implemented an offline GPT-based query expansion system that processes frequently occurring search tokens to identify misspellings and expand abbreviations, storing results in a key-value cache for real-time lookup. This approach reduced irrelevant search content by more than 50% compared to their previous method while maintaining sub-250ms latency requirements by avoiding real-time LLM inference.

title: LLM-Powered Search Relevance Re-Ranking System
short_summary: LeBonCoin, France's largest second-hand marketplace with nearly 30 million monthly active users and over 60 million classified ads, faced the challenge of improving search relevance across a highly volatile, user-generated catalogue. The Search team implemented an LLM-powered Re-Ranker using a bi-encoder (two-tower) architecture based on DistilBERT to compute click propensity scores between user queries and ads. The system pre-computes ad embeddings offline and stores them in a vector database, while query embeddings are computed in real-time. The Re-Ranker works in tandem with ElasticSearch, re-sorting the top-k retrieved results before display. This first iteration delivered significant improvements: up to +5% in click and contact rates, and up to +10% improvement in user experience KPIs including nDCG and average clicked/contacted positions.

title: Multilingual Content Navigation and Localization System
short_summary: Intercom, a B2B SaaS customer support platform, evolved from a traditional ML-based chatbot (Resolution Bot) with high curation friction to an LLM-powered solution called Fin. By leveraging GPT-4 with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), they achieved comparable accuracy rates without requiring extensive manual curation. The team shipped production features within weeks of ChatGPT's release—including summarization, tone adjustment, and text expansion—and later launched Fin, a customer-facing bot that draws from knowledge bases to answer support queries with minimal hallucination. Their development approach emphasizes breadth-first iteration, rapid time-to-first-customer-use, and starting with powerful but expensive models like GPT-4 before optimizing for cost.

title: Specialized Text Editing LLM Development through Instruction Tuning
short_summary: Grammarly developed CoEdIT, an instruction-tuned LLM specialized for text editing tasks, to address the limitations of general-purpose LLMs in writing assistance. The team compiled a high-quality dataset of text editing examples with natural language instructions and fine-tuned FLAN-T5 models of varying sizes (770M to 11B parameters). The resulting CoEdIT models achieved state-of-the-art performance on multiple text editing benchmarks while being 12 to 60 times smaller than comparable models like GPT-3-Edit (175B parameters). Human evaluators preferred CoEdIT's outputs 64% of the time compared to just 10% for GPT-3-Edit, and the model demonstrated strong generalization to adjacent and composite editing tasks it wasn't explicitly trained on.

title: Production-Ready Question Generation System Using Fine-Tuned T5 Models
short_summary: Digits, an accounting automation company, implemented a fine-tuned T5-based generative model to automatically generate contextual questions that accountants can send to clients about financial transactions. The solution addresses the tedium of manually crafting transaction inquiries by generating professional or casual questions based on transaction descriptions and user personas. The system includes multi-layered safety checks for toxicity, hallucination detection, and human review before any generated content reaches clients. The implementation leverages TensorFlow Extended (TFX) pipelines on Google Cloud Vertex AI, with comprehensive evaluation metrics including Levenshtein distance, semantic similarity, and ROUGE scores to ensure quality before deployment.

title: Building Product Copilots: Engineering Challenges and Best Practices
short_summary: This academic study conducted by researchers at Microsoft and GitHub interviewed 26 professional software engineers building AI-powered "copilot" products across various companies to understand the challenges of integrating LLMs into production systems. The research identified significant pain points across the entire engineering lifecycle including prompt engineering difficulties, orchestration complexity, testing challenges with non-deterministic outputs, safety and compliance concerns, and gaps in developer tooling. The findings revealed that traditional software engineering practices are strained by AI integration, with engineers facing issues like fragile prompts, flaky tests, high costs for evaluation, and a lack of standardized best practices. The study proposes opportunities for improved tooling including prompt linters, automated benchmark creation, better visibility into agent behavior, and more unified development workflows.

title: Evolving GitHub Copilot through LLM Experimentation and User-Centered Design
short_summary: GitHub's research team (GitHub Next) experimented with GPT-4 to extend GitHub Copilot beyond code completion into new developer workflow areas including pull request summaries, documentation search, and command-line assistance. The team developed four key experimentation pillars (predictable, tolerable, steerable, verifiable) and learned that user experience design was often more critical than model accuracy alone. Key products emerged including Copilot for Pull Requests, Copilot for Docs (using RAG with embeddings and vector databases), and Copilot for CLI, with the team discovering that presenting AI outputs as editable suggestions rather than authoritative answers significantly improved user acceptance.

title: Advanced Prompt Engineering Techniques for Production LLM Applications
short_summary: Instacart developed and documented a suite of advanced prompt engineering techniques for their internal productivity tooling, specifically for their Ava family of products. The problem addressed was how to effectively leverage LLMs (particularly GPT-4) for production use cases while overcoming common challenges like hallucinations, inconsistent outputs, and formatting issues. Their solutions included techniques such as "Room for Thought" (giving models space to plan before answering), "Monte Carlo" (generating multiple options before synthesizing a final answer), "Self Correction" (having the model critique its own outputs), "Classifying" (using logit_bias to force valid categorical outputs), and "Puppetry" (pre-filling assistant responses to guide output format). These techniques were successfully deployed in production systems including automated pull request title and description generation, demonstrating practical improvements in output quality and reliability.

title: Semantic Product Matching Using Retrieval-Rerank Architecture
short_summary: Delivery Hero developed a semantic product matching system to identify similar products across their inventory and competitor offerings for pricing strategies, assortment gap analysis, and duplicate detection. The solution evolved through three approaches: starting with lexical matching using BM25 and inverted indices, progressing to SBERT-based semantic encoders fine-tuned on internal product pair datasets, and ultimately implementing a Retrieval-Rerank architecture that combines fast lexical retrieval with transformer-based cross-encoder reranking. Hard negative sampling was employed to improve model discrimination between truly similar and dissimilar product pairs.

title: From Mega-Prompts to Production: Lessons Learned Scaling LLMs in Enterprise Customer Support
short_summary: GoDaddy shares practical lessons from deploying LLMs in their customer support messaging channels, handling over 60,000 daily contacts across SMS, WhatsApp, and web. The team evolved from mega-prompts to multi-agent architectures, learned to implement guardrails for safe AI behavior, addressed model reliability and latency challenges, optimized memory management for conversations, and developed effective RAG strategies including Sparse Priming Representations. Key findings include that prompts aren't portable across models, structured outputs require validation, and comprehensive testing remains one of the most labor-intensive aspects of LLM operationalization.

title: Scaling Data Infrastructure for AI Features and RAG
short_summary: Notion faced challenges with rapid data growth (10x in three years, doubling every 6-12 months) that strained their existing data warehouse architecture, particularly for supporting AI features. They built an in-house data lake using Debezium CDC connectors, Kafka, Apache Hudi, Spark, and S3 to handle their update-heavy workload (90% updates vs inserts). The solution reduced end-to-end ingestion time from over a day to minutes for small tables and a couple of hours for large ones, saved over a million dollars in 2022 alone with proportionally higher savings in subsequent years, and critically enabled the infrastructure needed for Notion AI features including Search and AI Embedding RAG systems launched in 2023 and 2024.

title: Optimizing Text-to-SQL Pipeline Using Agent Experiments
short_summary: IDInsight developed Ask-a-Metric, a WhatsApp-based AI data analyst that enables users in the development sector to query SQL databases using natural language. The initial simple pipeline suffered from accuracy issues and was difficult to modify due to tight coupling. Experimenting with CrewAI's agentic approach improved accuracy to 100% on test questions but was prohibitively slow (>1 minute) and expensive (~$0.30 per query). By analyzing the agent's consistent behavior patterns, they created a "pseudo-agent" pipeline that hardcodes the optimal sequence of steps and prompts discovered through agentic experimentation. This hybrid approach achieved response times under 15 seconds and costs below $0.02 per query while maintaining the accuracy improvements—meeting their production requirements of being 2-3x faster and 10x cheaper than the agentic version.

title: Building and Scaling LLM Applications at Discord
short_summary: Discord outlines their comprehensive approach to building LLM-powered features, from ideation through production deployment. The company addresses challenges of scaling generative AI for consumer applications by establishing a structured process that includes identifying suitable use cases, defining product requirements around latency and quality tradeoffs, prototyping with commercial LLMs like GPT-4, employing AI-assisted evaluation for prompt optimization, and ultimately deploying at scale with options for self-hosted open-source models like Llama and Mistral. Their methodology emphasizes rapid iteration through A/B testing, careful attention to safety and content moderation, and balancing cost against engineering effort when deciding between commercial APIs and self-hosted inference infrastructure.

title: Building Secure and Private Enterprise LLM Infrastructure
short_summary: Slack faced the challenge of integrating LLM-powered features into their collaboration platform while maintaining strict enterprise security, privacy, and compliance requirements. They solved this by developing a custom architecture that hosts closed-source LLMs within their own AWS trust boundary using an escrow VPC arrangement, employing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to avoid training on customer data, and enforcing user-level access controls. The result is Slack AI, which offers channel summarization and enhanced search capabilities while reportedly improving productivity for 90% of users who adopted it, all while maintaining FedRAMP Moderate authorization and existing compliance offerings.

title: Building a Scalable Retriever-Ranker Architecture: Malt's Journey with Vector Databases and LLM-Powered Freelancer Matching
short_summary: Malt, a freelancer marketplace platform, faced challenges with their monolithic matching system that suffered from slow response times (up to one minute) and scalability limitations. They implemented a retriever-ranker architecture combining bi-encoder models for fast initial retrieval with cross-encoder models for precise ranking, backed by Qdrant vector database. After benchmarking multiple solutions including Elasticsearch and PGVector, they chose Qdrant for its superior performance (90 queries per second vs 3-14 for alternatives) and geo-spatial filtering capabilities. The solution was deployed on Kubernetes with sharding and replication for high availability. Results showed dramatic improvement with p95 latency dropping from tens of seconds to under 3 seconds, while maintaining recommendation quality as confirmed by AB testing showing increased project conversion rates.

title: Enhancing E-commerce Search with LLM-Powered Semantic Retrieval
short_summary: Picnic, a European grocery delivery platform serving customers across the Netherlands, Germany, and France, faced the challenge of handling millions of diverse search queries across multiple languages while managing typos, ambiguous terms, and varying user intents. They implemented a semantic search system using GPT-3.5-turbo for prompt-based product description generation and OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small model for embeddings, with precomputation of common search terms to achieve millisecond-level latency. The solution leverages OpenSearch for fast retrieval and includes extensive caching mechanisms and sanity checks. The system underwent offline optimization followed by A/B testing to validate improvements in conversion rates, click-through rates, and customer satisfaction.

title: LLM Validation and Testing at Scale: GitLab's Comprehensive Model Evaluation Framework
short_summary: Gitlab faced the challenge of ensuring quality, reliability, and robustness for their AI-powered GitLab Duo features across diverse use cases without using customer data. They developed a Centralized Evaluation Framework (CEF) that utilizes thousands of curated prompts to test and validate LLM behavior at scale. The framework enables baseline model performance measurement, daily feature validation during development, and iterative prompt engineering improvements. By using metrics including Cosine Similarity Score, Cross Similarity Score, and LLM Judge techniques, GitLab can systematically evaluate multiple foundation models from providers like Google and Anthropic, ensuring their AI features continuously improve while avoiding overfitting or regression issues.
